- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 관계가 어휘 단서 없이 두 문장의 논리(양보 후 반전, 일반화 후 구체화, 원인 vs 결과 방향)에서 도출되는 문제. 오답 전환어도 일부 관계는 말이 된다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — On a crowded Nairobi matatu, aging rival conductors Kipchoge and Juma silently compete for passengers' respect until a medical crisis forces them to recognize each other's quiet dignity.

g.passage: For eleven years, Kipchoge and Juma had worked rival matatus on the Ngong Road route, each conductor quietly trying to outdo the other in courtesy, in the crisp folding of change, in remembering regular passengers' names. When an elderly passenger slumped against the window of Kipchoge's crowded vehicle one humid afternoon, Kipchoge glanced toward Juma, who had just boarded at the stage, and braced himself for a smirk at his rival's misfortune. ______ Juma pushed through the aisle without a word, loosened the old man's collar, and called out calmly for someone to pass him a bottle of water.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Instead,
Specifically,
As a result,
Nevertheless,
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 키프초게가 주마의 비웃음을 예상했다는 내용이고, 뒤 문장은 주마가 오히려 조용히 노인을 도왔다는 내용이다. 따라서 예상된 행동 대신 다른 행동이 일어났음을 나타내는 A가 정답이다. B는 앞의 내용을 구체화하는 연결어인데, 노인을 돕는 행동은 비웃음의 구체적 예가 아니다. C는 인과를 나타내지만, 키프초게가 마음의 준비를 했다고 해서 주마가 도운 것은 아니다. D는 양보 뒤의 반전을 나타내지만, 앞 문장은 인정된 사실이 아니라 빗나간 예상이므로 대체를 뜻하는 A가 더 정확하다.
g.explanation_en: The previous sentence tells you that Kipchoge expected Juma to smirk. The next sentence shows Juma quietly helping the old man. So Juma did something in place of what Kipchoge expected, and A expresses exactly that. B would introduce a specific detail of what came before, but helping the man isn't an example of smirking. C signals cause and effect, yet Kipchoge bracing himself didn't cause Juma to help. D signals a contrast that comes after a concession, but the first sentence is an expectation that turns out wrong, not a fact being conceded, so A's sense of replacement fits better.
g.design: There's no word in the text that points to the answer. To get it, you have to see that Kipchoge's expectation is reversed. B and C fit if you skim, and D shows up as a related contrast word that you have to compare carefully with A.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 관계가 어휘 단서 없이 두 문장의 논리(양보 후 반전, 일반화 후 구체화, 원인 vs 결과 방향)에서 도출되는 문제. 오답 전환어도 일부 관계는 말이 된다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — At a remote Mexican mountain bus depot, stray dog Ceniza adopts the Cortés family, transforming their isolated routine into unexpected tenderness that mocks their former loneliness.

g.passage: The following text is adapted from a short story. For eleven years, the Cortés family had run the bus depot at the top of the mountain road, selling tickets and coffee to passengers who rarely stayed longer than a cigarette. When a gray stray they named Ceniza began sleeping under the ticket counter, Señor Cortés insisted that she was useful only for barking at strangers, and he refused to let anyone feed her from the family table. ______ by the end of the rainy season, he was the one setting aside the best scraps of chicken each evening, murmuring to her as though she were an old friend who had finally come home.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Accordingly,
Even so,
In the same way,
Indeed,
g.explanation: 앞 문장에서 Señor Cortés는 개가 짖는 용도로만 쓸모 있다며 가족 식탁의 음식을 주지 못하게 했지만, 뒤 문장에서는 바로 그가 매일 저녁 가장 좋은 닭고기를 챙겨 주며 다정하게 말을 건넨다. 처음의 태도와 나중의 행동이 정반대이므로 대조·양보를 나타내는 B가 정답이다. A는 인과 관계를 나타내지만, 음식을 거부한 것이 나중에 음식을 챙겨 주게 된 원인이 될 수는 없다. C는 비슷한 행동을 나열할 때 쓰지만 두 행동은 비슷하지 않고 서로 반대된다. D는 앞의 내용을 강조하거나 확장하지만, 뒤 문장은 앞 문장의 거부를 강화하지 않고 오히려 뒤집는다.
g.explanation_en: In the first sentence, Señor Cortés says the dog is useful only for barking and won't let anyone feed her from the family table. In the next sentence, he is the one saving the best chicken for her every evening and talking to her fondly. His early attitude and his later behavior are opposites, so you need a contrast transition, which makes B the answer. A signals cause and effect, but refusing to feed the dog can't be the reason he later feeds her. C introduces a similar action, and these two actions are opposites, not parallels. D would emphasize or build on the earlier point, but the second sentence reverses his refusal instead of strengthening it.
g.design: 빈칸 앞에 전환을 드러내는 'but' 같은 단서 없이 태도가 뒤집히는 내용(거부→애정)을 배치했다. 그래서 두 문장을 비교해야 대조 관계를 파악할 수 있다. 'by the end of the rainy season'처럼 시간이 흐르는 표현이 있어 인과(A)나 강조(D)도 그럴듯해 보이도록 설계했다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Neighbors Rodrigo and Estéban on a Patagonian sheep ranch engage in an annual shearing contest where competition yields to appreciation of each other's weathered skill.

g.passage: Every November, Rodrigo and Estéban met at the shearing shed between their two ranches to see who could clip more ewes before sundown. For years the contest had been fierce: each man counted fleeces under his breath and glanced at the other's pile between animals. This year, Rodrigo pulled ahead early and seemed certain to win. ______ he found himself slowing down to watch Estéban turn a struggling ewe with one easy twist of his wrist, a move Rodrigo had never managed in forty seasons, and he forgot to keep counting.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Consequently,
For example,
Yet
Similarly,
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 Rodrigo가 앞서 나가 승리가 확실해 보였다는 내용이고, 뒤 문장은 그가 오히려 속도를 늦추고 Estéban의 기술을 지켜보며 세는 것도 잊었다는 예상 밖의 전개이므로 대조를 나타내는 C가 정답이다. A는 앞서 나간 것이 속도를 늦춘 원인인 것처럼 만드는데, 지문에서 그가 늦춘 이유는 Estéban의 솜씨이지 자신의 우위가 아니다. B는 뒤 문장을 앞서 나간 상황의 사례로 만들지만, 속도를 늦추는 것은 앞서 나가는 것의 예가 아니다. D는 두 문장이 비슷한 내용이라고 연결하지만, 둘은 서로 반대 방향이다.
g.explanation_en: The previous sentence says Rodrigo pulled ahead and seemed certain to win. The next sentence turns against that expectation: he slows down to admire Estéban's skill and stops counting. That is a contrast, so C is correct. A treats his lead as the cause of his slowing down, but the text says he slows down because of Estéban's skill, not because he is ahead. B presents slowing down as an example of pulling ahead, which doesn't make sense. D signals that the two ideas are alike, but they actually point in opposite directions.
g.design: 'pulled ahead … certain to win' 직후에 결과(Consequently)로 읽고 싶게 만들어 훑어 읽으면 A를 고르게 했다. 하지만 정독하면 기대가 반전된다는 점이 드러난다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 관계가 어휘 단서 없이 두 문장의 논리(양보 후 반전, 일반화 후 구체화, 원인 vs 결과 방향)에서 도출되는 문제. 오답 전환어도 일부 관계는 말이 된다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — On a 1930s Great Plains farmstead, Thomas misinterprets his neighbor's gift of seeds as criticism, only later grasping the generous intent behind the humble gesture.

g.passage: When Ezra Haldane rode over from the next section and left a flour sack of bean and squash seed on the porch, Thomas felt his face go hot. His own wheat had withered to stubble that August, and he was certain the gift was Haldane's quiet way of saying that a sensible man would have planted something hardier. ______ Haldane had pulled those seeds from his own meager harvest, saving out handfuls his family would have to do without come spring.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Similarly,
As a result,
For instance,
In reality,
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 Thomas가 선물을 비난으로 확신했다는 그의 해석이고, 뒤 문장은 Haldane이 자기 가족의 몫을 희생해 씨앗을 주었다는 실제 사정이므로, 잘못된 믿음과 실제를 대조하는 D가 정답이다. A는 두 문장이 같은 성격의 내용이라는 뜻이지만, 하나는 오해이고 다른 하나는 관대한 의도라서 서로 반대된다. B는 Thomas의 오해 때문에 Haldane이 씨앗을 아껴 두었다는 인과 관계를 만들지만, 씨앗을 모은 일은 오해보다 먼저 일어났고 오해의 결과도 아니다. C는 뒤 문장이 '비난'의 예라고 보는 것인데, 씨앗을 모은 구체적인 사정은 비난이 아니라 희생을 보여 준다.
g.explanation_en: The first sentence tells you what Thomas believed: the seeds were a rebuke. The next sentence shows what was actually true: Haldane gave up seed his own family needed. A transition that sets a mistaken belief against the real situation fits here, so D is correct. A suggests the two ideas are alike, but a suspected insult and a generous sacrifice are opposites. B makes Haldane's saving of the seeds a result of Thomas's suspicion, but Haldane set the seeds aside before Thomas misunderstood the gift, and the suspicion didn't cause it. C presents the second sentence as an example of the criticism, but the specific detail there shows sacrifice rather than criticism.
g.design: There is no word like "later" or "but" to signal the shift. To see the belief-versus-reality relationship, you have to recognize that the first sentence reports only Thomas's interpretation. B and C can tempt a reader who skims, because one sentence does follow the other in the story and the second sentence adds concrete detail.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — In 1920s Lagos market town, traders Adeyemi and Olusegun transform their cutthroat rivalry into cautious alliance when facing an external economic threat together.

g.passage: For eleven years, Adeyemi and Olusegun had kept their cloth stalls at opposite ends of the Ebute Metta market, each undercutting the other's prices and whispering to customers that the rival's indigo faded after one wash. When word spread in 1924 that a British trading firm would soon flood the town with cheap machine-printed fabric, Adeyemi expected Olusegun to slash his prices yet again, hoping to outlast them both. ______ Olusegun appeared at Adeyemi's stall one evening with a kola nut and a proposal: they would buy dye together, split the cost, and sell their hand-dyed cloth at a single shared price.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Instead,
As a result,
Similarly,
For example,
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 Adeyemi가 Olusegun이 또 가격을 내릴 것이라 예상했다는 내용이고, 뒤 문장은 Olusegun이 오히려 협력을 제안했다는 내용이므로, 예상과 다른 행동을 제시하는 A가 정답이다. B는 외국 회사의 위협이 협력의 원인처럼 보여 그럴듯하지만, 바로 앞 문장의 내용은 '가격 인하 예상'이므로 그 결과로 협력 제안이 나온다는 연결은 논리에 맞지 않는다. C는 두 행동이 비슷하다는 뜻인데, 가격 경쟁과 협력은 서로 반대되는 행동이다. D는 뒤 문장이 앞 문장의 예시여야 하지만, 협력 제안은 가격 인하 예상의 사례가 아니다.
g.explanation_en: The previous sentence tells you what Adeyemi expected: that Olusegun would cut his prices again. The next sentence shows Olusegun doing the opposite by proposing a partnership, so A, which introduces an alternative to what was expected, is correct. B is tempting because the British firm's threat really does cause the alliance, but the sentence right before the blank is about Adeyemi's expectation of more price-cutting, and a cooperative proposal does not follow as a result of that. C signals similarity, but price-cutting and cooperation are opposite actions. D would make the proposal an example of the expected price war, and it isn't one.
g.design: A cause-and-effect reading (threat → alliance) makes B attractive to someone skimming. To get it right, you have to notice that the sentence right before the blank sets up an expectation, and the next sentence goes against it.

- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A young woman and elderly man aboard a Nairobi matatu engage in an elaborate silent game about overhead seat possession, each testing the other's patience daily.

g.passage: Every morning on the matatu to Nairobi's city center, Wanjiru and the elderly man in the gray cap played the same game without saying a word. If she pushed her bag a few centimeters into the overhead rack above his seat, he would cough politely and slide his folded newspaper next to it. If he leaned his umbrella against her side of the rack, she would hum and adjust her scarf until he moved it back. To the other passengers, half asleep or scrolling on their phones, none of this would have looked like anything more than ordinary fidgeting. ______ for Wanjiru, each nudge and each cough was a carefully planned move in a contest that had now gone on for almost three months.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Indeed,
Yet,
Specifically,
Thus,
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 문장은 다른 승객들에게는 이 행동이 평범한 몸짓으로만 보였을 것이라고 말하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 Wanjiru에게는 그것이 치밀하게 계산된 수였다고 말한다. 같은 행동을 두고 다른 승객들의 시각과 Wanjiru의 시각이 반대되므로, 대조를 나타내는 B가 정답이다. A는 앞 문장의 내용을 강조하거나 더 밀고 나갈 때 쓰는데, 뒤 문장은 앞 문장을 강화하지 않고 뒤집는다. C는 구체적인 예를 들 때 쓰지만, 뒤 문장은 '평범한 몸짓'의 예시가 아니라 반대되는 해석이다. D는 인과 관계를 나타내지만, 다른 승객들이 눈치채지 못한 것이 Wanjiru가 이를 게임으로 여기는 원인은 아니다.
g.explanation_en: The sentence before the blank says that, to the other passengers, these actions would have looked like ordinary fidgeting. The sentence after it says that, for Wanjiru, each one was a carefully planned move. Because these two views of the same actions oppose each other, you need a contrast word, so B is correct. A is used to emphasize or build on the previous point, but the second sentence reverses that point instead of strengthening it. C introduces a specific example, but the second sentence is not an example of "ordinary fidgeting." It gives the opposite interpretation. D signals cause and effect, but the passengers' failure to notice is not what makes Wanjiru see the actions as a contest.
g.design: 문장 안에 대조 어휘 없이 '다른 승객들의 시각 vs Wanjiru의 시각'만으로 대조 관계를 만들었다. 훑어 읽으면 강조(A), 구체화(C), 인과(D)도 그럴듯해 보이도록 설계했다.

- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 관계가 어휘 단서 없이 두 문장의 논리(양보 후 반전, 일반화 후 구체화, 원인 vs 결과 방향)에서 도출되는 문제. 오답 전환어도 일부 관계는 말이 된다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Helmut inherits his estranged uncle's plain pocket watch from a Berlin allotment garden, discovering its engravings reveal a hidden family reconciliation decades old.

g.passage: Helmut had assumed the watch would tell him nothing about his uncle Rainer, whom he had not seen since childhood. Its steel case was scratched and unadorned, the kind sold at any Berlin train station kiosk, and the lawyer had handed it over in a paper envelope along with the key to the shed in Rainer's allotment garden. ______ when Helmut pried open the back cover that evening, he found two sets of initials engraved inside—his uncle's and his father's—above a date in 1991, two years after the brothers had supposedly quarreled for good.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Accordingly,
Similarly,
Even so,
For example,
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 시계가 평범하고 하찮게 건네져서 Helmut이 아무것도 알려 주지 않을 거라 여긴 이유를 보여 준다. 반면 마지막 문장은 그런 예상과 달리 화해를 암시하는 의미 있는 각인이 발견되었다는 내용이다. 따라서 앞의 내용을 인정하면서 예상 밖의 결과로 반전하는 C가 정답이다. A는 평범한 외관 때문에 각인을 발견했다는 인과 관계를 만들어 버리는데, 실제로는 기대를 뒤집는 내용이다. B는 비슷한 내용이 더해진다는 뜻이지만 의미 있는 각인은 평범한 외관과 비슷하지 않다. D는 각인을 시계가 평범하다는 것의 예시로 만드는데, 사실은 그 반대 내용이다.
g.explanation_en: The earlier sentences explain why Helmut expected nothing from the watch: it looked cheap and plain, and it was handed to him casually. The last sentence overturns that expectation, since the engravings point to a reconciliation between the brothers. That is a concession followed by a reversal, so C is correct. A sets up cause and effect, as if the plain case led to the discovery, but the discovery actually goes against what came before. B signals that the new detail is similar, but a meaningful engraving is not like a plain, ordinary case. D presents the engraving as an example of the watch's plainness, when it really shows the opposite.
g.design: There are no wording clues. The contrast comes only from Helmut's low expectations followed by a surprising discovery. Accordingly and For example look plausible at a glance because the sentences tell events in order and add details.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 관계가 어휘 단서 없이 두 문장의 논리(양보 후 반전, 일반화 후 구체화, 원인 vs 결과 방향)에서 도출되는 문제. 오답 전환어도 일부 관계는 말이 된다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — At a prairie Canadian grain elevator, Station Master Crawford's meticulous routine shatters when a sudden prairie storm forces him to trust his younger replacement's instincts.

g.passage: For thirty-one years, Station Master Crawford had refused to make any decision at the Wheatland grain elevator until he had copied the barometer reading into his ledger in neat, slanted figures. So when the sky to the west turned the color of bruised plums and his young replacement, Lise Moreau, called out that hail would reach the bins within minutes, his hand drifted toward the ledger as it always had. ______ he set the pencil down, looked once at her, and told her to seal the doors.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: As a result,
Similarly,
For instance,
Even so,
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 크로퍼드가 평소 습관대로 장부에 손을 뻗었다고 말하고, 뒷문장은 그가 연필을 내려놓고 후임자의 판단을 따랐다고 말하므로 습관과 반대되는 행동이 이어진다. 따라서 앞 내용을 인정한 뒤 반전시키는 D가 정답이다. A는 리즈의 경고를 원인으로 보면 그럴듯하지만, 바로 앞 내용은 습관적으로 장부에 손을 뻗은 행동이고 이것이 연필을 내려놓는 결과를 낳지는 않는다. B는 습관을 따르는 비슷한 행동이 이어질 때만 맞는데, 뒷문장은 습관을 깨는 행동이다. C는 뒷문장이 앞의 일반적 진술에 대한 사례가 아니므로 맞지 않다.
g.explanation_en: The previous sentence says Crawford's hand moved toward the ledger out of habit, and the next sentence shows him putting the pencil down and following Lise's call, which goes against that habit. So you need a transition that admits the first point and then reverses it, and that is D. A might look right if you treat Lise's warning as the cause, but the sentence right before the blank describes his habitual reach for the ledger, and that reach does not lead to him dropping the pencil. B would fit only if he did something similar that kept his routine, but he breaks it instead. C doesn't work because the final sentence is not an example of a general claim made earlier.
g.design: There is no word-level clue. Students must catch the reversal between his habitual reach for the ledger and his decision to trust her. A tempts readers who skim and see Lise's warning as the cause, and B tempts readers who focus on the habit.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 관계가 어휘 단서 없이 두 문장의 논리(양보 후 반전, 일반화 후 구체화, 원인 vs 결과 방향)에서 도출되는 문제. 오답 전환어도 일부 관계는 말이 된다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — In a Texas border town, widower Rafael reluctantly shelters a starving dog that gradually awakens his capacity to love again after years of deliberate numbness.

g.passage: For six years after his wife's death, Rafael had kept his small house on the edge of the border town silent and spare, letting nothing new take root there. When the starving dog appeared beneath his porch, he set out a bowl of water and told his neighbor, Mrs. Ochoa, that the animal would go to the county shelter the moment it could walk without limping. ______ that same evening he drove forty minutes to Laredo and came home with a cushioned bed, a leather collar, and a sack of food large enough to last a year.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Even so,
Accordingly,
For instance,
Likewise,
g.design: 빈칸 앞 문장(곧 보호소로 보내겠다는 말)과 뒤 문장(1년치 사료·목줄 구입)의 대비를 어휘 단서 없이 읽어 내야 한다. 훑어 읽으면 '다리 회복을 돕는 준비'로 보여 Accordingly를, '돌봄의 예'로 보여 For instance를 고를 수 있다.
g.explanation: 라파엘은 개가 다리를 절지 않게 되면 곧 보호소로 보내겠다고 말했지만, 바로 그날 밤 1년치 사료와 목줄, 침대를 사 온다. 일시적으로만 맡겠다는 말과 오래 키울 사람처럼 하는 행동이 서로 어긋나므로, 앞의 내용과 반대되는 사실을 덧붙이는 A가 정답이다. B는 물과 회복을 돕는 준비가 계획에 따른 결과처럼 보일 수 있지만, 1년치 사료와 목줄은 곧 보내겠다는 계획에서 나오지 않는다. C는 사 온 물건들이 그가 개를 돌본다는 예처럼 보이지만, 앞 문장은 일반적인 주장이 아니라 개를 보내겠다는 말이어서 뒤 문장이 그 예가 될 수 없다. D는 두 행동이 비슷하다는 뜻인데, 실제로는 두 행동이 서로 반대된다.
g.explanation_en: Rafael says the dog will go to the shelter as soon as it stops limping, but that same night he buys a year's worth of food, a collar, and a bed. What he says (the stay is temporary) clashes with what he does (he acts like a long-term owner), so A, which introduces a fact that goes against what came before, is correct. B might seem to work because getting supplies could look like part of helping the dog recover, but a year of food and a collar don't follow from a plan to give the dog away soon. C treats the purchases as an example of his caring, but the previous sentence is a statement that he'll give the dog up, not a general claim, so the purchases can't be an example of it. D signals that the two actions are similar, when they actually contradict each other.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 관계가 어휘 단서 없이 두 문장의 논리(양보 후 반전, 일반화 후 구체화, 원인 vs 결과 방향)에서 도출되는 문제. 오답 전환어도 일부 관계는 말이 된다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A 1970s Appalachian mining town resident walks two hours daily to retrieve a single library book, the irony of such effort for such small comfort never lost on her.

g.passage: Every morning, Ada Combs walked the two hours from Harlan Hollow down to the crossroads where the county bookmobile parked, and every morning she was permitted to borrow exactly one book. She understood better than anyone in the hollow how lopsided the bargain was: four hours of gravel road and coal-truck dust for a slim paperback she would finish before supper. ______ she laced her boots again each dawn, yesterday's book wrapped in wax paper and tucked inside her coat.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Accordingly,
Even so,
In other words,
Moreover,
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 Ada가 이 거래가 수고에 비해 터무니없이 손해라는 것을 잘 알고 있었다고 말하고, 마지막 문장은 그런데도 그녀가 매일 새벽 다시 길을 나섰다고 말한다. 불리함을 인정한 뒤 예상과 반대되는 행동이 이어지므로 양보 후 반전을 나타내는 B가 정답이다. A는 '그래서'라는 인과를 뜻하지만, 손해라는 인식은 계속 걸을 이유가 되지 않으므로 방향이 맞지 않는다. 그녀가 매일 걸었다는 내용만 보면 그럴듯해 보일 뿐이다. C는 앞 내용을 다시 풀어 말할 때 쓰는데, 다시 걸어가는 행동은 거래가 손해라는 말을 바꿔 말한 것이 아니다. D는 같은 방향의 정보를 덧붙이는 말이어서, 두 문장 사이의 긴장 관계를 놓친다.
g.explanation_en: The previous sentence says Ada knew better than anyone how lopsided the trade was. The final sentence says she set out again every dawn anyway. Because she admits the cost and then does the opposite of what you'd expect, the transition must show concession followed by contrast, so B is correct. A signals cause and effect, but seeing the trip as a bad bargain doesn't explain why she keeps going, so the logic runs the wrong way. It only seems to fit because she does walk every day. C introduces a restatement, but setting out again isn't a rewording of the idea that the trade was lopsided. D adds information that points the same way, so it misses the tension between the two sentences.
g.design: 빈칸 앞뒤에 대조를 알리는 어휘 단서는 두지 않았다. '손해임을 앎'에서 '그래도 매일 감'으로 이어지는 흐름에서 양보 관계를 추론해야 한다. 지문을 훑어 읽으면 매일 걸었다는 사실 때문에 인과(A)나 첨가(D)가 그럴듯해 보이도록 설계했다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 관계가 어휘 단서 없이 두 문장의 논리(양보 후 반전, 일반화 후 구체화, 원인 vs 결과 방향)에서 도출되는 문제. 오답 전환어도 일부 관계는 말이 된다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — At a Mexican mountain bus depot, young Lucía observes stranded travelers' unspoken sorrows that adults dismiss, her quiet noticing eventually comforting a grieving stranger.

g.passage: The bus to Oaxaca had been delayed for six hours by a rockslide, and the depot in the mountains had filled with tired travelers. The adults around Lucía complained loudly about the schedule and paid little attention to one another. Lucía, though, kept watching an elderly man in a gray suit who held a folded funeral card and never once looked up at the departures board. Her aunt told her the man was simply impatient, like everyone else. ______ Lucía had seen him smooth the card's edges again and again, and she slid onto the bench beside him and quietly offered him half of her sweet bread.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Accordingly,
Similarly,
Even so,
For instance,
g.explanation: 이모는 노인이 그저 조바심을 내는 것이라고 말하지만, 루시아는 그 말과 달리 노인의 슬픔을 알아채고 위로하러 다가간다. 따라서 앞 문장의 주장을 인정하면서도 반대되는 행동이 이어지는 양보·반전 관계이므로 C가 정답이다. A는 이모의 말 때문에 루시아가 다가갔다는 결과 관계를 만들지만, 이모의 설명은 오히려 다가갈 이유를 지워 버린다. B는 둘을 비슷한 것으로 묶지만, 루시아의 관찰은 이모의 판단과 반대된다. D는 뒤 문장을 '그저 조바심'이라는 말의 예시로 만들지만, 카드를 계속 매만지는 모습은 조바심이 아니라 슬픔을 보여 준다.
g.explanation_en: The aunt says the man is just impatient, but Lucía acts against that view: she has seen signs of his grief and goes to comfort him. That is a concession followed by a contrast, so C is correct. A makes Lucía's action a result of her aunt's remark, but the remark actually gives her no reason to go over to him. B treats the two sentences as alike, yet Lucía's observation goes against the aunt's judgment. D makes the next sentence an example of plain impatience, but smoothing a funeral card over and over shows sorrow, not impatience.
g.design: 빈칸 바로 앞에는 이모의 판단이 있고, 정답을 고르려면 이 판단과 루시아가 앞서 본 장례 카드라는 단서를 연결해야 한다. 훑어 읽으면 결과(A)나 예시(D)도 그럴듯해 보이도록 만들었다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 관계가 어휘 단서 없이 두 문장의 논리(양보 후 반전, 일반화 후 구체화, 원인 vs 결과 방향)에서 도출되는 문제. 오답 전환어도 일부 관계는 말이 된다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — In postwar Vienna, Frau Weber repairs a broken music box belonging to her boarding house tenant, its melody unlocking her own suppressed memories of lost loved ones.

g.passage: In the cold winter of 1947, Frau Weber spread the parts of her tenant's broken music box across the kitchen table of her Vienna boarding house. She told herself the work was purely practical: the young violinist upstairs was behind on his rent, and a small favor might keep him from leaving before spring. ______ when she finally fit the bent comb back into place and the cylinder began to turn, she found that she had set down her tweezers and was quietly humming along, recalling the lullaby her sister had sung to their children before the war took them all.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Consequently,
Indeed,
Similarly,
Even so,
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 Frau Weber가 수리를 순전히 실용적인 일(집세 문제)로 여겼다고 말하고, 뒷 문장은 멜로디가 그녀의 개인적 상실의 기억을 일깨워 실용적 태도와 어긋나는 반응을 보였다고 말하므로 대조를 나타내는 D가 정답이다. A는 실용적 동기가 감정적 반응을 일으켰다는 인과 관계를 만들지만, 집세 계산이 허밍과 회상의 원인이 될 수는 없다. B는 앞 내용을 강조하거나 확증하는 말인데, 뒷 문장은 '순전히 실용적'이라는 생각을 뒷받침하지 않고 오히려 뒤집는다. C는 두 문장이 비슷한 내용을 담고 있음을 뜻하지만, 실용적 동기와 감정적 회상은 서로 비슷하지 않고 대립한다.
g.explanation_en: The first sentence says Frau Weber saw the repair as purely practical, a way to keep a tenant who owed rent. The next sentence shows the melody pulling her into private grief, which goes against that practical view, so you need a contrast: choice D. Choice A sets up cause and effect, but her concern about rent can't explain why she ended up humming and remembering her sister. Choice B would confirm or stress the first sentence, yet the second sentence undercuts the idea that the work was "purely practical." Choice C suggests the two sentences say similar things, but practical motives and emotional memory pull in opposite directions here.
g.design: There's no "but" or "however" in the passage to signal the contrast. You have to see that "told herself... purely practical" is a claim the next sentence's emotional reaction overturns. A, B, and C each read smoothly if you skim, since the second sentence could look like a result, a stronger restatement, or a parallel point.

C might seem logical if you link the redone belts to the late-night practice, but the sentence right before the blank is about Cisco's practical motive, and that motive doesn't lead to decorative work. Still,
Similarly,
In other words,
g.design: 빈칸 앞은 떠나도 된다는 자기 설득(양보), 뒤는 몸이 마을에 매달리는 반응(반전)으로, 대조 어휘 없이 두 문장의 논리로 관계를 파악해야 한다. 오답은 '안정적인 연속 장면'이나 '같은 감정의 재진술'로 훑어 읽으면 그럴듯하게 보인다.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞에서 Sigríðr는 마을이 자신 없이도 괜찮다며 떠나는 것을 스스로 정당화하지만, 빈칸 뒤에서는 돌에 손을 대고 멈춰 서서 마을에 대한 애착을 드러낸다. 따라서 앞의 생각과 어긋나는 반응을 이끄는 B가 정답이다. A는 마을이 그녀를 필요로 하지 않는다는 생각이 멈춰 서는 행동의 원인이 되는 것처럼 만들지만, 실제로 그 행동은 그 생각에 맞서는 반응이다. C는 두 문장을 비슷한 내용으로 보지만, 하나는 떠남을, 다른 하나는 머묾을 향한다. D는 뒤 문장을 앞 문장의 재진술로 보지만, 뒤 문장은 앞의 내용을 다시 말하는 것이 아니라 그 내용을 뒤집는다.

After the blank, she stops walking and presses her hand to the stones, showing how attached she still is to the village. Because that reaction goes against what she just told herself, B is correct. A treats her belief that she isn't needed as the cause of her stopping, but her stopping actually pushes back against that belief. Even so,
Similarly,
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 선생님이 자신의 은퇴를 한 번도 언급하지 않았다고 말하고, 뒷문장은 그럼에도 학생들이 모든 예시에서 이별의 의미를 알아챘다고 말한다. 언급하지 않았는데도 알아챘다는 양보 후 반전 관계이므로 C가 정답이다. A는 뒷문장에 예시가 나열되어 그럴듯하지만, 그 예시들은 앞 문장에서 말한 '은퇴를 언급하지 않음'의 사례가 아니다. B는 언급하지 않은 것이 학생들이 알아챈 원인이 되는 것이 아니므로 인과가 맞지 않는다. D는 두 문장이 같은 종류의 내용이 아니라 서로 대조되므로 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The first sentence tells you Mr. Jayasinghe never mentioned that he was being replaced, and the next says the students still noticed that his examples were all about parting. They picked up on the farewell even though he never said it, so the sentences show a concession followed by a reversal, and C is correct. A is tempting because the second sentence lists examples, but those examples don't illustrate his silence about retiring. B is wrong because his silence isn't what caused the students to notice. D doesn't work because the two sentences contrast with each other instead of making similar points.
g.design: There is no word in the passage that signals the contrast. You have to see that "never mentioned" is set against "students noticed." The list of examples makes A look right, and B looks possible if you read too fast.

g.explanation: 앞 문장은 Otto가 부모의 말을 확인해 줄 편지를 기대했다는 내용이고, 뒷 문장은 실제로 위조 서류가 나왔다는 내용이므로 기대가 다른 것으로 대체되었음을 나타내는 D가 정답이다. A는 기대가 위조 서류의 원인이라는 뜻이 되어 인과 관계가 성립하지 않는다. B는 두 문장이 비슷한 내용이라는 뜻이지만 실제로는 정반대다. C는 대조를 담고 있어 그럴듯하지만, 앞 내용에도 '불구하고' 무언가가 계속된다는 양보를 나타낼 뿐이어서 기대가 다른 결과로 바뀌었다는 관계를 표현하지 못한다.

g.design: The text sets up an expectation and then reverses it, and no other word in the passage points to the answer. "Nevertheless" is a contrast-based distractor that only partly fits, so students have to tell replacement apart from concession.

options: trailed
trailing
having trailed
to trail
g.explanation: 두 번째 문장의 주어는 "the puppy"이고, 그 뒤의 관계절 "that he had carried home..."과 독립 분사구 "its coat still stiff..."는 수식어일 뿐이므로 이 주어에는 아직 정동사가 없다. 따라서 빈칸에는 과거 시제 정동사가 와야 하며, A "trailed"가 주어와 결합해 완전한 독립절을 만든다. B "trailing"과 C "having trailed"는 분사이므로 정동사 역할을 하지 못해 문장이 완성되지 않는데, 빈칸 앞의 긴 수식어구 때문에 동사가 이미 나온 것처럼 착각하기 쉽다. D "to trail"은 부정사라서 역시 주절의 동사가 될 수 없다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of the second sentence is "the puppy," and both the relative clause "that he had carried home..." and the absolute phrase "its coat still stiff..." are only modifiers, so the subject has no main verb yet. The blank therefore needs a finite past-tense verb, and A, "trailed," gives the sentence a complete independent clause. B, "trailing," and C, "having trailed," are participles, so they can't act as the main verb, and the sentence stays incomplete; the long modifiers before the blank can trick you into thinking a verb has already appeared. D, "to trail," is an infinitive, so it also can't be the main verb.
g.design: The subject is separated from the blank by a relative clause plus an absolute phrase, so you have to find the subject and notice the missing main verb (structure) before choosing the finite form over nonfinite ones.

having been

g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'list'이고, 'along with two jars...'는 삽입구라서 주어를 복수로 만들지 않는다. 또 'when she returned'와 지문 전체가 과거 시제이므로 단수 과거형 동사가 필요하다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 과거 시제는 맞지만, 삽입구 속 복수 명사 'jars'에 맞춘 복수형이라 틀리다. C는 단수형이지만 현재 시제라 과거 문맥과 어긋나고, D는 분사라서 문장에 정동사가 없게 된다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "list." The phrase "along with two jars..." is an interrupting phrase, so it doesn't make the subject plural. A is in the right tense, but it's plural because it agrees with "jars," the plural noun inside the interrupting phrase. C is singular but in the present tense, which clashes with the past-tense context, and D is a participle, so it leaves the sentence without a main verb.

g.design: 이 문항은 두 단계 판단이 필요하도록 만들었다. 첫째, 긴 관계절이 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어 있어 단수 주어 "The ritual"을 찾아야 한다. 둘째, 정동사(본동사)가 필요한지를 확인해야 한다. 오답 B는 가까운 복수 명사 "customers"에 맞춘 함정이고, C와 D는 비정동사(분사)라서 문장에 본동사가 없게 된다.

g.explanation_en: The subject of the sentence is the singular noun "The ritual," and the relative clause that begins with "which" ends at "section." So the blank needs a finite verb that is singular and fits the past-tense narration, which makes A correct. B is past tense, but it is plural, so it wrongly agrees with the nearby plural noun "customers." C and D are participles, not finite verbs, so with either one the sentence would have no main verb.

A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 콤마 스플라이스가 되는데, 삽입구 때문에 뒤쪽을 수식어로 잘못 읽으면 맞아 보인다. C는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문이다. D는 등위접속사 and를 쓰긴 했지만 쉼표가 and 앞이 아니라 뒤에 와서 잘못 배치되었다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("he wrote ... only dust") is an independent clause. The text after it ("each line of chalk ... seemed to him ...") is also an independent clause: its subject and verb are just separated by a long interrupting phrase. You can join two independent clauses with a semicolon, so B is correct. A joins them with only a comma, which creates a comma splice; it can look right if the interrupting phrase makes you misread the second part as a modifier. C fuses the two clauses with no punctuation, which makes it a run-on. D uses the conjunction "and," but the comma comes after "and" instead of before it, so it's misplaced.

g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'the first hail rattled against the swings'와 빈칸 뒤 'Mrs. Laing's whistle shrilled across the field'는 각각 독립절이므로, 세미콜론으로 연결한 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표 하나로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. B는 쉼표+and 조합까지는 맞지만 and 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣어 주어와 접속사를 갈라놓는다. D도 and 뒤에 쉼표가 붙어 있고 and 앞에는 쉼표가 없어 잘못된 구두점이다.

g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

beneath the lining,

g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "she found what the damage had long kept hidden"은 완전한 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "someone had etched..."도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 콜론은 앞 절이 예고한 '숨겨진 것'의 정체를 뒤 절이 밝혀 주므로 D가 정답이다. A는 두 독립절을 쉼표만으로 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. B는 "beneath the lining"이 앞 절의 hidden에 붙는 수식어처럼 읽혀 그럴듯하지만, 결국 쉼표 하나로 두 독립절을 연결하므로 역시 쉼표 오용이다. C는 세미콜론 뒤에 등위접속사 and를 불필요하게 덧붙여 어법에 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The part before the blank, "she found what the damage had long kept hidden," is a complete independent clause, and "someone had etched..." after the blank is also an independent clause with its own subject and verb. A colon works here because the second clause reveals what the first clause promises (the thing that was hidden), so D is correct. A joins the two independent clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B is tempting because "beneath the lining" seems to describe where something was hidden, but the clauses are still joined by a single comma, so it is also a comma splice. C adds the coordinating conjunction "and" after a semicolon, which is unnecessary and nonstandard.
g.design: A long appositive comes before the clause boundary, and the prepositional phrase in B can be read as attaching to "hidden," so a student skimming the sentence may miss that it's a comma splice. The colon choice only works if you notice that the first clause sets up a reveal.

g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: tenement,

tenement—
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 "The pigeon"이고 동사는 "healed"입니다. 그 사이에 있는 "a gray-banded creature ... tenement"는 쉼표로 시작된 비필수 동격어구이므로 같은 문장부호인 쉼표로 닫아야 하며, 따라서 A가 정답입니다. B는 동격어구를 닫지 않아 주어와 동사의 경계가 흐려집니다. C는 세미콜론이 앞부분을 독립절처럼 끊어 놓지만, 앞부분에는 동사가 없습니다. D의 대시는 삽입구를 닫을 수는 있으나, 쉼표로 연 삽입구를 대시로 닫아 문장부호가 서로 맞지 않습니다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "The pigeon," and its verb is "healed." Between them, "a gray-banded creature ... tenement" is a nonessential appositive that opens with a comma, so it must close with a comma too. That makes A correct. B never closes the appositive, which blurs where the subject ends and the verb begins. C uses a semicolon, which would treat the opening words as an independent clause, but those words have no verb. D's dash could close an interruption, but a dash can't close an appositive that opened with a comma because the marks have to match.
g.design: To answer correctly, students have to see that the long appositive opened with a comma and then find the verb "healed" that comes after it. D (dash) and C (semicolon) look plausible to students who skim, so each must be checked against the sentence.

The distractors are a comma splice, a run-on, and a fragment built with a subordinator.
g.explanation: "Hirokichi kept turning his cup"는 완전한 독립절이고, 그 뒤의 "a chipped celadon piece ... without apology"는 cup을 설명하는 동격구일 뿐입니다. 빈칸 뒤 "he did not seem to notice..."도 또 하나의 독립절이므로, 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결해야 하고 정답은 B입니다. g.explanation_en: "Hirokichi kept turning his cup" is a complete independent clause. The phrase "a chipped celadon piece ... without apology" is just an appositive that describes the cup. After the blank, "he did not seem to notice..." is another independent clause, so you need a semicolon to join the two clauses, which makes B correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, so it's a comma splice. C uses no punctuation at all, so it's a run-on sentence. D adds "while" after "and," which turns the second clause into a dependent clause, and that clause has no main clause to attach to, so the sentence ends up incomplete.

A fuses the two independent clauses with no punctuation at all, and B joins them with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. - 세부 기술 힌트: 삽입구·동격·긴 수식어 뒤에서 절 경계(콜론/대시/세미콜론/쉼표+등위접속사)를 판단하거나, 필수/비필수 수식어 쉼표를 가리는 문제. 선택지는 문장부호/접속 조합 4개.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — In a Bavarian brass band, young musician Felix inherits his grandfather's dented French horn and the cryptic journal inside revealing an anonymous love affair spanning fifty years.

g.passage: When Felix opened the battered case, the smell of valve oil and old paper rose to meet him. His grandfather, a soft-spoken man who had played second horn in the Mittenwald brass band for nearly six decades______ mention the small leather journal wedged beneath the dented bell. Its pages, Felix soon discovered, traced fifty years of letters to someone identified only as "L."
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: decades; had never once thought to
decades had never once thought to
decades, and had never once thought to
decades, had never once thought to
g.explanation: 주어 'His grandfather' 뒤에 쉼표로 시작한 비필수 동격구(a soft-spoken man ... decades)가 끼어 있으므로, 동격구를 닫는 쉼표가 필요하고 그 뒤에 본동사 'had never once thought'가 이어져야 한다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 세미콜론이 주어와 동사를 갈라 앞부분이 독립절이 되지 못한다. B는 동격구를 닫는 쉼표가 빠져 동격구가 열린 채 끝난다. C는 쉼표 뒤 'and'가 들어가 주어에 대응하는 본동사가 없는 상태에서 동사를 등위 연결하므로 문장이 성립하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject "His grandfather" is followed by a nonessential appositive that begins with a comma ("a soft-spoken man ... decades"), so you need a matching comma to close it before the main verb "had never once thought." That makes D correct. A uses a semicolon, which cuts the subject off from its verb, so the part before it can't stand as an independent clause. B leaves out the closing comma, so the appositive is never properly set off. C adds "and," which joins the verb to something even though the subject doesn't have a main verb yet, so the sentence doesn't work.
g.design: Between the subject and the verb, a long appositive with an embedded relative clause hides the sentence structure. Students who skim may see "decades" as the end of a clause and choose the semicolon or "and." They have to find the comma that opens the appositive and then close it with a matching comma.

- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — On a prairie Canadian grain elevator, freight handler Mackenzie drives six hours to deliver a single forgotten letter, the absurdity of her journey mirroring the town's slow disappearance.

g.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Freight handler Mackenzie has found an undelivered envelope in the office of a prairie grain elevator.

The elevator at Dunmore—its red paint flaking into the ditch, its town name stenciled in letters taller than ______ had stood empty of grain for three years when she finally agreed to drive the forgotten letter six hours west, past a dozen towns that, like Dunmore, were quietly closing.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: Mackenzie—
Mackenzie,
Mackenzie;
Mackenzie—it
g.explanation: "its red paint ... taller than Mackenzie"는 대시로 시작된 비필수 삽입구이므로 같은 대시로 닫아야 주어 "The elevator at Dunmore"와 동사 "had stood"가 연결된다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 쉼표로 닫아 앞의 대시와 짝이 맞지 않는다. C는 세미콜론으로 주어와 동사를 갈라 앞부분이 완전한 절이 되지 못한다. D는 대시로 제대로 닫지만 주어 "it"이 더해져 "The elevator at Dunmore"가 동사 없이 남게 된다.
g.explanation_en: The phrase "its red paint ... taller than Mackenzie" is a nonessential interruption that opens with a dash, so it has to close with a dash too. Then the subject "The elevator at Dunmore" connects to its verb "had stood," which makes A correct. B closes the interruption with a comma, so it doesn't match the opening dash. C puts a semicolon between the subject and the verb, which leaves the first part without a complete clause. D closes with a dash correctly, but the extra subject "it" leaves "The elevator at Dunmore" without a verb.
g.design: This medium item has two steps: notice the opening dash, then check that the subject still connects to its verb. Option D is built as a trap because its closing dash is correct.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — At a Patagonian sheep ranch, solitary rancher Tomas sets an unexpected place at supper for a stranger whose arrival forces him to confront decades of deliberate isolation.

g.passage: Tomas had not set a table for two in thirty-one years. Yet when the stranger's truck stalled at the gate of the ranch, he took down a second plate without thinking. That plate—chipped enamel with a faded blue rim, bought the spring his brother abandoned the sheep and the wind for a job in Río Gallegos______ now sat across from his own, as unsettling as a voice in an empty house.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , sat
—sat
; sat
: sat
g.design: 긴 비필수 삽입구가 대시로 열려 있어, 빈칸이 삽입구를 닫는 지점이며 주어 'That plate'와 동사 'sat'을 연결함을 두 단계로 파악해야 한다. 쉼표는 삽입구를 끝내는 기능처럼 보여 그럴듯한 함정이다.
g.explanation: 정답은 B이다. 삽입구 'chipped enamel ... Río Gallegos'는 대시로 시작했으므로 같은 대시로 닫아야 하고, 그래야 주어 'That plate'와 동사 'sat'이 이어진다. A는 삽입구를 끝내는 부호처럼 보이지만 대시로 연 삽입구를 쉼표로 닫아 부호가 짝이 맞지 않는다. C의 세미콜론은 앞뒤에 독립절이 와야 하는데 앞부분에는 동사가 없어 주어와 동사를 갈라놓는다. D의 콜론도 앞에 완전한 독립절이 필요하므로 주어와 동사 사이에 쓸 수 없다.
g.explanation_en: The answer is B. The descriptive phrase "chipped enamel ... Río Gallegos" opens with a dash, so it has to close with a dash too. That way the subject "That plate" connects cleanly to its verb "sat." A looks like it ends the interruption, but you can't close a phrase with a comma after opening it with a dash, because the punctuation has to match. C fails because a semicolon needs an independent clause on each side, and the part before the blank has no verb, so the semicolon cuts the subject off from its verb. D fails because a colon also needs a complete independent clause before it, so it can't go between a subject and its verb.

c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — At a Scottish island primary school, resilient teacher Ms. Finlay watches her struggling students transform during an unexpected storm, their newfound courage offering cautious hope for their futures.

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Tide Schoolhouse is a 2021 short story by Scottish author Morag Ellison.
- It is set in a three-room primary school on a small island in the Outer Hebrides.
- Its central character, teacher Ms. Finlay, has spent years trying to coax her shy, struggling pupils into speaking up.
- When a sudden gale cuts the school's power, the children calmly organize lanterns and lead a younger class to safety.
- The story ends with Ms. Finlay watching the storm clear, unsure whether the children's courage will last but quietly hopeful.
g.question: The student wants to emphasize the uncertain note on which the story concludes. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In Morag Ellison's 2021 short story The Tide Schoolhouse, a sudden gale cuts the power at a three-room island school, and the pupils calmly organize lanterns and lead a younger class to safety.
In Morag Ellison's 2021 short story The Tide Schoolhouse, teacher Ms. Finlay has spent years trying to coax her shy, struggling pupils on a small Outer Hebrides island into speaking up.
In Morag Ellison's 2021 short story The Tide Schoolhouse, Ms. Finlay watches a gale clear after her pupils' brave response to it, doubtful that their courage will endure yet quietly hopeful.
In Morag Ellison's 2021 short story The Tide Schoolhouse, shy pupils who once struggled to speak up surprise their teacher by leading a younger class to safety during a storm.
g.explanation: 목표는 이야기가 끝나는 '불확실한 분위기'를 강조하는 것이다. C는 마지막 메모를 활용해 Ms. Finlay가 아이들의 용기가 지속될지 확신하지 못하면서도 조용히 희망을 품는 결말을 제시하므로 정답이다. A는 폭풍 속 아이들의 행동만 묘사하고 결말의 불확실성은 언급하지 않는다. B는 이야기의 배경과 교사의 오랜 노력만 소개한다. D는 아이들의 변화를 보여 주지만, 결말이 아닌 사건의 중간 장면이며 의구심이 드러나지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: Your goal is to emphasize the uncertain note on which the story ends. C works because it draws on the final note, showing Ms. Finlay doubting whether the children's courage will last while still feeling quietly hopeful. A only describes what the pupils do during the storm and never touches on the ending's uncertainty. B just introduces the setting and the teacher's long effort. D shows the children's transformation, but it describes a mid-story event rather than the ending, and it includes no doubt.
g.design: 질문은 정답의 'doubtful/hopeful' 대신 'uncertain note'로 바꿔 썼다. 오답은 모두 같은 문장 틀로 정확한 메모를 활용하지만, D는 아이들의 변화라는 그럴듯한 내용을 담고 있어 결말과 구별해야만 배제된다.

c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — In a Bavarian brass band, rival trumpet players Ernst and Klaus engage in an annual musical contest that gradually reveals mutual respect beneath their competitive fury.

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- "The Brass of Oberwald" is a short story by the fictional author Liesl Brandauer.
- It follows Ernst and Klaus, rival trumpet players in a Bavarian village brass band.
- Every August, the two men compete in a solo contest judged by the village.
- Early in the story, Ernst mocks Klaus's vibrato as "a goat in a thunderstorm."
- In the final scene, after Klaus cracks a high note and loses, Ernst quietly hands him his own mouthpiece for next year.
- Brandauer wrote the story after years of playing tuba in a village band.
g.question: The student wants to emphasize how the relationship between the story's two main characters changes over its course. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In "The Brass of Oberwald," Liesl Brandauer, who played tuba in a village band for years, tells the story of Ernst and Klaus, rival trumpet players in a Bavarian brass band.
In "The Brass of Oberwald," Ernst and Klaus compete every August in a solo contest, and in the final scene Klaus cracks a high note and loses to his rival.
In "The Brass of Oberwald," Ernst mocks the vibrato of his rival Klaus, comparing it to "a goat in a thunderstorm" before their annual village contest.
In "The Brass of Oberwald," Ernst begins by ridiculing Klaus's vibrato as "a goat in a thunderstorm" but ends by quietly giving his defeated rival his own mouthpiece.
g.design: 정답은 초반 조롱 메모와 결말의 마우스피스 메모를 결합해야 '변화'가 드러나며, 오답은 각각 한 시점만 다루거나(B, C) 배경 정보에 그쳐 비교가 필요하다.
g.explanation: 목표는 두 인물의 관계가 이야기 동안 어떻게 바뀌는지 강조하는 것이므로, 처음과 끝의 태도를 함께 보여야 합니다. D는 초반의 조롱과 결말에서 패배한 경쟁자에게 마우스피스를 건네는 행동을 대비해 적대감에서 존중으로 바뀌는 과정을 보여 줍니다. A는 작가의 배경과 기본 설정만 소개하고 변화는 다루지 않습니다. B는 결말의 승패만 전할 뿐 Ernst의 존중을 보여 주는 행동이 빠져 관계 변화가 드러나지 않습니다. C는 초반의 조롱만 담고 있어 처음의 적대감만 보여 줍니다.
g.explanation_en: Your goal is to show how the two characters' relationship changes, so you need both a starting point and an ending point. D sets Ernst's early mockery against his closing gesture of handing his mouthpiece to the defeated Klaus, which shows a shift from hostility to respect. A gives only the author's background and the basic premise, with no change at all. B reports how the contest ends but leaves out Ernst's gesture, so it never shows the relationship changing. C gives only the early insult, so it shows the hostility at the start and nothing after.

c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — In a Bavarian brass band, seven-year-old Liesel notices the elderly timpani player crying during rehearsals, understanding something about loneliness that the adult musicians steadfastly ignore.

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- "The Kettledrum" is a 2019 short story by the Austrian writer Margit Brandl.
- It is set in a village brass band in Bavaria, where seven-year-old Liesel attends rehearsals with her father, a trombonist.
- Between pieces, Liesel sees the elderly timpani player, Herr Odenwald, weeping quietly behind his drums.
- The adult musicians tune their instruments and chat about the upcoming harvest festival, never mentioning his tears.
- Liesel guesses that Herr Odenwald has been alone since his wife died, and she begins sitting beside him at each rehearsal.
- Critics have praised Brandl's spare, understated prose.
g.question: The student wants to emphasize how differently Liesel and the grown band members react to Herr Odenwald's sorrow. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In Brandl's "The Kettledrum," the adult musicians tune up and chat about the harvest festival without mentioning Herr Odenwald's tears, but seven-year-old Liesel senses his loneliness and begins sitting beside him.

In Brandl's "The Kettledrum," set in a Bavarian village brass band, seven-year-old Liesel attends rehearsals with her father and sees the elderly timpani player, Herr Odenwald, weeping quietly behind his drums.

In Brandl's "The Kettledrum," the adult musicians tune up and chat about the harvest festival without mentioning Herr Odenwald's tears, a scene rendered in the spare, understated prose that critics have praised.
In Brandl's "The Kettledrum," seven-year-old Liesel, whose father plays trombone, guesses that Herr Odenwald has been alone since his wife died and begins sitting beside him at each rehearsal.
g.design: 목표가 두 대상(아이와 어른)의 반응 차이이므로 두 메모를 결합해야 한다. 오답은 모두 정확한 메모를 쓰되 한쪽 반응만 담거나 배경·평가로 빠진다.
g.explanation: 목표는 Liesel과 어른 단원들이 노인의 슬픔에 다르게 반응한다는 점을 강조하는 것이므로, 두 반응을 모두 담고 대비해야 한다. A는 어른들이 눈물을 외면하는 모습과 Liesel이 외로움을 알아채고 곁에 앉는 모습을 'but'으로 대비해 목표를 이룬다. B는 Liesel이 눈물을 보는 장면만 있고 어른들의 반응이 빠져 있다. C는 어른들의 무관심만 다루고 Liesel 대신 문체에 대한 평가를 덧붙인다. D는 Liesel의 반응만 자세히 서술하고 어른들과의 비교가 없다.
g.explanation_en: Your goal is to emphasize that Liesel and the adults react differently to the old man's grief, so the sentence needs both reactions set against each other. A does this: it shows the adults ignoring Herr Odenwald's tears and then uses "but" to set that against Liesel sensing his loneliness and sitting beside him. B shows Liesel seeing the tears but leaves out the adults' reaction entirely. C covers only the adults' indifference and swaps in critics' praise of the prose instead of Liesel's reaction. D describes only Liesel's response, with nothing about the adults to compare it to.

- Its main character, Harmon Lusk, is a cattle buyer who has lived alone for nearly twenty years.
- At the auction, Harmon takes home the auctioneer's neglected hound, a thin dog that flinches at every raised voice.
- Within a single season, the hound grows sleek and playful and greets visitors at Harmon's gate.

g.explanation: B는 개가 방문객을 반기게 된 변화와 하먼이 여전히 이웃을 돌려보낸다는 사실을 'yet'으로 대비시켜 목표를 정확히 달성한다. A는 하먼의 고독과 개를 데려온 일만 소개할 뿐 개의 변화는 담지 않는다. C는 개의 변화를 잘 보여주지만 하먼이 변하지 않았다는 점이 빠져 대조가 성립하지 않는다. D는 하먼이 변하지 않았다는 점과 문체 평가만 다루고 개의 변화는 언급하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: B places the dog's transformation (it now greets visitors) right next to Harmon's unchanged behavior (he still turns neighbors away) and links them with "yet," which creates exactly the contrast the goal asks for. A introduces Harmon's solitude and the dog's adoption, but it never shows the dog changing. C describes the dog's change well, but it leaves out how Harmon stays the same, so there is no contrast. - The story is set in a small village in Ethiopia's highlands.
- In a traditional Ethiopian coffee ceremony, three rounds are poured: abol, tona, and baraka; guests customarily stay until the third.
- The protagonist, Almaz, has been admitted to a university in Addis Ababa.

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- "The Last Timetable" is a 2019 short story by Canadian writer Maren Holt.
- It is set in Wendlow, a Saskatchewan town whose population has fallen from 900 to fewer than 60.
- The narrator, grain elevator manager Ollie Brandt, watches railway inspector Mr. Pask step off a train that arrived forty minutes late.
- Pask immediately checks his pocket watch and records the delay in a ledger, though no passengers are waiting on the platform.
- Ollie notes that Pask then inspects the posted schedule for a passenger service that was canceled six years earlier.
- Holt has said she wanted to show "rules outliving the people they were made for."
g.question: The student wants to illustrate the absurdity Ollie perceives in Pask's behavior by connecting it to the town's circumstances. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In Maren Holt's 2019 short story "The Last Timetable," grain elevator manager Ollie Brandt narrates the arrival of railway inspector Mr. Pask in Wendlow, Saskatchewan.
Mr. Pask's train arrives in Wendlow forty minutes late, and he immediately checks his pocket watch and records the delay in a ledger.
Holt has said that her story about Wendlow, a town that has shrunk from 900 residents to fewer than 60, aims to show "rules outliving the people they were made for."

In a Wendlow that has dwindled to fewer than 60 residents, Ollie watches Pask log a forty-minute delay that no waiting passenger could suffer and then inspect a schedule for a service canceled six years earlier.
g.explanation: 목표는 Pask의 행동이 지닌 부조리를 마을의 상황(인구 감소, 빈 승강장, 폐지된 노선)과 연결하는 것이다. D는 60명도 안 되는 마을, 기다리는 승객이 없는데 기록되는 지연, 6년 전 폐지된 운행 시간표 점검을 함께 제시해 두 요소를 결합한다. A는 작품과 인물을 소개할 뿐 행동이나 부조리를 보여 주지 않는다. B는 Pask의 행동은 담지만 마을의 상황과 연결하지 않아 부조리가 드러나지 않는다. C는 마을 상황과 작가의 의도를 말하지만 Ollie가 관찰한 Pask의 구체적 행동이 빠져 있다.
g.explanation_en: Your goal is to show the absurdity Ollie sees in Pask's behavior by linking it to the town's circumstances. D does this: it puts the town of fewer than 60 people next to Pask logging a delay that no waiting passenger could suffer and checking a schedule for a service canceled six years earlier. A only introduces the story and its characters, so it shows neither the behavior nor anything absurd about it. B describes what Pask does but never connects it to the emptying town, so the absurdity doesn't come through. C gives the town's decline and Holt's stated aim but leaves out the specific behavior Ollie observes.
g.design: To get it right, you have to combine two kinds of notes: Pask's behavior and the town's emptiness. Each wrong answer gets only one side right (B covers the behavior, C covers the town and Holt's intent) or just introduces the story (A). The question avoids words from the correct answer like "canceled" and "passengers."

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- "Splitting Ash" is a 2019 short story by Wren Caldwell.
- The story is set in a trail shelter in the Appalachian Mountains during a rainstorm.
- Boone, an aging carpenter, finds a lost hiker named Dell waiting out the storm in the shelter.
- Boone shows Dell how to mend a cracked bench plank using wooden pegs and glue.
- Neither character speaks during the repair; Caldwell describes only their hands working side by side.
- Critics argue that this wordless cooperation creates a bond deeper than conversation could.
g.question: The student wants to explain to readers who don't know the story how its central scene brings the two characters closer together. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In Wren Caldwell's "Splitting Ash," a carpenter named Boone teaches a lost hiker to mend a cracked plank, and because the two work without speaking, their shared task forms a bond deeper than talk.

g.explanation: 이 목표를 이루려면 두 가지가 필요하다. 이야기를 모르는 독자에게 장면과 인물을 소개해야 하고, 그 장면이 어떻게 두 사람을 가깝게 만드는지(말없이 함께 일하며 생기는 유대)를 설명해야 한다. A는 수리 장면과 '말없는 협력이 유대를 만든다'는 점을 함께 제시하므로 정답이다. B는 배경과 인물만 소개할 뿐 두 사람이 가까워지는 과정은 빠져 있다. C는 수리 방법을 자세히 묘사하지만 그것이 관계에 어떤 의미를 갖는지는 말하지 않는다. D는 유대를 언급하지만 인물과 장면을 소개하지 않아 이야기를 모르는 독자에게는 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: To meet this goal, a choice has to do two things: introduce the scene and characters to readers who don't know the story, and show how that scene brings the two characters together through their wordless shared work. Choice A does both, since it describes the repair and explains that working in silence creates a bond deeper than talk. Choice B introduces the setting and characters but never says how they grow closer. Choice C describes the repair technique in detail but doesn't say what it means for their relationship. Choice D mentions the bond, but it never introduces the characters or the scene, so it doesn't work for readers who are new to the story.
g.design: 정답이 되려면 장면 소개(인물·수리)와 말없는 협력의 의미를 둘 다 담아야 한다. 오답은 모두 같은 문장 틀에 정확한 메모를 쓰지만 둘 중 하나가 빠져 있다. 질문은 'silence/bond' 대신 'brings closer'라고 바꿔 써서 정답과 표면적으로 겹치지 않게 했다.

- "The Crossing" is a 2019 short story by Turkish writer Leyla Arıkan.
- In the story, Selim, a retired history teacher, rides a ferry across the Bosphorus from Kadıköy to Eminönü.

- As boys of twelve, the two had promised to meet again in Istanbul "when we are grown men."

g.explanation: 목표는 약속 이후 두 인물의 삶이 얼마나 다르게 전개되었는지 강조하는 것이다. B는 열아홉에 이스탄불로 온 셀림과 수십 년 독일에서 일하다 작년에야 도착한 누르한을 whereas로 대조하므로 목표에 맞는다. A는 두 사람의 공통 출신과 재회 장면만 전하고 이후 삶의 차이는 없다. C는 약속과 결말의 침묵을 대조할 뿐 두 사람의 서로 다른 인생 경로는 보여 주지 않는다. D는 셀림의 직업과 회상을 언급하지만 누르한의 삶은 다루지 않아 대조가 성립하지 않는다.

B does this by contrasting Selim, who moved to Istanbul at nineteen, with Nurhan, who spent decades in Germany and arrived only last year. g.passage: In the short story "Elevator Siding," Pavel Hrynchuk, a retired stationmaster, still lives beside the grain elevator in the Saskatchewan town where he worked for forty-one years. One autumn morning a letter arrives from England containing a faded photograph: a dozen children with name tags pinned to their coats, standing on Pavel's platform in 1940. They were evacuees sent overseas during the war, and Pavel, then a young clerk, had promised one of them, a girl named Margaret, that he would be at the station when her mother came to take her home. The mother never came that winter, and Margaret was eventually placed with a farm family farther west. Some readers see Pavel's decades in the town as simple contentment with prairie life. One critic, however, argues that Pavel never left because he continued to regard himself as bound by his words to Margaret, long after anyone could have held him to them.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the critic's interpretation?
options: Later in the story, Pavel takes the photograph out of its envelope each evening and recalls with evident fondness the way Margaret laughed at the noise of the grain trucks.
Later in the story, Pavel tells his grandchildren about the evacuation train in vivid detail, describing the smell of coal smoke and the rows of small suitcases on the platform.
Later in the story, Pavel admits to the letter's sender that he never found out whether Margaret's mother had survived the war or tried to reach Canada.
Later in the story, Pavel recalls turning down a promotion to a Winnipeg office, explaining to his wife that someone had to stay on the platform in case a parent ever arrived for one of the children.
g.explanation: 비평가의 주장은 두 부분으로 이루어져 있다. Pavel이 마을에 남은 것이 만족감 때문이 아니라는 점, 그리고 Margaret에게 한 약속에 여전히 묶여 있다고 느꼈다는 점이다. C는 약속과 관련된 미해결 상태를 보여 주지만, 그 사실이 Pavel이 마을에 머문 것과 어떤 관계인지는 드러나지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The critic's claim has two parts: Pavel did not stay in the town out of contentment, and he still felt bound by his promise to Margaret. Choice C shows that the matter of the promise was never resolved, but it doesn't connect that fact to Pavel's decision to remain in the town.

c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — In a 1970s Appalachian mining town, nine-year-old Tammy notices miners stuffing pockets with coal to sell illegally, the adults' hushed desperation striking her as both ridiculous and heartbreaking.

g.passage:
The following text is adapted from a 2019 novel. Set in a West Virginia coal town in 1974, it follows nine-year-old Tammy Kincaid.

Every evening the men came up the hill from the Number Four tipple walking stiff-legged, their jacket pockets sagging like overfilled feed sacks. Tammy watched from the porch steps as Mr. Ferrell, who sang bass in church, tried to wave hello without letting a lump of coal tumble out of his sleeve. Her daddy came last. He didn't look at her. He set his lunch pail down very gently, as if it might go off.

A literary critic argues that the novel does not let Tammy's reactions to the men's secret coal-taking settle into either amusement or sorrow alone; instead, the critic claims, the novel presents both feelings as arising for Tammy at the very same moment, each sharpening the other.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the critic's claim?
options: Later in the same scene, Tammy has to bite her cheek to keep from laughing at the men's lopsided walk, and in that same instant she realizes her throat has gone tight watching her daddy lower his pail.
Later in the same scene, Tammy laughs so hard at Mr. Ferrell's falling coal that her mother scolds her, and she goes to bed still giggling about how silly the grown men looked.
In a chapter set years later, Tammy, now an adult, weeps when she remembers the scene, although as a child she had only found the men's stiff walk comical.
Later in the same scene, Tammy's mother both laughs and cries while telling a neighbor about the men's pockets, though Tammy herself simply watches without understanding.
g.design: 비평가 주장의 두 요소(재미와 슬픔 모두 + '같은 순간'에 Tammy에게)를 모두 충족하는 발견만 정답이 되게 했고, 오답은 각각 한 요소만 충족하거나(B: 재미만, C: 두 감정이지만 시차, D: 두 감정이지만 다른 인물) 같은 문장 틀로 구성했다.
g.explanation: 비평가는 Tammy가 재미와 슬픔을 '동시에' 느끼며 두 감정이 서로를 날카롭게 만든다고 주장한다. A는 웃음을 참는 바로 그 순간 아버지를 보며 목이 메는 장면으로, 두 감정과 동시성을 모두 보여 주므로 주장을 가장 직접 뒷받침한다. B는 재미만 있어 오히려 한 감정으로 정착한다는 반례에 가깝다. C는 두 감정이 나타나지만 어린 시절과 성인기로 시간상 분리되어 '같은 순간'이라는 조건을 어긴다. D는 두 감정이 동시에 나타나지만 Tammy가 아닌 어머니의 반응이므로 주장과 무관하다.
g.explanation_en: The critic claims that Tammy feels amusement and sorrow at the same moment, with each feeling sharpening the other. Choice A shows Tammy holding back a laugh at the very instant her throat tightens as she watches her father, so it covers both feelings and the fact that they happen together. That makes A the most direct support. Choice B includes only amusement, so it actually suggests her reaction settles into one feeling. Choice C includes both feelings, but they are separated by years, which breaks the "same moment" condition. Choice D shows both feelings at once, but in Tammy's mother, not in Tammy.

The following text is adapted from a short story. Greta, a widow who tends a small plot in a Berlin allotment garden, has just received a letter that her sister Liesel wrote in 1945. The letter was located decades later through Red Cross tracing records and has only now been delivered.

Greta read the letter twice on the bench beside the bean rows, then folded it along its old creases. Liesel had written that she was sorry, that she had taken the last of their mother's ration coupons and left without saying goodbye, that she hoped Greta could someday forgive her. A literary critic has argued that the story presents Greta's response not as a sudden act of pardon but as a slow reckoning in which she must first admit that her own long silence, rather than Liesel's theft alone, kept the sisters apart.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the critic's claim?
options: Later in the story, Greta pins the letter to the wall of her garden shed and tells a neighbor that Liesel's apology came too late to matter, since the theft of the coupons was unforgivable.
Later in the story, Greta finds a 1952 address for Liesel in her own old diary and recalls that she once chose not to write, before she slowly begins a reply that starts with an apology of her own.
Later in the story, Greta immediately writes back that she forgives Liesel completely, explaining that the hardships of 1945 excused whatever either sister had done.
Later in the story, Greta learns from the Red Cross that Liesel had tried to send several other letters after 1945, all of which were lost in transit before reaching Berlin.
g.explanation: 비평가의 주장은 두 가지다: 용서가 즉각적이지 않고 점진적이라는 점, 그리고 그레타가 자신의 침묵도 단절의 원인이었음을 인정한다는 점이다. B는 그레타가 언니의 주소를 알고도 편지하지 않았던 사실을 떠올리고, 천천히 자기 사과로 답장을 시작하므로 두 요소를 모두 충족한다. A는 그레타가 리젤의 절도만 탓하고 자기 책임을 인정하지 않으므로 주장과 어긋난다. C는 용서가 즉각적이어서 '느린 성찰'과 모순된다. D는 침묵의 책임을 리젤 쪽의 분실된 편지로 돌릴 뿐 그레타 자신의 침묵 인정과는 무관하다.
g.explanation_en: The critic's claim has two parts: Greta's forgiveness is gradual rather than sudden, and she must admit that her own silence helped keep the sisters apart. B satisfies both, since Greta remembers that she had Liesel's address and chose not to write, and then slowly starts a reply that opens with her own apology. A doesn't work because Greta blames only the theft and accepts no responsibility herself. C contradicts the "slow reckoning" part of the claim, since her pardon comes immediately. D explains the silence through Liesel's lost letters, so it says nothing about Greta admitting her own part.
g.design: To reach the answer, students have to connect two parts of the claim (a slow process and Greta admitting her own silence). A, C, and D each touch only one part, or point the responsibility in the wrong direction, so they look plausible at first. The question also avoids the key words that appear in the correct option.

The following text is from a novel. At harvest time in a village high in the Andes, the widower Pascual visits the young weaver Yuki.

Pascual set the shuttle on her loom without a word. The wood was dark and smooth from hands that had used it long before his. "My mother carried this over the pass the year the frost took everything," he said finally. "Her mother wove with it while the soldiers burned the lower fields." Yuki started to say that she was not his family, that his granddaughters lived only two houses away. He shook his head. "They have hands," he said. "You have the patterns in you. That is what it asks for."

A literary critic argues that the novel treats belonging as something earned through skill and continued practice rather than something passed down by birth.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the critic's argument?

Later in the novel, the narrator explains that the shuttle was carved from a tree that Pascual's great-grandmother planted beside the family's first house.
Later in the novel, Yuki gives the shuttle not to her own cousins but to an orphan from a neighboring valley who has learned to weave the old patterns.

They deal with family feeling, lineage, or gratitude, so a quick reader may pick them even though they don't show the rule for who receives the shuttle.
g.explanation: The critic says that in this novel, belonging comes from skill and continued practice rather than birth. In C, Yuki passes the shuttle to an orphan who knows the patterns instead of to her own relatives. This repeats Pascual's choice and shows that skill, not kinship, decides who receives it, so C supports the critic most directly. A shows the family's anger, so it confirms that a bloodline was passed over, but it doesn't show the novel treating skill as the standard for belonging. B stresses the family line behind the shuttle, which leans toward inheritance by birth instead. D shows that Yuki is grateful, but it says nothing about who the shuttle goes to next.

g.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Kariuki, a street vendor, rides the same matatu (minibus) each morning as Benson, a motorcycle taxi driver whose bike is being repaired.

At every stop, while the conductor shouted for passengers, Kariuki opened his tin of glass beads on his knee. "Red for the blood of the people," he murmured, threading. "White for peace." Benson watched, then held out his hand. On the first day he had said he only wanted to make bracelets to sell to tourists at the Kenyatta Avenue lights, where riders waited with nothing to do. Kariuki had shrugged and given him a needle anyway. Now, by the third week, Benson's fingers moved more slowly than before, and he no longer counted aloud how many shillings each strand might bring.

A student argues that the story presents Benson's interest in beadwork as gradually changing from a way to earn money into a way of connecting with a heritage he had lost touch with.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the student's argument?
options: Later in the story, Benson sells a dozen bracelets at the Kenyatta Avenue lights in a single afternoon and proudly tells Kariuki how much he earned.
Later in the story, Benson practices beadwork every evening at home so that he can keep up with Kariuki during their next matatu ride.
Later in the story, Kariuki tells Benson that his own grandmother taught him the meaning of each bead color when he was a boy in Nyeri.
Later in the story, a tourist offers Benson a high price for a bracelet, but Benson declines, saying it uses the colors his grandmother once wore and is not for sale.
g.explanation: 학생의 주장은 두 요소, 즉 (1) 돈벌이라는 동기에서 벗어나고 (2) 잃어버린 유산과 연결되는 변화를 담고 있다. D는 높은 값을 거절하는 장면(금전 동기 이탈)과 할머니의 색이라는 이유(유산과의 연결)를 함께 보여 주므로 두 요소를 모두 뒷받침한다. A는 Benson이 여전히 수익에 주목한다는 내용이라 변화가 아니라 원래 동기를 보여 준다. B는 열심히 연습한다는 내용일 뿐 동기가 바뀌었는지는 알려 주지 않는다. C는 유산과 관련되지만 Benson이 아니라 Kariuki의 연결을 보여 준다.
g.explanation_en: The student's argument has two parts: Benson moves away from earning money, and he moves toward a heritage he had lost touch with. D shows both, since Benson turns down a high price (he's leaving the money motive behind) because the bracelet uses his grandmother's colors (a connection to heritage). A shows Benson still focused on profit, so it reflects his original motive, not a change. B shows that he's dedicated, but it doesn't say whether his reason for doing beadwork has changed. C is about heritage, but it describes Kariuki's connection to it, not Benson's.
g.design: Two-part claim (move away from money + toward heritage). Two distractors each touch only one part or the wrong character (A: money, C: heritage but Kariuki), and B is plausible but says nothing about motive. All options use the same "Later in the story..." structure.

g.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Rashid, an aging dyer at a riverside tannery in Fez, is teaching his grandson Karim, who will soon leave for university in Rabat.

Rashid lowered the hide into the vat of saffron dye and held it there, counting under his breath. Karim watched from the edge of the stone basin, arms folded. "You could write the times down for me," Karim said. Rashid did not answer. He lifted the hide, turned it so the light fell across its grain, and placed Karim's hand flat against the wet leather. "Feel where it drinks," he said. Karim pulled his hand back, then, after a moment, set it down again and left it there longer than he needed to.

A literary critic argues that, in this scene, Karim's reluctance is beginning to give way to an unspoken acceptance of what his grandfather is trying to pass on to him.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the critic's interpretation?
options: Later in the story, Karim judges the next hide's color by touch without being asked, even though he has said nothing about wanting to learn.
Later in the story, Karim tells a friend that he admires his grandfather's skill, even though he still plans to study engineering in Rabat.

The school boat bumped against the bamboo pier, and Teacher Rosario climbed out with her satchel held above the spray. On the schoolhouse steps lay a carabao calf, legs folded, chewing as if it had been hired to guard the door. She clapped; it blinked. She pushed; it sighed. By then the children had arrived and were watching her closely. Rosario looked at the workbook in her satchel, printed in Manila, its first lesson about measuring snowfall. Then she sat down beside the calf. "Who can tell me," she asked, "how many steps this animal is blocking, and how much it weighs compared to all of you?"

Text 2
Readers often celebrate the carabao scene as proof of Rosario's sudden, playful inventiveness, as though the calf alone sparks her new approach. But the story has already shown us her doubts about lessons written far from the island. The calf does not create her impulse to teach from the world around her; it simply gives her an excuse she has been waiting for to act on it.

As a moment when she takes up a welcome opportunity to drop lessons she had already found poorly suited to the island
As a reluctant compromise she makes only after her efforts to move the calf have failed
g.design: Text 2 rejects the popular reading, so a skimmer who matches 'playful inventiveness' picks B. D is partly supported by the failed pushing in Text 1, so you have to connect the 'Manila' workbook detail with Text 2's 'excuse' claim to reach C.
g.explanation: Text 2의 저자는 송아지가 Rosario의 충동을 '만들어 낸' 것이 아니라, 섬과 맞지 않는 교재에 대해 이미 품고 있던 의심을 실행할 '핑계'를 주었을 뿐이라고 본다. Text 1에서 눈 내린 양을 재는 마닐라 교재를 바라보는 장면이 이 해석을 뒷받침하므로 정답은 C이다. B는 Text 2가 명시적으로 반박하는 통념(송아지만이 계기)이다. D는 Text 1에서 송아지를 밀어내지 못한 점과는 맞지만, '마지못한' 타협이라는 해석은 반가운 기회라는 Text 2의 시각과 반대이다. A는 Text 2 어디에도 통제력 상실이라는 판단이 없다.
g.explanation_en: The author of Text 2 argues that the calf doesn't create Rosario's urge to teach from her surroundings. Instead, it just gives her the excuse she has been waiting for to act on doubts she already had about lessons written far from the island. In Text 1, she looks at the Manila workbook with its snowfall lesson right before she sits down, which supports this reading, so C is correct. B states the popular view that Text 2 explicitly rejects, the idea that the calf alone sparks her approach. D fits the detail that Rosario couldn't move the calf, but calling her choice "reluctant" contradicts Text 2's view that she welcomes the chance. A doesn't work because Text 2 never suggests that Rosario has lost control of her class.
