c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — In an Edo-period fishing village, young apprentice Masako learns net-weaving from her father while secretly knowing she'll abandon the trade for an arranged marriage to a merchant.

g.passage:
Text 1
In the following excerpt from a novel, Masako, the daughter of a fisherman in an Edo-period coastal village, practices net-weaving. A marriage to a merchant in the castle town has already been arranged for her, though her father does not know she has accepted it.
Her father guided her fingers through the knot again, his calloused thumb pressing hers against the twine. "Tighter," he said. "A loose knot lets the whole catch slip away." Masako pulled until the cord bit her skin. She told herself she was learning only to please him, that the skill would be useless behind a merchant's counter. Yet when the finished row lay taut and even across her lap, she found she could not stop looking at it.

Text 2
A literary critic comments on the novel.
Some readers take Masako's net-weaving scenes as proof that she secretly wants to stay in the village, as if the novel were quietly arguing against her marriage. This reading overlooks how firmly the author keeps Masako's choice intact: she never wavers in her plan to leave. What the weaving scenes reveal is not a hidden wish to remain but the cost of departure—Masako can value what her father gives her and still give it up. The novel's tension lies in that coexistence, not in any reversal.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to Masako's reaction to the finished row of netting in Text 1?
options: By claiming that it shows Masako has begun to doubt the arranged marriage and will likely remain in the village
By claiming that it shows Masako's pride is directed mainly at earning her father's approval rather than at the net itself
By claiming that it shows Masako's dismissal of the skill as useless is an accurate judgment the novel endorses
By claiming that it shows Masako's attachment to the craft can exist alongside her firm decision to leave it
g.explanation: Text 2의 비평가는 그물 짜기 장면이 마을에 남고 싶다는 숨은 욕망이 아니라, 아버지가 준 것을 소중히 여기면서도 떠나기로 한 결정은 흔들리지 않는다는 '공존'을 보여준다고 말한다. 따라서 완성된 그물에서 눈을 떼지 못하는 Masako의 반응을 결심과 애착이 함께 있는 것으로 볼 것이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 Text 2가 명시적으로 반박하는 해석(마음이 흔들려 남을 것이라는 해석)이다. B는 Text 1에서 Masako가 스스로 하는 말("only to please him")과 맞닿아 있지만, 그녀가 그물 자체를 바라본다는 점과 비평가의 초점을 놓친다. C는 그 기술이 쓸모없다는 Masako의 말을 그대로 받아들이지만, 비평가는 그녀가 그 기술을 소중히 여긴다고 강조한다.
g.explanation_en: The critic in Text 2 argues that the weaving scenes don't reveal a hidden wish to stay. Instead, they show that Masako can value what her father teaches her while her decision to leave stays firm. So the critic would read her inability to stop looking at the finished row as attachment existing alongside that decision, which makes D the answer. A is the very reading Text 2 rejects, since the critic says Masako never wavers. B echoes Masako's own claim that she is learning "only to please him," but it misses that she is looking at the net itself, and it ignores the critic's point about value and loss existing together. C takes Masako's dismissal of the skill as useless at face value, but the critic stresses that she truly values the craft.
g.design: I used two partly supported wrong answers: B draws on Masako's line from Text 1, and A is the reading Text 2 rejects. To get the answer, students have to link the critic's "coexistence" claim to the specific moment in Text 1. The correct option also avoids reusing the question's key wording.

c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — In a Bavarian brass band, clarinetist Wolfgang receives his orchestra placement alongside his lifelong rival, forcing him to choose between pursuing a prestigious city conservatory or staying home.

g.passage:
Text 1
In the novel's opening chapters, Wolfgang learns that the Munich conservatory has offered seats in its orchestra program to both him and Matthias, the clarinetist he has competed against since their first village festival. Reading the letter, Wolfgang decides at once to stay home with the Oberau brass band. The narrator presents the choice as plain resentment: Wolfgang would rather give up the city than spend another year sitting beside Matthias.

Text 2
Some readers treat Wolfgang's refusal as nothing more than spite, but that reading skips the scene in which he rehearses alone in the empty band hall. There he plays the solo his late teacher wrote for the Oberau band, and he realizes that no one else in the village can perform it. Matthias plays a part in his choice, but the novel suggests that loyalty to the band and to his teacher's music matters at least as much.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the account of Wolfgang's decision given in Text 1?
options: By arguing that it is incomplete, because it reduces to one motive a choice that the novel also links to Wolfgang's devotion to his teacher's work
By arguing that it is mistaken, because the novel shows that Matthias plays no role whatsoever in Wolfgang's choice to stay home
By arguing that it is accurate, because the rehearsal scene confirms that Wolfgang mainly wants to avoid sitting beside Matthias
By arguing that it is premature, because the novel later reveals that Wolfgang eventually accepts the conservatory's offer
g.explanation: Text 1은 볼프강의 결정을 순전히 라이벌 마티아스에 대한 원한으로 설명한다. Text 2는 마티아스가 결정에 '일부' 역할을 한다고 인정하면서도, 스승의 곡과 악단에 대한 충성심이 그만큼 중요하다고 본다. 따라서 Text 1의 설명이 틀렸다기보다 불완전하다고 볼 것이므로 A가 정답이다. B는 Text 2가 마티아스의 역할을 인정하므로 지나치고, C는 리허설 장면이 오히려 다른 동기를 보여 준다는 점을 거꾸로 읽었으며, D는 Text 2에 근거가 없는 내용이다.
g.explanation_en: Text 1 explains Wolfgang's decision purely as resentment toward his rival Matthias. Text 2 grants that Matthias plays a part, but argues that loyalty to the band and to his teacher's music matters at least as much. So Text 2's author would call Text 1's account incomplete rather than wrong, which makes A correct. B goes too far, since Text 2 explicitly says Matthias plays a part. C gets the rehearsal scene backward, because that scene reveals a different motive. D has no support anywhere in Text 2.
g.design: The answer requires seeing that Text 2 partly accepts and partly extends Text 1. Distractor B misreads the extent of the disagreement, C misreads the purpose of the scene, and D adds an invented plot detail.

c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — At a Moroccan riverside tannery, leather workers Karim and Hassan engage in their annual indigo-dyeing competition, though neither admits how much they'll miss these contests when age forces retirement.

g.passage:
Text 1
Karim lifted his hides from the vat, and the indigo ran off them like evening sky. Hassan barely looked. "Your blue is muddy again," he said. "I enter this contest only because someone must stop you from boasting. If the guild cancelled it tomorrow, I would sleep until noon and thank God." Karim laughed and called him a liar. Hassan spat into the river and began stirring his own vat harder than he needed to.

Text 2
In the riverside tannery scenes of the novel, the two old dyers almost never say anything kind to each other. A careless reader might take their constant complaints at face value. But the novelist keeps showing gestures that contradict the men's words: a vat stirred too fiercely, a glance held a moment too long. For these men, insults are how they express a bond that age will soon end and that neither can bring himself to name.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely interpret Hassan's statement that he would happily see the contest cancelled?
options: As a sincere admission that years of competing have left him tired and eager to retire
As a remark that hides how much the yearly contest means to him, as his action at the vat suggests
As a remark meant mainly to upset Karim before the judges examine the two men's hides
As evidence that Hassan, unlike Karim, has already come to terms with the end of their rivalry
g.explanation: Text 2의 저자는 두 염색공의 불평을 액면 그대로 받아들이면 안 되며, 지나치게 세게 통을 젓는 것 같은 몸짓이 말과 모순된다고 주장한다. 그러므로 Hassan의 "취소되면 좋겠다"는 말은 대회에 대한 애착을 감추는 말로 볼 것이고, Text 1의 거세게 젓는 행동이 이를 뒷받침하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 Text 2가 경고한 '액면 그대로의' 해석이다. C는 경쟁 상황에서는 그럴듯하지만, Text 2는 모욕을 상대를 흔드는 전술이 아니라 유대의 표현으로 본다. D는 Text 2가 두 사람 모두 끝을 입에 올리지 못한다고 말한 것과 반대된다.
g.explanation_en: The author of Text 2 warns against taking the dyers' complaints at face value and points to gestures, like stirring a vat too fiercely, that contradict what they say. So Hassan's claim that he'd be glad to see the contest cancelled would be read as hiding how much the contest matters to him, and his hard stirring in Text 1 backs this up. That makes B correct. A is exactly the face-value reading Text 2 rejects. C sounds plausible in a competition, but Text 2 sees the insults as a way of expressing a bond, not as a tactic to rattle an opponent. D contradicts Text 2's point that neither man can bring himself to name the coming end.
g.design: To answer, students must connect Text 2's general claim (gestures contradict words) to the specific stirring detail in Text 1. A and C are partly supported by the surface of Hassan's words or by the competitive setting, while D misreads Text 2's "neither."

c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — In a Hanoi street-food alley at dawn, vendor Hoa's routine pho-making shifts when a surprise monsoon floods her stall, scattering her carefully arranged ingredients and composure.

g.passage: The following text is adapted from a short story. Every morning before dawn, Hoa arranges her pho ingredients along the counter of her Hanoi stall in the same order: star anise, charred ginger, sliced shallots, then the herbs, always left to right. Regular customers joke that they could set their watches by her ladle. But this morning a monsoon arrives without warning, and water surges through the alley, sweeping her bowls of herbs into the gutter and knocking the shallots to the floor. Hoa stands motionless for a long moment. Then, instead of trying to rebuild her row, she pulls whatever is still within reach into the broth: a handful of rescued ginger, the anise, a few muddy scallions she rinses quickly in rainwater. When the first soaked customer ducks under her awning and asks whether she is open, she ladles him a bowl without apology. The detail suggests that Hoa's careful ordering of ingredients ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: was something her regular customers depended on more than the flavor of the soup itself.
had always made her stall unprepared for the sudden weather of the monsoon season.
was a habit she could set aside when circumstances required, rather than a condition for serving her customers.
was a source of pride that the flood permanently destroyed, leaving her unwilling to cook.
g.explanation: 홍수 전 Hoa는 매일 같은 순서로 재료를 배열하지만, 홍수 후에는 그 줄을 다시 세우지 않고 손에 닿는 재료로 국물을 만들어 사과 없이 손님에게 대접한다. 이 두 정보를 연결하면 정돈된 순서는 장사의 필수 조건이 아니라 상황에 따라 내려놓을 수 있는 습관이었다는 C가 정답이다. A는 단골들이 그녀의 규칙성에 대해 농담한다는 점에 근거하지만, 맛보다 순서에 더 의존했다는 내용은 지문에 없다. B는 폭우가 예고 없이 왔다는 점에 기대지만, 재료 배열 습관이 대비 부족의 원인이라는 근거는 없다. D는 그녀가 잠시 멈춰 섰다는 점에서 출발하지만, 결국 요리해 손님에게 내주므로 지문과 모순된다.
g.explanation_en: Before the flood, Hoa lays out her ingredients in the same order every day. After the flood, though, she doesn't rebuild that row. She cooks with whatever she can reach and serves her customer without apologizing. Putting those two facts together shows that the ordering was a habit she could drop when she had to, not something she needed in order to serve food, so C is correct. A builds on the regulars joking about her routine, but nothing in the text says they cared about the order more than the flavor. B builds on the storm arriving without warning, but the text never says her arranging habit left her unprepared. D builds on the moment she stands still, but it contradicts the passage, since she goes on to cook and serve.
g.design: Medium: you have to connect the established routine with how she responds after the flood. Each wrong answer starts from a real detail in the text (the joking regulars, the sudden storm, her pause) and then overreaches.

c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — At a 1920s Lagos market town schoolhouse, elderly teacher Mr. Adebayo delivers his final arithmetic lesson to restless pupils, his worn chalk communicating farewell more than numbers.

g.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story set in a market town near Lagos in the 1920s. Mr. Adebayo, who has taught at the schoolhouse for forty years, is giving his last lesson.

The pupils fidgeted, their eyes drifting to the window and the noise of the market traders outside. Mr. Adebayo did not scold them, as he had done every other afternoon. Instead, he wrote a long column of sums on the board, more than the hour could possibly allow, and pressed so hard that the stub of chalk crumbled to almost nothing between his fingers. When a boy in the front row pointed out that nobody could finish so many problems before the bell, the old teacher only nodded and kept writing. The column, it seemed, was not really meant to be solved; rather, by filling the board, Mr. Adebayo was ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: testing which pupils could work quickly enough to finish the sums before the bell rang.
punishing the restless pupils for paying more attention to the market than to the lesson.
using up the last of the school's chalk so that the next teacher would have to request more.
stretching out the final lesson he would ever teach, unwilling to let it come to an end.
g.explanation: 지문은 이것이 마지막 수업이고, 문제들이 '실제로 풀라고 낸 것이 아니다'라고 말한다. 따라서 칠판을 채우는 행동은 끝나가는 수업을 붙잡아 두려는 작별의 몸짓으로 보는 것이 가장 자연스러우며, 정답은 D이다. A는 제시간에 끝낼 수 없다는 지적과 '풀라고 낸 것이 아니다'라는 서술에 어긋난다. B는 학생들이 산만하다는 점과 연결되지만, 그가 평소와 달리 꾸짖지 않았다는 내용과 모순된다. C는 분필이 닳았다는 세부 사항만 붙잡았을 뿐 그런 의도를 뒷받침하는 근거가 지문에 없다.
g.explanation_en: The text tells you this is Mr. Adebayo's last lesson and that the sums were "not really meant to be solved." So filling the board is best read as a farewell gesture, a way of holding on to a lesson that is about to end. That makes D the answer. A doesn't fit, because the sums can't be finished in time and the text says they weren't meant to be solved. B links to the restless pupils, but it conflicts with the detail that he didn't scold them this time. C picks up on the crumbling chalk, but nothing in the text suggests he wanted to use up the supply.
g.design: To get the answer, you have to connect two pieces of information: this is the final lesson, and the sums aren't meant to be solved. Each wrong answer grabs one surface detail (speed, restlessness, chalk), so you can only rule it out by checking it against the rest of the context.

c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — In 1920s Lagos, retired teacher Oluwatoyin receives an unexpected visitor who reminds him of a former student lost to illness, reigniting both sorrow and unexpected grace.

g.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story set in Lagos in the 1920s.

For eleven years after Adebayo's death, Oluwatoyin had kept the boy's copybook in a drawer and never once opened it. When the young clerk at his door introduced himself as Adebayo's cousin and asked, shyly, whether the old teacher might help him prepare for the civil service examination, Oluwatoyin's first impulse was to refuse; he had sworn off pupils since that fever season. Yet that evening he cleared the dining table, set out two lamps, and, after a long hesitation, took the copybook from the drawer and laid it open beside the clerk's papers. His actions suggest that ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: he has begun to let his grief over Adebayo become a part of his renewed teaching rather than a reason to avoid it.
he has decided that the clerk is a more capable student than Adebayo was and needs no extra guidance.
he intends to use Adebayo's copybook to show the clerk exactly which answers will appear on the examination.
he has finally put his sorrow behind him and no longer thinks about the student he lost.
g.design: 독자는 두 가지 사실을 연결해야 한다. 하나는 학생을 받지 않겠다던 맹세를 뒤집은 것이고, 다른 하나는 공책을 덮어 두지 않고 펼친 것이다. 오답 D는 슬픔이 바뀌었다는 점까지는 맞지만 슬픔이 사라졌다고 지나치게 나아가며, B와 C는 지문의 세부(공책, 시험)를 엉뚱하게 해석한다.
g.explanation: 오루와토인은 학생을 받지 않겠다고 맹세했지만 결국 수업을 준비한다. 게다가 11년 동안 열어 보지 않던 아데바요의 공책을 꺼내 사촌의 공부 자료 옆에 펼쳐 놓는다. 이 행동은 슬픔을 피하지 않고 새 가르침 속으로 받아들이고 있음을 보여 주므로 A가 정답이다. D는 그의 변화를 포착했지만, 공책을 펼친 것은 아데바요를 의식적으로 기억하는 행동이므로 '더 이상 생각하지 않는다'는 진술과 모순된다. B의 능력 비교와 C의 시험 답 유출은 지문에 근거가 없다.
g.explanation_en: Oluwatoyin had sworn off teaching, but he still prepares a lesson. He also takes out Adebayo's copybook, which he hasn't opened in eleven years, and lays it open beside the cousin's papers. These actions show that he is bringing his grief into his teaching instead of avoiding it, so A is correct. D notices that he has changed, but opening the copybook is a deliberate act of remembering Adebayo, so it contradicts the claim that he no longer thinks about the boy. Nothing in the text supports B's comparison of the two students' abilities or C's idea that he is leaking exam answers.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — At a Mexican mountain bus depot, organizer Héctor watches the Independence Day festival's main stage collapse during opening ceremonies, exposing the town's fragile infrastructure and pride.

g.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Héctor has organized his mountain town's Independence Day festival, staged in the lot beside the bus depot.

When the stage gave way, it did not crash so much as sigh, its plywood sinking onto the cinder blocks the town had borrowed from the unfinished clinic. The mayor stepped off unhurt, still holding the flag. No one screamed. Instead, the crowd went quiet in a way Héctor recognized: it was the same silence that fell each spring when the road washed out and the buses stopped coming. He had expected anger, or laughter at his expense. But the people around him were already lifting the planks, stacking them neatly, as if they had done this before. Watching them, Héctor understood that the collapse had embarrassed him far more than it had surprised anyone else, because ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the townspeople had blamed the mayor rather than him for building the stage on the depot lot.
the townspeople were long accustomed to things in their town breaking down and being patched back together.
the townspeople had never before attended a festival large enough to need a stage.
the townspeople were too frightened by the collapse to react with the anger he had expected.
g.explanation: 이 장면은 군중의 침묵이 매년 도로가 유실될 때의 침묵과 같았고, 사람들이 '전에도 해 본 것처럼' 판자를 치웠다는 두 단서를 연결해야 한다. 그러면 마을 사람들이 무너지고 다시 수습하는 일에 익숙했기 때문에 놀라지 않았다는 B가 결론이 된다. A는 분노가 없었다는 점은 맞지만, 시장을 탓했다는 근거는 지문에 없다. C는 놀라지 않은 이유와 정반대로, 익숙함이 아니라 처음 겪는 일이라는 뜻이 된다. D는 침묵이라는 점은 맞지만, 사람들은 겁에 질린 것이 아니라 차분하게 정리하고 있었다.
g.explanation_en: To answer this, connect two clues: the crowd's silence was the same one that fell every spring when the road washed out, and people stacked the planks "as if they had done this before." Together, these clues show that the townspeople weren't surprised because they were used to things breaking and being patched up, so B is correct. A matches the lack of anger, but nothing in the text says anyone blamed the mayor. C points the opposite way, since it suggests the situation was new to them rather than familiar. D matches the silence, but the people weren't frightened; they were calmly cleaning up.
g.design: Two clues have to be linked: the silence they recognize from the road washing out, and the practiced cleanup. A and D each fit one surface detail (no anger, silence), so you have to compare them against the rest of the scene to rule them out.

c.instruction: 문장이 분사구문(-ing/-ed로 시작)이나 비교구문(Unlike/Like/As)으로 시작하고, 그 뒤에 콤마와 함께 주절이 이어지는 문법 문제를 만들어라. 정답은 수식어구가 의미적으로 가리키는 대상과 정확히 일치하는 주절 주어를 가져야 하며, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 수식어와 무관한 엉뚱한 명사를 주어로 둔 경우, (2) 수식 대상과 비슷하지만 다른 범주의 명사(예: 사람 대신 그 사람의 저작물)를 주어로 둔 경우, (3) 수일치는 맞지만 의미상 수식어가 가리킬 수 없는 대상을 주어로 둔 경우로 구성하라. 정답과 오답 모두 문법적으로는 완전한 문장이 되도록 만들어 순수하게 의미적 연결 판단만으로 정답을 가려내게 하라.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — In Kyoto's pottery district, young artisan Kenji's hands shape perfect bowls while his heart yearns for Tokyo's anonymity, torn between filial duty and artistic ambition.

g.passage: Smoke from the communal kiln was already drifting over the sloped lanes of Gojozaka when Kenji unlocked his father's workshop. He wet his hands, slapped a mound of clay onto the wheel, and pressed down with both thumbs. Trained since boyhood to center clay without ever glancing at it, ______ while his thoughts wandered to the departure board at Kyoto Station, where the next train to Tokyo was always only minutes away.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the smoke from the kiln curled steadily past the workshop window
Kenji's bowls rose one after another, each rim perfectly even,
Kenji raised one flawless bowl after another,
the old wheel spun steadily beneath his palms
g.explanation:
정답 C. 분사구 'Trained since boyhood to center clay without ever glancing at it'은 어릴 때부터 훈련받은 사람을 가리키므로, 콤마 뒤 주절의 주어는 Kenji여야 한다. C는 Kenji를 주어로 두어 수식 관계가 맞는다. 
A: 수식어와 아무 관련 없는 명사 smoke를 주어로 두었다. 연기가 점토를 중심에 맞추도록 훈련받았다는 뜻이 되어 현수 수식어(dangling modifier)가 된다. 
B: 주어가 Kenji's bowls로, Kenji 본인이 아니라 그가 만든 결과물이다. 소유격 Kenji's가 붙어 있어 맞는 것처럼 보이지만, 그릇은 훈련받을 수 없다. 
D: 단수 동사 spun과의 수일치는 맞고, 물레도 도예와 관련된 사물이라 그럴듯해 보인다. 하지만 물레가 훈련받았다는 의미가 되어 수식어가 가리킬 수 없는 대상이다. 
네 선택지 모두 문장 자체는 문법적으로 완전하므로, 수식어가 의미상 누구를 가리키는지로만 판단해야 한다.
g.explanation_en:
The answer is C. The opening phrase "Trained since boyhood to center clay without ever glancing at it" describes a person who was trained. In Standard English, the subject right after the comma must be the one the phrase describes, so that subject has to be Kenji. Choice C makes Kenji the subject, so the phrase correctly modifies him.
A: The subject is "the smoke from the kiln," which has nothing to do with the phrase. This would mean the smoke was trained to center clay, so the modifier is left dangling.
B: The subject is "Kenji's bowls." These are things Kenji made, not Kenji himself. The possessive "Kenji's" makes this choice look right, but bowls can't be trained.
D: The singular verb "spun" agrees with "the old wheel," and a wheel belongs in a pottery scene, so this choice seems plausible. Still, a wheel can't be trained since boyhood, so the phrase can't describe it.
All four choices are grammatically complete sentences. The only way to choose is to ask whom the opening phrase actually describes.
g.design: 이 문항은 분사구로 시작하는 문장에서 수식 대상과 주절 주어가 일치하는지를 묻는다. 오답은 지시대로 세 가지다. 무관한 명사(smoke), 같은 사람의 결과물(Kenji's bowls), 수일치는 맞지만 수식어가 가리킬 수 없는 관련 사물(wheel)을 주어로 두었다. 네 선택지가 모두 같은 '주어+과거동사' 틀의 완전한 문장이라서, 문법 형태가 아니라 의미 연결만으로 정답을 가려야 한다.

c.instruction: 완전한 독립절 두 개가 이어지는 문장을 만들되, 두 절 사이의 논리적 관계(대조, 인과, 부연설명 중 하나)를 분명히 드러내라. 정답은 그 관계에 어울리는 구두점 전략(등위접속사+쉼표, 세미콜론, 또는 마침표) 하나이며, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 구두점 종류는 맞지만 절 관계와 안 맞는 접속사를 쓴 경우, (2) 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이은 콤마 스플라이스, (3) 절 경계가 아닌 곳에 세미콜론을 넣어 절을 어색하게 쪼갠 경우로 만들어라. 정답 선택 시 단순히 구두점 유무가 아니라 절 간 의미 관계까지 고려해야 정답을 고를 수 있도록 하라.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — At an Icelandic fishing port, five-year-old Björn notices the harbor master silently feeding abandoned cats each dawn, understanding his loneliness before any adult acknowledges it.

g.passage: Every dawn at the small port of Húsavík, the harbor master carried a tin of fish scraps behind the ice house and set it down for the cats that departing sailors had left behind. The adults of the town described him as gruff and perfectly content with his solitude ______ who watched him crouch among the cats without saying a word, had already understood that the old man was lonely.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , so five-year-old Björn,
, five-year-old Björn,
, but five-year-old Björn;
, but five-year-old Björn,
g.explanation:
이 문장은 독립절 두 개로 되어 있다. 하나는 "The adults ... described him as gruff and ... content with his solitude"이고, 다른 하나는 "five-year-old Björn ... had already understood that the old man was lonely"이다. 두 번째 절의 주어 Björn과 동사 had understood 사이에는 비제한적 관계절 "who watched him ... word"가 끼어 있다. 어른들의 판단(고독에 만족함)과 Björn의 이해(외로워함)가 서로 반대되므로 두 절은 대조 관계이다. 정답 D는 쉼표와 대조 접속사 but으로 두 절을 잇고, Björn 뒤의 쉼표로 삽입절을 연다. 이 쉼표는 word 뒤의 쉼표와 짝을 이룬다.
A: '쉼표+등위접속사'라는 구두점 방식은 맞다. 하지만 so는 인과 관계를 나타낸다. 어른들이 그를 만족한 사람으로 봤기 때문에 Björn이 외로움을 알아챘다는 논리는 성립하지 않으므로 의미가 맞지 않는다.
B: 접속사 없이 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이은 콤마 스플라이스이다.
C: 세미콜론이 절 경계가 아니라 주어 Björn과 그를 꾸미는 관계절 사이에 들어가 있다. 그 결과 세미콜론 뒤의 "who watched ... lonely"는 독립절이 될 수 없다. 또한 word 뒤의 쉼표와 짝을 이루지도 못한다.
g.explanation_en:
This sentence is made of two independent clauses. The first is "The adults ... described him as gruff and ... content with his solitude." The second is "five-year-old Björn ... had already understood that the old man was lonely." In the second clause, the subject (Björn) is separated from its verb (had understood) by the nonrestrictive clause "who watched him ... word." The adults believe he is content alone, while Björn understands that he is lonely, so the two clauses contrast. Choice D joins the clauses with a comma plus the contrasting conjunction "but." Its comma after "Björn" opens the inserted clause, and the comma after "word" closes it.
A: Using a comma plus a coordinating conjunction is the right strategy, but "so" signals cause and effect. The adults' view did not cause Björn's insight, so the logic doesn't work.
B: Joining two independent clauses with only a comma creates a comma splice.
C: The semicolon is not at the boundary between the clauses. It falls between "Björn" and the relative clause that describes him, which leaves "who watched ... lonely" as a fragment that isn't an independent clause. It also fails to pair with the comma after "word."
g.design: I wrote two contrasting independent clauses and put a relative clause inside the second one, so you have to judge both the logical relationship and where the clause boundary falls. The three wrong answers are a mismatched conjunction (so), a comma splice, and a semicolon placed where it isn't a clause boundary.

c.instruction: 짧은 부사적 삽입어구(however, for example, in fact 등)가 문장 중간에 등장하되, 이것이 두 독립절 사이에 낀 것인지 아니면 한 절 내부의 단순 삽입인지 헷갈리게 설계하라. 정답은 실제 절 구조(삽입어 앞뒤가 독립절인지 아닌지)에 맞는 구두점이며, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 삽입어를 절 경계로 착각해 불필요하게 세미콜론/마침표를 쓴 경우, (2) 실제 절 경계인데 쉼표만 찍어 콤마 스플라이스를 만든 경우, (3) 삽입어 앞뒤 쉼표를 하나만 찍어 비대칭으로 만든 경우로 구성하라. 문장을 읽고 삽입어 앞뒤가 각각 완전한 절인지 아닌지를 판별해야만 정답을 고를 수 있게 하라.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — On Cairo rooftops, pigeon keeper Rashad discovers a cracked ceramic feeding bowl bearing inscriptions revealing it belonged to his estranged grandfather decades ago.

g.passage: On the rooftop above Shubra, Rashad scraped dried seed from the bottom of the old ceramic bowl his pigeons had eaten from for as long as he could remember. He had always assumed it was a cheap market purchase. The faded script pressed into its cracked underside ______ spelled out the name of his grandfather Mahmoud, a man who had stopped speaking to the family long before Rashad was born, along with a date: 1961.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , in fact,
; in fact,
. In fact,
, in fact
g.explanation:
정답 A. 빈칸 앞 'The faded script pressed into its cracked underside'는 주어(+수식어구)일 뿐 동사가 없고, 빈칸 뒤 'spelled out ...'는 주어가 없는 서술부다. 즉 두 독립절의 경계가 아니라 한 절의 주어와 동사 사이에 'in fact'가 삽입된 구조이므로, 삽입어 앞뒤에 쉼표를 하나씩 찍어야 한다.
B: 세미콜론은 두 독립절을 이을 때 쓰는데, 앞부분에 동사가 없어서 독립절이 아니다. 'in fact'를 절의 경계로 잘못 본 오답이다.
C: 마침표를 찍으면 앞부분이 동사 없는 조각문이 되고, 뒷부분도 주어 없는 조각문이 된다. B와 같은 오개념에서 나온 오답이다.
D: 쉼표가 삽입어 앞에만 있고 뒤에는 없어서 비대칭이다. 그 결과 쉼표 하나가 주어와 동사 사이를 부적절하게 끊는다.
g.explanation_en:
The answer is A. Look at what comes before the blank: "The faded script pressed into its cracked underside." That is only a subject with a modifier. It has no main verb ("pressed into" is a participle that describes "script"). The part after the blank, "spelled out the name...", is a predicate with no subject. So the blank isn't a boundary between two independent clauses. "In fact" is an interrupter placed between the subject and its verb, so it needs a comma on both sides.
B is wrong because a semicolon has to join two independent clauses, and the first part isn't one. This choice treats "in fact" as if it marked a clause boundary.
C is wrong for the same reason. A period would leave a fragment with no verb before it and a fragment with no subject after it.
D is wrong because it puts only one comma around the interrupter. That lopsided comma ends up splitting the subject from its verb.
g.design: 'in fact'를 'pressed into'라는 분사구 뒤에 두었다. 그래서 앞부분이 완전한 절처럼 보이지만 실제로는 동사가 없는 주어다. 동사가 있는지 판별해야만 세미콜론·마침표(경계 착각)와 비대칭 쉼표를 지울 수 있다. 실제로는 절 경계가 없기 때문에 지시의 '콤마 스플라이스' 오답 유형은 그대로 쓸 수 없었다. 그래서 그 자리는 마침표로 경계를 착각한 오답으로 바꾸었다.

c.instruction: 문장이 분사구문(-ing/-ed로 시작)이나 비교구문(Unlike/Like/As)으로 시작하고, 그 뒤에 콤마와 함께 주절이 이어지는 문법 문제를 만들어라. 정답은 수식어구가 의미적으로 가리키는 대상과 정확히 일치하는 주절 주어를 가져야 하며, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 수식어와 무관한 엉뚱한 명사를 주어로 둔 경우, (2) 수식 대상과 비슷하지만 다른 범주의 명사(예: 사람 대신 그 사람의 저작물)를 주어로 둔 경우, (3) 수일치는 맞지만 의미상 수식어가 가리킬 수 없는 대상을 주어로 둔 경우로 구성하라. 정답과 오답 모두 문법적으로는 완전한 문장이 되도록 만들어 순수하게 의미적 연결 판단만으로 정답을 가려내게 하라.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — In postwar Vienna, boarding house tenant Ernst and newcomer Klaus develop an awkward friendship that gradually unravels as each pursues different rebuilding paths.

g.passage: Klaus arrived in the spring of 1946 carrying one cardboard suitcase and a letter from a parish priest in Linz. Ernst, who had been the first to open the door, watched the newcomer study the peeling wallpaper with obvious dismay. Having lived in the boarding house on Gumpendorfer Strasse since before the war, ______ which stair creaked loudly enough to wake the landlady and which tap ran only cold.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the hallway's oldest radiator reminded Klaus
Ernst quietly warned Klaus
Ernst's handwritten list quietly warned Klaus
the boarding house itself quietly warned Klaus
g.explanation: 정답 B. 분사구문 "Having lived in the boarding house ... since before the war"의 의미상 주어는 전쟁 전부터 하숙집에 살아온 사람, 즉 Ernst이다. 주절 주어가 Ernst이어야 수식이 맞다. A: 라디에이터는 수식어와 관계없는 엉뚱한 명사이고 '살아온' 주체가 될 수 없다. C: Ernst의 손글씨 목록은 Ernst와 비슷하지만 그의 결과물일 뿐 사람이 아니므로 하숙집에서 살 수 없다. D: 단수 동사 warned와 수는 맞지만, 하숙집 자체가 '그 하숙집에서 살아왔다'는 것은 의미상 불가능하다. 네 선택지 모두 문법적으로는 완전한 문장이 되므로 수식 관계만으로 판단해야 한다.
g.explanation_en: The correct answer is B. The opening phrase "Having lived in the boarding house ... since before the war" describes a person who has lived there for years, and that person is Ernst. So the subject of the main clause must be Ernst. A: the radiator has nothing to do with the modifier, and it can't have "lived" anywhere. C: Ernst's list is connected to Ernst, but it's something he made, not a person, so it can't have lived in the boarding house. D: the singular subject agrees with the verb, but it makes no sense to say the boarding house has lived in the boarding house. All four choices are grammatical sentences, so you can only find the answer by checking what the opening phrase logically describes.
g.design: I started the sentence with a participial phrase whose logical subject is a long-time tenant. Each wrong choice uses one of the three required subject errors: an unrelated noun, something Ernst made instead of Ernst himself, and a noun that agrees in number but can't logically be what the phrase describes. All choices share the same sentence frame.

c.instruction: 완전한 독립절 두 개가 이어지는 문장을 만들되, 두 절 사이의 논리적 관계(대조, 인과, 부연설명 중 하나)를 분명히 드러내라. 정답은 그 관계에 어울리는 구두점 전략(등위접속사+쉼표, 세미콜론, 또는 마침표) 하나이며, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 구두점 종류는 맞지만 절 관계와 안 맞는 접속사를 쓴 경우, (2) 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이은 콤마 스플라이스, (3) 절 경계가 아닌 곳에 세미콜론을 넣어 절을 어색하게 쪼갠 경우로 만들어라. 정답 선택 시 단순히 구두점 유무가 아니라 절 간 의미 관계까지 고려해야 정답을 고를 수 있도록 하라.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — In 1920s Lagos, restless trader Taiwo receives an inheritance letter offering her passage to London, forcing her to abandon her mother's market stall and unspoken expectations.

g.passage: Taiwo read the letter twice beneath the awning while the noon heat pressed down on Balogun Market. The solicitor's words were crisp and generous: the letter promised her a berth on a steamer bound for Liverpool and a room in her late uncle's London house______ it said nothing about who would sit each morning behind her mother's indigo stall, folding cloth the way her mother had always assumed Taiwo one day would.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , so it
, it
, but it
but; it
g.design: 독립절 두 개를 대조 관계로 잇게 하고, 오답은 관계에 맞지 않는 접속사(so), 콤마 스플라이스, 접속사 뒤에 잘못 둔 세미콜론으로 구성했다.
g.explanation:
정답 C. 빈칸 앞 절(편지가 배편과 방을 약속함)과 뒤 절(어머니의 노점을 누가 지킬지는 언급하지 않음)은 둘 다 독립절이며, 너그러운 제안과 빠진 부분이 대조를 이룬다. 따라서 쉼표에 대조 접속사 but을 더한 ', but'이 알맞다.
A: 쉼표와 등위접속사 조합이라 구두점 형식은 맞지만, so는 인과를 나타낸다. 제안이 있었기 때문에 노점 이야기를 하지 않았다는 뜻이 되어 논리가 맞지 않는다.
B: 쉼표 하나로 두 독립절을 이어 콤마 스플라이스가 된다.
D: 세미콜론이 절 경계가 아니라 접속사 but 바로 뒤에 놓여 but이 앞 절에 어색하게 붙는다. 그래서 문장이 잘못 쪼개진다.
g.explanation_en:
C is correct. Both sides of the blank are independent clauses. The first says the letter offers passage and a room, and the second says it ignores who will run her mother's stall. That generous offer set against what the letter leaves out is a contrast, so a comma plus the coordinating conjunction "but" is the right choice.
A uses the correct punctuation pattern (comma + coordinating conjunction), but "so" signals cause and effect. It wrongly suggests that the letter left out the stall because it made the offer.
B joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice.
D places the semicolon right after "but" instead of at the boundary between the clauses. This leaves the conjunction stranded at the end of the first clause and splits the sentence awkwardly.

c.instruction: 짧은 부사적 삽입어구(however, for example, in fact 등)가 문장 중간에 등장하되, 이것이 두 독립절 사이에 낀 것인지 아니면 한 절 내부의 단순 삽입인지 헷갈리게 설계하라. 정답은 실제 절 구조(삽입어 앞뒤가 독립절인지 아닌지)에 맞는 구두점이며, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 삽입어를 절 경계로 착각해 불필요하게 세미콜론/마침표를 쓴 경우, (2) 실제 절 경계인데 쉼표만 찍어 콤마 스플라이스를 만든 경우, (3) 삽입어 앞뒤 쉼표를 하나만 찍어 비대칭으로 만든 경우로 구성하라. 문장을 읽고 삽입어 앞뒤가 각각 완전한 절인지 아닌지를 판별해야만 정답을 고를 수 있게 하라.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — On Cairo rooftops, pigeon keepers Amr and Samir's daily companionship fragments when Amr's daughter demands he relocate for her marriage, testing their lifelong bond.

g.passage: For thirty years, Amr and Samir had released their pigeons at dawn from neighboring rooftops in Shubra, watching the flocks circle above the minarets before settling back onto the wire coops. Now Amr's daughter, Nadia, insisted that he move with her to Alexandria after her wedding. The speckled birds that Amr had raised since boyhood ______ could not make the journey, and so, without saying anything, he began carrying their feed sacks across the low wall to Samir's roof.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: ; however,
, however;
however,
, however,
g.explanation:
정답 D. 빈칸 앞 'The speckled birds that Amr had raised since boyhood'는 주어(명사구+관계절)일 뿐 완전한 절이 아니고, 빈칸 뒤 'could not make the journey'는 그 주어의 동사다. 따라서 however는 한 절 내부의 삽입어이므로 앞뒤 모두 쉼표로 감싸야 한다.
A: 세미콜론은 두 독립절 사이에 쓰는데, 앞부분은 동사가 없는 주어뿐이라 불완전하다. 삽입어를 절 경계로 착각한 오류다.
B: however 뒤에 세미콜론을 두면 'could not make the journey...'를 별개의 절처럼 다루게 되고, 주어와 동사가 끊긴다. 뒷부분을 경계로 오인해 구두점을 찍은 오류다.
C: however 뒤에만 쉼표가 있어 삽입 표시가 비대칭이다. 삽입어는 앞뒤 쉼표가 짝을 이루어야 한다.
g.explanation_en:
The answer is D. Look at what comes before the blank: "The speckled birds that Amr had raised since boyhood." That's only a subject (a noun phrase with a relative clause), not a complete clause. Its verb comes after the blank: "could not make the journey." So "however" is an aside dropped into the middle of one clause, between the subject and its verb. An aside like this needs a comma on both sides.
A is wrong because a semicolon has to join two independent clauses. The part before it has no main verb, so it's a fragment. This choice mistakes the aside for a break between clauses.
B is wrong because the semicolon after "however" cuts the subject off from its verb. It treats "could not make the journey..." as if it were a separate clause.
C is wrong because it puts a comma only after "however." That leaves the aside lopsided, since it needs matching commas on both sides.
g.design: The long subject with a relative clause ("that Amr had raised since boyhood") reads like a complete clause, so "however" looks as if it sits at a clause boundary. In fact it's an aside between the subject and its verb. The wrong answers are an unnecessary semicolon, a semicolon that cuts the subject from its verb, and a single comma that leaves the aside lopsided.

c.instruction: 문장이 분사구문(-ing/-ed로 시작)이나 비교구문(Unlike/Like/As)으로 시작하고, 그 뒤에 콤마와 함께 주절이 이어지는 문법 문제를 만들어라. 정답은 수식어구가 의미적으로 가리키는 대상과 정확히 일치하는 주절 주어를 가져야 하며, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 수식어와 무관한 엉뚱한 명사를 주어로 둔 경우, (2) 수식 대상과 비슷하지만 다른 범주의 명사(예: 사람 대신 그 사람의 저작물)를 주어로 둔 경우, (3) 수일치는 맞지만 의미상 수식어가 가리킬 수 없는 대상을 주어로 둔 경우로 구성하라. 정답과 오답 모두 문법적으로는 완전한 문장이 되도록 만들어 순수하게 의미적 연결 판단만으로 정답을 가려내게 하라.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — During monsoon season in Mumbai, neighbors Priya and Deepak engage in competitive gardening contests from their adjoining rooftops, each refusing to acknowledge their deepening affection.

g.passage: The rain had finally thinned to a drizzle over the Mumbai rooftops when Priya stepped out to assess the damage. Deepak's marigolds, she noted with satisfaction, had been flattened overnight. Leaning over the low wall between their rooftops, a dripping trowel still in her hand, ______ all while pretending not to notice that Deepak had paused his watering to watch her.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: Priya counted the broken stems with exaggerated care,
the monsoon wind scattered the broken stems with exaggerated care,
Priya's gaze counted the broken stems with exaggerated care,
the flattened bed displayed its broken stems with exaggerated care,
g.explanation:
분사구 "Leaning over the low wall..., a dripping trowel still in her hand"는 담장 너머로 몸을 기울이고 손에 모종삽을 든 사람, 즉 Priya를 수식한다. 따라서 주절 주어는 Priya여야 한다. A가 정답이다.
B: 'the monsoon wind'는 수식어와 아무 상관없는 명사다. 바람은 몸을 기울이지도, 모종삽을 들지도 못한다.
C: 'Priya's gaze'는 Priya와 관련은 있지만 사람이 아니라 사람에게 딸린 것이다. 시선에는 손이 없으니 모종삽을 들 수 없다.
D: 'the flattened bed'는 단수라서 동사와 수는 맞고 지문 속 소재와도 이어진다. 하지만 짓눌린 화단이 담장 너머로 몸을 기울일 수는 없다. 네 선택지 모두 문법적으로는 완전한 절이므로, 수식 대상이 누구인지 의미로 판단해야 답을 고를 수 있다.
g.explanation_en:
The opening modifier, "Leaning over the low wall between their rooftops, a dripping trowel still in her hand," describes a person who is leaning and holding a trowel. That person is Priya, so the main clause has to start with Priya as its subject. That makes A correct.
B: "The monsoon wind" has nothing to do with the modifier. Wind can't lean over a wall or hold a trowel.
C: "Priya's gaze" is connected to Priya, but it belongs to her rather than being her. A gaze has no hand, so it can't hold a trowel.
D: "The flattened bed" is singular, so it agrees with the verb, and it comes from the scene. But a flower bed can't lean over a wall. All four choices are grammatically complete clauses, so you can only pick the answer by deciding who the modifier actually describes.
g.design: 이 문항은 소유자 관계와 상황 정보를 담은 분사구로 시작한다. 오답은 지시대로 세 유형이다. 관련 없는 명사(바람), 같은 사람에게 딸린 다른 범주의 명사(Priya의 시선), 수일치는 맞지만 의미상 수식될 수 없는 명사(화단)를 각각 주어로 두었다. 네 선택지는 모두 같은 문장 틀로 썼다.

c.instruction: 문장 앞부분에 분사구문(예: ~ing, having p.p., ~ed로 시작하는 수식어구)을 배치하고, 그 수식어구가 실제로 가리키는 행위자가 문장 중간이나 뒤쪽 명사구에 숨어 있도록 지문을 구성하라. 정답은 그 행위자를 주어 자리에 정확히 배치한 문장이어야 하며, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 수식어구와 표면상 가장 가까운 무생물 명사를 주어로 착각, (2) 문장 앞부분의 배경 명사를 주어로 착각, (3) 수식어구가 가리키는 행위자와 문법적으로만 비슷한 다른 인물/사물을 주어로 착각하여 만들어라.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — On a 1960s Chicago elevated platform, newcomer Samuel overhears whispers about his interracial family moving into the neighborhood, yet finds unexpected allies among the curious.

g.passage: The Lake Street platform was crowded that October morning in 1962, and the wind off the lake rattled the tin sign above the stairs. Samuel, who had moved to the neighborhood only the week before, kept his back to the two women behind him as they murmured about "that mixed family" on Washburne Avenue. Pretending to study the timetable posted on the iron pillar in front of him, ______ until a boy in a Cubs cap tapped his elbow and asked, with frank curiosity, whether his mother really painted pictures for the Art Institute.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the timetable's fine print held Samuel's gaze while the whispers grew sharper,
Samuel held his gaze on the fine print while the whispers grew sharper,
the crowded platform held Samuel's gaze on the fine print while the whispers grew sharper,
the women behind him held their gaze on the fine print while the whispers grew sharper,
g.explanation:
정답 B. 분사구문 "Pretending to study the timetable posted on the iron pillar in front of him"의 의미상 주어는 주절의 주어와 같아야 한다. 시간표를 보는 척할 수 있는 건 사람뿐이고, 지문에서 그 사람은 여자들에게 등을 돌린 채 수군거림을 못 들은 척하는 Samuel이다. B만 Samuel을 주어로 두었다.
A: 수식어구 바로 앞에 나오는 무생물 명사(timetable)를 주어로 삼았다. 시간표의 글씨가 무언가를 보는 척할 수는 없으므로 현수 수식어(dangling modifier) 오류다.
C: 문장 앞부분에서 배경으로 깔린 명사(platform)를 주어로 삼았다. 승강장은 행위자가 아니다.
D: 사람이라서 문법적으로는 그럴듯해 보이지만, 여자들은 Samuel의 '뒤'에서 수군거리는 당사자들이다. 'in front of him'의 기둥에 붙은 시간표를 보는 척하며 수군거림을 견디는 인물은 Samuel이므로 수식어구의 실제 행위자와 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en:
The answer is B. A participial phrase at the start of a sentence has to describe the subject of the main clause that follows. Only a person can pretend to study a timetable. In this passage, that person is Samuel: he keeps his back to the whispering women and acts as if he can't hear them. Choice B is the only option that puts Samuel in the subject position.
A is wrong because it makes "the timetable's fine print" the subject. That's the nearest noun to the phrase, but print can't pretend to do anything, so the modifier dangles.
C is wrong because it makes "the crowded platform" the subject. The platform is just part of the setting, and it can't perform the action either.
D is wrong because it makes the women the subject. They are people, so this choice looks grammatically fine at first. However, the women are behind Samuel, and they're the ones doing the whispering. The person pretending to read the timetable on the pillar in front of him while the whispers grow sharper is Samuel, not the women.
g.design: I opened the sentence with the participial phrase "Pretending to study..." and put the real agent, Samuel, in the subject position of the correct answer only. Each wrong answer uses the same sentence frame but swaps in a different subject: the nearest inanimate noun (timetable), the background noun (platform), or other people who are grammatically possible (the women).

c.instruction: 두 개의 절을 제시하되 그 사이의 논리 관계(대조/인과/단순나열 중 하나)가 접속사나 구두점 없이도 문맥상 명확히 드러나도록 구성하고, 학생이 먼저 그 관계를 파악한 뒤 알맞은 구두점·접속사 조합을 고르게 하라. 정답은 논리관계에 맞는 올바른 결합(세미콜론+접속부사, 종속접속사 등)이어야 하며, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 콤마만으로 두 절을 이은 콤마 스플라이스, (2) 논리 관계가 반대인 접속사(대조인데 인과 접속사 사용 등) 사용, (3) 불필요한 접속사 중복(and+however 등 형태)을 사용하여 만들어라.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — In a 1970s Appalachian mining town, rivals Carl and Donnie gradually develop respect while competing in weekend wrestling matches, each recognizing the other's dignified struggle.

g.passage: Every Saturday night in the cinder-block gym behind the union hall, Carl Mabry and Donnie Pruitt circled each other while miners still gray with coal dust stamped on the bleachers. Everyone in town expected the old grudge between their fathers to finally boil over on the mat. Carl had pinned Donnie three weekends running______when the referee raised Carl's arm that night, Carl bent down and pulled his rival to his feet before he acknowledged the cheering crowd.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , nevertheless,
; therefore,
; nevertheless,
, and however,
g.explanation:
먼저 두 절의 논리 관계부터 파악한다. 앞 절은 Carl이 세 주 연속 Donnie를 이겼다는 내용이고, 앞 문장에서 마을 사람들은 두 집안의 묵은 원한이 터지기를 기대했다. 그런데 뒤 절에서 Carl은 승리를 인정받는 순간 관중에게 답하기도 전에 라이벌을 일으켜 세운다. 앞의 예상과 정반대인 행동이므로 두 절은 '대조' 관계다. 두 독립절을 대조의 접속부사로 이으려면 세미콜론과 nevertheless를 함께 써야 하므로 C가 정답이다.
A: 접속부사 nevertheless는 접속사가 아니므로 콤마만으로 두 독립절을 이으면 콤마 스플라이스(comma splice)가 된다.
B: 구두점(세미콜론)은 맞지만 therefore는 인과 관계를 나타낸다. 연승한 것이 상대를 일으켜 세운 '이유'가 아니라 예상을 뒤집는 대조이므로 논리가 맞지 않는다.
D: 등위접속사 and와 대조 접속부사 however를 겹쳐 쓴 불필요한 중복이다. 게다가 and는 대조가 아니라 단순 나열을 나타낸다.
g.explanation_en:
Start by working out how the two clauses relate. The first clause says Carl had beaten Donnie three weekends in a row. The sentence before it says the town expected the families' old grudge to boil over. The second clause shows the opposite of that expectation: as soon as Carl wins, he helps his rival up before he even responds to the crowd. So the relationship is contrast. When you join two independent clauses with a conjunctive adverb, you need a semicolon before it. That's why "; nevertheless," (C) is correct.
A is wrong because "nevertheless" is a conjunctive adverb, not a conjunction. Joining two independent clauses with only a comma before it creates a comma splice.
B uses the correct punctuation, but "therefore" signals cause and effect. Carl's winning streak isn't the reason he helps Donnie up; his gesture goes against what everyone expected.
D is wrong because it stacks the conjunction "and" on top of the conjunctive adverb "however," which is redundant. Also, "and" signals simple addition, not contrast.
g.design: I didn't put a connecting word between the clauses, so you have to figure out the relationship from context: the expected grudge and Carl's win versus his generous gesture. Only after recognizing that contrast can you choose the semicolon plus "nevertheless." The wrong answers are built from three specific errors: a comma splice, a cause-and-effect connector where contrast is needed, and a redundant "and" with "however."

c.instruction: 인용문(따옴표 안 문장)과 이를 감싸는 주절, 혹은 병렬로 나열된 여러 절을 함께 제시하고 그 전체에 걸쳐 시제나 형태가 일관되어야 하는 문장을 만들어라. 정답은 인용문/병렬구조 전체 맥락과 시제가 일치하는 형태이며, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 인용문 시제와 어긋나는 시제 선택, (2) 병렬 구조 중 한 항목만 다른 시제/형태로 만든 것, (3) 문장 내 한 절과는 맞지만 전체 문맥과는 어긋나는 시제를 사용하여 만들어라.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Aboard a Kerala backwater houseboat, widow Radha encounters fisherman Thomas seeking shelter from a monsoon, their brief conversation revealing parallel griefs and unexpected understanding.

g.passage: Rain drummed on the thatched roof of the houseboat as Radha handed the fisherman a dry cloth. Thomas wrung the water from his shirt and stared at the brown current for a long while. When he finally spoke, he explained that since his son had drowned two monsoons earlier, his routine had not changed at all: "Each morning I still mend two nets, row out past the temple steps, and ______ beside the empty place in the boat until the light comes." Radha said nothing, but she thought of the second plate she continued to set out at dinner.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: sat
sitting
had sat
sit
g.explanation:
정답 D(sit): 빈칸은 인용문 안의 병렬 구조 "I still mend ..., row ..., and ___"의 세 번째 항목이다. 따옴표 안에서 Thomas는 지금도 반복하는 습관을 현재시제로 말하고 있고("Each morning", "still", "comes"), 주어 I에 맞춰 현재형 sit을 써야 mend, row와 병렬이 맞는다.
A(sat): 따옴표 밖 서술부(spoke, explained)의 과거시제에 끌려 고른 오답이다. 인용문은 직접 화법이라 원래 말한 시제(현재)를 그대로 유지해야 하므로 인용문 시제와 어긋난다.
B(sitting): 시제는 문제 될 것이 없어 보이지만 mend, row가 정동사인데 이 항목만 분사이다. 병렬 항목 하나만 형태가 달라 구조가 깨진다.
C(had sat): 주절의 "had drowned", "had not changed"와 같은 과거완료에 맞춘 것으로, 문장 속 한 절과는 맞지만 인용문 전체가 현재의 습관을 말한다는 맥락과 어긋난다.
g.explanation_en:
Choice D, "sit," is correct. The blank is the third item in a parallel series inside the quotation: "I still mend ..., row ..., and ___." Inside the quotation marks, Thomas describes a habit he still keeps today, so he speaks in the present tense ("Each morning," "still," "comes"). The present-tense verb "sit" goes with the subject "I" and matches "mend" and "row."
Choice A, "sat," copies the past tense of the narration outside the quotation ("spoke," "explained"). But a direct quotation keeps the speaker's own tense, which here is present, so "sat" clashes with the rest of the quotation.
Choice B, "sitting," breaks the parallel structure. "Mend" and "row" are finite verbs, and "sitting" is a participle, so only this item has a different form.
Choice C, "had sat," matches the past perfect verbs in the narrator's clause ("had drowned," "had not changed"). It fits that one clause but not the context of the quotation, which describes a present habit.
g.design: I placed a present-tense parallel series inside a direct quotation and wrapped it in past and past perfect narration. Each wrong answer is built from one trap: A copies the narration's past tense, B breaks the parallel form, and C matches only the past perfect clause.

c.instruction: 문장 앞부분에 분사구문(예: ~ing, having p.p., ~ed로 시작하는 수식어구)을 배치하고, 그 수식어구가 실제로 가리키는 행위자가 문장 중간이나 뒤쪽 명사구에 숨어 있도록 지문을 구성하라. 정답은 그 행위자를 주어 자리에 정확히 배치한 문장이어야 하며, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 수식어구와 표면상 가장 가까운 무생물 명사를 주어로 착각, (2) 문장 앞부분의 배경 명사를 주어로 착각, (3) 수식어구가 가리키는 행위자와 문법적으로만 비슷한 다른 인물/사물을 주어로 착각하여 만들어라.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — At a Moroccan riverside tannery, young worker Fatima secretly saves money to leave for Marrakech, torn between honoring her father's legacy and reclaiming her freedom.

g.passage: Each evening the tannery vats along the river fell quiet beneath the copper light of the setting sun, and the smell of lime and dye drifted over the water. Having tucked another folded banknote into the tin she kept hidden beneath the drying racks, ______ wondering whether her father, who had worked these same pits for forty years, would have called her journey to Marrakech a betrayal or a beginning.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: Fatima lingered among the stacked hides,
the tin rested among the stacked hides, with Fatima
the tannery vats stood silent around Fatima,
Fatima's father seemed to linger among the stacked hides, with Fatima
g.design: 문두 분사구문 'Having tucked…'의 실제 행위자 Fatima는 'she'와 뒤쪽 명사구 속에만 드러난다. 오답은 각각 가장 가까운 무생물(tin), 앞 문장의 배경 명사(vats), 비슷한 인물(father)을 주어로 삼게 했다.
g.explanation:
'Having tucked another folded banknote…'는 지폐를 깡통에 넣은 사람을 수식하는 분사구문이다. 따라서 주절의 주어가 바로 그 행위자여야 한다. 'the tin she kept'의 she와 문맥상 그 사람은 Fatima이므로, Fatima를 주어로 둔 A가 정답이다. 이어지는 분사 wondering도 Fatima를 자연스럽게 수식한다.
B: 수식어구 바로 안에 있는 무생물 tin을 주어로 삼았다. 깡통이 지폐를 넣었다는 뜻이 되므로 현수 수식어(dangling modifier)다.
C: 앞 문장의 배경 명사 vats를 주어로 삼았다. 통이 지폐를 넣은 셈이 되어 틀렸다.
D: 같은 사람이라 그럴듯한 아버지를 주어로 삼았다. 그러나 지폐를 모으는 사람은 Fatima이고, 아버지는 'her father'로 따로 언급되는 다른 인물이므로 행위자가 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en:
The opening phrase "Having tucked another folded banknote into the tin she kept hidden…" describes whoever put the money away. A modifier like this must be followed directly by the person who performed the action. The pronoun "she" and the context show that this person is Fatima, so choice A is correct. The later phrase "wondering…" also fits Fatima.
B makes "the tin" the subject. The tin is the inanimate noun closest to the modifier, but this wording says the tin tucked the banknote away, which is a dangling modifier.
C makes "the tannery vats" the subject. They are background nouns from the first sentence, and vats can't hide money.
D makes Fatima's father the subject. He is a person, so this choice seems plausible, but Fatima is the one saving money. The passage mentions her father separately ("her father"), so he can't be the one who tucked the banknote away.

c.instruction: 두 개의 절을 제시하되 그 사이의 논리 관계(대조/인과/단순나열 중 하나)가 접속사나 구두점 없이도 문맥상 명확히 드러나도록 구성하고, 학생이 먼저 그 관계를 파악한 뒤 알맞은 구두점·접속사 조합을 고르게 하라. 정답은 논리관계에 맞는 올바른 결합(세미콜론+접속부사, 종속접속사 등)이어야 하며, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 콤마만으로 두 절을 이은 콤마 스플라이스, (2) 논리 관계가 반대인 접속사(대조인데 인과 접속사 사용 등) 사용, (3) 불필요한 접속사 중복(and+however 등 형태)을 사용하여 만들어라.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — On a Caribbean island ferry, traveler Marcus misinterprets his old friend's gift of island rum as judgment rather than affection, creating painful distance between them.

g.passage: As the ferry pulled away from the dock, Delroy pressed a bottle of dark island rum into Marcus's hands and grinned the way he had when they were boys. The gift was meant as pure affection, a reminder of the nights they had spent laughing on the old jetty______ heard in it only a quiet rebuke for the twelve years he had stayed away, and he said nothing as the water widened between them.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , Marcus
; however, Marcus
; therefore, Marcus
; and however, Marcus
g.explanation: 앞 절은 선물이 '순수한 애정'으로 의도되었다는 내용이고, 뒤 절은 Marcus가 그것을 '책망'으로 받아들였다는 내용이므로 두 절은 대조 관계다. 두 독립절을 세미콜론으로 나누고 대조의 접속부사 however를 쓴 B가 정답이다. A: 콤마만으로 두 독립절을 이은 콤마 스플라이스다. C: 구두점은 맞지만 therefore는 인과를 나타내므로 대조 관계와 맞지 않는다(애정이 있었기 때문에 책망으로 들었다는 말이 되어 버린다). D: and와 however를 함께 써서 연결어가 불필요하게 겹치고, 세미콜론 뒤 'and however'는 문법적으로도 성립하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: Start with the logic. The first clause says the gift was meant as pure affection. The second says Marcus heard only a rebuke in it. Those two ideas contrast. Both are independent clauses, so you can join them with a semicolon followed by a contrast word like "however," which makes B correct. A is a comma splice: a comma alone can't join two independent clauses. C gets the punctuation right, but "therefore" shows cause and effect, which would mean the affection caused Marcus to hear a rebuke. That doesn't make sense. D stacks two connectors, "and" and "however," which is redundant and ungrammatical after a semicolon.
g.design: The contrast between intended affection and perceived rebuke is clear from meaning alone. Wrong answers: a comma splice, the cause-and-effect word "therefore," and the doubled "and however." All four choices use the same frame.

c.instruction: 인용문(따옴표 안 문장)과 이를 감싸는 주절, 혹은 병렬로 나열된 여러 절을 함께 제시하고 그 전체에 걸쳐 시제나 형태가 일관되어야 하는 문장을 만들어라. 정답은 인용문/병렬구조 전체 맥락과 시제가 일치하는 형태이며, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 인용문 시제와 어긋나는 시제 선택, (2) 병렬 구조 중 한 항목만 다른 시제/형태로 만든 것, (3) 문장 내 한 절과는 맞지만 전체 문맥과는 어긋나는 시제를 사용하여 만들어라.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — At a Mexican mountain bus depot, young Alejandra inherits her grandmother's silver ring and finally reads the cryptic note inside, reframing her entire family history.

g.passage: At the mountain bus depot outside Real del Monte, Alejandra turned her grandmother's silver ring over in her palm. Tucked inside the velvet box was a note in faded ink: "This ring is not mine to give; it belongs to the woman your grandfather loved first." For years Alejandra had believed the family story of a single, faithful marriage without question. Now she reread the line twice, pressed the ring onto her finger, and ______ toward the idling bus as though the whole valley had shifted beneath her.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: stumbles
stumbling
stumbled
had stumbled
g.explanation:
정답 C. 빈칸은 "reread ... pressed ... and ______"로 이어지는 병렬 구조의 세 번째 동사이며, 서술은 단순과거로 진행된다. 따라서 단순과거 stumbled가 앞의 두 동사와 형태·시제 모두 일치한다.
A(stumbles): 따옴표 속 인용문의 현재시제(is, belongs)에 이끌린 선택이다. 인용문은 쪽지 내용이라 현재형이지만 서술은 과거형이므로 틀렸다.
B(stumbling): 병렬 항목 중 하나만 분사 형태로 바꾼 것이다. 주어 she에 이어지는 정동사 자리가 필요하므로 병렬이 깨진다.
D(had stumbled): 앞 문장의 "had believed"(과거완료)와는 맞지만, 이 행동은 Now 이후 다시 읽고 반지를 끼운 뒤에 일어난 일이므로 과거완료로 앞선 시점을 표시하면 사건 순서가 어긋난다.
g.explanation_en:
C is correct. The blank is the third verb in a parallel series: "reread ... pressed ... and ______." The story is narrated in the simple past, so "stumbled" matches the other two verbs in both form and tense.
A ("stumbles") picks up the present tense of the quoted note ("is," "belongs"). The note is in present tense because it is quoting what was written, but the narration around it is in the past, so the present tense doesn't fit here.
B ("stumbling") switches just one item in the series to a participle. Like the other two verbs, this one needs to be a finite verb with "she" as its subject, so B breaks the parallel structure.
D ("had stumbled") matches the past perfect in the earlier sentence ("had believed"). But the stumbling happens after she rereads the note and puts on the ring. The past perfect would wrongly place it before those actions.
g.design: The passage puts a present-tense quoted note and a past perfect clause inside past-tense narration, and the blank sits in a parallel series of past-tense verbs. Each wrong answer matches one local cue: the quote's tense, a different verb form within the series, or the nearby past perfect clause.

c.instruction: 문장 앞부분에 분사구문(예: ~ing, having p.p., ~ed로 시작하는 수식어구)을 배치하고, 그 수식어구가 실제로 가리키는 행위자가 문장 중간이나 뒤쪽 명사구에 숨어 있도록 지문을 구성하라. 정답은 그 행위자를 주어 자리에 정확히 배치한 문장이어야 하며, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 수식어구와 표면상 가장 가까운 무생물 명사를 주어로 착각, (2) 문장 앞부분의 배경 명사를 주어로 착각, (3) 수식어구가 가리키는 행위자와 문법적으로만 비슷한 다른 인물/사물을 주어로 착각하여 만들어라.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — At a Montana ranch auction, cynical auctioneer Buck encounters a mysterious woman who was his childhood sweetheart, their unexpected reunion unsettling his hardened solitude.

g.passage: The bidding on the last lot, a sun-bleached saddle with a cracked horn, had stalled at forty dollars when Buck noticed the woman at the edge of the corral. She wore a gray felt hat pulled low, but the way she tilted her head as she listened was something he had not seen in thirty years. Lowering the microphone from his mouth and squinting past the glare off the stock trailers, ______ that it was Ellen Marsh, the girl who had once carved both their initials into the schoolhouse fence.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the glare off the trailers made Buck realize
the stalled bidding on the saddle gave Buck the realization
the woman in the gray hat let Buck realize
Buck realized
g.explanation:
문장 앞의 분사구 "Lowering the microphone ... and squinting past the glare ..."의 의미상 주어는 마이크를 내리고 눈을 찡그린 사람, 즉 경매사 Buck이다. 따라서 콤마 바로 뒤 주어 자리에 Buck이 와야 하므로 정답은 D "Buck realized"이다.
A: 수식어구 바로 앞에 나온 무생물 명사 'glare'를 주어로 삼았다. 그러면 눈부심이 마이크를 내리고 눈을 찡그린 꼴이 되어 현수 수식어(dangling modifier) 오류가 생긴다.
B: 지문 앞부분의 배경 정보인 '멈춘 입찰(stalled bidding)'을 주어로 삼았다. 입찰은 마이크를 내릴 수 없다.
C: 'woman'도 사람이라 문법적으로는 그럴듯해 보이지만, 마이크를 든 사람은 경매사 Buck이지 그녀가 아니다. 행위자가 잘못 지정되었다.
g.explanation_en:
The opening phrase "Lowering the microphone from his mouth and squinting past the glare..." must describe the noun that comes right after the comma. The person lowering the microphone is the auctioneer, Buck, so Buck has to be the subject. That makes D, "Buck realized," the correct answer.
A puts "the glare," the nearest non-living noun, in the subject position. That would mean the glare lowered the microphone, which is a dangling modifier.
B uses the background detail from the start of the passage, the stalled bidding, as the subject. Bidding can't lower a microphone or squint.
C might look right because the woman is also a person, but she isn't holding the microphone. Buck is, so C gives the action to the wrong person.
g.design: 문장 앞의 분사구가 가리키는 행위자 Buck을 지문 중간에 숨겨 두었다. 오답 세 개는 각각 가까운 무생물 명사(glare), 앞부분의 배경 명사(bidding), 같은 사람이지만 다른 인물(woman)을 주어로 삼게 만들었고, 네 선택지 모두 같은 문장 틀을 쓰도록 했다.

c.instruction: 텍스트 1은 주장과 이유를, 텍스트 2는 같은 주제의 다른 접근을 각각 짧게 제시하되 서로를 언급하지 않게 쓴다. 질문은 '텍스트 2의 저자라면 텍스트 1의 주장에 어떻게 반응할 것인가'로 한다. 정답은 텍스트 2의 전제에서만 도출되는 반응으로 만들고, 오답 3개는 텍스트 1의 내용을 반복하는 선택지, 텍스트 2의 결론만 되풀이하는 선택지, 텍스트 2가 다루지 않은 쟁점을 끌어온 선택지로 만든다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — In a Berlin allotment garden, refugee Anke learns traditional German vegetable cultivation from her elderly mentor, their hands speaking trust across language and loss.

g.passage:
Text 1
In the allotment chapters of Mara Lindqvist's novel *Beet Rows*, the refugee Anke and her elderly mentor, Herr Vogt, hardly exchange a full sentence. He shows her how deep to set the leek seedlings by pressing her fingers into the soil, and she thanks him by leaving a jar of pickled beets at his shed door. Because the novel builds their trust almost wholly through such gestures, it seems to argue that spoken language is a barrier to human connection, one the two characters are lucky to escape.

Text 2
Readers sometimes forget how much of *Beet Rows* is told in words before Anke ever reaches the garden. In the opening chapters, Vogt's letters to his late wife describe the plot she tended for forty years and his fear of letting it go to weeds. When he later guides Anke's hands through the leek bed, the gesture moves us only because we already know what that soil means to him. The novel's silent scenes carry meaning that its written passages have stored up.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the claim made in Text 1 about what the novel suggests regarding spoken language?
options: By arguing that the wordless scenes owe their power to things the novel has already told in words, so they do not show that language stands in the way of connection
By arguing that the scarcity of dialogue between Anke and Vogt shows that the novel presents speech as something its characters are better off without
By arguing that Vogt's letters to his late wife reveal how long she tended the plot and how much he fears it going to weeds
By arguing that the novel's account of planting leeks and pickling beets misrepresents how allotment gardens in Berlin are actually worked
g.explanation: 정답 A: Text 2의 전제는 침묵 장면의 의미가 앞서 편지(언어)로 쌓인 맥락에서 나온다는 것이다. 그러면 '말은 연결의 장벽'이라는 Text 1의 해석은 성립하지 않는다. 이 반응은 Text 2의 전제에서 추론해야만 나온다. B는 Text 1의 주장을 되풀이할 뿐 Text 2의 관점과 맞지 않는다. C는 Text 2의 세부 내용만 반복하고 Text 1의 주장에 대한 반응이 되지 못한다. D는 원예 관행이 정확한가라는, 두 지문 모두 다루지 않은 쟁점을 끌어온다.
g.explanation_en: A is correct. Text 2 assumes that the silent garden scenes matter only because of what the novel has already told in words, mainly Vogt's letters. If that's true, the wordless moments depend on language, so they can't show that language is a barrier. You have to infer this response from Text 2's premise. B just repeats Text 1's claim, and Text 2 would reject that claim. C restates details from Text 2 but never connects them to Text 1's claim about language. D raises a question neither text discusses: whether the novel gets Berlin gardening practices right.
g.design: 두 비평은 서로를 언급하지 않는다. 정답은 Text 2의 전제(침묵 장면의 의미는 앞선 서술에서 온다)를 Text 1의 주장에 적용해야만 나온다. 오답은 같은 'By arguing that' 틀로 썼고, 각각 Text 1 반복, Text 2 세부 반복, 다루지 않은 쟁점에 해당한다.

c.instruction: 텍스트 1은 하나의 결론을 이끄는 주장을, 텍스트 2는 그 주장의 핵심 근거를 약하게 만들 수 있는 별개의 관찰이나 연구를 제시한다. 질문은 '텍스트 2의 저자가 텍스트 1의 어느 부분에 가장 이의를 제기할 것인가'로 한다. 정답은 텍스트 1의 결론이 아니라 그 결론이 기대는 가정으로 하고, 오답 3개는 결론 자체, 텍스트 1의 부수적 세부, 텍스트 2가 오히려 동의하는 부분으로 만든다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — On a Brooklyn tenement stoop in 1910s, Italian immigrant Rosa watches her younger sister board a boat for California, wrestling with duty to family versus hunger for escape.

g.passage:
Text 1
In Lucia Ferrante's novel The Stoop on Sackett Street, set in 1910s Brooklyn, Rosa watches from her tenement stoop as her younger sister, Nina, leaves to board a steamer for California. Nina calls up to her twice, but Rosa says nothing and only raises a hand. Critic Daniel Ames argues that this wordless moment is the emotional center of the book. In his view, Rosa's refusal to speak shows a longing to escape that she cannot admit, and the scene therefore shows that the novel treats family duty as a trap that silences immigrant daughters.

Text 2
Scholar Teresa Valli also considers the departure scene central to Ferrante's novel, but she points out how Rosa behaves elsewhere in the book. When Rosa turns down a suitor who offers to take her to Chicago, and again when she agrees to run her father's fruit stand, she also says nothing. In both cases, the narrator describes her afterward as "settled" and "at ease." Valli concludes that in Ferrante's novel, Rosa falls silent when she has made a choice she accepts, not when she is hiding a regret.
g.question: Based on the texts, with which part of Ames's argument in Text 1 would Valli (Text 2) most likely disagree?
options: The claim that Ferrante's novel presents family duty as a trap for immigrant daughters
The claim that Rosa's not speaking as Nina leaves reveals a desire she cannot express
The claim that Nina calls up to Rosa twice before leaving for the steamer
The claim that the departure scene is the emotional center of Ferrante's novel
g.explanation:
정답 B: Ames의 결론(가족 의무=덫)은 'Rosa의 침묵은 말하지 못한 탈출 욕망을 드러낸다'는 해석에 기대고 있다. Valli는 소설 속 다른 장면에서 Rosa의 침묵이 받아들인 선택 뒤의 평온함을 나타낸다고 보여 주므로, 바로 이 근거가 되는 가정을 직접 공격한다.
A: 결론 자체다. Valli의 관찰은 결론을 간접적으로 약하게 만들 뿐, 그녀가 직접 문제 삼는 것은 결론을 떠받치는 침묵의 해석이다. 또 다른 근거로 결론이 성립할 가능성도 Valli는 배제하지 않는다.
C: Nina가 두 번 부른다는 것은 줄거리의 부수적 세부일 뿐이고, Valli는 이를 다루지 않는다.
D: Valli도 이 장면이 중심적이라고 명시적으로 동의한다("also considers the departure scene central").
g.explanation_en:
Choice B is correct. Ames's conclusion that the novel treats duty as a trap depends on his reading of Rosa's silence as hidden longing to escape. Valli shows that elsewhere in the novel, Rosa falls silent after choices she accepts, and the narrator then calls her "settled" and "at ease." That evidence goes straight at Ames's interpretation of the silence, which is the assumption his argument rests on.
Choice A is incorrect because it is Ames's overall conclusion. Valli's evidence weakens it only indirectly, by undercutting its support. The specific point she challenges is how the silence should be read. Choice C is incorrect because Nina calling up twice is a minor plot detail that Valli never questions. Choice D is incorrect because Valli explicitly agrees that the departure scene is central.
g.design: Text 2 presents a separate pattern in the novel showing that Rosa's silences mean acceptance, which undercuts the assumption that her silence means longing. The distractors are Ames's conclusion, a minor plot detail, and the scene's centrality, which Valli agrees with. The question avoids words like "silence" and "desire" so the answer can't be found by matching surface wording.

c.instruction: 텍스트 1의 저자가 좋은 설명이나 해결책의 기준(예: 재현 가능성, 단순성, 장기적 효과)을 분명히 드러내게 쓰고, 텍스트 2는 그 기준과 어긋날 수 있는 결론을 내리게 쓴다. 질문은 '텍스트 1의 저자의 기준에서 텍스트 2의 결론을 어떻게 평가할 것인가'로 한다. 오답 3개는 텍스트 2 저자의 기준으로 평가한 결과, 두 저자의 기준을 섞은 평가, 일반 상식에 따른 평가로 만든다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — During a Seoul apartment complex power outage, elderly widow Min-ja and her distant daughter Soo-jin take shelter together as rain drums overhead, finally speaking honestly.

g.passage:
Text 1
In reviewing Hana Lee's novel The Fourteenth Floor, the critic Jae-won Park argues that a reconciliation scene in fiction convinces readers only when the characters themselves bring it about. If a storm, an accident, or a sudden darkness is what pushes estranged people to speak, Park contends, the novelist has let circumstance do the work that the characters' choices should do, and the resulting closeness feels borrowed rather than earned.

Text 2
In Lee's novel, a power outage leaves the widow Min-ja and her daughter Soo-jin, who rarely visits, sitting together in a dark Seoul apartment while rain drums on the windows. Unable to see each other's faces, the two finally admit what they have each resented for years. Critic Mi-rae Cho praises the scene as the most persuasive reconciliation in the book, arguing that it is precisely the blackout and the noise of the rain, which strip away the women's usual excuses for leaving, that make their honesty believable.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would Park (Text 1) most likely evaluate Cho's assessment of the outage scene in Text 2?
options: Park would agree with it, since Cho shows that the darkness and rain make the women's long-delayed honesty believable to readers.
Park would partly agree with it, since the women do eventually speak for themselves even though the outage first brings them together.
Park would reject it, since the very feature Cho praises—the outage forcing the conversation—is what Park thinks makes closeness feel unearned.
Park would endorse it, since a blackout in a crowded apartment complex is a realistic event that grounds the scene in everyday life.
g.explanation:
정답 C: Park의 기준은 화해가 인물의 선택에서 나와야 하며, 폭풍·어둠 같은 외부 상황이 대화를 강제하면 친밀감이 '빌려온 것'처럼 느껴진다는 것이다. Cho는 바로 그 정전과 빗소리가 정직함을 믿을 만하게 만든다고 칭찬하므로, Park의 기준에서는 Cho가 칭찬하는 요소가 오히려 결함이 된다.
A: Cho 자신의 기준(상황이 정직함을 가능하게 함)으로 평가한 것이다. Park는 바로 그 점을 문제 삼는다.
B: 두 기준을 섞은 평가다. 인물이 결국 직접 말한다는 점을 Park의 기준에 끌어오지만, Park는 대화를 촉발한 것이 상황이라면 화해가 얻어낸 것이 아니라고 본다. Cho도 정전이 결정적이라고 강조한다.
D: 일반 상식(사실적인 설정이면 좋다)에 따른 평가로, Park의 기준은 사건의 현실성이 아니라 화해의 원인이 누구에게 있는지에 관한 것이다.
g.explanation_en:
Correct answer, C: Park's standard is that a reconciliation is convincing only when the characters' own choices bring it about. When a storm or sudden darkness forces the conversation, Park says the closeness feels "borrowed rather than earned." Cho praises the scene specifically because the blackout and rain drive the women to be honest. By Park's standard, the feature Cho praises is the scene's flaw.
A applies Cho's own standard, that the circumstances make the honesty believable. This is exactly the point Park objects to.
B blends the two critics' standards. Yes, the women speak for themselves, but Park cares about what causes the conversation, and Cho stresses that the outage causes it.
D uses a common-sense standard, that a realistic setting is a good thing. Park's standard isn't about whether the event is realistic. It's about whether the characters or the circumstances produce the reconciliation.
g.design: Text 1 sets out Park's standard: a reconciliation must come from the characters' choices, not from circumstance. Text 2 concludes that the outage is what makes the reconciliation convincing. The question asks how Park would judge Cho's conclusion. The wrong answers are built from Cho's standard (A), a blend of both standards (B), and a common-sense realism standard (D).

c.instruction: 텍스트 1은 주장과 이유를, 텍스트 2는 같은 주제의 다른 접근을 각각 짧게 제시하되 서로를 언급하지 않게 쓴다. 질문은 '텍스트 2의 저자라면 텍스트 1의 주장에 어떻게 반응할 것인가'로 한다. 정답은 텍스트 2의 전제에서만 도출되는 반응으로 만들고, 오답 3개는 텍스트 1의 내용을 반복하는 선택지, 텍스트 2의 결론만 되풀이하는 선택지, 텍스트 2가 다루지 않은 쟁점을 끌어온 선택지로 만든다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — On a Philippine island school boat, aging teacher Mr. Reyes mentors his rival for decades of unacknowledged respect, their competition dissolving into shared legacy.

g.passage:
Text 1
In Marisol Abad's novel The Tide Schedule, the aging teacher Mr. Reyes spends forty years competing with Mr. Dalisay, the younger teacher on the island's school boat. Near the end, Reyes quietly hands Dalisay his worn lesson ledger. Critic Lorna Vibal reads this as surrender: with retirement near, Reyes gives up the rivalry that has defined him and admits that Dalisay has won.

Text 2
Critic Ben Aquino points out that Reyes's ledger is not a clean record of his own lessons. Its margins are full of notes reacting to Dalisay's methods: "D. tried this with fractions—better," "Answer D.'s tide-chart lesson next week." Aquino argues that for decades each man built his teaching partly in reply to the other, so their rivalry worked as a long, unspoken collaboration.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would Aquino (Text 2) most likely respond to Vibal's reading of the ledger scene (Text 1)?
options: He would agree that the scene shows Reyes finally accepting that his retirement means the rivalry has to end.
He would point out that the margins of the ledger show both teachers improving their lessons over many years.
He would argue that the school boat setting, more than the ledger, carries the main symbolic weight of the ending.
He would argue that calling the gesture an admission of defeat assumes the ledger belonged to one competitor, when it was really a record both men had shaped.
g.explanation:
정답 D: Text 2의 전제는 장부가 두 사람이 서로에게 응답하며 함께 만든 기록이라는 것이다. 그렇다면 장부를 건네는 것을 '패배 인정'으로 읽는 Vibal의 해석은 장부가 승패가 있는 경쟁에서 한쪽에만 속한 소유물이라고 가정하고 있는 셈이다. Aquino는 바로 이 가정을 반박할 것이다. 이 반응은 Text 2에 직접 쓰여 있지 않고, Text 2의 전제로부터 추론해야만 나온다.
A: Text 1의 해석(은퇴, 경쟁의 끝)을 그대로 되풀이한다. Aquino는 이 장면을 끝이 아니라 협력이 완성되는 순간으로 볼 것이다.
B: Text 2의 결론(여백 메모, 서로의 개선)만 다시 말할 뿐, Vibal의 '항복' 해석에 대한 반응이 아니다.
C: 배라는 배경의 상징성은 Text 2가 전혀 다루지 않은 쟁점이다.
g.explanation_en:
D is correct. Text 2 starts from the idea that the ledger is a record both men built together, with each one answering the other's lessons. Vibal reads the handover as Reyes admitting defeat, but that only works if the ledger belonged to one competitor in a contest someone could win. Aquino would challenge exactly that assumption. Text 2 never says this response outright; you have to infer it from what Text 2 assumes.
A is wrong because it simply repeats Text 1's reading (retirement ends the rivalry). Aquino would see the scene as completing a collaboration, not ending a contest.
B is wrong because it only restates Text 2's own evidence. It never actually answers Vibal's "surrender" reading.
C is wrong because Text 2 says nothing about the symbolism of the boat setting. That issue is brought in from outside the texts.
g.design: Text 1과 Text 2는 서로를 언급하지 않는다. 정답은 Text 2의 전제(장부를 두 사람이 함께 만들었다)에서 Text 1이 숨겨 둔 가정(장부는 한 사람의 소유이고 경쟁에는 승자가 있다)을 반박하는 방식으로만 나온다. 오답은 각각 Text 1을 반복하는 선택지, Text 2의 결론만 되풀이하는 선택지, 지문에 없는 쟁점을 끌어온 선택지로 만들었고 모두 정답과 같은 'He would…' 문장 틀로 썼다.

c.instruction: 텍스트 1은 하나의 결론을 이끄는 주장을, 텍스트 2는 그 주장의 핵심 근거를 약하게 만들 수 있는 별개의 관찰이나 연구를 제시한다. 질문은 '텍스트 2의 저자가 텍스트 1의 어느 부분에 가장 이의를 제기할 것인가'로 한다. 정답은 텍스트 1의 결론이 아니라 그 결론이 기대는 가정으로 하고, 오답 3개는 결론 자체, 텍스트 1의 부수적 세부, 텍스트 2가 오히려 동의하는 부분으로 만든다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — In a Hanoi street-food alley at dawn, apprentice Duc learns pho-broth technique from his grandmother while she subtly corrects his father's growing shortcuts, preserving tradition through irony.

g.passage:
Text 1
In the dawn scene of Linh Tran's novel The Long Simmer, set in a Hanoi street-food alley, Duc's grandmother teaches him to char ginger and skim the beef-bone broth. The scene opens in the dark, with the pot already steaming from its overnight simmer. When Duc's father stirs bouillon powder into a second pot, she remarks, "Of course—bones are so slow, and customers never notice." Because this mock approval plainly rebukes her son, the scene sets the old woman's tradition against the father's shortcuts, and the novel finally condemns him as a man who has given up his inheritance.

Text 2
Readers who hear only scorn in the grandmother's line overlook an earlier chapter. There, recalling the rationing years, she says almost the same words about the powder she herself once stirred into her broth, and she laughs as she says them. Her son laughs too. The phrase is a family joke, used to poke fun at oneself, and it shows Duc that every cook is tempted by shortcuts. Whatever the novel finally decides about the father, this line cannot show it. Still, the scene clearly shows the grandmother passing her broth technique on to Duc.
g.question: Based on the texts, which element of the argument in Text 1 would the author of Text 2 most likely challenge?
options: The assumption that the grandmother's ironic remark expresses scorn toward Duc's father
The assumption that the novel ultimately condemns Duc's father for giving up his inheritance
The assumption that the scene's opening in darkness stresses the long overnight simmer
The assumption that the scene shows the grandmother teaching Duc how to make the broth
g.explanation:
정답 A: Text 1의 결론(소설이 아버지를 단죄함)은 할머니의 반어적 말이 아들을 '꾸짖는다'는 전제에 기대고 있다. Text 2는 할머니가 앞 장에서 자신을 두고 같은 말을 하며 웃었고 아들도 함께 웃었다는 점을 들어, 그 말이 자기 자신을 비꼬는 가족 농담이라고 본다. 즉 Text 2는 바로 이 전제를 공격한다.
B(결론 자체): Text 2는 'Whatever the novel finally decides about the father'라고 하여, 결론을 직접 부정하지 않고 판단을 보류한다. 문제 삼는 것은 이 대사가 결론의 근거가 될 수 있느냐는 점뿐이다.
C(부수적 세부): 새벽 어둠과 밤샘 끓이기에 관한 묘사는 Text 2가 전혀 다루지 않는다.
D(동의하는 부분): Text 2의 마지막 문장은 할머니가 Duc에게 육수 기술을 전수한다는 점에 분명히 동의한다.
g.explanation_en:
Choice A is correct. Text 1's conclusion, that the novel condemns the father, depends on the idea that the grandmother's ironic line "plainly rebukes her son." Text 2 goes after exactly this idea. In an earlier chapter, she says nearly the same words about her own shortcuts and laughs, and her son laughs with her. So the line is a self-mocking family joke, not scorn.
Choice B is the conclusion itself. Text 2 does not reject it. It says "whatever the novel finally decides about the father" and argues only that this line can't support that judgment.
Choice C is a minor detail from Text 1 that Text 2 never mentions.
Choice D is something Text 2 agrees with. Its final sentence says the scene clearly shows the grandmother passing her technique on to Duc.
g.design: Text 1 argues from the grandmother's irony to the claim that the novel condemns the father. Text 2 gives evidence from an earlier chapter that undercuts the key assumption that her irony is scorn. The wrong answers are the conclusion (which Text 2 explicitly sets aside), a minor detail (the dawn setting), and a point Text 2 agrees with (passing on the technique). All four options use the same "The assumption that…" frame.

c.instruction: 노트에 제시된 서로 다른 두 개의 사실(예: 각각 다른 대상/사건/수치에 대한 독립된 정보)을 하나의 문장으로 자연스럽게 결합하여 주어진 목표(예: 두 대상을 비교하거나 관계를 설명)를 달성하는 문제를 만들어라. 오답은 각각 (1) 한쪽 사실만 담아 목표를 절반만 달성, (2) 두 사실을 결합했지만 목표와 무관한 조합, (3) 노트에 없는 내용을 추가해 사실을 왜곡한 문장으로 구성하라.

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Seam Below is a 2019 novel by Ruth Carver.
- It is set in 1974 in Harlan Ridge, a coal-mining town in eastern Kentucky.
- Years before the story opens, mine foreman Dale Pruitt, drunk at his dying brother Wes's bedside, promised to bury Wes beside their father.

- In 1974, Wes's widow arrives in Harlan Ridge and asks Dale to keep his word.
g.question: The student wants to explain why Dale cannot fulfill the obligation at the center of the novel. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In Ruth Carver's The Seam Below, mine foreman Dale Pruitt, drunk at his dying brother's bedside, promised years earlier to bury Wes beside their father.
In Ruth Carver's The Seam Below, Dale Pruitt once vowed to bury his brother Wes beside their father, but the father's grave has lain underwater since a reservoir flooded its cemetery in 1971.
