g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

- In a 2022 reading-group study, about 60% of participants linked the tear to the death of Karim's father; the rest linked it to the tannery's economic decline.

g.question: The student wants to report the novel's central event as a plain fact while signaling that one critic's interpretation of that event remains open to debate. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In The Indigo Vat, the ceremonial cloth tears as it is unveiled at the Indigo Festival, an event that represents grief Karim's family has never spoken aloud, as scholar Amina Berrada has demonstrated.

In The Indigo Vat, the ceremonial cloth seems to tear as it is unveiled at the Indigo Festival, an event that, according to scholar Amina Berrada, likely represents grief Karim's family has never spoken aloud.
In The Indigo Vat, the ceremonial cloth tears as it is unveiled at the Indigo Festival, an event that, according to scholar Amina Berrada, likely reflects a real accident Haddad witnessed in 2009.

In The Indigo Vat, the ceremonial cloth tears as it is unveiled at the Indigo Festival, an event that, according to scholar Amina Berrada, likely represents grief Karim's family has never spoken aloud.
g.explanation:
정답 D: 천이 찢어지는 사건은 노트에 줄거리상 사실로 나와 있으므로 단정적으로 서술하고, Berrada의 해석은 'according to ... likely'로 한정해 학자 한 명의 잠정적 견해임을 드러낸다. 목표의 두 조건을 모두 충족한다.
A: 해석을 'represents ... as ... has demonstrated'로 서술해 잠정적 주장('likely')을 입증된 사실로 과장했다.
B: 해석의 확실성 수준은 맞지만, 소설 속에서 실제로 일어나는 사건을 'seems to tear'로 불필요하게 약화했다.
C: 확실성 수준의 형식은 맞지만 내용을 혼동했다. 2009년 실제 사고는 Berrada의 해석이 아니라 Haddad 본인이 인터뷰에서 확인한 사실이다.
g.explanation_en:
D is correct. The cloth tearing is something that definitely happens in the novel's plot, so D states it plainly. It then limits Berrada's reading with "according to" and "likely," which shows the interpretation is one critic's tentative view. That meets both parts of the goal.
A is wrong because it turns Berrada's tentative claim into a proven one ("represents... as Berrada has demonstrated"). That overstates how certain the interpretation is.
B handles the interpretation correctly, but it weakens a plot fact for no reason. The cloth doesn't just "seem" to tear in the novel. It actually tears.
C uses the right level of certainty but mixes up the content. The connection to a real 2009 accident is something Haddad herself confirmed in interviews. It isn't Berrada's interpretation, and it isn't open to debate.
g.design: I paired a definite plot fact with a scholar's tentative interpretation. Each wrong answer is built on the same sentence frame. One overstates the interpretation, one hedges the plot fact, and one keeps the right hedging but swaps in content from the author's interview. For example,
g.explanation:
정답 C(Still,). 바로 앞 문장은 바구니를 계속 채울 실용적인 이유가 사라졌다는 점을 보여 준다. 시빌레는 이제 자기 콩을 직접 길러서 베르너의 콩이 더 이상 필요 없다. 그런데도 베르너는 바구니를 계속 채운다. 마지막 문장이 강조하는 것은 채소 자체가 아니라 둘 사이의 관계를 이어 가려는 의도다. 따라서 '그렇다 하더라도'라는 양보의 뜻을 가진 Still이 가장 자연스럽다.
A(Accordingly,): '수확이 남아돌아서 그 결과 바구니를 채웠다'는 인과로 읽으면 앞 문장의 부수적 사실(남는 수확)과는 맞는 것처럼 보인다. 하지만 마지막 문장은 '담긴 것 때문이 아니다(not for the sake of what it held)'라고 그 이유를 직접 부정하므로, 지문의 핵심 강조점과 어긋난다.
B(Instead,): 앞 내용과 대비된다는 방향은 맞는다. 그러나 Instead는 앞의 행동을 다른 행동으로 바꿀 때 쓰는 대체 관계를 나타낸다. 이 지문에서는 베르너가 무언가를 그만두고 다른 일을 한 것이 아니라 하던 일을 그대로 계속하므로 논리 관계가 맞지 않는다.
D(For example,): 마지막 문장은 앞 문장의 사례가 아니다. 앞 내용과 전혀 다른 성격의 연결이다.
g.explanation_en:
The answer is C (Still,). The sentence before the blank removes every practical reason to keep filling the basket: Sibylle now grows her own beans and no longer needs Werner's. Even so, he keeps filling it. The last sentence stresses that the basket matters as a way to stay in touch with her, not as a way to share food. "Still" expresses this "even so" contrast.
A (Accordingly,) is wrong. It treats his extra harvest as the cause, which fits a side detail in the text. But the last sentence says he fills the basket "not for the sake of what it held," which rejects that reason directly.
B (Instead,) is wrong. It does signal a contrast, but it means one action replaces another. Werner doesn't swap one action for another; he keeps doing the same thing.
D (For example,) is wrong. The last sentence isn't an example of anything said earlier.
g.design: I listed several facts: the six-year ritual, the lack of talk this July, Werner's surplus, and Sibylle no longer needing his beans. Only the fact that she no longer needs the beans connects directly to the answer. The final sentence stresses intention (keeping the bond) rather than outcome (the produce), so the solver has to choose a concessive transition. The distractors are a cause-based reading that matches the surplus detail, a contrast word with the wrong logic (replacement), and an unrelated exemplifying transition.

c.instruction: 서로 배치되거나 상반된 것처럼 보이는 두 가지 관찰(실험 결과, 사례, 수치)이 제시된 짧은 지문을 만들고, 두 관찰을 종합했을 때 나오는 결론을 마지막 문장에서 올바른 전환어로 연결해야 정답이 되게 하라. 오답 3개는 (1)한쪽 관찰만 반영한 전환어, (2)두 관찰이 상반된다는 점만 보고 단순 대조로 처리한 전환어, (3)종합 결론과 무관한 전환어로 구성하라. 계산이나 복잡한 수치 없이 정성적 진술만으로 구성한다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — On a Brooklyn tenement stoop in 1915, Irish immigrant Liam and Polish immigrant Szymek watch their sons leave for different wars, their friendship fracturing beneath unspoken accusation.

g.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story set in Brooklyn in 1915.

On the stoop, Liam talked without pause—about the price of coal, the heat in the stairwell, the Dodgers' poor season—but he never once spoke the name of the ship that had carried his son toward the British army. Beside him, Szymek said nothing at all, turning his cap slowly in his hands, though his own boy had sailed that same week to join the Polish Legions on the other side of the war. One man filled every silence, and the other refused to break any. ______ each was guarding the same unspoken accusation: that the other's son had chosen the wrong flag.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Instead,
Even so,
Meanwhile,
In their different ways,
g.explanation:
정답 D. 지문은 겉보기에 정반대인 두 행동, 즉 쉬지 않고 떠드는 Liam과 끝까지 침묵하는 Szymek을 보여 준다. 마지막 문장은 두 행동이 결국 같은 목적, 곧 같은 비난을 입 밖에 내지 않으려는 것이었다는 종합 결론을 내린다. 'In their different ways'는 방식은 달라도 결과는 같다는 이 종합을 정확히 연결한다.
A(Instead): 한쪽 관찰만 반영한 오답이다. Szymek의 침묵이 말을 대신했다는 데서 나온 '대체' 관계인데, 마지막 문장은 앞의 행동을 대신하는 내용이 아니라 두 사람 모두에게 해당하는 내용이다.
B(Even so): 두 행동이 상반된다는 점만 보고 단순 대조로 처리한 오답이다. 마지막 문장은 앞의 내용을 거스르는 양보가 아니라, 상반되어 보이는 두 행동을 하나로 묶는 결론이다.
C(Meanwhile): 동시에 일어난 다른 일을 덧붙이는 전환어로, 종합 결론과는 관계가 없다. 마지막 문장은 별개의 사건이 아니라 앞에 묘사된 행동을 해석하는 문장이다.
g.explanation_en:
The answer is D. The text shows two behaviors that look like opposites: Liam talks without pause, while Szymek stays completely silent. The last sentence brings them together and shows that both behaviors serve the same purpose. Each man is holding back the same accusation. "In their different ways" fits this conclusion: the two men act differently, but the result is the same.
A ("Instead") reflects only one observation. It treats Szymek's silence as a replacement for speech. But the final sentence doesn't replace anything that came before. It describes what both men are doing.
B ("Even so") treats the two behaviors as a simple contrast. The final sentence doesn't concede a point against what came before. It joins the two seemingly opposite behaviors into one conclusion.
C ("Meanwhile") adds a separate event happening at the same time. It has nothing to do with the conclusion. The final sentence interprets the behavior already described rather than adding a new event.
g.design: 상반되어 보이는 두 관찰(쉬지 않는 수다와 완전한 침묵)을 같은 숨은 비난을 감추는 행동으로 종합하는 결론을 마지막 문장에 두었다. 오답은 한쪽 관찰만 반영한 대체(Instead), 단순 대조(Even so), 결론과 무관한 동시 진행(Meanwhile)으로 구성했다.

c.instruction: 한 문장 안에서 수식어구나 비교 표현이 인접한 명사가 아니라 문장 앞부분의 다른 요소(주어나 앞 문장의 대상)를 가리키도록 설계된 짧은 지문을 만들고, 이 실제 지시 관계를 올바르게 파악해야 정답 전환어를 고를 수 있게 하라. 오답 3개는 (1)인접한 명사를 지시 대상으로 잘못 본 전환어, (2)문법적으로는 자연스럽지만 실제 지시관계와 어긋나는 전환어, (3)전혀 다른 요소를 지시 대상으로 삼은 전환어로 구성하라. 문장은 짧고 단순한 구조를 유지한다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — At a Patagonian sheep ranch, solitary rancher Matilde receives word that a woman she promised marriage to decades ago has finally returned, alive but transformed.

g.passage: After forty years away, Elena climbed down from the supply truck with white hair and a slow, careful walk. Matilde stood waiting beside the young foreman, as unchanged, she thought, as the fence posts she had set the summer Elena left. ______ Elena recognized her at once, calling her by a childhood name no one on the ranch had ever heard.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Accordingly,
Even so,
Instead,
By contrast,
g.explanation:
정답 A. 'as unchanged ... as the fence posts'는 바로 옆 명사 'the young foreman'이 아니라 문장의 주어 Matilde를 수식한다(그녀 자신이 그렇게 생각함). Matilde가 거의 변하지 않았으므로 Elena가 그녀를 곧바로 알아본 것은 자연스러운 결과이다. 따라서 결과를 나타내는 'Accordingly,'가 알맞다.
B(Even so): '변하지 않은' 대상을 인접한 명사인 젊은 감독관으로 잘못 보면, Matilde가 변했는데도 알아봤다는 양보 관계로 오해하게 된다. 실제로 변하지 않은 사람은 Matilde이므로 양보 관계가 성립하지 않는다.
C(Instead): 문법적으로는 자연스럽지만, 앞 문장에서 부정되거나 대체된 행동이 없으므로 '대신'이라는 관계가 지시 관계와 맞지 않는다.
D(By contrast): 첫 문장에서 변해 버린 Elena를 비교 대상으로 삼는 연결어이다. 하지만 빈칸 뒤 문장은 Elena의 변화와 대조되는 내용이 아니라 Matilde가 변하지 않은 데 따른 결과를 서술한다.
g.explanation_en:
The answer is A. The phrase "as unchanged ... as the fence posts" doesn't describe the nearby noun "the young foreman." It describes the subject, Matilde, and it is her own view of herself. Since Matilde has barely changed, it makes sense that Elena recognizes her right away. That is a result, so "Accordingly," is the logical transition.
B ("Even so,") is wrong. It only works if you attach "unchanged" to the foreman and assume Matilde has changed, which turns the recognition into a surprise. But the person who is unchanged is Matilde, so there is nothing to concede.
C ("Instead,") is wrong. It sounds fine grammatically, but it signals a replacement, and the text doesn't reject or replace any earlier action.
D ("By contrast,") is wrong. It sets up a contrast with Elena's transformation from the first sentence. But the sentence after the blank doesn't contrast with that change. It describes what follows from Matilde being unchanged.
g.design: The comparison "as unchanged ... as the fence posts" sits right next to "the young foreman," but it actually describes the subject, Matilde. Each wrong answer matches a different misreading: B treats the adjacent noun as the referent, C is grammatical but doesn't fit the logic, and D takes Elena from the first sentence as the point of comparison.

c.instruction: 학술적 소재(연구, 인물, 현상 등)에 대한 3~4문장의 짧은 지문을 만들고, 마지막 문장은 앞 내용 중 특정 목적이나 강조점(예: 결과가 아니라 의도, 수치가 아니라 방향성)에 부합하는 전환어를 골라야 정답이 되게 하라. 오답 3개는 (1)앞 문장의 결과·부수적 사실과는 맞지만 지문의 핵심 강조점과는 어긋나는 전환어, (2)방향은 맞지만 논리관계(원인/대조 등)가 틀린 전환어, (3)전혀 다른 내용과 연결되는 전환어로 구성하라. 지문에 여러 개의 정보가 나열되되 그중 한 가지만 답과 직결되도록 설계한다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — On a Sri Lankan tea estate, widow Priya and her former supervisor Rajesh grow quiet on the garden bench where they once laughed, their ease slowly replaced by careful distance.

g.passage: Years ago, Priya and Rajesh had traded jokes on this garden bench while the pickers' baskets filled on the slopes below. Now, as mist drifted up from the valley and a kettle whistled somewhere in the line rooms, the widow and her former supervisor sat with a measured gap between them. Rajesh, who once interrupted her freely, waited until she had finished every sentence before speaking; he intended this restraint as a mark of respect for her grief. ______ to Priya, each of his careful pauses felt like a door being quietly closed.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Consequently,
Even so,
In other words,
Meanwhile,
g.explanation:
정답 B(Even so,): 바로 앞 문장의 핵심은 결과가 아니라 Rajesh의 '의도'다. 그는 자제를 슬픔에 대한 존중으로 의도했다. 그런데 마지막 문장에서 Priya는 그 침묵을 문이 닫히는 것처럼 받아들인다. 선의의 의도와 상대가 받은 상처가 어긋나므로, 앞의 내용을 인정하면서 대조하는 'Even so'가 맞다.
A(Consequently,): 그의 멈춤이 Priya가 받은 인상을 낳았다는 인과 관계로 표면적으로는 들어맞는다. 하지만 '존중하려는 의도' 때문에 '거부당한 느낌'이 생겼다고 하면 의도와 결과 사이의 엇갈림이라는 지문의 핵심이 사라진다.
C(In other words,): 두 문장 모두 그의 조심스러움을 다룬다는 점은 맞다. 하지만 마지막 문장은 앞 문장을 바꿔 말한 것이 아니다. 존중과 닫힌 문은 서로 반대되는 해석이다.
D(Meanwhile,): 안개나 주전자 소리 같은 배경 묘사와 '동시에 일어나는 일'로 잇게 만드는 함정이다. 마지막 문장은 별개의 사건이 아니라 바로 앞에 나온 그의 행동을 Priya가 어떻게 받아들였는지를 말한다.
g.explanation_en:
B (Even so,) is correct. The key point of the previous sentence isn't what Rajesh does. It's why he does it: he means his restraint as respect for Priya's grief. The final sentence shows Priya experiencing that same restraint as a door quietly closing. His kind intention clashes with the hurt she feels, so you need a transition that accepts the first idea and then contrasts it. That's "Even so."
A (Consequently,) is tempting because his pauses really do cause her impression. But a cause-and-effect link hides the gap between his respectful intent and the rejection she feels, and that gap is the whole point.
C (In other words,) wrongly treats the last sentence as a restatement. "Respect" and "a closing door" are opposite readings of the same behavior.
D (Meanwhile,) points you back to the background details (the mist, the kettle) and suggests something happening at the same time. The last sentence actually describes how Priya reacts to Rajesh's behavior from the previous sentence.
g.design: 지문에 배경 묘사, 과거의 웃음, 행동, 의도를 나열했지만 정답과 직결되는 것은 '의도'뿐이다. 오답은 결과에만 맞는 인과(A), 방향은 맞지만 관계를 바꿔 말하기로 잘못 본 것(C), 배경 묘사와 잇는 전환어(D)로 구성했다.

c.instruction: 서로 배치되거나 상반된 것처럼 보이는 두 가지 관찰(실험 결과, 사례, 수치)이 제시된 짧은 지문을 만들고, 두 관찰을 종합했을 때 나오는 결론을 마지막 문장에서 올바른 전환어로 연결해야 정답이 되게 하라. 오답 3개는 (1)한쪽 관찰만 반영한 전환어, (2)두 관찰이 상반된다는 점만 보고 단순 대조로 처리한 전환어, (3)종합 결론과 무관한 전환어로 구성하라. 계산이나 복잡한 수치 없이 정성적 진술만으로 구성한다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — At a Moroccan riverside tannery, elderly craftsman Amara teaches his final apprentices the indigo process, each gesture weighted with the knowledge he will not return next season.

g.passage: This season, Amara lowered each length of cloth into the indigo vats more slowly than his apprentices had ever seen him do, often stopping over the dark water as if he had lost track of the next step. Yet by the week's end, Youssef and Hamid could tell whether a vat was ready by its smell alone, something no earlier group of apprentices had learned before spring. ______ the old man's pauses had never been lapses at all: each one had been a lesson, held open long enough for the young men to step inside it.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Regrettably,
Nevertheless,
Evidently,
Meanwhile,
g.explanation:
지문의 두 관찰은 서로 맞지 않는 것처럼 보인다. 하나는 아마라의 손이 유난히 느려지고 자주 멈췄다는 점(쇠퇴처럼 보임), 다른 하나는 제자들이 이전 어느 기수보다 빨리 숙련에 도달했다는 점이다. 마지막 문장은 두 관찰을 합쳐서 '그 멈춤은 실수가 아니라 가르침이었다'는 결론을 내린다. 따라서 앞의 증거에서 결론을 끌어내는 'Evidently,'(C)가 정답이다.
A 'Regrettably,'는 첫 번째 관찰(느려짐=노쇠)만 반영해 안타까움을 표현한다. 하지만 마지막 문장은 멈춤이 실수가 '아니었다'고 긍정적으로 다시 해석하므로 어조와 논리가 맞지 않는다.
B 'Nevertheless,'는 두 관찰이 상반된다는 점만 보고 단순 대조로 처리한 것이다. 마지막 문장은 앞 내용에 맞서는 진술이 아니라 두 관찰을 하나로 묶어 설명하는 결론이다.
D 'Meanwhile,'는 동시에 일어난 별개의 일을 덧붙일 때 쓴다. 앞의 증거에서 나온 결론과는 관계가 없다.
g.explanation_en:
The text gives two observations that seem to clash. First, Amara works unusually slowly and keeps pausing, which looks like decline. Second, his apprentices master the craft faster than any earlier group. The last sentence puts these together and concludes that his pauses were never mistakes but lessons. "Evidently," is the right choice because it signals a conclusion drawn from the evidence before it.
A, "Regrettably," only reflects the first observation, reading the slowness as sad decline. But the final sentence says the pauses were NOT lapses, so the regretful tone doesn't fit.
B, "Nevertheless," treats the two observations as a simple contrast. The final sentence doesn't push back against what came before; it explains both observations at once.
D, "Meanwhile," adds a separate event happening at the same time. It has nothing to do with drawing a conclusion from the evidence.
g.design: 두 관찰(느려진 장인과 비정상적으로 빠른 제자들의 숙련)을 한데 묶은 결론 앞에 빈칸을 두었다. 오답은 지시대로 구성했다. 한쪽 관찰만 반영한 Regrettably, 단순 대조로 처리한 Nevertheless, 결론과 무관한 Meanwhile이다.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — In an Edo-period fishing village, young apprentice Noboru gifts his employer a carved wooden fish meant as gratitude, but it's mistaken for mockery of his clumsy net-work.

g.passage:
The following text is adapted from a novel set in an Edo-period fishing village.

At dawn, Noboru set the small carving on the mat beside his master's tea. It was a sea bream, its scales cut one by one with a borrowed knife over many nights. Gonzō picked it up and turned it over. Then his face darkened. "A fish," he said quietly, "caught without a net. Is that what you think of my work?" He dropped the carving and walked out to the boats, leaving Noboru staring at the gift he had meant as thanks.

A literary critic argues that Gonzō's angry reaction comes less from the carving itself than from shame he already feels about his own poor skill at mending and casting nets.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the critic's interpretation?
options: Earlier in the novel, Noboru is described as spending his rare free hours carving small animals from scraps of driftwood.
Earlier in the novel, the narrator explains that apprentices in the village usually thanked their masters with gifts of rice cakes.
Later in the novel, Noboru leaves the village and becomes a respected woodcarver in a nearby castle town.
Earlier in the novel, Gonzō hides his tangled nets from the other fishermen and snaps at anyone who looks at them.
g.explanation: 비평가의 주장은 곤조의 분노가 그물 다루는 솜씨에 대해 원래 느끼던 수치심에서 나왔다는 것이다. D는 곤조가 엉킨 그물을 숨기고 누가 보기만 해도 화를 낸다는 내용이므로, 선물을 받기 전부터 그 수치심이 있었음을 직접 보여 준다. A는 노보루의 조각 취미만 설명하고 곤조의 감정은 다루지 않는다. B는 마을의 선물 관습에 관한 내용일 뿐 곤조의 수치심과는 관련이 없다. C는 노보루의 미래 이야기여서 곤조가 왜 화를 냈는지 설명하지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: The critic claims that Gonzō gets angry because he is already ashamed of his poor net skills, not because of anything in the carving. D shows Gonzō hiding his tangled nets and snapping at anyone who looks at them, which is clear evidence that he felt this shame before he ever got the gift. A only tells us about Noboru's carving hobby and says nothing about how Gonzō feels. B is about village gift customs, which has nothing to do with Gonzō's shame. C is about Noboru's future, so it doesn't explain why Gonzō reacted the way he did.
g.design: This is an easy item that tests one rule: the correct answer has to show the specific cause the critic names, which is Gonzō's existing shame about his nets. Each wrong answer is a related story detail that doesn't speak to that cause.

c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — On an Appalachian trail shelter, eight-year-old Waylon notices an injured songbird that all the adults dismiss, his urgent attention to its suffering both tender and troubling.

g.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Eight-year-old Waylon is resting with a group of adult hikers at a trail shelter in the Appalachian Mountains.

The bird lay beside the woodpile, one wing bent at a wrong angle. Waylon crouched over it while the grown-ups unpacked their stoves. "Leave it," his uncle said without looking. "Nature takes care of its own." Waylon did not leave it. He cupped his hands around the small body, and he stayed there long after the others had begun to talk about tomorrow's climb.

A literary critic argues that Waylon's intense focus on the injured bird reflects his own sense of being ignored by the adults around him.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the critic's interpretation?
options: Later in the story, Waylon whispers to the bird that the grown-ups never listen to him either.
Later in the story, the adults spend the evening discussing which route up the mountain will be safest.
Later in the story, a hiker identifies the bird as a type of wren that is common in the Appalachian region.
In an interview, the author says she hiked Appalachian trails often when she was a child.
g.explanation: 비평가의 주장은 새에 대한 Waylon의 집착이 어른들에게 무시당한다는 그 자신의 감정을 반영한다는 것이다. A는 Waylon이 새에게 어른들이 자기 말도 듣지 않는다고 속삭이는 장면으로, 새의 처지와 자신의 소외감을 직접 연결하므로 주장을 뒷받침한다. B는 어른들의 대화 주제만 보여 줄 뿐 Waylon의 감정과 새를 연결하지 않는다. C는 새의 종류에 관한 정보로 Waylon의 심리와 무관하다. D는 작가의 경험에 관한 것이어서 등장인물의 감정에 대한 해석을 뒷받침하지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: The critic claims that Waylon's focus on the bird reflects his own feeling of being ignored by adults. Choice A shows Waylon telling the bird that the grown-ups never listen to him either, which directly links the bird's situation to his own sense of being overlooked, so it supports the claim. Choice B only shows what the adults talk about and says nothing about how Waylon feels or why he cares about the bird. Choice C identifies the bird's species, which has nothing to do with Waylon's emotions. Choice D is about the author's life, not about the character's feelings, so it can't support this interpretation.
g.design: Easy: one step is needed—find the finding that connects Waylon's care for the bird to his own feeling of being ignored. The wrong answers are typical traps that seem related to the story (what the adults do, the bird's species, the author's life).

c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Aboard a Kerala backwater houseboat, child Asha watches her grandmother scatter flower petals at dawn and understands something about acceptance that no adult voice can articulate.

g.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Asha, a young girl, is traveling with her grandmother on a houseboat in the backwaters of Kerala, India, a few weeks after her grandfather's death.

At dawn the water was the color of weak tea. Asha woke to find her grandmother already at the edge of the deck, holding a brass bowl of marigold and jasmine petals. Asha had expected her to cry, as she had at the funeral. Instead, her grandmother scattered the petals one handful at a time and watched them drift away with the slow current toward the palms. She did not try to call them back. Asha sat very still beside her. No one had been able to explain to her why the house now felt calm instead of broken, but watching the petals go, she thought she finally understood.
g.question: A student claims that in the text, Asha comes to understand acceptance by watching her grandmother rather than by being told about it. Which quotation from the text most directly supports this claim?
options: "At dawn the water was the color of weak tea."
"No one had been able to explain to her why the house now felt calm instead of broken, but watching the petals go, she thought she finally understood."
"Asha had expected her to cry, as she had at the funeral."
"Asha woke to find her grandmother already at the edge of the deck, holding a brass bowl of marigold and jasmine petals."
g.explanation: 이 주장은 두 가지를 말한다. Asha가 무언가를 이해하게 된다는 점, 그리고 그 이해가 누군가의 설명이 아니라 지켜보는 것에서 온다는 점이다. B는 아무도 설명해 주지 못했다는 내용과 꽃잎이 떠내려가는 것을 보며 마침내 이해했다는 내용을 함께 담고 있어 두 가지를 모두 뒷받침한다. A는 배경 묘사일 뿐이다. C는 Asha의 예상만 보여 줄 뿐 무엇을 이해했는지는 드러내지 않는다. D는 할머니를 처음 보는 장면이지만 이해나 설명에 관한 내용이 없다.
g.explanation_en: The claim has two parts: Asha comes to understand something, and that understanding comes from watching, not from being told. B covers both parts. It says no one had been able to explain things to her, and that she finally understood while watching the petals float away. A only describes the setting. C shows what Asha expected, but it does not show that she understood anything. D shows Asha first seeing her grandmother, but it says nothing about understanding or explanation.
g.design: 이 문항은 "직접 설명 없이 보면서 이해한다"는 주장의 두 요소를 모두 담은 인용문을 고르는 한 단계 추론만 요구한다. 오답은 같은 지문의 그럴듯한 인용문으로 구성했다.

c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — In a California Gold Rush camp, prospector Ezra inherits his brother's pocket watch and discovers it contains dried flowers and coordinates to an unmapped claim.

g.passage: In a California mining camp in 1851, Ezra receives the pocket watch that belonged to his late brother, Silas. When he pries open the back cover, he finds a few pressed blue flowers and a slip of paper listing a set of coordinates. Ezra checks the coordinates against every claim map in the camp office, but none of the maps shows any claim at that spot. Silas had spent his last months walking alone into the hills each week and coming back without saying where he had gone. Because the coordinates match no recorded claim, Ezra concludes that ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: Silas must have bought the watch from another miner who had already filed a claim at that location.
the coordinates must point to the camp office, where Silas had kept the claim maps.
Silas may have found a site that he never officially registered with the camp.
the blue flowers must have been picked from land that already appeared on the camp's claim maps.
g.explanation: 지문의 핵심 단서는 좌표가 캠프의 어떤 채굴권 지도에도 나오지 않는다는 점이다. 기록된 채굴권이 없으니, Silas가 공식 등록하지 않은 장소를 찾았을 수 있다는 C가 가장 논리적인 결론이다. A는 '이미 등록된 채굴권'이 있다고 하는데, 이는 지도에 아무 기록도 없다는 사실과 맞지 않는다. B는 캠프 사무실이 좌표의 위치라고 하지만, 사무실은 좌표를 확인한 곳일 뿐 좌표가 가리키는 곳은 아니다. D 역시 해당 땅이 지도에 이미 나와 있다고 하므로 지문의 단서와 정면으로 충돌한다.
g.explanation_en: The key clue is that the coordinates do not match any claim on the camp's maps. If no claim was recorded there, the most logical conclusion is that Silas may have found a site he never officially registered, which is choice C. Choice A says someone had already filed a claim at that location, but that contradicts the fact that no map shows a claim there. Choice B treats the camp office as the place the coordinates point to, but the office is only where Ezra checked the maps. Choice D says the land already appeared on the claim maps, which also directly contradicts the passage.
g.design: 쉬운 문항이 되도록 한 단계 추론만 필요하게 만들었다. '지도에 기록된 채굴권이 없다'는 사실에서 '등록되지 않은 장소'라는 결론만 끌어내면 된다. 오답은 모두 같은 문장 구조로 썼고, 지문 속 요소(사무실, 지도, 꽃)를 잘못 연결한 그럴듯한 함정으로 구성했다.

c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — On a Lisbon tram line, conductor Neves and passenger Vitor spend years dismissing each other as incompetent until a mechanical failure forces them to collaborate brilliantly.

g.passage: For eleven years, tram conductor Neves had considered the passenger Vitor a know-it-all who could not stop criticizing how she drove the old No. 28 car up the hills of Lisbon. Vitor, a retired clockmaker, had always assumed Neves had no real understanding of the machine she operated. Then one rainy morning the tram stalled halfway up a steep street, its brakes locked. Neves knew exactly which lever to hold, and Vitor knew how to free the stuck gear with his pocket tools; working side by side, they had the car moving in ten minutes. As the passengers cheered, Neves and Vitor looked at each other in surprise, and each realized that ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the other had been right all along to doubt their skill with the tram.
the other would probably never ride or drive the No. 28 car again.
the other cared more about the cheering passengers than about the tram.
the other was far more capable than they had believed for years.
g.explanation: 지문은 두 사람이 11년간 서로를 무능하다고 여겼지만, 고장 상황에서 각자의 전문성(레버 조작, 기어 수리)으로 함께 문제를 해결했다고 말한다. 따라서 둘이 놀라며 깨달은 것은 상대가 생각보다 훨씬 유능하다는 점이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 서로의 실력을 의심한 것이 옳았다는 내용으로, 성공적인 협력과 반대된다. B는 앞으로 전차를 타거나 운전하지 않는다는 근거가 지문에 없다. C는 승객의 환호에 대한 관심을 다루지만, 그들의 놀람은 상대의 능력에 관한 것이다.
g.explanation_en: The text says Neves and Vitor spent eleven years thinking the other was incompetent, but when the tram broke down, each used real expertise (the lever, the gear) to fix it together. So their surprise shows they realized the other was much more skilled than they had thought, which makes D correct. A says their doubts were justified, which is the opposite of what their successful teamwork shows. B has no support, since nothing suggests either of them will stop riding or driving the tram. C is about the passengers' cheering, but their surprise is about each other's ability.
g.design: 쉬운 난이도: 서로를 무능하다고 여겼다는 명시적 대조 후 성공적 협력이라는 한 단계 추론으로 결론을 완성; 오답은 같은 'the other ...' 문장 틀로 반대·무근거·초점 이탈을 담음.

c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — In a Norwegian coastal sauna, fisherman Halvard receives a hand-knitted scarf from his estranged daughter and assumes it's debt repayment rather than wordless reconciliation.

g.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Halvard, a fisherman, sits in a sauna on the Norwegian coast after receiving a package from his daughter, Ingrid, who has not spoken to him in six years.

Halvard turned the gray scarf over in his hands. Years ago he had lent Ingrid money for her first apartment, and she had moved away before paying it back. Now here was a scarf, knitted stitch by stitch, with no letter inside. He decided at once that it must be her way of settling the old loan. Yet the scarf held a pattern of small boats, the same pattern his late wife had knitted into his sweaters every winter, a detail Ingrid could only have chosen with him in mind. Halvard's conclusion about the gift therefore suggests that ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: he has overlooked a sign that Ingrid may be reaching out to him rather than paying off a debt.
he has noticed that Ingrid copied the pattern because she wanted to sell similar scarves.
he has realized that Ingrid sent the scarf because she plans to borrow more money from him.
he has understood that Ingrid chose the pattern because his wife had asked her to finish it.
g.explanation: 지문은 Halvard가 목도리를 빚 갚기로 단정하지만, 아내가 그를 위해 짜던 배 무늬가 들어 있어 딸이 아버지를 생각하며 고른 선물임을 보여 준다. 따라서 그의 결론은 화해의 신호를 놓친 것이므로 A가 정답이다. B의 판매 목적은 지문에 근거가 없다. C의 추가 대출 계획도 언급되지 않으며, D의 아내의 부탁은 지문에 없는 내용이다.
g.explanation_en: Halvard assumes the scarf is repayment for the old loan, but the text points out that it carries the boat pattern his late wife knitted for him, which Ingrid could only have chosen with him in mind. That means his conclusion misses a sign that she may be reaching out to him, so A is correct. B is wrong because nothing in the text mentions selling scarves. C is wrong because the text never says she plans to borrow more money. D is wrong because the text never says his wife asked Ingrid to finish anything.
g.design: 쉬운 문항: 단서 하나(아버지를 생각해 고른 무늬)가 빚 갚기라는 해석과 어긋난다는 점을 한 단계로 추론하게 했다. 선택지는 모두 같은 문장 틀을 쓰고, 오답은 지문에 근거 없는 동기를 내세운다.

c.instruction: 그래프나 표에 두 개 이상의 변수(또는 텍스트 설명과 그래프 수치)가 함께 제시된 자료를 주고, 두 요소를 동시에 봐야만 결론을 낼 수 있는 질문을 만들어라. 정답은 두 변수를 모두 반영해야 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 '한쪽 변수만 본 결론', '다른 쪽 변수만 본 결론', '자료에 없는 제3의 변수로 결론'을 만든 것으로 구성하라.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — On a 1930s Great Plains farmstead, elderly widower Jonas receives a letter revealing that the hired hand he knew in youth survived the Depression and kept their youthful pact.

g.passage:
The following text is adapted from a 2019 novel. In 1936, Jonas Brandt, an elderly widower, is on his Nebraska farm.

The envelope had come through three post offices before it found him, and the handwriting on it was unsteady. Jonas read the letter standing by the windmill. Walt Sorensen, who had worked as a hired hand on the Brandt place in the summer of 1889, was alive in Montana. "I kept to what we said by the creek," Walt wrote. "Every spring I planted one cottonwood for each year since. There are forty-seven now." Jonas folded the page and looked across his own yard, where no tree had stood for a long time. He had made the same promise, and the drought and the bank had taken the place he had meant to plant. He laughed once, quietly, and then he did not laugh again.

A literary scholar argues that in this scene the letter works as both a comfort and a rebuke to Jonas: Walt's faithfulness to the pact pleases him, but it also makes him face the fact that he broke his own word.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the scholar's interpretation?
options: In the author's notebook, a note on the letter scene reads: "Jonas should feel only warmth here—proof at last that his old friend survived the hard years."
In the author's notebook, a note on the letter scene reads: "Walt's trees are a gift to Jonas and a measure of him at once—he cannot be glad for one without counting the other."
In the author's notebook, a note on a later chapter reads: "Jonas's abandoned promise should come back to trouble him again and again until the last page."
In the author's notebook, a note on the novel's background reads: "My grandfather spent the 1890s working as a hired hand on farms across the Dakotas."
g.explanation:
학자의 해석은 두 요소로 이루어진다. ① 편지가 주는 위안(Walt가 약속을 지켜서 기쁨)과 ② 그 위안이 동시에 질책이 됨(Jonas 자신의 깨진 약속을 마주하게 함). 이 둘이 같은 장면에서 함께 작동한다는 주장이다. B는 편지 장면에 관한 메모에서 Walt의 나무를 '선물'이자 '자신을 재는 척도'라고 부르고, 한쪽 없이 다른 쪽도 느낄 수 없다고 적고 있어 두 요소를 모두, 그리고 서로 연결된 것으로 담아낸다. 그래서 정답이다.
A: 위안 쪽만 반영한다. 게다가 'only warmth'라고 해서 질책의 요소를 오히려 배제하므로 해석을 약화한다.
C: 질책(깨진 약속) 쪽만 반영한다. 그것도 편지 장면이 아니라 이후 장(章)에 관한 메모라서, 이 장면에서 위안과 질책이 함께 나타난다는 점을 보여 주지 못한다.
D: 작가의 가족사라는, 해석과 무관한 제3의 요소를 끌어온다. 장면이 Jonas에게 어떤 의미인지에 대해서는 아무것도 알려 주지 않는다.
g.explanation_en:
The scholar's claim has two parts that must work together in this scene: (1) the letter comforts Jonas because Walt kept the pact, and (2) it also rebukes him because it forces him to face his own broken promise. Choice B is correct because its note is about the letter scene itself. It calls Walt's trees both a "gift" and "a measure" of Jonas and says he can't feel one without the other, so it covers both parts and links them.
Choice A covers only the comfort. By saying "only warmth," it actually rules out the rebuke, which weakens the claim.
Choice C covers only the rebuke, and it's about a later chapter, not the letter scene. So it can't show comfort and rebuke happening together here.
Choice D brings in a third factor, the author's family history. That says nothing about what the scene means for Jonas.
g.design: 이 해석은 위안과 질책이라는 두 요소를 동시에 요구한다. 정답은 두 요소를 모두 결합했다. 오답은 위안만 반영한 것(A), 질책만 반영한 것(C), 무관한 제3 요소인 작가의 전기를 근거로 든 것(D)이다. 선택지 네 개는 모두 같은 '노트 메모' 문장 틀로 썼다.

c.instruction: 지문에 상관관계나 동시 발생 사실만 제시하고, 이를 근거로 특정 가설(주장)의 인과성을 지지하는지 판단해야 하는 문항을 만들어라. 정답은 인과 방향과 대안 설명 가능성을 함께 고려해 타당하게 지지하는 것이어야 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 '상관을 그대로 인과로 오해', '인과 방향을 반대로 설정', '무관한 제3의 원인을 인과로 제시'로 구성하라.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — At a Louisiana bayou fish camp, aging guide Cletus teaches his reluctant grandson the names of medicinal plants, each lesson a farewell disguised as instruction.

g.passage: In the novel Low Water, the aging fishing guide Cletus poles his skiff along a Louisiana bayou with his reluctant grandson, Remy, naming plants as they pass: "That's yaupon. Boil it when the cough sits deep. That one's elderberry—your grandmama swore by it." Remy rarely answers. Across the novel, these lessons grow longer: early chapters cover one or two plants, while the final chapters cover a dozen or more. Over the same chapters, the narrator describes Cletus as increasingly ill. One literary critic argues that Cletus's growing sense that he is dying is what drives the lengthening lessons. In her reading, each lesson is a farewell disguised as instruction, and the more certain Cletus feels that he is near death, the more he tries to pass on.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the critic's claim about what causes the change in Cletus's lessons?
options: The novel's final chapter contains the longest lesson in the book, and it is also the chapter in which the narrator describes Cletus as weakest.
After each of the longest lessons, the narrator notes that Cletus has to rest for hours and that his breathing is worse than it was before the lesson began.
In one late chapter, a doctor tells Cletus he is recovering, and that day his lesson covers only a single plant, even though the narrator describes the banks as crowded with plants in bloom.
The later chapters are set in late summer, when the narrator notes that more of the bayou's medicinal plants are in flower and that the heavy heat leaves Cletus short of breath.
g.explanation:
비평가는 Cletus가 죽음이 가깝다고 느끼는 감각이 수업을 길게 만드는 '원인'이라고 주장한다. 지문이 보여 주는 것은 수업 길이와 병세가 함께 커진다는 상관관계뿐이다. C는 Cletus가 회복 중이라는 말을 들어 죽음에 대한 확신이 약해지자, 이름을 댈 식물이 많았는데도 수업이 식물 하나로 줄었다는 내용이다. 원인(죽음을 예감하는 정도)만 바뀌었을 때 결과(수업 길이)도 함께 바뀌었고, '식물이 많아서'라는 대안 설명도 배제한다. 따라서 인과 주장을 가장 직접적으로 지지한다.
A: 수업이 가장 긴 장과 병세가 가장 심한 장이 겹친다는 상관을 한 번 더 보여 줄 뿐이다. 인과를 확인하지 못하므로 상관을 인과로 오해한 오답이다.
B: 긴 수업이 Cletus를 더 지치게 하고 병을 악화시킨다는 내용이다. 이는 수업이 병세의 원인이라는 반대 방향의 인과를 시사하므로 오답이다.
D: 늦여름이라는 제3의 요인이 꽃이 핀 식물 수(긴 수업)와 더위로 인한 호흡 곤란(병세)을 함께 설명할 수 있다. 오히려 비평가의 인과 주장을 약화시키므로 오답이다.
g.explanation_en:
The critic claims that Cletus's growing sense that he is dying is what causes his lessons to get longer. The passage only shows a correlation: the lessons get longer as his illness gets worse.

**Why C is correct:** When Cletus is told he is recovering, his sense that death is near weakens, and his lesson shrinks to a single plant. Many plants are in bloom at that moment, so a shortage of plants can't explain the short lesson. Only the proposed cause changed, and the effect changed with it. That makes C the most direct support for the causal claim.

**Why the other options are wrong:**
- **A** just shows the same correlation again: the longest lesson and the weakest Cletus appear in the same chapter. Treating this as proof of cause confuses correlation with causation.
- **B** suggests the lessons themselves wear Cletus out and make him sicker. That reverses the direction of cause.
- **D** offers a third factor, late summer. It could explain both effects: more plants in flower would make the lessons longer, and heavy heat would worsen his breathing. This actually weakens the critic's claim.
g.design: I gave only a correlation (longer lessons and worsening illness) and asked which finding supports a causal claim. The correct answer changes only the cause and also rules out an alternative explanation. Each wrong answer matches one assigned error type: treating correlation as causation, reversing the direction of cause, or offering a third cause.

c.instruction: 지문에 가설(주장)만 제시하고, 그 가설을 뒷받침하려면 어떤 추가 증거나 결과가 있어야 하는지 묻는 문항을 만들어라. 정답은 지문에 없는 가상의 결과이지만 가설의 논리 구조와 정확히 들어맞아야 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 '가설과 무관한 사실', '가설을 반박하는 결과', '이미 지문에 있는 사실을 재진술한 것'으로 구성하라.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — On a Lisbon tram line, rival vendors Mateus and Guida engage in competitive flower-selling until a tourist's photograph reveals them laughing together, complicating their feud.

g.passage: The following text is adapted from a short story. Every morning on the Lisbon tram line 28, flower vendors Mateus and Guida set up their buckets at opposite ends of the same stop, each lowering prices whenever the other did and calling out insults about wilted carnations. One afternoon a tourist shows Guida a photograph taken the day before: in it, Mateus and Guida are bent over the same bucket, laughing. Guida studies the image for a long moment, then hands the phone back without a word. A literary critic argues that the story presents the feud not as genuine hostility but as a shared performance the two vendors maintain because it draws customers to their stop.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the critic's interpretation?
options: Later in the story, the narrator notes that tram line 28 passes through the Alfama district, where many tourists stop to photograph the old buildings.
Later in the story, Mateus quietly moves his buckets to a different tram stop after a tourist pays him for the last of his roses, and he never sees Guida again.
Later in the story, Guida again looks at the tourist's photograph showing her and Mateus laughing over a single bucket of flowers.
Later in the story, once the last tram of the day has passed, Mateus and Guida split their unsold flowers evenly before agreeing on which insults to use the next morning.
g.explanation: 비평가의 주장은 두 요소로 이루어져 있다. (1) 반목은 진짜 적대가 아니라 함께 꾸민 연기이고, (2) 그 연기를 하는 이유는 손님을 끌기 위해서다. D는 손님(트램)이 모두 떠난 뒤 둘이 협력하고 다음 날 할 욕설을 미리 맞춘다는 내용이다. 관객이 있을 때만 싸운다는 점은 연기라는 사실과 그것이 장사를 위한 것임을 함께 보여 주므로 정답이다. A는 관광객과 노선에 관한 배경 정보일 뿐, 반목의 본질과는 관계가 없다. B는 마테우스가 떠나 다시 만나지 않는다는 내용이어서 두 사람이 연기를 함께 유지한다는 해석과 어긋나고, 오히려 주장을 약하게 만든다. C는 지문에 이미 나온 사진 장면을 다시 말한 것이다. 함께 웃은 순간이 한 번 있었다는 것만으로는 반목이 의도된 연기라는 점도, 그 목적이 손님 유치라는 점도 증명되지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The critic's claim has two parts: (1) the feud is a performance the two vendors put on together rather than real hostility, and (2) they keep it up because it brings customers to their stop. D shows them cooperating as soon as the last tram, and with it the audience, is gone. They even agree on the next day's insults ahead of time. That one finding supports both parts: the feud is staged, and it is staged for business. A is background about the route and tourists and says nothing about what the feud really is. B has the vendors splitting up for good, which goes against the idea of a performance they keep up together, so it weakens the claim. C just repeats the photograph scene that is already in the passage. One shared laugh doesn't prove the feud is deliberately staged or that it's meant to attract customers.
g.design: 지문에는 가설만 제시하고, 정답은 가설의 두 요소(연기라는 점, 손님 유치라는 목적)를 모두 충족하는 가상 장면으로 만들었다. 오답은 무관한 사실(A), 가설을 반박하는 결과(B), 지문 재진술(C)로 구성하고, 네 선택지 모두 같은 'Later in the story' 문장 틀로 썼다.

c.instruction: 그래프나 표에 두 개 이상의 변수(또는 텍스트 설명과 그래프 수치)가 함께 제시된 자료를 주고, 두 요소를 동시에 봐야만 결론을 낼 수 있는 질문을 만들어라. 정답은 두 변수를 모두 반영해야 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 '한쪽 변수만 본 결론', '다른 쪽 변수만 본 결론', '자료에 없는 제3의 변수로 결론'을 만든 것으로 구성하라.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — At a Louisiana bayou fish camp, six-year-old Baptiste notices the alligator's nest that adults have overlooked, his discovery carrying weight they cannot yet understand.

g.passage: In the opening scene of a novel set at a Louisiana bayou fish camp, six-year-old Baptiste squats at the edge of the marsh grass while his uncles argue over a tangled trotline. "There's eggs in the mud pile," he says, pointing to a mound of rotting cattails near the boat slip. No one looks up. Baptiste goes on watching the mound, quiet and patient, as the men load their skiff and push off into the brown water. One literary critic argues that the scene sets up a pattern for the whole novel: what matters most in the story is often seen first by Baptiste alone, and the adults understand it only after it has already shaped what happens to them.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the critic's claim?
options: Details that only Baptiste remarks on in the early chapters reappear in the final chapters as the causes of the adults' main reversals, while details the adults discuss early on rarely matter later.
In the early chapters, Baptiste points out far more features of the marsh than any adult character does, and the adults seldom reply to what he says.
The final chapters focus on a series of sudden events, including a flood and a lost boat, that change the adults' way of earning a living for good.
Baptiste's narration uses more Cajun French words and local plant names than the dialogue of any adult in the novel, a contrast that becomes sharper as the book goes on.
g.explanation: 비평가의 주장에는 두 요소가 함께 들어 있다. (1) 중요한 것을 Baptiste 혼자 먼저 본다. (2) 그것이 나중에 어른들의 운명을 좌우하고, 어른들은 그 뒤에야 깨닫는다. A는 두 요소를 동시에 충족한다. Baptiste만 언급한 세부가 마지막 장에서 어른들이 겪는 반전의 원인이 되고, 어른들이 언급한 세부는 대조적으로 별로 중요하지 않다. B는 Baptiste가 더 많이 알아차린다는 관찰 쪽만 다룬다. 그가 본 것이 나중에 중요해지는지는 보여 주지 않는다. C는 결말에서 어른들의 삶이 바뀐다는 결과 쪽만 다룬다. 그 원인이 Baptiste만 본 세부라는 연결이 없다. D는 어휘·방언이라는, 주장에 없는 제3의 변수를 근거로 삼고 있어 주장과 무관하다.
g.explanation_en: The critic's claim combines two parts: (1) Baptiste alone notices what matters first, and (2) those things later shape the adults' fates before the adults understand them. Choice A covers both parts. Details only Baptiste notices end up causing the adults' main reversals, and by contrast, the details the adults discuss don't matter much later. Choice B covers only the noticing part. It shows Baptiste observes more, but not that what he sees turns out to matter. Choice C covers only the outcome part. The adults' lives change, but nothing connects those changes to details Baptiste alone saw. Choice D relies on a third variable the claim never mentions (vocabulary and dialect), so it is irrelevant.
g.design: The claim has two linked variables: who notices a detail and whether it later matters. The correct answer combines both. Of the wrong answers, one uses only the noticing variable, one uses only the outcome variable, and one uses a third variable (dialect).

c.instruction: 지문에 상관관계나 동시 발생 사실만 제시하고, 이를 근거로 특정 가설(주장)의 인과성을 지지하는지 판단해야 하는 문항을 만들어라. 정답은 인과 방향과 대안 설명 가능성을 함께 고려해 타당하게 지지하는 것이어야 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 '상관을 그대로 인과로 오해', '인과 방향을 반대로 설정', '무관한 제3의 원인을 인과로 제시'로 구성하라.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Aboard a 19th-century Mississippi riverboat, gambler Silas adopts an abandoned puppy that gradually transforms the household's cold calculations into unexpected tenderness and risk.

g.passage: In the novel The Low Water Hand, a work of fiction set aboard the Mississippi riverboat Corinna in the 1850s, the cardsharp Silas Venn finds an abandoned puppy shivering behind the cotton bales and, to the crew's surprise, keeps it. In the chapters that follow, the once-calculating Silas begins folding hands he could easily win against desperate passengers, quietly lends money to the boat's stewards, and even risks his own stake to cover a deckhand's debt. One student argues that the puppy is what causes Silas's transformation: caring for a helpless creature, the student claims, wears away the cold arithmetic by which Silas has always lived. Another reader is unconvinced, noting that these same chapters also include the death of Silas's longtime partner, Dutch, and the Corinna's passage through a cholera-stricken stretch of river, events that could themselves explain why Silas changes.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the student's claim?
options: The chapters in which Silas folds the most winning hands are also the chapters in which the puppy is mentioned most often.
When the puppy goes missing ashore for two chapters after Dutch's death, Silas returns to ruthless play, and his generosity resumes only once the puppy is found again.
Silas had already begun lending money to the stewards before the puppy appeared, and one grateful steward is the person who brings him the abandoned animal.
Silas's generosity first appears in the chapter immediately after Dutch's funeral, which takes place in the same week that Silas finds the puppy.
g.explanation:
정답 B: 강아지가 사라지면 Dutch의 죽음과 콜레라 구간 같은 다른 요인이 그대로인데도 Silas가 냉혹하게 돌아가고, 강아지가 돌아오면 너그러움이 다시 나타난다. 원인으로 지목된 요인만 바뀔 때 결과도 함께 바뀌므로 대안 설명을 배제하고 인과를 직접 지지한다.
A: 강아지 언급과 패를 접는 행동이 같은 장에 함께 나온다는 상관관계일 뿐이다. 이를 인과로 보는 것은 오해이고, 다른 사건들의 영향도 배제하지 못한다.
C: 너그러움이 먼저 나타났고, 그 결과로 강아지가 Silas에게 오게 되었으므로 인과 방향이 반대다. 오히려 학생의 주장을 약화한다.
D: 변화를 Dutch의 죽음이라는 제3의 원인과 연결한다. 시기가 겹치는 것은 다른 독자의 대안 설명을 뒷받침할 뿐이다.
g.explanation_en:
Correct answer, B: When the puppy disappears, Silas goes back to ruthless play. Dutch's death and the cholera stretch still apply during that time. When the puppy returns, so does his generosity. Only the proposed cause changes, and the effect changes with it. That rules out the alternatives and directly supports the claim that the puppy causes the change.
A: This only shows that mentions of the puppy and Silas folding hands happen in the same chapters. That's a correlation, and treating it as proof of cause is a mistake. It also can't rule out the other events.
C: This reverses the direction. Silas's generosity came first, and it led to the puppy reaching him. If anything, this weakens the claim.
D: This ties the change to a third cause, Dutch's death. The overlap in timing supports the other reader's alternative explanation, not the student's claim.
g.design: The passage presents only events that happen at the same time and names other possible causes. The correct answer works like a natural experiment: the puppy is removed and then returns while the other factors stay the same. Each wrong answer matches one assigned flaw: correlation treated as cause, reversed direction, or a third cause.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 수식어가 짧은 주어-동사 수 일치, 시제 일관성, 대명사 격/수 일치처럼 한 규칙을 묻는 문제.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — On a Sri Lankan tea estate, widow Amara discovers that the stray leopard killing her livestock once belonged to a boy she loved who disappeared forty years ago.

g.passage: Amara crouched beside the fence of her tea estate, where the leopard had taken another goat during the night. In the mud lay a strip of leather that the animal had torn loose on the wire. The collar, faded and cracked by the hill country rain, ______ the letters that Sunil had burned into it the summer before he vanished, forty years ago.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: still bear
are still bearing
still bears
have still borne
g.explanation: 빈칸에 들어갈 동사의 주어는 단수 명사 "The collar"이며, 쉼표 사이의 수식어 "faded and cracked by the hill country rain"는 주어의 수에 영향을 주지 않는다. 따라서 단수 동사 C "still bears"가 정답이다. A "still bear"는 복수 동사이며, 수식어 속 "rain"이나 의미상 "letters"에 끌려 고르기 쉽다. B "are still bearing"과 D "have still borne"도 복수형 조동사(are, have)를 사용하므로 단수 주어 "collar"와 수가 일치하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of the blank's verb is the singular noun "The collar"; the phrase set off by commas, "faded and cracked by the hill country rain," only describes the collar and doesn't change its number. So you need a singular verb, which makes C, "still bears," correct. A, "still bear," is a plural verb, and you might pick it if you get distracted by "rain" or by "letters." B, "are still bearing," and D, "have still borne," also use plural helping verbs (are, have), so neither agrees with the singular subject "collar."
g.design: 이 문항은 쉬운 단일 규칙 문제로, 짧은 삽입 수식어가 끼어 있을 때의 주어-동사 수 일치만 묻는다. 오답 세 개는 모두 같은 동사 'bear'의 복수형으로 구성했다.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 수식어가 짧은 주어-동사 수 일치, 시제 일관성, 대명사 격/수 일치처럼 한 규칙을 묻는 문제.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — On Cairo rooftops, pigeon keeper Samir travels across the city to deliver a single escaped bird to a girl he once knew, his journey revealing both devotion and farce.

g.passage: Samir crossed half of Cairo with a single gray pigeon tucked inside his shirt. The bird had escaped weeks earlier and somehow flown back to his coop, and now he meant to return it to Laila, the girl who had named it years before. Twice the pigeon wriggled loose on the crowded tram, and twice Samir crawled beneath the seats after it while the passengers laughed. Still, the soft feathers against his chest ______ him a strange courage as he climbed the stairs to her old rooftop.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: gives
has given
is giving
gave
g.explanation: 이 지문은 crossed, wriggled, crawled, laughed, climbed처럼 과거 시제로 서술되므로 빈칸의 동사도 과거형이어야 합니다. 따라서 과거형 gave를 쓴 D가 정답입니다. A는 현재형, B는 현재완료형, C는 현재진행형이라서 모두 이야기의 과거 시제와 맞지 않습니다. 게다가 A, B, C는 단수형이라서 바로 앞의 chest를 주어로 착각하게 만드는 함정이기도 합니다. 실제 주어는 복수 명사 feathers입니다.
g.explanation_en: The passage tells its story in the past tense (crossed, wriggled, crawled, laughed, climbed), so the verb in the blank should also be in the past tense. That makes choice D, "gave," the correct answer. Choice A uses the present tense, choice B uses the present perfect, and choice C uses the present progressive, so none of them fits the past-tense narration. Choices A, B, and C are also singular forms, which might tempt you to treat "chest" as the subject. The real subject is the plural noun "feathers."
g.design: 이 문항은 시제 일관성이라는 한 가지 규칙만 묻습니다. 과거 시제 동사가 여러 개 있어 단서가 분명합니다. 오답은 모두 현재 계열 시제여서 규칙을 알면 바로 배제됩니다.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 수식어가 짧은 주어-동사 수 일치, 시제 일관성, 대명사 격/수 일치처럼 한 규칙을 묻는 문제.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — In a Soviet-era Georgian mountain village, boy Giorgi overhears whispers that the newcomer woman is actually the village elder's forbidden daughter, now returned from exile.

g.passage: Giorgi presses his ear to the cracked door of the bakery, where two women are whispering about the quiet stranger who arrived in the mountain village this spring. The story told by the old shepherds ______ that she is the village elder's forbidden daughter, sent into exile long ago and now secretly returned.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: claims
claim
are claiming
have claimed
g.design: 수식어 "told by the old shepherds"가 단수 주어 story와 동사 사이에 끼어 있다. 오답은 모두 복수 동사형이라 가까운 명사 shepherds에 동사를 맞추게 하는 함정이 된다.
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 "story"이고, "told by the old shepherds"는 주어를 꾸미는 수식어일 뿐입니다. 따라서 동사도 단수형이어야 하므로 A의 "claims"가 정답입니다. B, C, D는 모두 복수 동사형입니다. 이 선택지들은 동사 바로 앞에 있는 복수 명사 "shepherds"에 동사를 잘못 맞춘 것입니다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "story." The phrase "told by the old shepherds" just describes the story, so it doesn't change the subject. Because the subject is singular, the verb has to be singular too, which makes A, "claims," correct. B, C, and D are all plural verb forms. They wrongly match the verb to the nearby plural noun "shepherds" instead of the real subject.

c.instruction: 지문에 두 변수 사이의 이론적 관계(예: A가 클수록 B도 커진다, 정직한 신호일수록 비용이 크다)를 제시하고, 이 이론을 새로운 구체적 집단이나 사례에 적용했을 때 나올 결론을 빈칸으로 묻는다. 정답은 이론이 제시한 방향을 그대로 새 사례에 적용한 것이어야 하며, 오답 3개는 각각 관계의 방향을 반대로 뒤집기, 원인과 결과를 바꾸기, 이론과 무관한 제3의 요인을 결론으로 제시하기의 실제 오개념을 사용해 만든다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — On a Brooklyn tenement stoop in 1910s, rival shopkeepers Dominic and Francesco initially battle over territory until they realize they're both supporting the same orphan secretly.

g.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story set in Brooklyn in 1913. For two years, grocer Dominic and baker Francesco have argued over who owns the stretch of sidewalk between their shops.

Dominic's father had left him one rule about people: the harder a man works to keep a kindness from being seen, the more of himself he has put into it. Dominic trusted it the way he trusted his scale. So he was stunned on the morning he saw Francesco, his rival, slip a warm loaf and a pair of mended boots through the cellar window where Tommaso, the orphan Dominic had been feeding in secret, slept. Later that day, in front of the whole stoop, Francesco loudly called the boy a thief and chased him off, as if to make sure no one would ever link the two of them. Watching, Dominic understood that, by his father's rule, ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: Francesco's gifts to the boy must have mattered very little to him, since he took such care to hide them.
Francesco's gifts to the boy must have cost him far more of himself than Dominic had ever imagined.
Francesco's gifts to the boy must have come to matter to him only because hiding them had become a habit.
Francesco's gifts to the boy must have been driven mainly by his wish to win the quarrel over the sidewalk.
g.explanation:
규칙: 친절을 숨기려 애쓸수록 그 친절에 자신을 더 많이 쏟은 것이다. Francesco는 몰래 선물하고 공개적으로 아이를 꾸짖어 관계를 철저히 숨겼다 → 숨기려는 노력이 매우 큼 → 그만큼 자신을 많이 쏟았다(B).
A: 관계의 방향을 뒤집었다. 숨길수록 덜 중요하다는 결론은 규칙과 정반대다.
C: 원인과 결과를 바꿨다. 규칙에서 숨김은 깊은 헌신을 드러내는 신호이지, 숨기는 습관이 애정을 만들어낸다는 뜻이 아니다.
D: 규칙과 무관한 제3의 요인(보도 다툼)을 결론으로 내세웠다. 게다가 몰래 한 선물로는 다툼에서 이길 수도 없다.
g.explanation_en:
Start with the rule: the harder a man works to hide a kindness, the more of himself he has put into it. Francesco goes to great lengths to hide his: he delivers the gifts in secret, then publicly calls the boy a thief so no one will connect the two of them. Applying the rule in the same direction, his gifts must have cost him a great deal of himself. That's choice B.
A reverses the rule. It claims that more hiding means the gifts mattered less, which is the opposite of what the rule says.
C swaps cause and effect. In the rule, hiding is a sign of deep investment. It doesn't say that a habit of hiding creates the caring.
D brings in an outside factor, the sidewalk rivalry, that the rule never mentions. Also, secret gifts couldn't help Francesco win a public quarrel anyway.
g.design: I gave Dominic an inherited rule linking how hard a kindness is hidden to how much of oneself it costs, then applied it to Francesco's behavior. Each wrong answer uses one of the required misconceptions: reversing the direction, swapping cause and effect, or bringing in an unrelated third factor. All four choices use the same sentence frame.

c.instruction: 짧은 표나 그래프 하나와 이를 설명하는 가설 문장 하나를 함께 제시하고, 두 정보를 결합해야만 답할 수 있는 결론을 빈칸으로 묻는다. 정답은 시각 자료의 특정 수치와 가설 문장을 연결해야 나오고, 오답 3개는 각각 시각 자료만 보고 가설을 무시한 결론, 가설 문장만 보고 시각 자료를 무시한 결론, 시각 자료의 다른 항목을 잘못 짝지은 결론으로 만든다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — On a Lisbon tram line, commuters Helena and Gustavo unknowingly play the same naming game with passengers—she calls them by imagined stories, he by overheard secrets—until they collide.

g.passage:
In Inês Prata's short story "Line 28," two commuters on a Lisbon tram, Helena and Gustavo, privately play the same game: each gives the other passengers names. Helena bases hers on stories she imagines, and Gustavo bases his on secrets he overhears. Neither knows the other is playing until the final scene, when they collide at the tram doors. The table shows how many new names each character makes up at each stop, in the order the stops appear in the story.

| Stop | Names made up by Helena | Names made up by Gustavo |
|---|---|---|
| Estrela | 5 | 3 |
| Graça | 4 | 3 |
| Baixa | 0 | 3 |
| Alfama | 2 | 0 |

A literary critic argues that Prata uses the game to show attention: a character stops making up names for strangers at the exact stop where that character first notices the other player. If the critic is right, the table suggests that ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: Helena noticed Gustavo less than Gustavo noticed her, since she made up more names across the four stops than he did.
Helena and Gustavo first noticed each other at the same moment, when they collided at the tram doors in the final scene.
Helena first noticed Gustavo at Baixa, one stop before Gustavo first noticed her at Alfama.
Gustavo first noticed Helena at Baixa, one stop before Helena first noticed him at Alfama.
g.design: 표의 0값 위치(헬레나는 Baixa, 구스타보는 Alfama)를 비평가의 가설(이름 짓기 중단 = 상대를 처음 알아챔)과 연결해야 정답이 나온다. 오답은 표만 본 결론(총합 비교), 가설과 줄거리만 본 결론(충돌 순간), 인물-정류장을 잘못 짝지은 결론으로 구성했다.
g.explanation:
정답 C: 비평가에 따르면 인물이 이름 짓기를 멈춘 정류장이 상대를 처음 알아챈 지점이다. 표에서 헬레나는 Baixa에서 0개(멈춤), 구스타보는 Alfama에서 0개다. 따라서 헬레나가 Baixa에서 먼저, 구스타보가 그다음 정류장인 Alfama에서 알아챘다.
A(표만 봄): 헬레나 11개, 구스타보 9개라는 총합 비교는 표만으로 나온다. 하지만 가설은 총 개수가 아니라 이름 짓기를 멈춘 시점을 기준으로 삼으므로 근거가 되지 않는다.
B(가설·줄거리만 봄): 마지막 장면의 충돌만 보고 두 사람이 동시에 알아챘다고 본 것이다. 그러나 표에서 두 사람이 멈춘 정류장은 서로 다르다.
D(잘못 짝지음): Baixa의 0은 헬레나의 열에, Alfama의 0은 구스타보의 열에 있다. D는 인물과 정류장을 서로 바꿔 짝지었다.
g.explanation_en:
Correct answer, C: The critic says a character stops making up names at the exact stop where that character first notices the other player. In the table, Helena drops to 0 new names at Baixa, and Gustavo drops to 0 at Alfama, the next stop. So Helena noticed Gustavo first, at Baixa, and Gustavo noticed her one stop later, at Alfama.
A is wrong because it uses only the table. Helena did make up more names in total (11 vs. 9), but the critic's claim is about when a character stops naming people, not about how many names they make up.
B is wrong because it uses only the story's ending and ignores the table. The two characters stop naming people at different stops, so they did not notice each other at the same moment.
D is wrong because it mixes up the columns. The 0 at Baixa belongs to Helena and the 0 at Alfama belongs to Gustavo, not the other way around.

c.instruction: 하나의 결론이나 가설을 먼저 제시한 뒤, 그것을 뒷받침/약화/무관하게 만드는 추가 사실 하나를 골라야 하는 빈칸 문제를 만든다. 정답은 가설의 핵심 조건을 직접 충족하거나 위배하는 사실이어야 하며, 오답 3개는 각각 표면적으로만 관련 있어 보이지만 실제로는 무관한 사실, 가설과 반대 방향으로 작용하는 사실을 지지 사실인 것처럼 제시한 것, 결론과 무관한 배경 정보를 결론 지지처럼 위장한 것으로 만든다.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — In a Bavarian village brass band, musician Florian travels two hours to deliver sheet music for a single rehearsal, the errand masking his real need to hear the timpani player's solo.

g.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Florian, a clarinetist, has driven two hours to a Bavarian village to deliver sheet music to its brass band.

Florian set the folder on the conductor's stand and murmured something about the new arrangements. He did not take off his coat. When the rehearsal began, he lingered by the door of the hall, his eyes on the back row where Lena bent over the timpani, tightening a head with small, patient turns of the key.

Some readers interpret this scene as showing that the delivery is only a pretext and that Florian's true reason for making the long trip is to hear Lena play her solo. This interpretation would be most strongly supported if the story later revealed that ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the timpani, as the loudest instrument in the band, was always placed in the back row of the hall so that it would not drown out the woodwinds.
Florian left the hall within minutes of handing over the folder, well before the band reached the passage in which the timpani played alone.
the village band had performed the same arrangements at its harvest festival every autumn for more than a century without any changes to the program.
the conductor had received copies of the scores by mail a week earlier, yet Florian stayed until the timpani solo ended and then drove home without speaking to anyone.
g.explanation:
정답 D: 이 해석은 두 가지 조건이 함께 성립해야 한다. (1) 악보 배달은 꼭 필요한 일이 아니었다(구실), (2) 진짜 목적은 솔로를 듣는 것이었다. D는 악보가 이미 우편으로 도착해 있었다는 사실로 (1)을 충족하고, 솔로가 끝나자마자 떠났다는 사실로 (2)를 충족한다.
A: 팀파니가 뒷줄에 놓인다는 내용은 지문 속 'back row'와 겉으로만 연결될 뿐, Florian의 동기와는 관계가 없다.
B: 솔로를 듣기도 전에 떠났다면 오히려 해석을 약화한다. 떠나는 행동 자체가 수상해 보여 지지하는 사실처럼 보이게 만든 함정이다.
C: 악단의 역사는 배경 정보일 뿐이라 배달이 구실이었는지를 판단하는 데 아무 근거가 되지 않는다.
g.explanation_en:
Answer D: For this interpretation to hold, two things must both be true. (1) The delivery was not actually necessary, so it was only a pretext. (2) Florian's real goal was to hear the solo. D meets condition (1) because the scores had already arrived by mail. It meets condition (2) because Florian stayed exactly until the solo ended and then left.
A: The fact that the timpani sits in the back row only echoes the passage's mention of "the back row." It tells you nothing about why Florian came.
B: If Florian left before the solo, that would actually weaken the interpretation. This choice is a trap because leaving early can look suspicious, which makes it seem like support.
C: The band's history is just background. It gives you no evidence about whether the delivery was a pretext.
g.design: 해석(가설)을 먼저 제시하고 빈칸에 지지 사실을 고르게 했다. 정답은 가설의 두 핵심 조건(배달이 불필요했음, 솔로가 진짜 목적이었음)을 직접 충족한다. 오답은 각각 겉으로만 관련된 사실, 지지처럼 보이지만 실제로는 가설을 약화하는 사실, 결론과 무관한 배경 정보로 구성했다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 관계가 어휘 단서 없이 두 문장의 논리(양보 후 반전, 일반화 후 구체화, 원인 vs 결과 방향)에서 도출되는 문제. 오답 전환어도 일부 관계는 말이 된다.
c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Byzantine manuscript illumination and lapis lazuli pigment sourcing from Afghan mines in medieval scriptoriums

g.passage: Byzantine illuminators prized ultramarine, a brilliant blue made from lapis lazuli, above nearly every other pigment. The stone came almost entirely from mines in the Badakhshan region of present-day Afghanistan, and it reached Constantinople only after a journey of thousands of kilometers through the hands of many traders. Grinding the stone into usable pigment was also slow work, since impurities had to be washed out repeatedly. ______ scribes in many monastic workshops reserved ultramarine for the robes of Christ and the Virgin, painting less sacred figures with cheaper blues such as azurite.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Consequently,
Nevertheless,
Similarly,
For instance,

It then says Wagner solved the first problem with fan-shaped seating. The sentence after the blank, about hiding the orchestra, solves the second problem in the same spirit, so B, which adds a parallel measure, is correct. A makes hiding the orchestra sound like a result of the seating plan, but the two choices weren't cause and effect; they were separate steps toward the same goal. D treats the hidden orchestra as an example of the seating arrangement, but it's actually a separate design feature, not one instance of the seating.

g.passage: For decades, scholars studying khipu—the knotted cords the Inca used to keep records—focused almost entirely on the knots, because researchers in the early twentieth century had shown that knot types and positions encoded numbers in a base-ten system. Anthropologist Sabine Hyland has argued that this emphasis left much of each khipu unexamined. Working with two khipu kept by a village in the Peruvian Andes, she found that local elders described the colors and fiber types of the cords, such as whether a strand was made of llama or alpaca wool, as carrying distinct meanings, including the names of family lineages. Hyland does not dispute that many khipu served as numerical accounts for tribute and labor; rather, she suggests that the features long treated as decoration may have recorded categories of information that numbers alone could not express.
g.question: According to the text, what does Hyland propose about khipu?
options: Khipu were mainly used to record family lineages rather than tribute and labor, so the numerical reading developed by earlier researchers was mistaken.
The base-ten knot system found in early studies was used only in certain Andean villages, which is why it cannot explain most surviving khipu.
Physical traits of the cords that scholars had treated as ornamental may have stored kinds of information in addition to the numbers recorded by the knots.
Village elders' descriptions of khipu reveal that color and fiber were chosen mainly to make the numerical knots easier to read.
g.explanation: Hyland은 매듭의 수치 해석을 부정하지 않으면서, 장식으로 여겨지던 색과 섬유가 숫자로 표현할 수 없는 정보(예: 가계 이름)를 기록했을 수 있다고 본다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 가계 이름이라는 세부는 맞지만, 지문은 그녀가 수치 해석을 반박하지 않는다고 분명히 밝히므로 틀리다. B는 십진법 매듭이라는 세부를 쓰지만, 그것이 일부 마을에만 국한된다는 내용은 지문에 없다. D는 장로들의 설명을 언급하지만, 색과 섬유가 숫자를 읽기 위한 보조가 아니라 별개의 의미를 지녔다고 했으므로 틀리다.
g.explanation_en: Hyland accepts that the knots recorded numbers, but she argues that cord color and fiber, long seen as decoration, may have recorded other information, such as lineage names. That makes C the answer. A picks up the detail about lineages, but the text says plainly that Hyland does not dispute the numerical reading. B mentions the base-ten knot system, but nothing in the text says that system was limited to certain villages. D refers to the elders' descriptions, but they said color and fiber carried meanings of their own, not that these features helped people read the knots.
g.design: Each wrong choice uses a real detail from the text (lineages, base-ten knots, elders) but adds a claim the text doesn't support or that contradicts it. c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Ukiyo-e woodblock printing technique and Hokusai's compositional perspective influencing European Impressionist artists

g.passage: When Japanese woodblock prints began reaching Paris in the 1860s, many European collectors prized them chiefly as exotic curiosities, admiring their bright, flat colors. Yet the painters who studied them most closely, among them Edgar Degas and Claude Monet, were drawn less to the prints' novelty than to the way artists such as Katsushika Hokusai organized space. In Hokusai's series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, the famous peak is often pushed to the margins or shrunk to a small triangle behind a towering wave or a cooper's barrel, while foreground objects are abruptly cropped by the edge of the sheet. Such choices broke with the European convention, inherited from Renaissance linear perspective, of placing the principal subject at the center of a balanced, deep scene. Degas's off-center dancers, sliced by the frame, and Monet's high horizons suggest that these painters found in ukiyo-e not a style to imitate but a model for rethinking how a picture could be composed.

options: European collectors valued Japanese prints mainly for their vivid, flat colors, which Impressionist painters then copied directly in their own canvases.
Hokusai's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji was the first Japanese print series to reach Paris, where it replaced Renaissance perspective in French art schools.
Degas and Monet rejected Japanese prints as mere curiosities and instead returned to the centered, balanced scenes of Renaissance painting.
Certain European painters drew on Japanese prints less for their surface appeal than for an unconventional approach to arranging a scene, which reshaped their own compositions.

The black cloak removed at the start represented the grave and worldly attachment; the right palm, turned upward, received divine grace, while the left, turned downward, passed that grace to the earth. Even the counterclockwise rotation around the heart was understood as aligning the body with the circling of planets and of pilgrims around the Kaaba. Novices trained for a thousand and one days before joining the ceremony, and much of that training concerned not balance but the inner recitation that was meant to accompany every turn.

Although the Mevlevi ceremony began as a form of prayer, Ottoman-era dervishes came to value it mainly for the physical skill it displayed.

g.passage: For centuries, violinists and collectors have claimed that instruments made by Antonio Stradivari in the early 1700s possess a tone no modern maker can match, and many researchers have tried to explain this supposed superiority through the materials he used. One popular hypothesis holds that the spruce for his soundboards grew during a period of unusually cold European winters, producing dense, evenly spaced growth rings that would vibrate with exceptional clarity. Yet when acoustician Claudia Fritz and her colleagues asked experienced soloists to play both old Italian violins and high-quality new ones while wearing modified goggles that hid each instrument's identity, the players could not reliably tell the two groups apart, and several actually preferred a new violin. These results suggest that the celebrated sound of a Stradivarius may owe less to its wood than to the expectations listeners and players bring to it.

options: Although cold winters produced the dense spruce Stradivari used, modern makers have found ways to treat new wood so that it vibrates with the same clarity.
Although Stradivari's violins are widely thought to sound uniquely good because of their materials, a blind test indicates that their reputation may rest largely on players' beliefs.
Although soloists prefer the sound of old Italian violins, a blind test indicates that they cannot explain which features of the wood create that sound.
Although researchers have studied Stradivari's spruce for centuries, a blind test indicates that the density of growth rings matters more than the age of the wood.
g.explanation: 지문은 스트라디바리우스의 음색이 목재 때문에 뛰어나다는 통념을 소개한 뒤, 눈을 가린 실험에서 연주자들이 옛 악기와 새 악기를 구별하지 못했다는 결과를 들어 명성이 기대감에서 비롯될 수 있다고 결론짓는다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 추운 겨울 가설을 사실로 확정하고 현대의 목재 처리라는 언급되지 않은 내용을 덧붙인다. C는 연주자들이 옛 악기를 선호한다고 하지만, 실험에서는 구별하지 못했고 일부는 오히려 새 악기를 선호했다. D는 지문에서 다루지 않은 나이테 밀도와 목재 나이의 비교를 결론으로 삼는다.

A treats the cold-winter hypothesis as proven fact and adds a claim about modern wood treatment that the text never makes. C says soloists prefer old violins, but in the test they couldn't tell the two groups apart, and some actually preferred new ones. D concludes something about ring density versus the age of the wood, and the text never makes that comparison.

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Tuvan throat singing (khöömei) lets a single performer produce two or more pitches at once: a steady low drone and a whistle-like melody of overtones above it.
- Singers create the melody by reshaping the mouth and tongue to amplify selected overtones of the drone.
- In a 2019 study, acoustician Lena Ortiz recorded 24 Tuvan singers and found that the overtone melodies of herders tended, on average, to fall within the frequency range of steppe wind and flowing water.
- Ortiz cautioned that her sample was small and that the pattern suggests, but does not establish, that the style developed by imitating natural sounds.
- A separate 2021 survey by ethnomusicologist Bat-Erdene Dorj found that the number of formal throat-singing schools in Tuva and western Mongolia more than doubled between 2000 and 2020.
g.question: The student wants to present Ortiz's finding about the origins of the vocal style with an appropriate degree of confidence. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Ortiz's recordings of 24 singers indicate that herders' overtone melodies tend to fall within the frequency range of wind and water, possibly reflecting an origin in imitating natural sounds.
Ortiz's recordings of 24 singers show that herders' overtone melodies match the frequencies of wind and water, proving that the style originated as an imitation of natural sounds.
Ortiz's recordings of 24 singers suggest that throat singers may perhaps be able to produce more than one pitch at a time, possibly reflecting an origin in imitating natural sounds.
Ortiz's recordings of 24 singers indicate that throat-singing schools tend to have grown in number, possibly reflecting renewed interest in imitating natural sounds.
g.explanation:
정답 A: Ortiz의 결과는 '평균적으로 경향이 있다'는 통계적 결과이며 기원은 '시사할 뿐 입증하지 않는다'고 했으므로, 'tend to'와 'possibly'로 잠정성을 유지한 A가 적절하다.
B: 경향을 'match', 'proving'으로 확정적으로 과장했다. Ortiz 본인의 경고와 어긋난다.
C: 한 가수가 여러 음을 동시에 낸다는 것은 노트에서 확정적 사실인데 'may perhaps'로 불필요하게 축소했고, Ortiz의 연구 내용도 아니다.
D: 잠정적 어조는 맞지만 학교 수 증가는 Dorj의 2021 조사 내용으로, Ortiz의 연구와 혼동했다.
g.explanation_en:
A is correct. Ortiz's result is a statistical tendency ("tended, on average"), and she said it suggests, but does not establish, a natural-sound origin. By using "tend to" and "possibly," A keeps that tentative tone.
B is wrong because it overstates the finding. Words like "match" and "proving" contradict Ortiz's own caution.
C is wrong because the notes state as a fact that singers produce two or more pitches at once. C needlessly hedges that fact with "may perhaps," and producing multiple pitches isn't Ortiz's finding anyway.
D is wrong even though its tentative tone fits. The growth in schools comes from Dorj's 2021 survey, so D confuses it with Ortiz's study.
g.design: I paired a definite fact (singers produce several pitches at once) with Ortiz's tentative statistical finding. Each wrong choice makes one of the three required errors: overstating the finding, hedging a fact, or keeping the right tone but swapping in the other study. All four choices use the same sentence frame, and the question avoids the key words of the correct answer.

It covers both manuscripts and says what different part of medieval life each one shows: the St. Gallen scribe's complaint shows the conditions copyists worked under, and the Luttrell Psalter's scenes show the farming tools of fourteenth-century England. - Zeugma is a literary device in which a single word, usually a verb, governs two or more other words in a sentence.

- The device thus pairs grammatical parallelism with semantic tension: the structure looks balanced, but the meanings pull apart.
- John Donne (1572–1631) was an English poet associated with the "metaphysical" style, known for its elaborate conceits.
- Some readers trace a zeugma-like doubling in Donne's verse, where one word joins physical and spiritual meanings at once.

Zeugma is one of many literary devices, and poets from many periods, including John Donne, who wrote in the metaphysical style, have used it and other devices in their verse.
Zeugma's sentences appear grammatically balanced, since one word governs several others, yet that word shifts meaning with each, so the meanings strain against the structure.
John Donne, a metaphysical poet known for elaborate conceits, later became dean of St. Paul's Cathedral in London, a post he held from 1621 until his death.
