g.passage: At many Zen temples in Kyoto, gardeners rake the white gravel into fresh wave patterns each morning. The patterns, which wind and rain soon blur, are never meant to last; the gardeners accept their fading rather than protecting them. ______ the moss beds beside the gravel are allowed to spread unevenly over decades, and the gardeners make no attempt to fix them into a final shape.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: As a result,
By contrast,
For example,
Likewise,
g.explanation:
두 번째 문장의 핵심은 바로 앞 명사 'wind and rain'이 아니라 문장 앞부분의 주체인 정원사들의 태도이다. 정원사들은 무늬가 사라지는 것을 받아들이고 보존하려 하지 않는다. 세 번째 문장도 같은 정원사들이 이끼를 최종 형태로 고정하려 하지 않는다고 말하므로, 같은 태도(무상함의 수용)가 다른 대상에도 나타난다는 유사 관계이다. 따라서 'Likewise,'가 정답이다.
A(As a result,): 인접 명사인 '바람과 비'를 원인으로 보고, 이끼가 퍼지는 것이 그 결과라고 오해한 선택지다. 그러나 지문은 이끼가 퍼지는 원인을 바람과 비라고 말하지 않는다.
B(By contrast,): '매일 아침'과 '수십 년'이라는 표면적 시간 차이만 보면 문법적으로 자연스럽다. 그러나 두 문장이 실제로 가리키는 정원사의 태도는 같으므로 대조가 아니다.
C(For example,): 첫 문장의 '갈퀴질'을 일반 진술로 보고 이끼를 그 사례로 삼은 선택지다. 그러나 이끼를 방치하는 일은 갈퀴질의 예가 아니라 같은 태도가 별개로 나타난 경우다.
g.explanation_en:
The key point of the second sentence is not the nearby nouns "wind and rain." It is the attitude of the sentence's earlier subject, the gardeners. They accept that the patterns fade and do not try to protect them. The third sentence says these same gardeners make no attempt to fix the moss into a final shape. That is the same acceptance of impermanence, now applied to something else, so the relationship is similarity: "Likewise," is correct.
A ("As a result,") treats the adjacent "wind and rain" as the cause of the moss spreading, but the text never makes that causal link.
B ("By contrast,") sounds natural if you focus only on "each morning" versus "decades." However, the gardeners' attitude, which is what both sentences describe, is the same, so there is no contrast.
C ("For example,") treats the raking in the first sentence as a general claim with the moss as one instance of it. But leaving the moss alone is not an example of raking. It is a separate, parallel case of the same attitude.
g.design: The relative clause "which wind and rain soon blur" puts tempting nouns right next to the blank. However, the real referent for the comparison is the gardeners' accepting attitude from earlier in the sentence. The wrong answers come from three errors: reading the adjacent noun as the cause, contrasting surface time scales, and treating the moss as an example of the raking in the first sentence.

c.instruction: 학술적 소재(연구, 인물, 현상 등)에 대한 3~4문장의 짧은 지문을 만들고, 마지막 문장은 앞 내용 중 특정 목적이나 강조점(예: 결과가 아니라 의도, 수치가 아니라 방향성)에 부합하는 전환어를 골라야 정답이 되게 하라. 오답 3개는 (1)앞 문장의 결과·부수적 사실과는 맞지만 지문의 핵심 강조점과는 어긋나는 전환어, (2)방향은 맞지만 논리관계(원인/대조 등)가 틀린 전환어, (3)전혀 다른 내용과 연결되는 전환어로 구성하라. 지문에 여러 개의 정보가 나열되되 그중 한 가지만 답과 직결되도록 설계한다.
c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Sonnet form structural constraints and volta thematic turn in Shakespeare's romantic love poetry sequences

g.passage: Shakespeare's sonnets follow a strict pattern: fourteen lines of iambic pentameter, three quatrains, and a closing rhymed couplet. Many readers assume that this rigid frame left little room for surprise, and in a purely statistical sense they are right, since the volta, or thematic turn, falls at or near the couplet in the large majority of the poems. Literary scholar Helen Vendler argues, however, that Shakespeare used this predictable placement to set up expectations that the couplet could then complicate rather than simply resolve. ______ in Sonnet 130 the couplet does not reverse the speaker's unflattering catalog of his mistress's features so much as reframe it, insisting that honest description is itself a form of devotion.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: For instance,
As a result,
Granted,
Similarly,
g.explanation:
지문에는 정보가 여러 개 나열된다. 소네트의 형식, 볼타가 대부분 2행 연구 근처에 온다는 통계적 사실, 그리고 Vendler의 주장(예측 가능한 위치를 이용해 결말에서 해결하기보다 복잡하게 만든다)이다. 마지막 문장은 Sonnet 130의 2행 연구가 앞의 묘사를 뒤집지 않고 재구성한다는 내용이므로, 이 중 Vendler의 주장을 보여 주는 구체적 사례에 해당한다. 따라서 예시를 나타내는 'For instance,'가 정답이다.
B(As a result,): 앞에서 말한 '볼타의 위치가 예측 가능하다'는 사실과는 표면적으로 이어지는 것처럼 보인다. 그러나 Sonnet 130의 사례는 그 주장에서 생긴 결과가 아니라 주장을 보여 주는 예이므로, 인과 관계로 연결하는 것은 맞지 않는다.
C(Granted,): 앞 내용에 대한 양보나 예외를 이끄는 표현이다. 그러나 마지막 문장은 Vendler의 주장을 뒷받침하므로 논리 관계가 다르다.
D(Similarly,): 비슷한 다른 현상을 덧붙일 때 쓰는 표현이다. 그러나 마지막 문장은 별개의 유사 사례가 아니라 바로 앞 주장 자체의 구체적인 예이므로 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en:
The text lists several pieces of information: the sonnet's form, the statistical fact that the volta usually falls at or near the couplet, and Vendler's claim that Shakespeare used this predictable placement to complicate the ending rather than resolve it. The last sentence describes Sonnet 130's couplet reframing, rather than reversing, what came before. That is a concrete illustration of Vendler's claim, so "For instance," is correct.
B ("As a result,") seems to fit the fact about the volta's predictable placement. However, the Sonnet 130 case doesn't result from Vendler's claim. It illustrates the claim, so a cause-and-effect link is wrong.
C ("Granted,") introduces a concession or exception. The final sentence supports Vendler's claim instead of conceding a point against it.
D ("Similarly,") adds a separate, parallel case. The final sentence is not a parallel case. It is a direct example of the claim just made.
g.design: 지문에는 형식, 통계, 학자의 주장이라는 세 가지 정보를 나열했고, 그중 학자의 주장(해결이 아니라 복잡화)만 마지막 문장과 예시 관계로 직결되도록 설계했다. 오답은 (1) 부수적 사실에 끌리는 결과 전환어(As a result), (2) 논리 관계가 틀린 양보 전환어(Granted), (3) 별개의 유사 사례로 연결하는 전환어(Similarly)로 구성했다.

c.instruction: 서로 배치되거나 상반된 것처럼 보이는 두 가지 관찰(실험 결과, 사례, 수치)이 제시된 짧은 지문을 만들고, 두 관찰을 종합했을 때 나오는 결론을 마지막 문장에서 올바른 전환어로 연결해야 정답이 되게 하라. 오답 3개는 (1)한쪽 관찰만 반영한 전환어, (2)두 관찰이 상반된다는 점만 보고 단순 대조로 처리한 전환어, (3)종합 결론과 무관한 전환어로 구성하라. 계산이나 복잡한 수치 없이 정성적 진술만으로 구성한다.
c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Chinese landscape painting negative space and atmospheric perspective in literati scholar artist tradition

g.passage: Many landscapes by Chinese literati painters of the Song and Yuan dynasties leave more than half of the silk or paper untouched, and some early Western collectors read these bare areas as signs of hasty, casual execution. Yet the scholar-artists' own treatises describe deciding where the blank zones would fall before making a single brushstroke, and infrared imaging of several scrolls reveals faint preliminary lines marking the edges of areas meant to stay empty. ______ the unpainted expanses seem to have been planned as carefully as the mountains themselves, serving as mist and distance rather than simple absence.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Admittedly,
Taken together,
Nevertheless,
For instance,
g.explanation: 정답 B. 지문은 상충하는 듯한 두 관찰을 제시한다. 그림 대부분이 비어 있다는 점(대충 그린 것처럼 보임)과, 논저와 적외선 밑선이 그 빈 공간이 미리 계획되었음을 보여 준다는 점이다. 마지막 문장은 두 관찰을 종합해 '빈 공간은 의도적으로 구성된 요소'라는 결론을 내리므로, 종합을 나타내는 'Taken together,'가 알맞다. A 'Admittedly,'는 첫 번째 관찰(성의 없이 그렸다는 해석)에 대한 양보만 반영한다. 그런데 마지막 문장은 그 해석을 인정하는 것이 아니라 뒤집는다. C 'Nevertheless,'는 두 관찰이 상반된다는 점만 보고 단순 대조로 처리한 것이다. 바로 앞 문장(계획의 증거)과 결론은 같은 방향이므로 대조가 성립하지 않는다. D 'For instance,'는 예시를 도입하는 말이다. 마지막 문장은 앞 내용의 예가 아니라 결론이므로 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The answer is B. The passage gives two observations that seem to clash. First, the paintings are mostly blank, which some collectors took as a sign of careless work. Second, the painters' treatises and the infrared underdrawings show that those blank areas were planned. The last sentence combines both observations into one conclusion: the emptiness was deliberately composed. "Taken together," signals exactly that kind of synthesis. A ("Admittedly,") only concedes the first observation, the "hasty execution" reading, but the final sentence overturns that reading instead of granting it. C ("Nevertheless,") treats the two observations as a simple contrast. However, the sentence right before the blank (the evidence of planning) points the same way as the conclusion, so there is nothing to contrast. D ("For instance,") introduces an example, but the final sentence is a conclusion, not an example of what came before.
g.design: Two observations seem to conflict: blank space looks careless, but there is evidence it was planned. Each wrong answer matches a distractor type from the recipe: a concession to one observation only, a simple contrast, and an unrelated example signal. The correct transition, which signals synthesis, does not repeat any key word from the question.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).

c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Bauhaus Constructivism graphic design and geometric abstraction influencing twentieth-century commercial visual communication

g.passage: In the 1920s, designers at Germany's Bauhaus school rejected ornate lettering and decorative borders in favor of bold sans-serif type, primary colors, and simple geometric shapes. Their approach soon spread beyond the classroom ______ by midcentury, advertisers and corporations around the world were using clean grids and abstract forms to make posters and logos that could be understood at a glance.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: classroom,
classroom
classroom;
classroom, and,
g.design: 빈칸 앞뒤가 모두 명백한 독립절이라 세미콜론 하나의 규칙만으로 풀리며, 오답은 쉼표 스플라이스·무부호 연결·접속사 뒤 잘못된 쉼표라는 전형적 오개념이다.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Their approach soon spread beyond the classroom"과 빈칸 뒤 "by midcentury, advertisers ... were using ..."은 각각 완전한 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표 하나만으로 두 독립절을 잇는 쉼표 스플라이스이다. B는 부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다. D는 등위접속사 "and" 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣어 문장의 흐름을 끊는다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank, "Their approach soon spread beyond the classroom," and the text after it, "by midcentury, advertisers ... were using ...," are both complete independent clauses. You can join two independent clauses with a semicolon, so C is correct. A is a comma splice, because a comma alone can't join two independent clauses. B is a run-on sentence, since it joins the clauses with no punctuation at all. D puts an unnecessary comma after the coordinating conjunction "and," which breaks up the sentence for no reason.

g.passage: Traditional Georgian folk songs are usually sung in three distinct vocal parts. The top voice often carries the main melody ______ the lowest voice provides a steady drone that supports the other two singers.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: melody,
melody
melody, and,
melody, while
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "The top voice often carries the main melody"와 뒤 "the lowest voice provides a steady drone..."는 각각 독립절이다. D는 쉼표와 접속사 while로 두 절을 올바르게 연결한다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. B는 아무 부호나 접속사 없이 두 절을 붙여 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. C는 and 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표가 들어가 접속사와 다음 절의 주어를 부당하게 분리한다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("The top voice often carries the main melody") and the text after it ("the lowest voice provides a steady drone...") are both independent clauses. Choice D correctly joins them with a comma and the conjunction "while." Choice A uses only a comma, which creates a comma splice. Choice B joins the two clauses with no punctuation or conjunction at all, which makes a run-on sentence. Choice C adds an extra comma after "and," which wrongly separates the conjunction from the subject of the clause that follows.
g.design: 독립절 두 개 사이의 연결 방식만 묻는 단일 규칙 문항으로, 쉼표 스플라이스·run-on·접속사 뒤 불필요한 쉼표라는 전형적 오개념을 오답으로 배치했다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 관계가 어휘 단서 없이 두 문장의 논리(양보 후 반전, 일반화 후 구체화, 원인 vs 결과 방향)에서 도출되는 문제. 오답 전환어도 일부 관계는 말이 된다.
c.seed: social science research — Milgram obedience experiments 1961-1962 and participant willingness to administer electric shocks to learners

g.passage: In the baseline version of Stanley Milgram's 1961–1962 obedience experiments, about 65 percent of participants continued to the maximum 450-volt level when an experimenter instructed them to keep shocking a "learner" (who was actually an actor receiving no real shocks). Popular retellings often cite this figure as evidence that ordinary people obey authority almost unconditionally. ______ Milgram's own variations of the study suggested a more conditional picture: when the experimenter gave instructions by telephone rather than in the room, full compliance dropped to roughly 21 percent.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: However,
Moreover,
For example,
Consequently,
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 대중적 해석(사람들은 거의 무조건 복종한다)을 소개하고, 뒷문장은 실험자가 전화로 지시하자 복종률이 21%로 떨어졌다는 Milgram 자신의 결과로 그 해석에 반박한다. 따라서 대조를 나타내는 A가 정답이다. B는 앞의 주장에 같은 방향의 근거를 덧붙일 때 쓰지만, 뒷문장은 그 주장을 약화한다. C는 뒷문장이 구체적 실험 결과를 담고 있어 그럴듯해 보이지만, 무조건적 복종의 예가 아니라 반례이다. D는 대중적 해석 때문에 변형 실험 결과가 나온 것이 아니므로 인과 관계가 성립하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The previous sentence presents a popular interpretation: ordinary people obey authority almost unconditionally. The next sentence challenges it with Milgram's own data, which show that compliance dropped to about 21 percent when the experimenter gave orders by phone. Since the text moves from a claim to evidence against it, the contrast transition in A is correct. B would add support in the same direction, but this sentence weakens the claim. C may seem to fit because the sentence gives a specific result, but that result is a counterexample to unconditional obedience, not an example of it. D is wrong because the popular interpretation did not cause the variation's results.
g.design: 여기에는 어휘 단서 없이 '대중적 해석 → 이를 약화하는 반례'라는 논리가 있다. 훑어 읽는 학생은 구체적 수치만 보고 C나 B를 고르도록 유도했다.

- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 관계가 어휘 단서 없이 두 문장의 논리(양보 후 반전, 일반화 후 구체화, 원인 vs 결과 방향)에서 도출되는 문제. 오답 전환어도 일부 관계는 말이 된다.
c.seed: social science research — Implicit Association Test racial bias measurement and automatic stereotype activation in response times

g.passage: The Implicit Association Test (IAT) asks participants to sort faces and words as quickly as possible, and in one version Black and White faces share response keys with positive or negative words. Across thousands of participants, responses are reliably slower when the key pairings run counter to widespread racial stereotypes. Many researchers see this pattern as evidence that stereotypes can be activated automatically, before a person consciously reflects. ______ when the same individual takes the test twice a few weeks apart, the two scores often differ substantially, which limits how much any single score can reveal about that particular person.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Specifically,
Even so,
In addition,
As a result,
g.explanation: 앞 문장들은 집단 수준에서 IAT 결과가 안정적이며 자동적 고정관념 활성화의 증거로 여겨진다고 말하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 개인 점수가 반복 측정에서 크게 달라 개인에 대해서는 알려주는 것이 제한적이라고 한다. 따라서 앞의 강점을 인정한 뒤 한계를 제시하는 양보·반전 관계이므로 B가 정답이다. A는 뒤 문장을 앞 내용의 구체적 세부로 보지만, 개인 점수의 불안정성은 집단 결과를 구체화하는 것이 아니라 그 결과와 긴장 관계에 있다. C는 둘 다 IAT에 대한 사실이라는 점에서 그럴듯하지만, 뒤 문장은 같은 방향의 증거를 덧붙이는 것이 아니라 반대 방향의 한계를 말한다. D는 집단 결과가 안정적이라는 사실이 개인 점수의 불안정성을 낳는 원인이 아니므로 인과 관계가 성립하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The earlier sentences say the IAT produces a reliable pattern across large groups and is treated as evidence that stereotypes activate automatically. The sentence after the blank says an individual's scores can change a lot from one test to the next, which limits what a single score tells us. That is a concession followed by a contrast, so B is correct. A doesn't work because the unstable individual scores don't give a specific detail of the group finding. Instead, they push against it. C is tempting because both sentences describe the IAT, but the second one points out a limitation rather than adding support in the same direction. D is wrong because reliable group results don't cause individual scores to be unstable, so there's no cause-and-effect link.
g.design: There is no word like "but" before the blank, so students have to notice that the passage moves from reliable group results to unreliable individual scores. The wrong answers each fit part of the passage: A treats the second idea as a detail of the first, C treats it as more of the same, and D treats it as a result. c.seed: social science research — Pygmalion effect classroom study 1968 and teacher expectancy influencing student intellectual performance gains

g.passage: In 1968, psychologist Robert Rosenthal and school principal Lenore Jacobson reported the results of a study at an elementary school in California. At the start of the school year, students took a test that the researchers described to teachers as a measure of who was likely to "bloom" intellectually. The researchers then told teachers which students had scored as likely bloomers. In fact, those students had been chosen at random and did not differ from their classmates. When the students were tested again months later, the randomly labeled children, especially those in the earliest grades, showed larger gains in IQ scores than their peers did. Rosenthal and Jacobson concluded that the teachers' beliefs about the students had somehow translated into real differences in how much the students improved.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: A 1968 study found that a test given at the start of the school year could accurately identify which young students would make the largest intellectual gains.
A 1968 study found that students in the earliest grades improved more on IQ tests over a school year than did students in later grades.
A 1968 study found that what teachers were led to believe about certain students appeared to shape how much those students' test performance improved.
A 1968 study found that teachers at an elementary school were often unable to tell which of their students had scored highest on an intelligence test.
g.explanation: 지문의 핵심은 무작위로 뽑힌 학생들이 '성장할 학생'으로 소개되었고, 그 학생들이 더 큰 IQ 향상을 보였으며, 연구자들이 이를 교사의 믿음이 낳은 결과로 결론지었다는 것이다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 시험이 실제로 성장을 예측했다고 하지만, 지문에서 학생들은 무작위로 선정되었으므로 시험이 예측한 것이 아니다. B는 낮은 학년이 더 큰 향상을 보였다는 세부 내용을 왜곡한 것인데, 지문은 학년 간 비교가 아니라 무작위로 지목된 학생과 또래의 비교를 다루며, 낮은 학년 언급은 부수적인 세부일 뿐이다. D는 교사가 고득점자를 알아보지 못했다고 하지만, 지문은 그런 능력을 다루지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The text explains that randomly chosen students were presented to teachers as likely "bloomers," that those students later showed bigger IQ gains, and that the researchers credited the teachers' beliefs for this. That makes C correct. A says the test really predicted growth, but the students were picked at random, so the test predicted nothing. B distorts a detail: the text compares the labeled students with their peers, not younger grades with older grades, and the mention of the earliest grades is only a side detail. D claims teachers couldn't tell who scored highest, but the text never looks at that ability.

c.seed: social science research — Ainsworth Strange Situation procedure infant attachment classification and secure versus insecure bonding patterns

g.passage: In the 1970s, developmental psychologist Mary Ainsworth introduced the Strange Situation, a laboratory procedure in which a toddler is briefly separated from and then reunited with a caregiver while researchers observe the child's behavior. Early studies using the procedure focused heavily on how much a child cried when the caregiver left, but Ainsworth argued that this measure revealed little on its own: some securely attached children cried intensely, while some insecurely attached children showed no distress at all. What distinguished the groups, she found, was the reunion. Securely attached children typically sought contact with the returning caregiver and were soon calmed enough to resume playing, whereas insecurely attached children either avoided the caregiver or clung to the caregiver while remaining agitated.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Ainsworth found that children who cried intensely during separation were usually the ones who later avoided their caregivers during the reunion.
Ainsworth found that the Strange Situation was more reliable when researchers combined measures of crying with observations of how long children played alone.
Ainsworth found that securely attached children tended to show less distress during separation than insecurely attached children did.
Ainsworth found that the way a child responded when the caregiver came back was more revealing of attachment type than the child's reaction to the caregiver's departure.
g.explanation: 지문은 분리 시 울음의 정도만으로는 애착 유형을 알 수 없고, 양육자가 돌아왔을 때의 반응(재회)이 안정·불안정 애착을 구분한다는 것이 핵심이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 강하게 우는 아이가 재회 시 회피한다는 연관을 지문에서 언급하지 않으며, 오히려 안정 애착 아이도 강하게 울 수 있다고 했다. B는 울음 측정과 혼자 노는 시간의 결합을 제안하지만 지문은 재회 행동을 강조할 뿐이다. C는 안정 애착 아이가 분리 시 덜 괴로워한다고 하지만, 지문은 분리 시 괴로움이 두 집단을 구분하지 못한다고 말한다.
g.explanation_en: The text argues that how much a child cries at separation says little by itself, and that the reunion is what distinguishes secure from insecure attachment, so D is correct. A claims that children who cry intensely later avoid the caregiver, but the text never makes that link and even notes that securely attached children may cry intensely. B suggests combining crying with time spent playing alone, but the text emphasizes reunion behavior, not that combination. C says securely attached children show less separation distress, yet the text states that separation distress does not reliably separate the groups.
g.design: To get this right, you have to connect two ideas in the passage: that crying doesn't tell the groups apart and that the reunion does. Choices A and C use details from the passage but reverse or twist the claim about crying, and B sounds believable but is about method.

c.seed: social science research — Festinger cognitive dissonance theory and attitude change following counterattitudinal behavior commitment

g.passage:
In a 1959 experiment, psychologists Leon Festinger and James Carlsmith had participants spend an hour on deliberately tedious tasks, such as turning pegs on a board. Afterward, each participant was asked to tell the next person waiting that the tasks had been enjoyable. Some participants were paid one dollar for telling this lie; others were paid twenty dollars. When later asked privately how much they had actually liked the tasks, those paid one dollar rated them as noticeably more enjoyable than did those paid twenty dollars.

Festinger argued that the result reflects a drive to reduce the discomfort of holding beliefs that conflict with one's own actions. Twenty dollars was a sufficient reason for lying, so those participants felt little tension. One dollar was not, so participants who had already committed to the false statement could ease the inconsistency only by revising their private opinion of the tasks to bring it closer to what they had said.
g.question: According to the text, why did the participants who received one dollar report more favorable views of the tasks?
options: Lacking an adequate outside justification for their statement, they shifted their own evaluation to match it.
Lacking an adequate reward for their effort, they exaggerated their evaluation to please the researchers.
Lacking a strong financial incentive, they paid closer attention to the tasks and discovered they enjoyed them.
Lacking the tension felt by better-paid participants, they had no reason to criticize the tasks afterward.
g.design: 정답을 '정당화 부족→태도 조정'으로 바꿔 말해 표면 일치를 피했고, 오답은 같은 'Lacking ~' 틀에 금전 보상·긴장 등 지문 요소를 부분적으로 섞되 인과를 왜곡했다.
g.explanation: 지문에 따르면 1달러는 거짓말을 할 충분한 이유가 되지 못했고, 그래서 참가자들은 불일치를 줄이려고 과제에 대한 사적인 평가를 자신이 한 말 쪽으로 바꾸었다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 '보상 부족'이라는 요소를 쓰지만, 지문의 평가는 비공개로 이루어졌고 연구자를 기쁘게 하려 했다는 언급도 없다. C는 주의를 더 기울여 즐거움을 발견했다고 하지만, 지문은 과제가 일부러 지루하게 만들어졌다고 하며 이런 설명을 내놓지 않는다. D는 관계를 거꾸로 말한다. 긴장을 느낀 쪽은 1달러를 받은 참가자들이고, 20달러를 받은 참가자들은 긴장을 거의 느끼지 않았다.
g.explanation_en: The text says one dollar wasn't enough of a reason to lie. To ease the inconsistency, those participants revised their private opinion of the tasks to bring it closer to what they had said, so A is correct. B uses the idea of a small reward, but the ratings were given privately, and the text never says anyone was trying to please the researchers. C claims the participants paid closer attention and discovered they liked the tasks, but the text describes the tasks as deliberately tedious and never offers this explanation. D gets the relationship backward: it was the one-dollar participants who felt tension, while the twenty-dollar participants felt little.

c.seed: social science research — Asch conformity experiments 1951 and peer pressure influence on perceptual judgment accuracy

g.passage: In 1951, psychologist Solomon Asch asked college students to match the length of a line to one of three comparison lines, a task so easy that people working alone almost never erred. In the experimental sessions, however, each real participant sat among several confederates who had been instructed to give the same wrong answer on certain trials. Across those trials, participants went along with the incorrect majority about a third of the time. Asch's later variations complicated the popular reading of this result as proof that people readily abandon the evidence of their own eyes. When even one confederate broke from the group and gave the correct answer, conformity dropped sharply, and when participants could write their answers privately rather than announce them aloud, errors also fell. Most participants, moreover, resisted the majority on most trials.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Asch's experiments showed that people working alone make frequent errors on simple perceptual tasks unless a group helps them reach the correct answer.

Asch's experiments revealed real pressure to conform, but his variations suggest that this pressure depends heavily on social conditions rather than showing that people easily distrust their own perceptions.
Asch's experiments demonstrated that people usually abandon accurate perceptions whenever a unanimous majority contradicts them in public.
Asch's experiments indicated that participants conformed mainly because the line-matching task was too difficult to judge with confidence.
g.explanation: 지문은 약 3분의 1의 동조라는 결과를 제시한 뒤, 반대자 한 명이나 비공개 응답 같은 조건에서 동조가 줄었고 대부분의 참가자가 대부분의 시행에서 저항했다는 점을 들어 '사람들은 쉽게 자기 눈을 버린다'는 통념을 복잡하게 만든다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 혼자 할 때 거의 틀리지 않았다는 진술과 반대된다. C는 공개 상황의 만장일치가 동조를 높인다는 부분적 근거가 있지만, '대개' 포기한다는 말은 3분의 1 비율 및 다수의 저항과 맞지 않는다. D는 과제가 매우 쉬웠다는 진술과 모순된다.
g.explanation_en: The text reports that participants conformed about a third of the time, then uses Asch's variations (one dissenter, private answers) and the fact that most participants resisted on most trials to complicate the idea that people readily abandon their own perceptions, so B is correct. A contradicts the statement that people working alone almost never erred. C draws on the real point that public, unanimous majorities increased conformity, but saying people "usually" give in conflicts with the one-third rate and the widespread resistance. D contradicts the text's description of the task as very easy.
g.design: 정답은 결과와 이를 제한하는 후속 변형 실험을 연결해야 도출되며, C는 앞부분만 훑은 독자를 노린 부분 정답형, A·D는 세부 오독형으로 구성했다.

g.passage: In 1973, psychologist David Rosenhan published a study in which eight mentally healthy volunteers sought admission to psychiatric hospitals by claiming to hear voices. Once admitted, they stopped reporting any symptoms and behaved normally, yet staff kept them for an average of nineteen days, and nearly all were discharged with a diagnosis of schizophrenia "in remission." Rosenhan argued that the hospital setting itself shaped how staff read behavior: one pseudopatient's habit of taking notes, for instance, was recorded in his chart as "engaging in writing behavior." __Notably, several actual patients on the wards voiced suspicions that the volunteers were journalists or researchers rather than people who were ill.__ For Rosenhan, this contrast suggested that the difficulty lay less in the volunteers' behavior than in the expectations that came with an institutional label.

It provides an observation that helps support the claim that staff judgments were driven by the label rather than by the volunteers' conduct.
It raises a doubt about whether the volunteers successfully kept up their pretense after being admitted to the hospitals.

g.passage: The Sapir-Whorf hypothesis, in its strongest form, held that the language a person speaks determines the categories through which that person can perceive the world. Most linguists have since abandoned this claim, but a weaker version, that language can nudge perception, has found experimental support. In a 2007 study, Jonathan Winawer and colleagues tested Russian speakers, whose language obligatorily distinguishes lighter blue (goluboy) from darker blue (siniy), and English speakers, who use the single word "blue." Russian speakers were faster at telling apart two shades that fell on opposite sides of the goluboy/siniy boundary than two shades from the same category; English speakers showed no such advantage. __Yet when Russian participants simultaneously performed a task that occupied verbal memory, such as silently rehearsing a string of digits, their advantage at the category boundary disappeared.__ The researchers concluded that language shapes color discrimination not by permanently rewiring perception but by being actively recruited while perceptual judgments are made.

It presents a result indicating that English speakers would gain the same advantage if they were taught the Russian color terms.

g.passage: Linguist Noam Chomsky argued that children could not learn language from experience alone, because the speech they hear is fragmentary, full of errors, and never contains examples of many sentence types they nonetheless come to understand. g.passage: In 1962, linguist William Labov wanted to know whether New Yorkers' pronunciation of "r" after vowels, as in "fourth floor," varied with social class. Rather than recruit volunteers, who might speak carefully once they knew they were being studied, he visited three Manhattan department stores that served customers of different income levels: Saks Fifth Avenue, Macy's, and S. Klein. He asked employees where a certain item could be found, already knowing that the answer would be "the fourth floor," and then pretended not to hear so they would repeat it. __Because the clerks believed they were simply helping a customer, the speech Labov recorded reflected how they ordinarily talked rather than how they thought they ought to talk.__ The results showed a clear pattern: "r" was pronounced most often at Saks and least often at Klein, and it became more frequent in the careful, repeated answers.

g.passage: In the late 1970s and early 1980s, Nicaragua opened its first schools for deaf children in Managua. The students arrived using only simple home signs, gestures each had invented with family members, and teachers tried to instruct them in lip-reading Spanish. On buses and in schoolyards, however, the children began combining their gestures into a shared pidgin-like system. Researchers who later studied the community noticed something unexpected. __Younger children who entered the schools after this shared system already existed did not simply copy it; they regularized its grammar, adding consistent ways to mark who did what to whom and to break motions into ordered parts.__ This pattern suggested to linguists that children do more than learn a language from older speakers: they can also impose structure on rough input, turning an improvised code into a full language through a process much like creolization.

g.passage:

Drawing on Pierre Bourdieu's concept of cultural capital, many sociologists argue that schools reward familiarity with elite tastes—classical music, canonical literature, museum visits—that children from privileged homes acquire informally. Because teachers read this ease as natural talent, the argument goes, schools convert inherited class advantage into academic merit and thereby reproduce social stratification.

Erving Goffman's dramaturgical model holds that people manage impressions on a "front stage," where an audience is present, and relax on a "backstage," where they drop their performances. By contending that the waiter's kitchen conduct is less revealing than his behavior toward diners, which reflects his true character
By contending that the waiter's kitchen conduct shows that the distinction between front stage and backstage cannot be observed in workplaces

g.passage: Psychologist Lev Vygotsky argued that a child's development is best described not only by what the child can do alone but also by what the child can do with guidance from a more skilled partner; the gap between these two levels he called the zone of proximal development. Researchers testing this idea studied two groups of eight-year-olds who scored identically on a solo puzzle-solving test. When an adult offered brief hints, children in the first group solved puzzles far harder than those on the solo test, while children in the second group improved only slightly. Since the two groups' independent performance was the same, a researcher relying solely on the solo test would ______

options: Champollion's notebooks show that he matched the cartouche of Ptolemy on the stone to its Greek equivalent and assigned sound values to its signs more accurately than Young had.

Champollion's notebooks show that his first successful readings came when he applied sound values from foreign royal names to cartouches of native pharaohs such as Ramesses, which the Greek text of the stone did not name.
Champollion's notebooks show that he relied heavily on the Greek section of the stone, cross-checking nearly every hieroglyphic passage against its translation before proposing a reading.
Champollion's notebooks show that he studied Coptic, a late form of the Egyptian language, for years before 1822, which helped him guess how many hieroglyphic words were pronounced.
g.explanation: 역사학자들의 주장은 두 가지다. 샹폴리옹이 표음 기호가 외국 이름을 넘어 이집트 고유의 표기에도 쓰였다고 본 것이 돌파구였고, 그 돌파구는 이중 언어 텍스트만으로 이루어진 것이 아니라는 것이다. B는 외국 이름에서 얻은 음가를 람세스 같은 이집트 고유 파라오 이름에 적용해 성공했으며, 그 이름이 그리스어 대역문에 없었음을 보여 주므로 두 요소를 모두 직접 뒷받침한다. A는 여전히 외국 이름인 프톨레마이오스에만 머물러 영의 접근을 더 정교하게 다듬은 것에 불과하다. C는 오히려 그리스어 대역문에 의존했음을 보여 주어 주장을 약화시킨다. D의 콥트어 학습은 그럴듯한 배경이지만, 표음 기호가 고유 단어에 쓰였다는 통찰 자체를 보여 주지는 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The historians make two claims. First, Champollion's breakthrough was seeing that phonetic signs appeared in native Egyptian writing, not only in foreign names. Second, this insight did the work, not the bilingual text alone. B supports both: he took sound values from foreign names, applied them to native pharaohs' names such as Ramesses, and succeeded even though the Greek text did not name those rulers. A stays within the foreign name Ptolemy, so it only shows a sharper version of Young's approach. C shows heavy reliance on the Greek translation, which actually weakens the argument. D is a plausible piece of background, but studying Coptic does not show the specific insight that phonetic signs were used for native words.
g.design: To reach the answer, students must link two parts of the claim: phonetic signs in native writing, and independence from the Greek text. Choice A tempts careless readers with phonetic success that is still limited to a foreign name, and choice D offers a related linguistic skill that does not demonstrate the insight.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: history and civics — South African apartheid system 1948-1994 and legalized racial segregation enforcing separate development doctrine

g.passage:
Text 1
Some historians describe South Africa's apartheid system, which lasted from 1948 to 1994, mainly as a set of laws about where people could live. In this view, the Group Areas Act and similar laws on housing were the true core of apartheid.

Text 2
Housing laws were only one part of apartheid. The government also separated schools, hospitals, beaches, and jobs, and it controlled who could marry whom. Under the idea of "separate development," racial segregation reached into almost every area of daily life, not just where people lived.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the historians' view described in Text 1?
options: By agreeing that housing laws were the true core of apartheid and that other laws mattered little
By arguing that apartheid's housing laws were rarely enforced and had little effect on daily life
By claiming that the view is too narrow because apartheid's segregation extended well beyond housing
By suggesting that apartheid ended much earlier than 1994 once housing laws were changed
g.explanation: Text 1은 아파르트헤이트를 주로 주거에 관한 법으로 설명하지만, Text 2는 주거법이 '일부'에 불과하고 학교·병원·직업·결혼 등 생활 거의 전반에 분리가 미쳤다고 말한다. 따라서 Text 2의 저자는 그 견해가 너무 좁다고 반응할 것이므로 C가 정답이다. A는 Text 2가 주거법만이 핵심이라는 주장을 부정하므로 틀렸다. B는 Text 2가 주거법이 효과가 없었다고 말하지 않으므로 틀렸다. D는 종료 시점에 대한 언급이 Text 2에 없으므로 틀렸다.
g.explanation_en: Text 1 describes apartheid mainly as a set of housing laws, but Text 2 says housing laws were "only one part" and that segregation reached schools, hospitals, jobs, and marriage. So the author of Text 2 would say the Text 1 view is too narrow, which makes C correct. A is wrong because Text 2 rejects the idea that housing alone was the core. B is wrong because Text 2 never says housing laws had little effect. D is wrong because Text 2 says nothing about when apartheid ended.
g.design: Text 2의 'only one part ... not just where people lived'라는 직접 단서 하나로 '범위가 너무 좁다'는 반응을 고르는 쉬운 문항이다. 오답은 같은 'By ...' 문장 틀을 쓰며 전형적인 오개념(동의, 효과 부정, 무관한 시기 주장)으로 구성했다.

- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: history and civics — Printing press proliferation sixteenth-century Europe and religious reformation enabled by mass-produced vernacular Bible distribution

g.passage:
Text 1
Many historians argue that the printing press made the Protestant Reformation possible. Because printers could quickly produce thousands of Bibles in German and other everyday languages, ordinary people could read scripture for themselves, and this direct access led them to question church authority.

Text 2
Printed Bibles were important, but they were also expensive, and most sixteenth-century Europeans could not read. Many people learned about new religious ideas mainly by hearing sermons, songs, and conversations in town squares. Printing helped spread reform, but much of the spreading happened through spoken words rather than private reading.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the claim in Text 1 about how ordinary people encountered scripture?
options: By agreeing that most ordinary people read printed Bibles on their own and that printing alone explains the Reformation
By arguing that the printing press played no role at all in spreading new religious ideas
By claiming that printed Bibles were cheap enough for nearly every household to own
By pointing out that many people could not read or afford Bibles, so they often learned reform ideas by listening instead
g.explanation: Text 1은 평범한 사람들이 인쇄된 성경을 직접 읽었다고 주장하지만, Text 2는 성경이 비쌌고 대부분이 글을 읽지 못해 설교·노래·대화로 사상을 접했다고 말한다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 Text 2가 개인적 독서를 부정하므로 틀렸다. B는 Text 2가 인쇄가 개혁 확산에 도움이 되었다고 인정하므로 지나치다. C는 Text 2가 성경이 비쌌다고 한 내용과 반대된다.
g.explanation_en: Text 1 says ordinary people read printed Bibles for themselves, but Text 2 notes that Bibles were expensive and most people couldn't read, so they heard reform ideas through sermons, songs, and conversations. That makes D the answer. A is wrong because Text 2 questions the idea that private reading was the main route. B goes too far, since Text 2 admits that printing helped spread reform. C contradicts Text 2's statement that Bibles were expensive.
g.design: Easy: Text 2 directly qualifies Text 1's one claim (literacy/cost → oral spread). The distractors are common errors: agreeing completely, rejecting printing completely, and reversing a detail.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 삽입구·동격·긴 수식어 뒤에서 절 경계(콜론/대시/세미콜론/쉼표+등위접속사)를 판단하거나, 필수/비필수 수식어 쉼표를 가리는 문제. 선택지는 문장부호/접속 조합 4개.
c.seed: economics and business — Containerization shipping standard and twenty-foot equivalent unit adoption revolutionizing global maritime trade logistics efficiency

g.passage: In 1956, trucking entrepreneur Malcom McLean loaded fifty-eight steel boxes onto a converted tanker in Newark, New Jersey. A decade later, shippers had agreed on a common box size—the twenty-foot equivalent unit, or TEU______ ports worldwide began rebuilding their docks around cranes built to lift that standard box, cutting loading costs dramatically.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: ; soon,
, soon
—soon,
, and soon,
g.explanation: 대시 뒤 'the twenty-foot equivalent unit, or TEU'는 'a common box size'를 설명하는 동격어로 문장 끝까지 이어지므로, 빈칸은 두 독립절('shippers had agreed...'와 'ports worldwide began...')의 경계이다. A는 세미콜론으로 두 독립절을 올바르게 연결한다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. C는 두 번째 대시를 써서 동격어가 문장 중간에 삽입된 것처럼 만드는데, 대시 쌍 안의 내용을 빼면 'agreed on a common box size soon, ports...'가 되어 여전히 두 절이 접속어 없이 이어진다. D는 쉼표+and가 그럴듯해 보이지만, 대시로 시작된 동격어 뒤에서 쉼표를 쓰면 문장부호가 짝이 맞지 않고, 대시 뒤 동격어 다음에 오는 쉼표+등위접속사 구조는 문장을 어색하게 만든다.
g.explanation_en: The phrase after the dash, "the twenty-foot equivalent unit, or TEU," is an appositive that renames "a common box size." That means the blank marks the boundary between two independent clauses: "shippers had agreed..." and "ports worldwide began...." Choice A correctly joins those two clauses with a semicolon. Choice B joins them with only a comma, which is a comma splice. Choice C adds a second dash, which turns the appositive into an interruption. If you remove that interruption, though, the two clauses are still joined by nothing at all. Choice D may look acceptable because of the comma plus "and," but a phrase opened with a dash can't be closed with a comma, so the punctuation doesn't match.
g.design: The appositive after the dash and the long modifier make the clause boundary harder to see. Choices B, C, and D are each partly reasonable (a comma, a matching dash pair, comma + and), so students have to compare them against the punctuation rules to rule them out.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 삽입구·동격·긴 수식어 뒤에서 절 경계(콜론/대시/세미콜론/쉼표+등위접속사)를 판단하거나, 필수/비필수 수식어 쉼표를 가리는 문제. 선택지는 문장부호/접속 조합 4개.
c.seed: economics and business — Dual labor market segmentation hypothesis and wage gap persistence between primary secondary employment sectors

g.passage: Proposed by economists Peter Doeringer and Michael Piore in 1971, the dual labor market hypothesis divides employment into two sectors: a primary sector offering stable jobs, internal promotion ladders, and rising wages, and a secondary sector marked by high turnover and few routes upward. Crucially, the theory holds that workers in the secondary sector cannot easily move into the primary ______ experience in low-wage, short-term jobs is often read by primary-sector employers as a sign of instability rather than as evidence of skill.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: sector, their
sector: their
sector their
sector, because of their
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "workers ... cannot easily move into the primary sector"와 뒤 "their experience ... is often read ..."는 각각 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이며, 뒤 절은 앞 절의 이유를 설명한다. 따라서 콜론으로 연결한 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. C는 아무 부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문이다. D는 "because of"가 전치사구를 만들어 "their experience"를 목적어로 삼으므로 뒤의 동사 "is"가 주어를 잃어 문법적으로 성립하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("workers ... cannot easily move into the primary sector") and the text after it ("their experience ... is often read ...") are both independent clauses, and the second one explains the first. A colon correctly joins them, so B is the answer. A uses only a comma to join two independent clauses, which creates a comma splice. C puts the clauses together with no punctuation at all, which makes it a run-on sentence. D turns "their experience" into the object of the preposition "because of," so the verb "is" is left with no subject and the sentence is ungrammatical.
g.design: 빈칸 앞에 긴 수식어가 있어 문장 끝을 어디서 끊을지 판단해야 하고, 뒤의 절도 긴 수식어 때문에 독립절이라는 점이 잘 드러나지 않습니다. D는 이유를 나타내는 의미는 맞아 그럴듯해 보이지만, 주어와 동사의 짝을 확인해야 걸러낼 수 있습니다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: economics and business — Retail markdown optimization algorithms and dynamic price adjustment timing maximizing inventory turnover profit margins

g.passage: Retailers once cut prices on seasonal stock according to fixed calendars, marking down every item by the same percentage on the same date. Markdown optimization software instead tracks how quickly each product is selling at each store and recommends discounts only where sales lag. Analysts at one apparel chain found that the software's recommendations were notably ______: rather than slashing prices early across the board, it often held prices steady on fast-moving items for weeks and applied deep cuts to a narrow set of slow sellers, preserving margins while still clearing inventory before the season ended.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: aggressive
uniform
selective
delayed
g.explanation: 지문은 소프트웨어가 전면적인 가격 인하 대신 잘 팔리는 품목은 가격을 유지하고, 소수의 부진 품목에만 큰 할인을 적용했다고 설명한다. 따라서 대상을 골라서 적용한다는 뜻의 C 'selective'가 가장 정확하다. A는 '큰 할인(deep cuts)'만 보면 그럴듯하지만, 소프트웨어가 대부분의 품목에서는 오히려 가격을 유지했으므로 전체적인 성격을 나타내지 못한다. B는 모든 품목을 똑같이 인하하던 기존 달력 방식을 묘사하는 말이므로 지문과 정반대이다. D는 몇 주간 가격을 유지했다는 부분과 일부 맞지만, 부진 품목에는 할인이 적용되었으므로 핵심인 '품목별 차별화'를 담지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: The passage explains that the software didn't cut prices everywhere: it kept prices steady on fast-moving items and applied deep cuts only to a narrow set of slow sellers. That's a description of choosing targets carefully, so C, "selective," is the most precise fit. A might look tempting because of the "deep cuts," but for most items the software actually held prices steady, so "aggressive" doesn't describe its overall behavior. B describes the old fixed-calendar approach, where every item got the same markdown, so it's the opposite of what the passage says. D matches the part about holding prices for weeks, but slow sellers did get discounts, so "delayed" misses the main point that the software treated each product differently.
g.design: A와 D는 지문의 일부 정보(deep cuts, held steady for weeks)에 부분적으로 들어맞아서, 두 정보를 연결해서 읽어야만 배제할 수 있다. B는 지문 앞부분의 기존 방식과 연결되는 함정이다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: economics and business — Agricultural commodity futures markets and hedging strategy adoption by smallholder farmers managing price volatility

g.passage: Economists have long assumed that smallholder farmers would welcome futures contracts, since locking in a sale price months before harvest protects against sudden market slumps. Yet surveys of maize growers in Kenya and Zambia found that adoption remained low even where contracts were cheap and easy to access. The researchers concluded that the farmers' reluctance was ______: many had seen neighbors commit to a fixed price only to watch market prices climb sharply at harvest, and they reasonably judged that giving up such gains could cost them more than an occasional slump.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: unprecedented
inflexible
temporary
well-founded
g.explanation: 콜론 뒤 내용은 농민들이 실제 이웃의 경험을 근거로 합리적으로(reasonably) 판단했다는 것이므로, 망설임이 '근거가 충분한' 것이었다는 D가 정답이다. A는 '전례 없는'이라는 뜻이지만, 지문은 이 망설임이 새로운지가 아니라 왜 생겼는지를 설명하므로 맞지 않는다. B '완고한'은 낮은 채택률이 계속된 점과는 얼핏 맞지만, 비합리적인 고집을 암시하므로 '합리적 판단'이라는 문맥과 어긋난다. C '일시적인'은 연구자들이 망설임이 사라질 것이라고 봤다는 근거가 지문에 없다.
g.explanation_en: The text after the colon explains that the farmers based their decision on what actually happened to their neighbors and "reasonably judged" the risk, so their reluctance was justified. That makes D the correct answer. A ("unprecedented") doesn't fit because the passage explains why the reluctance exists, not whether it's new. B ("inflexible") might seem to match the continued low adoption, but it suggests stubbornness that isn't rational, which goes against the idea of a reasonable judgment. C ("temporary") has no support, since nothing in the passage says the researchers expected the reluctance to fade.
g.design: To get this right, students have to connect the colon's explanation with the word "reasonably." Choice B fits the low adoption rate and C fits the survey context, so a quick skim could lead to either, and each has to be ruled out by checking it against the passage.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: economics and business — Venture capital syndication networks and geographic clustering of startup funding concentration in technology hubs

g.passage: Venture capital firms rarely fund promising startups alone; instead, they form syndicates, sharing both the risk and the due diligence with trusted partners. Economist Olav Sorenson and colleagues have argued that because these partnerships depend on frequent face-to-face contact and long-standing personal ties, syndication networks tend to ______ funding in a few technology hubs rather than spreading it evenly: investors favor deals near partners they already know, so capital keeps flowing to the same regions year after year.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: entrench
diversify
accelerate
regulate
g.explanation: 이 글은 신디케이트 네트워크가 자금을 고르게 퍼뜨리지 않고, 해마다 같은 지역에 자금이 계속 흘러들게 만든다고 설명한다. 따라서 소수의 허브에 자금을 고착·집중시킨다는 뜻의 A(entrench)가 가장 정확하다. B(diversify)는 위험 분산이라는 신디케이트의 특징과 연결되어 그럴듯해 보이지만, '고르게 퍼뜨리는 것이 아니라(rather than spreading it evenly)'는 표현과 정면으로 충돌한다. C(accelerate)는 자금 흐름이 늘어난다는 느낌은 주지만, 글의 핵심인 '같은 장소에 머무르는 지속성'은 담지 못한다. D(regulate)는 공식적인 통제를 뜻하므로, 개인적 유대에서 생겨나는 비공식적 패턴과 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The text says syndication networks keep capital flowing to the same few regions year after year instead of spreading it evenly, so you need a word meaning "firmly lock in place." That makes A (entrench) the most precise choice. B (diversify) is tempting because syndicates do share risk, but it directly contradicts "rather than spreading it evenly." C (accelerate) hints that funding grows, but it misses the key idea that funding stays in the same locations over time. D (regulate) means formal control, which doesn't fit a pattern that comes from informal personal ties.
g.design: 빈칸 앞의 '위험 공유'는 diversify를, 뒤의 '자금이 계속 흐른다'는 accelerate를 떠올리게 한다. 그래서 정답을 고르려면 'rather than spreading evenly'와 'same regions year after year'를 함께 연결해 읽어야 한다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: economics and business — Labor union density decline and wage inequality correlation in post-industrial manufacturing regions since 1980

g.passage: Economists studying former manufacturing hubs in the American Midwest have long noted that union membership and wage inequality moved in opposite directions after 1980. Economist Mara Delgado cautions, however, that this pattern alone does not show that falling unionization caused inequality to rise. Plant closures and automation, she argues, may have independently weakened unions and widened pay gaps, so the link between the two trends could simply ______ their shared exposure to these broader forces rather than any direct effect of one on the other.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: counteract
reflect
accelerate
obscure
g.explanation: Delgado는 공장 폐쇄와 자동화라는 공통 원인이 두 추세를 각각 만들었을 수 있으므로, 둘 사이의 연관성은 그 공통 노출을 '반영할' 뿐이라고 주장한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 공통 원인이 연관성을 만든다는 논리와 반대로 상쇄를 뜻한다. C는 외부 요인이 추세를 강화했다는 인상과 맞아 보이지만, 연관성이 공통 노출을 '가속한다'는 말은 논리가 맞지 않는다. D는 인과가 가려진다는 경고 분위기와 닮았지만, 연관성은 공통 원인을 가리는 것이 아니라 오히려 그것에서 생겨난 결과이다.
g.explanation_en: Delgado argues that plant closures and automation may have produced both trends independently, so the correlation between them could simply mirror, or reflect, that shared exposure. That makes B correct. A means to offset, which contradicts the idea that the common forces create the link. C fits the general sense that outside forces intensified the trends, but it makes no sense to say the correlation speeds up the shared exposure. D matches the cautionary tone about hidden causes, but in Delgado's view the correlation comes from the shared forces rather than hiding them.
g.design: 허위 상관(공통 원인) 논리를 이해해야 정답이 나온다. obscure와 accelerate는 경고하는 어조와 외부 요인이라는 표면적 단서에 이끌리는 함정이다.

c.instruction: 지문에 두 변수 사이의 이론적 관계(예: A가 클수록 B도 커진다, 정직한 신호일수록 비용이 크다)를 제시하고, 이 이론을 새로운 구체적 집단이나 사례에 적용했을 때 나올 결론을 빈칸으로 묻는다. 정답은 이론이 제시한 방향을 그대로 새 사례에 적용한 것이어야 하며, 오답 3개는 각각 관계의 방향을 반대로 뒤집기, 원인과 결과를 바꾸기, 이론과 무관한 제3의 요인을 결론으로 제시하기의 실제 오개념을 사용해 만든다.
c.seed: economics and business — Real estate appraisal bias and algorithmic valuation models reproducing racial discrimination in mortgage lending

g.passage: Automated valuation models (AVMs) estimate a home's price by learning from records of past sales and past appraisals. Economists studying these tools argue that an AVM inherits whatever distortions exist in its training data: the more heavily a neighborhood's historical appraisals were marked down for reasons unrelated to the condition or features of its homes, the further the model's current estimates for that neighborhood will fall below what the homes would sell for in an unbiased market. Researchers examined two neighborhoods with nearly identical housing stock. In the first, a predominantly Black area, mid-century appraisers routinely discounted homes because of residents' race, while in the second, a predominantly white area, no such discounting occurred. If the economists' argument is correct, then an AVM trained on both neighborhoods' records should ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: produce estimates for the first neighborhood that sit closer to unbiased market prices than its estimates for the second neighborhood do, since the first neighborhood's records contain more variation.
cause appraisers in the first neighborhood to discount homes more heavily in the future, since the model's low figures would become the source of earlier markdowns.
undervalue homes in the first neighborhood by a larger margin than it undervalues comparable homes in the second neighborhood.
value homes in the second neighborhood less accurately than those in the first, since the second neighborhood's housing stock is likely to be newer and harder to compare.
g.explanation:
정답 C: 이론은 '과거 감정평가의 부당한 할인이 클수록 현재 AVM 추정치가 공정 시장가보다 더 낮다'는 정방향 관계다. 첫 번째 동네는 인종 때문에 체계적 할인을 받았고 두 번째는 받지 않았으므로, 모델은 첫 번째 동네를 더 크게 저평가해야 한다.
A(방향 역전): 왜곡이 많은 동네가 오히려 공정가에 더 가깝다고 하여 관계를 뒤집었다. '변동이 많다'는 근거도 이론과 무관하다.
B(인과 역전): 이론은 과거 평가 → 모델 추정치 방향인데, 이 선택지는 모델의 수치가 과거의 할인을 만들어 낸 원인이라고 하여 원인과 결과를 바꾼다.
D(제3 요인): 주택 연식·비교 가능성이라는 이론 밖의 요인을 끌어들이며, 지문은 두 동네의 주택이 거의 같다고 했다.
g.explanation_en:
Correct answer, C: The theory gives a direct relationship. The more heavily a neighborhood's past appraisals were marked down for reasons unrelated to its homes, the further below unbiased market prices the AVM's current estimates will fall. The first neighborhood's homes were discounted because of residents' race, and the second neighborhood's homes were not. So the model should undervalue the first neighborhood by a larger margin.
A reverses the direction of the relationship. It claims the neighborhood with more biased records gets estimates closer to fair value. Its reason, more variation in the data, also has nothing to do with the theory.
B swaps cause and effect. In the theory, past appraisals shape the model's estimates. This choice instead treats the model's figures as the source of the earlier markdowns.
D brings in an outside factor, the age of the homes and how easy they are to compare. The theory doesn't mention this, and the passage says the two neighborhoods have nearly identical housing stock.
g.design: I stated a direct relationship (more historical appraisal bias leads to a bigger gap between current AVM estimates and fair market prices) and asked students to apply it to two contrasting neighborhoods. Each wrong answer uses a different misconception: reversing the direction (A), swapping cause and effect (B), or citing a factor outside the theory (D).

c.instruction: 짧은 표나 그래프 하나와 이를 설명하는 가설 문장 하나를 함께 제시하고, 두 정보를 결합해야만 답할 수 있는 결론을 빈칸으로 묻는다. 정답은 시각 자료의 특정 수치와 가설 문장을 연결해야 나오고, 오답 3개는 각각 시각 자료만 보고 가설을 무시한 결론, 가설 문장만 보고 시각 자료를 무시한 결론, 시각 자료의 다른 항목을 잘못 짝지은 결론으로 만든다.
c.seed: economics and business — Supply chain diversification strategy and geographic concentration risk following COVID-19 pandemic disruptions

g.passage:
Economists studying how manufacturers responded to pandemic-era disruptions surveyed firms in four industries in 2019 and again in 2023, recording the share of each industry's key components sourced from a single country. Researcher Lena Okafor hypothesizes that diversification after the pandemic was driven less by how concentrated an industry's sourcing originally was than by how long its production lines actually sat idle in 2020: in her view, only industries that endured shutdowns longer than eight weeks substantially reduced their reliance on a single country.

Industry | Single-country share, 2019 | Single-country share, 2023 | Weeks of 2020 shutdown
Medical devices | 58% | 31% | 11
Consumer electronics | 72% | 66% | 4
Auto parts | 49% | 27% | 9
Household furniture | 81% | 77% | 3

If Okafor's hypothesis is correct, the data suggest that consumer electronics firms ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: made only modest changes because their 2019 single-country share was already lower than that of furniture makers.
reduced their single-country share by more than auto parts makers did because they began with a higher degree of concentration.
cut their single-country share by roughly half, as medical device makers did after a shutdown of more than eight weeks.
changed their sourcing little not because their reliance on one country was modest but because their idle period was too brief to prompt a shift.
g.design: 표의 전자제품 수치(72%→66%, 4주)와 '8주 초과 셧다운만 다변화'라는 가설을 결합해야 정답이 나오게 했다. 오답은 표만 본 결론(A), 가설의 결과를 무시하고 초기 집중도 논리를 쓴 결론(B), 의료기기 항목과 잘못 짝지은 결론(C)으로 구성했다.
g.explanation:
정답 D: 전자제품은 2019년 집중도가 72%로 높았지만 셧다운은 4주뿐이었다. 오카포르의 가설은 8주를 넘는 셧다운만 큰 다변화를 부른다고 보므로, 집중도가 66%로 조금만 줄어든 것은 원래 집중도가 낮아서가 아니라 셧다운 기간이 짧았기 때문이라는 결론이 나온다.
A: 가구 업체와 비교해 초기 집중도로 설명한 것으로, 표 숫자만 보고 가설을 무시한 오답이다. 가설은 초기 집중도가 핵심 요인이 아니라고 말한다.
B: 처음 집중도가 높을수록 더 많이 다변화한다는 직관에 기댄 것으로, 실제 감소폭(6%p 대 22%p)도 표와 어긋나고 가설의 핵심 변수도 외면한다.
C: 의료기기 행(58%→31%, 11주)을 전자제품에 잘못 짝지은 오답이다.
g.explanation_en:
Correct answer D: Consumer electronics started out highly concentrated (72%) but sat idle for only 4 weeks, and its share fell just to 66%. Okafor's hypothesis says only shutdowns longer than eight weeks led to substantial diversification. So the small change came from the short shutdown, not from low reliance on one country.
A: This choice explains the result using 2019 concentration compared with furniture. It reads the table but ignores the hypothesis, which says starting concentration was not what drove diversification.
B: This choice relies on the intuition that firms that start more concentrated diversify more. It ignores the hypothesis, and it also contradicts the table: electronics fell 6 points, while auto parts fell 22.
C: This choice pairs electronics with the medical devices row (58% to 31%, 11 weeks), which belongs to a different industry.

c.instruction: 하나의 결론이나 가설을 먼저 제시한 뒤, 그것을 뒷받침/약화/무관하게 만드는 추가 사실 하나를 골라야 하는 빈칸 문제를 만든다. 정답은 가설의 핵심 조건을 직접 충족하거나 위배하는 사실이어야 하며, 오답 3개는 각각 표면적으로만 관련 있어 보이지만 실제로는 무관한 사실, 가설과 반대 방향으로 작용하는 사실을 지지 사실인 것처럼 제시한 것, 결론과 무관한 배경 정보를 결론 지지처럼 위장한 것으로 만든다.
c.seed: economics and business — Gig economy labor misclassification and independent contractor status legal challenges to platform business models

g.passage: Platform companies that coordinate delivery and ride-hailing work typically classify their workers as independent contractors rather than employees, which exempts the firms from paying minimum wage, overtime, and payroll taxes. Several courts have evaluated this classification using a test whose decisive question is whether the company controls how the work is performed. Economist Lena Varga hypothesizes that in a given city, a platform's contractor classification is most likely to be overturned when its app sets the prices workers charge and penalizes workers who decline assignments. If Varga's hypothesis is correct, a court applying this test would be most likely to rule against a platform that ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: fixes each fare through its algorithm and lowers the ratings of drivers who turn down too many requests.
lets drivers set their own fares and accept or reject requests without any effect on their standing.
pays drivers more per trip than most taxi companies in the same city pay their employees.
has grown faster than any rival platform since it began operating in the city a decade ago.
g.explanation:
정답 A: 가설의 두 핵심 조건—앱이 가격을 정하고, 배정을 거절하면 불이익을 준다—을 모두 직접 충족하므로 '작업 방식 통제'를 보여 주어 분류가 뒤집힐 가능성이 가장 크다.
B: 노동자가 가격과 수락 여부를 스스로 정하므로 오히려 독립계약자 분류를 강화한다. 가설과 반대 방향으로 작용하는 사실이다.
C: 보수 수준은 노동자 처우와 관련 있어 보이지만, 판단 기준은 '통제' 여부이므로 표면적으로만 관련 있고 실제로는 무관하다.
D: 회사의 성장 속도와 운영 기간은 배경 정보일 뿐 통제 여부와 무관하다.
g.explanation_en:
Choice A is correct. The hypothesis names two conditions: the app sets the prices, and workers who decline assignments are penalized. A platform that sets every fare through its algorithm and lowers the ratings of drivers who turn down requests meets both conditions. That shows the company controls how the work is done, which is the deciding question in the court's test.
Choice B is incorrect because it points the other way. If drivers set their own prices and can refuse requests freely, that supports treating them as independent contractors.
Choice C is incorrect because pay level seems related to worker welfare, but the test asks about control, not how much workers earn.
Choice D is incorrect because how fast the company grew and how long it has operated are background facts. They say nothing about whether the company controls the work.
g.design: I stated the hypothesis's two conditions first: price setting and penalties for declining work. The correct answer meets both directly. The wrong answers are a fact that works against the hypothesis (B), a fact that only looks relevant (pay, C), and an unrelated background fact (growth, D). All four use the same sentence pattern.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: life science — Hagfish slime production and protein fiber gel defense mechanism against predatory shark attacks

g.passage: When a shark bites down on a hagfish, the eel-shaped scavenger releases a small amount of mucus and thread-like protein fibers from pores along its body. Within a fraction of a second, these materials absorb enormous quantities of seawater, swelling into a slimy gel that can fill the attacker's mouth and gills. Video footage collected by marine biologist Vincent Zintzen and colleagues shows sharks gagging and retreating after such encounters. Researchers had long assumed that the slime's mucus alone was responsible for this rapid expansion, but experiments by Douglas Fudge's team suggest otherwise. When the threads were removed from samples, the remaining mucus dispersed into the water instead of forming a cohesive mass; the fibers, it turns out, act as a scaffold that traps water and holds the gel together.
g.question: According to the text, what did the experiments by Fudge's team reveal?
options: The protein fibers released by hagfish expand more quickly in seawater than the mucus does, allowing the gel to form in under a second.
The protein fibers released by hagfish give the gel its structure, without which the mucus fails to form a cohesive mass.
The protein fibers released by hagfish clog a shark's gills on their own, while the mucus mainly fills the shark's mouth.
The protein fibers released by hagfish cause sharks to gag and retreat, as video footage of attacks later confirmed.
g.explanation: 정답은 B이다. 지문은 섬유를 제거하자 점액이 흩어져 응집된 덩어리를 만들지 못했다고 하며, 섬유가 물을 가두고 젤을 붙잡아 두는 뼈대 역할을 한다고 설명한다. A는 젤이 1초 안에 형성된다는 지문 내용을 끌어왔지만, 섬유와 점액의 팽창 속도를 비교한 내용은 없다. C는 아가미와 입에 대한 언급을 활용했지만, 섬유와 점액이 역할을 나눠 맡는다는 내용은 지문에 없다. D의 영상은 Fudge 연구팀이 아니라 Zintzen 연구팀의 자료이며, 섬유만의 효과를 확인한 것도 아니다.
g.explanation_en: B is the correct answer. The text says that when the threads were removed, the mucus dispersed instead of forming a cohesive mass, so the fibers act as a scaffold that holds the gel together. A borrows the detail that the gel forms in a fraction of a second, but the text never compares how fast the fibers and the mucus expand. C draws on the mention of the mouth and gills, but the text doesn't say the fibers and the mucus do separate jobs. D refers to video footage collected by Zintzen's team, not Fudge's, and that footage didn't test the fibers on their own.
g.design: 세부 정보 문항으로 만들었다. 학생은 Fudge 연구팀의 실험 결과와 지문 앞부분의 영상·속도 정보를 구분해야 한다. 오답은 모두 지문의 실제 세부 내용을 잘못 연결한 것이라 꼼꼼히 비교해야 걸러낼 수 있다.

c.instruction:

c.seed: life science — Vampire bat saliva anticoagulant peptides and host blood feeding physiological adaptation mechanisms

g.passage: Common vampire bats (Desmodus rotundus) feed exclusively on the blood of other animals, a diet that poses a basic mechanical problem: blood begins to clot within minutes of leaving a wound. Researchers long assumed that the bats overcame this obstacle mainly by producing large quantities of saliva. However, biochemist Rosa Ibarra and colleagues found that the volume of saliva a bat releases while feeding is actually quite small. What matters, their analysis suggests, is the saliva's composition: it contains a peptide the team named draculin, which blocks two separate steps in the clotting cascade, along with an enzyme that dissolves clots that have already begun to form. Because these compounds act on different stages of coagulation, a bat can keep blood flowing from a tiny bite for thirty minutes or more without needing to reopen the wound.
g.question: According to the text, what did Ibarra and colleagues conclude about how vampire bats keep a host's blood from clotting?
options: The bats keep blood flowing by releasing a large volume of saliva that dilutes the blood before clotting can begin.
The bats keep blood flowing mainly by reopening the bite repeatedly, since their saliva works only for a few minutes.
The bats keep blood flowing because several substances in their saliva interfere with clotting at different points in the process.
The bats keep blood flowing because draculin dissolves clots once they have formed, which makes other salivary compounds unnecessary.
g.explanation: 지문은 침의 양이 아니라 성분이 중요하며, draculin이 응고 과정의 두 단계를 막고 다른 효소가 이미 생긴 혈전을 녹여 서로 다른 단계에 작용한다고 설명하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 연구 이전의 통념(많은 양의 침)으로, 연구진이 반박한 내용이다. B는 상처를 다시 열 필요가 없다는 지문 내용과 반대된다. D는 혈전을 녹이는 역할을 draculin이 아닌 별도의 효소에 잘못 돌리고, 여러 성분의 결합 작용을 부정한다.
g.explanation_en: The text says that what matters is the saliva's composition, not its volume: draculin blocks two steps in clotting while a separate enzyme dissolves clots already forming, so the compounds act at different stages, which makes C correct. A gives the older assumption about large volumes of saliva, which the researchers rejected. B is wrong because the text says the bat does not need to reopen the wound. D gives the clot-dissolving job to draculin instead of the separate enzyme, and it ignores how the compounds work together.
g.design: To answer, you have to combine two details: draculin acts at two steps, and a separate enzyme handles clots that are already forming. The wrong choices are traps built from real details in the text: the rejected assumption (A), the wound detail (B), and the names of the compounds swapped (D).

c.seed: life science — Platyfish live-bearing reproductive strategy and male sexual coercion behavioral ecology adaptation

g.passage:
Platyfish (Xiphophorus maculatus) are live-bearers: fertilization happens inside the female, and she gives birth to free-swimming young rather than laying eggs. Because males transfer sperm with a modified fin called a gonopodium, they can attempt to mate without any courtship, and male platyfish frequently approach females from behind in sudden, unsolicited thrusts. Researchers once treated these attempts mainly as a cost to females, who lose feeding time while evading males.

Recent laboratory work by behavioral ecologists suggests that females are not simply passive targets, however. Female platyfish can store sperm for months and appear to favor sperm from preferred males when fertilizing their eggs, so a male that succeeds in a forced mating does not necessarily father offspring. In addition, females that were harassed often moved closer to larger groups, where the attention of males was spread across many females. These findings indicate that coercive mating by males has shaped female counterstrategies at both the behavioral and the physiological level.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Because male platyfish use a gonopodium to transfer sperm, they no longer need to court females, which has made courtship displays disappear from the species.
Female platyfish lose substantial feeding time while evading males, and this loss is the most significant cost of the live-bearing reproductive strategy.
Female platyfish prefer to live in large groups, which explains why males in the species rarely succeed in forced mating attempts.
Although male platyfish often attempt to mate by force, females have evolved ways of reducing the impact of those attempts on which males sire their young.
g.explanation: 지문은 수컷의 강제 교미 시도를 소개한 뒤, 암컷이 정자 저장·선택과 큰 무리로의 이동이라는 대응 전략을 갖는다는 것이 핵심이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 구애 없이 교미를 시도할 수 있다는 세부를 과장해 구애 행동이 사라졌다고 단정하며, 중심 내용도 아니다. B는 먹이 시간 손실을 언급하지만, 그것은 과거 연구자들의 관점일 뿐이며 지문은 이를 수정한다. C는 무리 이동이라는 세부를 다루지만 암컷이 원래 큰 무리를 선호한다거나 강제 교미가 드물게 성공한다는 내용은 지문에 없고, 생리적 대응도 빠져 있다.
g.explanation_en: The text introduces males' forced mating attempts and then shows that females counter them through sperm storage and selection and by moving into larger groups, so D is the best answer. A takes the detail that males can mate without courtship and stretches it into the claim that courtship has disappeared, which the text never says, and this isn't the main point anyway. B mentions lost feeding time, but that was earlier researchers' view, and the text goes on to revise it. C touches on group behavior, but the text never says females naturally prefer large groups or that forced matings rarely succeed, and C also leaves out the physiological counterstrategy.
g.design: 수컷의 강제 행동과 암컷의 행동적·생리적 대응이라는 두 단락을 연결해야 하는 medium 문항으로 설계했다. 오답 B와 C는 지문 세부를 부분적으로 활용했고, A는 그럴듯한 과잉 추론이다.

c.seed: life science — Lungfish estivation dormancy and metabolic rate suppression during seasonal drought conditions

g.passage: African lungfish survive seasonal droughts by burrowing into the mud of drying riverbeds and secreting a mucus cocoon around their bodies, a dormant state known as estivation. Researchers long assumed that the fish endured these months simply by drawing down stored energy at a normal pace until the rains returned. Measurements of oxygen consumption in estivating lungfish, however, tell a different story: the fish lower their metabolic rate to a small fraction of its usual level, and genes involved in tissue repair and protection against cellular damage become more active. Rather than passively waiting out the drought, the lungfish appears to shift its body into a distinct, actively regulated state that conserves energy while guarding its organs against harm.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Evidence suggests that lungfish survive drought through a controlled physiological transformation instead of merely depleting their reserves.
Evidence suggests that lungfish survive drought mainly because their mucus cocoons prevent the loss of water from their bodies.
Evidence suggests that lungfish survive drought by storing unusually large amounts of energy before the rivers dry up.
Evidence suggests that lungfish survive drought only in riverbeds whose mud remains moist throughout the dry season.
g.explanation: 지문은 기존 가정(저장 에너지를 평소 속도로 소모)과 달리, 폐어가 대사율을 크게 낮추고 보호 유전자를 활성화하는 능동적으로 조절된 상태로 전환한다고 주장하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 지문에 나오는 점액 고치를 언급하지만, 수분 손실 방지가 생존의 주된 이유라는 내용은 없으며 핵심 주장도 아니다. C는 저장 에너지라는 지문 속 단어를 쓰지만, 지문은 저장량이 아니라 에너지 사용 방식의 변화를 강조한다. D는 진흙 서식지를 언급하지만, 수분이 유지되는 진흙이라는 조건은 지문에 없다.
g.explanation_en: The text contrasts an old assumption (the fish just burn stored energy at a normal pace) with new evidence that lungfish sharply lower their metabolism and switch on protective genes, which is an actively regulated state. That makes A correct. B mentions the mucus cocoon from the text, but the text never says that preventing water loss is the main reason the fish survive. C uses the idea of stored energy, but the text focuses on how the fish change their energy use, not on how much energy they store. D refers to the mud, but the text never says the mud has to stay moist.
g.design: 오답들이 지문 속 세부(고치, 저장 에너지, 진흙)를 재활용해서, 대조 구조(가정 vs 증거)를 파악해야 A를 고를 수 있게 했다.

c.seed: earth and space science — Stratospheric ozone depletion and chlorofluorocarbon photochemical reactions above Antarctic continent

g.passage: When chemists Mario Molina and F. Sherwood Rowland warned in 1974 that chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) could destroy stratospheric ozone, they predicted a slow, gradual thinning spread fairly evenly across the globe. The dramatic seasonal hole discovered over Antarctica in 1985 was far deeper than their model allowed. Researchers later traced the discrepancy to the region's extreme winter cold: at temperatures below about −78°C, polar stratospheric clouds form, and on the surfaces of their ice particles, relatively inert chlorine compounds are converted into forms that sunlight can readily break apart. When the Sun returns in the austral spring, the freed chlorine atoms destroy ozone at rates that gas-phase reactions alone could never achieve. The original theory about CFCs was thus not wrong, but it had overlooked how a particular atmospheric setting could greatly accelerate the chemistry it described.
g.question: According to the text, why did the ozone loss observed over Antarctica exceed what Molina and Rowland had predicted?
options: Sunlight in the austral spring is more intense over Antarctica than elsewhere, so it breaks down CFC molecules faster than the model had assumed.
Cloud particles that form only in intense cold provide surfaces where chlorine is changed into forms that sunlight easily releases, speeding ozone destruction.
Gas-phase reactions involving chlorine turned out to be faster at very low temperatures than chemists in the 1970s had measured.
CFCs released worldwide tend to collect in the Antarctic stratosphere, so the region holds far more chlorine than the global average.
g.explanation: 지문은 −78°C 이하에서 생기는 극성층권 구름의 얼음 입자 표면에서 비활성 염소 화합물이 햇빛에 쉽게 분해되는 형태로 바뀌고, 그 결과 오존 파괴가 크게 가속된다고 설명하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 봄철 햇빛이 언급되긴 하지만 햇빛이 더 강하다는 내용은 없고, 핵심 원인인 구름 표면 반응을 빠뜨린다. C는 지문이 오히려 기체상 반응만으로는 그런 속도가 불가능하다고 말한 것과 반대된다. D는 남극에 CFC가 모인다는 내용이 지문에 없으며, 지문은 염소의 양이 아니라 화학 반응의 가속을 원인으로 든다.
g.explanation_en: B is correct because the text says that below about −78°C, polar stratospheric clouds form, and on their ice particles inert chlorine compounds are turned into forms sunlight easily breaks apart, which speeds up ozone destruction a lot. A brings up spring sunlight, but the text never says the sunlight is more intense there, and A leaves out the key cloud-surface step. C contradicts the text, which says gas-phase reactions alone could never reach these rates. D claims CFCs collect over Antarctica, which the text never says; the text explains the extra loss by faster chemistry, not by more chlorine.
g.design: To get this right, students have to connect two details: the cold that forms the clouds and the chlorine conversion on the cloud surfaces. The wrong answers reuse words from the passage (sunlight, gas-phase reactions, Antarctic chlorine) but distort or reverse what it says, so a quick skim can lead to the wrong choice.
