c.seed: earth and space science — Submarine landslide tsunami generation mechanism and 1755 Lisbon earthquake offshore sediment failure

g.passage: Most tsunamis are attributed to the sudden vertical shift of the seafloor along a fault during an earthquake. Yet some historical tsunamis were larger, or arrived at different times along different coasts, than fault movement alone would predict. The 1755 Lisbon earthquake is one such case: waves struck parts of the Portuguese and Moroccan coasts with a pattern of heights that models based only on faulting have struggled to reproduce. Marine geologist Pedro Terrinha and colleagues have mapped thick deposits of jumbled sediment on the slopes off southwestern Iberia, some of which appear to date to roughly the time of the earthquake. Because a mass of sediment sliding rapidly downslope can displace a large volume of overlying water, the researchers suggest that shaking-triggered slope failures may have added their own waves to those produced by the fault, helping to explain why the 1755 tsunami behaved as it did.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Researchers have concluded that the 1755 tsunami was generated entirely by submarine landslides rather than by movement along a fault.
Researchers have found that sediment deposits off southwestern Iberia formed gradually over centuries and therefore record many separate tsunamis.
Researchers have proposed that underwater slope failures set off by the earthquake may account for features of the 1755 tsunami that faulting alone does not explain.
Researchers have shown that the 1755 tsunami was larger along the Moroccan coast than along the Portuguese coast because of differences in fault orientation.
g.explanation: 지문은 단층 운동만으로는 1755년 쓰나미의 파고 분포를 설명하기 어렵다는 문제를 제시한 뒤, 지진으로 촉발된 해저 사면 붕괴가 단층이 만든 파도에 '더해져' 그 특징을 설명할 수 있다는 연구자들의 제안을 소개하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 산사태를 언급하지만 '전적으로' 산사태 때문이라고 해 지문의 '추가적 기여'라는 주장을 과장한다. B는 퇴적물 지도 작성이라는 세부 사항을 다루지만, 지문은 일부 퇴적물이 지진 무렵의 것으로 보인다고 했을 뿐 수세기에 걸친 형성을 말하지 않는다. D는 두 해안을 언급하지만 해안별 파고 비교나 단층 방향 설명은 지문에 없다.
g.explanation_en: The text first points out that faulting alone can't explain the pattern of wave heights in 1755. It then presents the researchers' suggestion that slope failures triggered by the earthquake added their own waves to the fault-generated ones, so C is correct. A does bring in landslides, but it says the tsunami came "entirely" from them, which overstates the text's claim that landslides added to the fault's effect. B picks up on the sediment mapping, but the text says some deposits seem to date to around the time of the earthquake, not that they built up over centuries. D mentions both coasts, but the text never compares their wave heights or brings up fault orientation.
g.design: 세 오답 모두 지문 속 세부 정보(산사태, 퇴적물, 두 해안)를 가져와 같은 'Researchers have ...' 틀로 썼다. 그래서 '추가적 기여'라는 범위와 퇴적 시기를 꼼꼼히 비교해야만 오답을 걸러낼 수 있다.

c.seed: earth and space science — Loess plateau wind-blown silt deposition and Chinese Yellow River suspended sediment load transport

g.passage: China's Loess Plateau was built grain by grain: for roughly 2.6 million years, winds blowing from Central Asian deserts dropped fine silt across the region, eventually piling it more than 100 meters deep in places. Yet this thick deposit is far from durable. Its loosely cemented particles are easily ______ by intense summer downpours, which carry them into the Yellow River and help give that river one of the highest suspended sediment loads on Earth.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: deposited
compacted
sorted
dislodged
g.explanation: 지문은 퇴적층이 '전혀 견고하지 않다'고 말한 뒤, 폭우가 입자를 황하로 운반한다고 설명하므로, 빈칸에는 빗물이 입자를 제자리에서 떼어 낸다는 의미가 필요하다. 따라서 '떼어 내다, 이탈시키다'를 뜻하는 D가 정답이다. A는 바람이 실트를 쌓은 과정과 관련된 단어지만, 빗물이 입자를 강으로 옮겨 가는 과정과는 반대 방향을 나타낸다. B는 빗물이 흙을 다지는 것이 실제로 가능해 보이지만, 다져진다면 오히려 더 견고해지므로 '견고하지 않다'는 내용과 맞지 않는다. C는 물이 퇴적물을 분급할 수는 있지만, 입자가 쉽게 침식된다는 점이나 퇴적층이 약하다는 점을 설명하지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: The text says the deposit is "far from durable" and then explains that downpours carry the particles into the Yellow River, so the blank needs a word meaning the rain loosens the particles and moves them from where they sit. That makes D correct, since "dislodged" means knocked loose or forced out of position. A describes how the wind built up the silt, but the rain is doing the opposite by carrying the particles away. B might sound reasonable because rain can pack soil down, but packed soil would be sturdier, which contradicts "far from durable." C names something water can really do to sediment, but sorting doesn't explain why the deposit is fragile or how it erodes so easily.
g.design: Solving this takes two steps: first link "far from durable" to the river carrying the particles away, then pick the verb that fits rain eroding loose silt. The distractors are all believable sediment processes. A matches the deposition idea, B fits rain acting on soil, and C fits water acting on sediment, so you have to compare each against the passage to rule it out.

- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: earth and space science — Milankovitch orbital cycles and glacial-interglacial climate oscillation Pleistocene ice age timing drivers

g.passage: Milankovitch cycles—slow, regular changes in the shape of Earth's orbit and the tilt and wobble of its axis—alter how much sunlight reaches high northern latitudes in summer. Many climate scientists argue that these orbital shifts did not by themselves supply enough energy to melt the vast Pleistocene ice sheets. Instead, the cycles ______ glacial retreat: a modest rise in summer sunlight started melting, and feedbacks such as shrinking reflective ice cover and rising atmospheric carbon dioxide then amplified the warming far beyond what the orbital change alone could produce.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: initiated
sustained
prevented
concluded
g.explanation: 지문은 궤도 변화가 혼자서는 빙하를 녹일 만큼 강하지 않았고, 처음 융해를 '시작'한 뒤 되먹임 작용이 온난화를 키웠다고 설명한다. 따라서 과정을 촉발했다는 뜻의 A가 정답이다. B는 궤도 주기가 후퇴를 계속 이어 갔다는 뜻이 되는데, 지문은 지속과 증폭을 되먹임의 몫으로 돌리므로 맞지 않는다. C는 융해가 시작됐다는 내용과 정반대이다. D는 주기가 과정의 끝에 작용했다는 뜻이지만, 지문은 주기를 출발점으로 묘사한다.
g.explanation_en: The text says orbital changes alone were too weak to melt the ice sheets, but a small rise in sunlight "started melting," and feedbacks then amplified the warming. So the cycles set the process in motion, which makes A correct. B would mean the cycles kept the retreat going, but the text gives that role to the feedbacks, not the orbital changes. C contradicts the statement that melting began. D puts the cycles at the end of the process, while the text presents them as the starting point.
g.design: 이 문제를 맞히려면 두 정보를 연결해야 합니다. 하나는 궤도 주기의 힘이 그것만으로는 부족했다는 점이고, 다른 하나는 융해가 시작된 뒤 되먹임 작용이 온난화를 증폭했다는 점입니다. 그럴듯한 오답인 B(sustained, 지속시켰다)는 시간 순서를 잘못 읽은 학생을 노린 것입니다.

c.instruction: 지문에 '한때 ~라고 여겨졌으나(통념)' 다음 'however/but/실제로는' 류의 전환어와 함께 이를 뒤집는 새 증거나 반박 문장을 제시하고, 빈칸이 그 반박된 결과를 표현하도록 한다. 정답은 통념과 정반대 방향의 의미를 가진 어휘로 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 통념 쪽 단어를 그대로 쓴 것, (2) 전환어를 못 읽고 통념과 같은 방향이지만 강도만 다른 단어, (3) 반박 대상과 무관한 제3의 의미 단어로 구성한다. 전환 지점 앞뒤 문장만으로 답이 결정되게 하고 문장 길이나 어휘 난이도는 중간 수준을 유지한다.
c.seed: earth and space science — Oceanic dead zone hypoxia formation and Mississippi River nutrient runoff eutrophication Gulf Mexico

g.passage: For years, many scientists assumed that cutting fertilizer use in the Mississippi River basin would shrink the Gulf of Mexico's hypoxic "dead zone" almost at once, since less nitrogen would wash downstream to feed the algal blooms that strip oxygen from the water. A 2018 modeling study, however, found that decades of intensive farming have left large stores of "legacy" nitrogen in soils and groundwater, and this nitrogen will keep seeping into rivers long after farmers apply less fertilizer. The benefits of reduced fertilizer use for the Gulf are therefore likely to be ______.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: immediate
deferred
prompt
localized
g.explanation: 정답 B(deferred). 통념은 비료를 줄이면 데드존이 '거의 즉시' 줄어든다는 것이었으나, 'however' 뒤의 연구는 토양·지하수에 쌓인 잔류 질소가 비료 사용이 줄어든 뒤에도 오랫동안 강으로 계속 흘러든다는 점을 보여 준다. 따라서 걸프만이 얻는 이익은 '늦게 나타나는(deferred)' 것이 논리적이다. A(immediate)는 반박된 통념을 그대로 옮긴 단어이다. C(prompt)는 전환어를 놓치고 통념과 같은 방향(빠른 효과)을 조금 약하게 표현한 단어여서 역시 틀렸다. D(localized)는 효과의 범위(공간)에 관한 단어로, 지문이 반박하는 시점 문제와 관련이 없다.
g.explanation_en: The correct answer is B (deferred). Scientists used to assume that cutting fertilizer use would shrink the dead zone "almost at once." After "however," the study shows that legacy nitrogen stored in soils and groundwater will keep seeping into rivers long after farmers use less fertilizer. So the benefits for the Gulf will show up only after a delay, which is what "deferred" means. A (immediate) just repeats the old assumption that the study overturned. C (prompt) misses the reversal and points the same way as the old view, saying the benefits will come quickly, just a little less strongly than "immediate." D (localized) is about where the effects happen, but the passage is about when they happen, so it doesn't respond to the point being argued.
g.design: I set up the old view ("almost at once"), then used "however" to bring in the legacy-nitrogen evidence that reverses it. The blank expresses the result of that reversal: the benefits come late. The wrong answers are A, which repeats the old view; C, which goes the same direction as the old view at a different strength; and D, which shifts to an unrelated idea (where rather than when).

c.instruction: 지문에 'is not X, but rather Y' 또는 'it isn't that A; instead B' 형태로 부정어 뒤에 대조 표현이 이어지는 문장을 만들고, 빈칸이 그 대조 표현(B) 자리에 오게 한다. 정답은 부정된 개념(X)과 반대 극성을 가진 어휘로 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 부정어를 무시하고 X와 같은 의미 단어, (2) 부정 구조를 이중으로 잘못 해석해 극성을 다시 뒤집은 단어, (3) 대조 구조와 무관한 유사 발음/철자 단어로 구성한다.
c.seed: earth and space science — Monsoonal circulation pattern reversal and Indian Ocean seasonal wind regime atmospheric pressure gradient

g.passage: In late spring, the Indian subcontinent heats up faster than the surrounding Indian Ocean. This creates a zone of low atmospheric pressure over land that draws moist ocean air inland. Meteorologists long pictured the resulting monsoon onset as a slow, even swing of the prevailing winds from northeasterly to southwesterly over several weeks. However, recent reanalysis of atmospheric data suggests that the seasonal reversal is not gradual but rather ______: once the land–sea pressure gradient crosses a critical threshold, the wind regime flips within a matter of days.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: incremental
prolonged
abrupt
abject
g.explanation:
정답 C(abrupt): 'not gradual but rather ______' 구조에서 빈칸에는 부정된 'gradual(점진적)'의 반대 개념이 들어가야 한다. 이어지는 콜론 뒤 내용인 '임계점을 넘으면 며칠 만에 바람 체계가 뒤바뀐다'가 '급작스러운'이라는 뜻을 직접 뒷받침한다.
A(incremental): '조금씩 늘어나는'이라는 뜻으로 gradual과 같은 의미다. 부정어 not을 무시하고 부정된 개념을 그대로 고른 오답이다.
B(prolonged): '오래 지속되는'이라는 뜻이다. 대조 구조를 이중으로 잘못 해석해 극성을 다시 뒤집은 오답이다. 이렇게 읽으면 '여러 주에 걸친 느린 변화'라는 기존 견해 쪽으로 되돌아가며, '며칠 만에'라는 설명과도 모순된다.
D(abject): 철자와 발음이 abrupt와 비슷하지만 '비참한, 극도로 비굴한'이라는 뜻이다. 바람의 변화 속도와는 관련이 없다.
g.explanation_en:
C (abrupt) is correct. The sentence uses a "not gradual but rather ______" contrast, so the blank needs a word with the opposite meaning of "gradual." The clause after the colon supports this: once the pressure gradient crosses a threshold, the wind regime flips "within a matter of days." That describes a sudden change, so "abrupt" fits.
A (incremental) means "happening in small steps," which is basically the same as "gradual." Choosing it ignores the word "not" and picks the idea the sentence rejects.
B (prolonged) means "lasting a long time." It comes from misreading the contrast twice, which flips the meaning back. That points toward the older view of a slow change over several weeks, and it contradicts "within a matter of days."
D (abject) looks and sounds like "abrupt," but it means "miserable" or "degraded." It has nothing to do with how fast the winds change.
g.design: I set up a "not gradual but rather ______" contrast and put the blank in the contrast slot. The answer is the opposite of the rejected idea. The wrong answers are: (1) a synonym of the rejected idea (incremental), (2) a word that comes from reading the contrast twice and flipping it back (prolonged), and (3) a word that looks and sounds like the answer (abject).

c.instruction: 지문을 두 단계(예: 상황 묘사 후 화자의 숙고, 또는 기존 주장 소개 후 저자의 반박/선언)로 구성하고, 빈칸을 두 번째 단계의 시작 지점에 배치해 앞 단계와 다른 서술 기능을 하도록 한다. 정답은 두 번째 단계의 기능(숙고, 반박, 선언 등)에 맞는 어휘로 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 첫 번째 단계에 어울리는 단어, (2) 두 단계 어디에도 맞지 않는 중립적 단어, (3) 의미는 비슷하나 문장이 요구하는 품사/기능이 다른 단어로 구성한다.
c.seed: earth and space science — Radiometric dating potassium-argon method and volcanic mineral crystallization absolute age determination archaeology

g.passage: Because potassium-40 in volcanic minerals decays to argon-40 at a known rate, and because argon gas escapes from molten rock but becomes trapped once crystals form, the potassium-argon method can assign absolute ages to ash layers lying above and below archaeological finds. Dates obtained this way at East African sites have long anchored the chronology of early stone tools. Geochronologist Ama Ofori, however, ______ that reliance, pointing out that crystals formed in an earlier eruption and later swept into a younger ash deposit can retain their accumulated argon, making a layer seem older than it actually is.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: confirms
describes
skeptical of
questions
g.explanation:
지문의 첫 단계는 칼륨-아르곤 연대측정법의 원리와 그것이 초기 석기 연대를 뒷받침해 왔다는 기존의 신뢰를 소개한다. 'however'로 시작하는 두 번째 단계에서 Ofori는 오래된 결정이 섞여 들어와 아르곤이 남아 있으면 지층이 실제보다 오래되어 보일 수 있다고 지적하므로, 그런 신뢰에 이의를 제기하는 동사 'questions'(D)가 정답이다.
A 'confirms'는 첫 단계의 신뢰하는 어조에는 맞지만, 'however'와 오류 가능성을 지적하는 내용과는 모순된다.
B 'describes'는 중립적인 동사여서 뒤따르는 비판적 지적과 'however'가 나타내는 반박 기능을 담아내지 못한다.
C 'skeptical of'는 의미는 비슷하지만 형용사구라서 동사가 필요한 자리('Ofori ... ______ that reliance')에 들어갈 수 없다(문법적으로 'is skeptical of'가 되어야 함).
g.explanation_en:
The first part of the text explains how the potassium-argon method works and notes that scientists have long relied on it to date early stone tools. The second part begins with "however" and reports Ofori's point that older crystals mixed into younger ash can keep their argon, which would make a layer look older than it really is. Because she is raising doubts about that reliance, "questions" (D) is the answer.
A, "confirms," fits the trusting tone of the first part, but it contradicts "however" and the problem Ofori points out.
B, "describes," is too neutral. It doesn't show that Ofori is challenging the reliance, which is what "however" and her criticism signal.
C, "skeptical of," has a similar meaning, but it's an adjective phrase. The sentence needs a main verb after "Ofori," so this choice is ungrammatical without "is."
g.design: The text first presents the method and the long-standing trust in it, then shifts to the author's challenge. The blank is the verb at the start of that challenge. The wrong answers are a word that fits only the first part (confirms), a neutral word (describes), and a phrase with a similar meaning that is the wrong part of speech (skeptical of).

c.instruction: 두 개의 짧은 텍스트(또는 텍스트와 연구 결과 요약)를 제시하고, 두 번째 텍스트의 저자나 연구자가 첫 번째 텍스트의 주장에 대해 보일 반응을 추론하는 문제를 만든다. 오답은 (1) 한쪽 텍스트 내용만으로 답한 경우, (2) 두 입장을 반대로 뒤바꾼 경우, (3) 두 텍스트 어디에도 없는 제3의 입장을 만든 경우로 구성한다.
c.seed: earth and space science — Limestone karst topography cenote formation and Yucatan Peninsula subsurface groundwater aquifer dissolution

g.passage:
Text 1
The roughly circular cenotes scattered across Mexico's Yucatan Peninsula are often explained entirely by slow dissolution from above. In this view, slightly acidic rainwater seeped down through fractures in the limestone over hundreds of thousands of years, enlarging cavities until their roofs collapsed. Because this process works wherever water and limestone meet, geologist Mara Ellison argues, the pattern of cenotes needs no special trigger: they are simply what limestone becomes under a wet climate given enough time.

Text 2
Hydrogeologist Tomás Villanueva studied water chemistry in flooded caves beneath the peninsula. He found that the most aggressive dissolution occurs not near the surface but deep below, at the boundary where fresh groundwater floats on denser seawater that has seeped inland. Water mixed at this boundary can dissolve limestone even when neither the fresh water nor the seawater alone could. Villanueva also noted that a famous ring of cenotes traces the buried rim of the Chicxulub impact crater, where fractured rock channels groundwater flow.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would Villanueva (Text 2) most likely respond to Ellison's account of cenote formation (Text 1)?
options: He would contend that her account overlooks deep processes and underlying structures that help determine where cenotes form.
He would agree that cenotes require no special trigger because rainwater seeping through fractures is sufficient to dissolve limestone anywhere.
He would contend that cenotes form mainly from processes near the surface, whereas Ellison wrongly attributes them to dissolution deep underground.
He would contend that cenotes are produced chiefly by the impact itself, which blasted open the cavities without any dissolution.
g.explanation:
정답 A: Ellison은 위에서 내려오는 빗물 용해만으로 충분하며 특별한 계기가 없다고 본다. Villanueva는 깊은 담수-해수 경계의 혼합수 용해와 칙술루브 충돌구 테두리의 균열 구조가 세노테 분포에 관여함을 제시하므로, Ellison의 설명이 깊은 과정과 지하 구조를 간과한다고 반박할 것이다.
B: Text 1의 주장만 보고 답한 경우로, Villanueva의 발견은 '특별한 계기 불필요'라는 주장과 충돌한다.
C: 두 입장을 뒤바꿨다. 지표 근처 과정을 강조한 쪽은 Ellison이고, 깊은 용해를 강조한 쪽이 Villanueva다.
D: 두 텍스트 어디에도 없는 제3의 입장이다. Villanueva는 충돌구가 지하수 흐름을 유도한다고 했을 뿐, 용해 없이 충돌이 직접 공동을 만들었다고 하지 않았다.
g.explanation_en:
Correct answer, A: Ellison says rainwater dissolving the rock from above is enough to explain cenotes, with no special trigger needed. Villanueva shows that the strongest dissolution happens deep underground, where fresh water mixes with seawater. He also points out that a ring of cenotes follows fractured rock along the rim of the Chicxulub crater. So he would say her account leaves out deep processes and underground structures that affect where cenotes form.
B relies only on Text 1. Villanueva's findings contradict the idea that no special trigger is needed.
C swaps the two positions. Ellison is the one who focuses on processes near the surface, while Villanueva points to dissolution deep underground.
D makes up a view that neither text holds. Villanueva says the crater's fractures direct groundwater flow. He never says the impact itself created the cavities without dissolution.
g.design: This is a paired-text reaction question. Each wrong answer matches one assigned error type: B uses only one text, C swaps the stances, and D invents a third position. The question avoids the key wording of the correct answer.

c.instruction: 인물의 행동이나 진술에 표면적으로 드러나지 않는 의도나 태도를 짧은 지문으로 제시하고, 겉으로 말한 것과 실제 상황(또는 결과) 사이의 어긋남으로부터 함의를 추론하게 한다. 오답은 (1) 지문에 명시된 문장을 그대로 가져온 오답, (2) 어긋남을 반대로 해석한 오답, (3) 지문과 무관한 일반적 상식을 답으로 만든 오답으로 구성한다.
c.seed: earth and space science — Atmospheric pressure systems and anticyclonic wind rotation Coriolis effect northern hemisphere weather patterns

g.passage: On the first day of her forecasting seminar, meteorologist Dana Ruiz told her students that the high-pressure system parked over their region was "the dullest weather there is": sinking air, clear skies, and light winds spiraling clockwise outward from the center, as the Coriolis effect dictates in the Northern Hemisphere. She then asked them to record surface conditions beneath the system every morning for a week. By Friday, their logs showed dense valley fog at dawn and steadily rising levels of particulate pollution, both trapped under the layer of warm, sinking air that the system maintained. Ruiz had not predicted either outcome aloud, but weeks earlier she had already scheduled Friday's session as a lecture titled "Hazards of Calm."
g.question: Based on the text, what can most reasonably be inferred about Ruiz's remark on the first day of the seminar?
options: It was meant as an accurate summary of the system, which had sinking air, clear skies, and light winds circulating clockwise.
It deliberately played down the system's importance so that students would find its risks through their own observations.
It reflected her real expectation that the system would be uneventful, so the fog and pollution in the students' logs surprised her.
It was mainly meant to stress that the Coriolis effect makes winds around high-pressure systems rotate clockwise in the Northern Hemisphere.
g.explanation:
정답 B: Ruiz는 고기압을 '가장 지루한 날씨'라고 했지만, 학생들에게 일주일간 관측을 시켰고, 몇 주 전에 이미 금요일 강의를 '고요함의 위험'으로 잡아 두었다. 그러므로 그녀는 안개와 오염 축적을 예상하고 있었으면서 일부러 그 중요성을 낮춰 말해 학생들이 직접 발견하게 했다고 추론할 수 있다.
A: 지문에 나온 묘사(하강 기류, 맑은 하늘, 시계 방향 바람)를 그대로 옮긴 오답이다. 그녀의 말을 말 그대로의 요약으로 보면 금요일 강의를 미리 준비했다는 사실과 말한 내용이 어긋나는 점을 놓친다.
C: 어긋남을 거꾸로 해석했다. '고요함의 위험' 강의를 몇 주 전에 미리 잡아 둔 것은 그녀가 놀란 것이 아니라 이 결과를 예상했음을 보여 준다.
D: 코리올리 효과에 관한 일반 상식으로는 맞지만, 그녀의 발언이 무엇을 노렸는지에 대한 추론은 아니다.
g.explanation_en:
Correct answer B: Ruiz called the high-pressure system "the dullest weather there is." But she then had her students log conditions for a week, and weeks earlier she had already scheduled a lecture called "Hazards of Calm" for Friday. This suggests she expected the fog and pollution to build up and played down the system on purpose so that students would discover its risks themselves.
A copies the description straight from the text (sinking air, clear skies, clockwise winds). If you take her remark as a literal summary, you miss the gap between what she said and the lecture she had already planned.
C gets the gap backward. Scheduling "Hazards of Calm" weeks in advance shows she expected these results and wasn't surprised by them.
D is true as general science about the Coriolis effect, but it isn't an inference about what her remark was meant to do.
g.design: I built the item on a mismatch: Ruiz's dismissive remark versus the "Hazards of Calm" lecture she had scheduled in advance. Students have to infer that she understated the system on purpose. The wrong answers are (1) a sentence lifted from the text, (2) a reversed reading of the mismatch, and (3) general knowledge about the Coriolis effect.

c.instruction: 지문에 하나의 넓은 주장과 그를 뒷받침하는 좁은 세부사실을 함께 제시하고, 지문 전체의 핵심 요지로 가장 적절한 범위의 진술을 고르게 한다. 오답은 (1) 세부사실 하나만을 전체 요지인 것처럼 과잉축소한 것, (2) 지문이 다루지 않은 범위까지 과잉확장한 것, (3) 넓은 주장과 세부사실을 뒤섞어 범위가 어긋난 것으로 구성한다.
c.seed: earth and space science — Seafloor hydrothermal vent chemosynthetic bacteria and archaea sulfide oxidation energy metabolism extremophile

g.passage: For most of the twentieth century, biologists assumed that nearly every food web on Earth ultimately depended on sunlight captured by photosynthesis. The discovery of communities clustered around seafloor hydrothermal vents in the late 1970s challenged that assumption. There, in total darkness, bacteria and archaea obtain energy by oxidizing hydrogen sulfide dissolved in the hot fluid that flows out of the vents, and they use that energy to turn carbon dioxide into organic matter. Some of these microbes live freely on mineral surfaces, while others live inside the tissues of animals such as giant tubeworms, which have no mouth or gut and rely entirely on their microbial partners for nourishment. Researchers have also found that certain vent archaea keep growing at temperatures above 110°C, far hotter than most organisms can survive.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Giant tubeworms at hydrothermal vents survive without a mouth or gut because microbes living inside their tissues supply all of their nourishment.
Microbes at hydrothermal vents show that chemical energy, rather than sunlight, sustains most food webs in the deep ocean and possibly on other worlds.
Microbes at hydrothermal vents show that a food web can be powered by chemical energy from sulfide rather than by sunlight, overturning a long-held assumption.
Microbes at hydrothermal vents overturned the assumption about sunlight mainly because some vent archaea can keep growing at temperatures above 110°C.
g.explanation: 정답 C: 지문은 먹이망이 햇빛에 의존한다는 기존 가정을 소개한 뒤, 열수구 미생물이 황화물을 산화해 얻은 화학 에너지로 유기물을 만든다는 점을 들어 그 가정이 흔들렸다고 설명한다. 관벌레와 고온 고세균은 이를 뒷받침하는 세부 사실이다. A는 관벌레라는 세부 사실 하나만을 요지로 삼아 범위를 지나치게 좁혔다. B는 지문에 없는 '심해 먹이망 대부분'과 '다른 천체'까지 주장을 넓혔다. D는 넓은 주장과 세부 사실을 뒤섞었다. 지문은 기존 가정이 뒤집힌 근거로 화학 에너지 이용을 들고 있으며, 110°C 이상에서 자란다는 내성을 근거로 들지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: C is correct. The text first presents the old assumption that food webs depend on sunlight. It then explains that vent microbes oxidize sulfide to get chemical energy and use it to make organic matter in total darkness, which challenged that assumption. The tubeworms and the heat-tolerant archaea are details that support this point. A is too narrow: it treats the tubeworm detail as if it were the main idea. B goes too far: the text never says chemical energy sustains most deep-ocean food webs, and it never mentions other worlds. D mixes up the main claim with a detail. The assumption was overturned because microbes use chemical energy, not because some archaea can grow above 110°C.
g.design: 이 문항은 넓은 주장(햇빛 의존 가정을 깨는 화학합성 먹이망)과 좁은 세부 사실(관벌레, 고온 고세균)을 함께 제시한다. 오답은 각각 범위를 지나치게 좁힌 것, 지나치게 넓힌 것, 주장과 세부 사실을 뒤섞은 것으로 구성했고, 네 선택지 모두 같은 문장 틀을 쓴다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 관계가 어휘 단서 없이 두 문장의 논리(양보 후 반전, 일반화 후 구체화, 원인 vs 결과 방향)에서 도출되는 문제. 오답 전환어도 일부 관계는 말이 된다.
c.seed: physical science — Cavitation bubble collapse in ultrasonic cleaning and shockwave erosion mechanisms on metal surfaces

g.passage: In ultrasonic cleaning, high-frequency sound waves create tiny vapor bubbles in a liquid that swell and then collapse violently. A bubble that collapses far from any solid object stays roughly spherical, releasing a shockwave that weakens rapidly as it spreads outward through the liquid. ______ a bubble that collapses beside a metal surface caves in unevenly, driving a narrow jet of liquid into the metal at high speed—which helps explain why erosion pits cluster precisely where bubbles touched the surface.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: As a result,
Similarly,
Specifically,
By contrast,
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 표면에서 멀리 떨어져 붕괴하는 기포(구형 유지, 퍼지며 약해지는 충격파)를, 뒷 문장은 금속 표면 옆에서 붕괴하는 기포(비대칭 붕괴, 금속을 직접 때리는 집중된 제트)를 설명하므로 두 상황을 대조하는 D가 정답이다. A는 먼 곳의 충격파가 약해지는 것이 표면 근처의 비대칭 붕괴를 일으키는 원인처럼 만들지만, 두 문장은 서로 다른 기포를 다루므로 인과 관계가 없다. B는 두 문장 모두 기포 붕괴를 다룬다는 점에서 그럴듯해 보이지만, 붕괴 방식과 결과가 정반대이므로 '유사함'으로 볼 수 없다. C는 뒷 문장이 앞 문장의 세부 설명일 때 쓰는 말인데, 뒷 문장은 앞 문장과 다른 조건을 제시하므로 맞지 않다.
g.explanation_en: The first sentence describes a bubble that collapses far from any surface (it stays spherical and its shockwave weakens as it spreads), while the second describes a bubble that collapses beside metal (it collapses unevenly and fires a focused jet into the surface). Because these two cases are being contrasted, D is correct. A suggests that the weakening shockwave far away causes the uneven collapse near the metal, but the sentences describe two different bubbles, so there's no cause-and-effect link. B may look tempting since both sentences are about bubble collapse, but the way each bubble collapses and what it does are opposites, not similar. C would work only if the second sentence gave more detail about the first, but it describes a different condition instead.
g.design: 빈칸 앞뒤에 '반면'을 알려주는 어휘 단서를 두지 않았다. 대조 관계는 서로 다른 두 조건(표면에서 먼 곳 vs. 표면 옆)을 비교해야만 드러난다. 오답 A·B·C에는 그럴듯해 보이는 근거(인과처럼 보이는 연결, 같은 주제, 세부 설명처럼 보이는 구조)를 각각 넣었다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 관계가 어휘 단서 없이 두 문장의 논리(양보 후 반전, 일반화 후 구체화, 원인 vs 결과 방향)에서 도출되는 문제. 오답 전환어도 일부 관계는 말이 된다.
c.seed: physical science — Metamaterial negative refractive index bending light backwards through periodic subwavelength structure arrangement

g.passage: Many metamaterials are assembled from tiny split-ring resonators and thin wires made of ordinary metals such as copper, and none of these components, taken individually, can bend light backward. ______ when physicists arrange the components in a repeating lattice whose spacing is smaller than the wavelength of the incoming radiation, the resulting structure exhibits a negative refractive index, steering waves to the opposite side of the normal from where conventional materials would send them.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Nevertheless,
Consequently,
For example,
Similarly,
g.design: 어휘 단서 없이 '개별 부품은 빛을 거꾸로 굴절시키지 못한다'는 진술과 '배열하면 음의 굴절률이 나타난다'는 진술 사이의 반전 관계를 파악하게 했다. 인과(B)와 예시(C)가 부분적으로 그럴듯해 보이도록 구성했다.
g.explanation: 첫 문장은 구리 같은 평범한 금속 부품 하나하나로는 빛을 거꾸로 굴절시킬 수 없다고 말하고, 둘째 문장은 그 부품들을 파장보다 작은 간격으로 배열하면 음의 굴절률이 나타난다고 말한다. 앞의 예상과 반대되는 결과가 나오므로 대조를 나타내는 A가 정답이다. B는 둘째 문장의 결과가 부품의 평범함 때문에 생긴다는 뜻이 되지만, 실제 원인은 배열 방식이다. C는 둘째 문장을 첫 문장의 사례로 만들지만, 둘째 문장은 첫 문장과 정반대의 내용이다. D는 두 문장이 비슷한 내용이라는 뜻인데, 실제로는 서로 대립한다.
g.explanation_en: The first sentence says that each ordinary metal component, on its own, can't bend light backward. The second says that arranging those same components in a subwavelength lattice produces a negative refractive index. That result goes against what the first sentence would lead you to expect, so a contrast transition fits, and that's why A is correct. B wrongly suggests the result happens because the parts are ordinary, when the real cause is how they're arranged. C presents the second sentence as an example of the first, but it actually says the opposite. D says the two ideas are similar, when they're really in contrast.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: physical science — Sonoluminescence light emission from imploding cavitation bubbles and theoretical quantum vacuum energy debates

g.passage: When a tiny gas bubble trapped in water is driven by intense sound waves, it can expand and then collapse so violently that it emits a brief flash of light, a phenomenon called sonoluminescence. Because the flashes last only trillionths of a second and the collapsing bubble is microscopic, measuring what happens inside it has proved extremely difficult. In the 1990s, this uncertainty left room for exotic explanations, including physicist Julian Schwinger's proposal that the light arises from energy released by the quantum vacuum as the bubble's boundary rapidly shifts. Later studies, however, recorded spectra resembling those of extremely hot, compressed gas and detected signatures of ionized atoms inside collapsing bubbles. Most researchers now regard these results as strong support for the view that the bubble's contents are heated by compression until they glow, though some details of the process remain unsettled.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Although sonoluminescence is difficult to measure, Schwinger's quantum vacuum proposal remains the most widely accepted explanation for the light the bubbles emit.
Although the brevity and small scale of sonoluminescence once encouraged unusual theories, later evidence has led most researchers to favor an explanation based on heating of compressed gas.
Although researchers have detected ionized atoms inside collapsing bubbles, they have been unable to determine how long the flashes of sonoluminescence last.
Although sonoluminescence was first explained by compressed-gas heating, recent spectral data have revived interest in quantum vacuum explanations.
g.explanation: 지문은 측정의 어려움 때문에 슈윙거의 양자 진공 가설 같은 이색적 설명이 나왔으나, 이후 고온 압축 기체 스펙트럼과 이온화 원자 증거로 대부분의 연구자가 압축 가열 설명을 지지하게 되었다는 흐름이므로 B가 정답이다. A는 슈윙거 가설이 언급되긴 했지만 현재 가장 널리 받아들여진다는 것은 지문과 반대이다. C는 이온화 원자 검출이라는 세부는 맞지만, 섬광 지속 시간(조 분의 1초)은 지문에 명시되어 있어 틀리다. D는 두 설명이 모두 등장하지만 시간 순서와 증거의 방향을 뒤집었다.
g.explanation_en: The text moves from a problem (flashes too brief and bubbles too small to measure easily) that allowed exotic ideas like Schwinger's quantum vacuum proposal, to later evidence—hot-gas spectra and ionized atoms—that convinced most researchers of the compression-heating view, so B is correct. A mentions Schwinger's proposal, but the text says most researchers now favor a different explanation. C correctly notes the ionized atoms, but the text states that the flashes last trillionths of a second, so their duration is known. D includes both explanations but reverses their order and the direction of the evidence.
g.design: 오답 A·C·D가 모두 지문 세부(슈윙거, 이온화 원자, 스펙트럼)를 담아 부분적으로 맞아 보이게 하고, 같은 'Although…' 틀로 통일해 전체 흐름(이색 이론→증거→합의)을 파악해야 B를 고를 수 있게 했다.

c.seed: physical science — Shape memory alloy martensitic phase transformation and pseudoelastic strain recovery upon heating cycles

g.passage: Shape memory alloys such as nickel-titanium can be bent into a new form at room temperature and then, when warmed, spring back to their original shape. This behavior depends on a change in crystal structure. At lower temperatures the alloy exists as martensite, a phase whose atoms are arranged in many small, tilted domains that can shift and reorient under stress without breaking atomic bonds. When the metal is heated past a characteristic temperature, it transforms into austenite, a more orderly phase with only one possible arrangement, so the domains are forced back into the single configuration that matches the original shape. Engineers long assumed that this recovery could be repeated almost indefinitely. Repeated heating cycles, however, reveal a limitation: each transformation leaves behind a small number of dislocations, defects that do not disappear when the alloy reverts to austenite. Over hundreds of cycles these defects accumulate, gradually lowering the amount of strain the alloy can fully recover and shifting the temperature at which the transformation begins.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Shape memory alloys recover their original form because heating breaks the atomic bonds that held the deformed martensite domains in place.
Shape memory alloys can be reshaped at room temperature because austenite is a flexible phase whose domains reorient easily under stress.
Shape memory alloys recover their shape through a heat-driven phase change, but repeated cycling builds up defects that weaken that recovery over time.
Shape memory alloys lose their ability to change phase after a single heating cycle because dislocations prevent austenite from forming.
g.explanation: 지문은 마르텐사이트에서 오스테나이트로의 상변태가 형상 회복을 일으킨다는 원리를 설명한 뒤, 반복 가열 시 전위가 누적되어 회복 능력이 점차 줄어든다는 한계를 제시하므로 두 내용을 모두 담은 C가 정답이다. A는 가열과 회복을 언급하지만, 지문에 따르면 도메인은 결합을 끊지 않고 움직이므로 원리를 잘못 서술했다. B는 상온 변형을 언급하지만 유연한 상은 오스테나이트가 아니라 마르텐사이트이다. D는 결함 누적을 다루지만, 지문은 수백 번의 사이클에 걸친 점진적 감소를 말할 뿐 한 번 만에 상변태가 불가능해진다고 하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The text first explains that heating converts martensite to austenite, which restores the original shape, and then points out that repeated cycles leave dislocations that gradually reduce this recovery. Choice C captures both parts, so it is correct. Choice A mentions heating and recovery, but the text says the domains shift without breaking atomic bonds, so it gets the mechanism wrong. Choice B mentions room-temperature reshaping but assigns flexibility to austenite, when the text attributes it to martensite. Choice D brings up defects, but the text describes a gradual decline over hundreds of cycles, not a total failure after one cycle.
g.design: 오답들은 지문의 실제 요소(가열·회복, 상온 변형, 결함)를 하나씩 빌리되 메커니즘·상 이름·규모를 비틀어, 지문 전반부와 후반부를 연결해야 C를 고를 수 있게 했다.

c.seed: physical science — Ferrofluids magnetic particle suspension behavior and magnetorheological viscosity damping applications engineering

g.passage: A ferrofluid is a liquid in which tiny magnetic particles are suspended. Without a magnetic field, the particles drift randomly and the fluid pours much like ordinary oil. A related material, magnetorheological fluid, contains larger particles, and engineers value it for a striking property: when a magnetic field is applied, the particles line up into chains that resist flow, and the fluid thickens almost instantly. Because this change can be reversed in milliseconds simply by switching the field off, automotive designers use such fluids in shock absorbers whose stiffness can be ______ continuously to match changing road conditions.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: reinforced
suspended
preserved
modulated
g.design: 핵심 단서 두 가지(밀리초 안에 되돌릴 수 있음 + 계속 변하는 도로 상황에 맞춤)를 연결해야 '양방향으로 조절'이라는 뜻을 고를 수 있다. 오답 A는 '굳어진다'는 정보에, B는 지문의 'suspended' 표면어에, C는 '안정적으로 유지'라는 직관에 기대어 그럴듯하게 만들었다.
g.explanation: 지문에 따르면 이 유체는 자기장을 걸면 굳고 자기장을 끄면 밀리초 안에 원래대로 돌아오며, 이 덕분에 쇼크업소버의 강성을 계속 변하는 도로 상황에 맞출 수 있다. 따라서 강성을 올렸다 내렸다 '조절하다'라는 뜻의 D가 가장 정확하다. A는 유체가 굳는다는 내용과 일부 맞지만, 강성을 높이는 한 방향만 뜻해서 '되돌릴 수 있다'는 핵심을 놓친다. B는 지문에서 입자에 대해 쓰인 단어를 그대로 가져온 것으로, 강성을 '중단하다'라는 뜻이 되어 문맥과 맞지 않는다. C는 상태를 그대로 유지한다는 뜻이라 계속 바뀌는 조건에 맞춘다는 내용과 정반대다.
g.explanation_en: The text says the fluid thickens when a magnetic field is applied and goes back to normal within milliseconds when the field is switched off. That is why a shock absorber's stiffness can keep matching changing road conditions. Choice D fits best because "modulated" means adjusted up or down. Choice A partly fits, since the fluid does thicken, but "reinforced" means making something stronger in one direction only, so it misses the point that the change is reversible. Choice B reuses a word the text uses for the particles, but saying the stiffness is "suspended" (put on hold) makes no sense here. Choice C means keeping something the same, which is the opposite of adjusting to changing conditions.

g.passage: Silica aerogel is often described as "frozen smoke": up to 99 percent of its volume is air trapped in pores only a few nanometers wide. Because these pores are narrower than the distance an air molecule typically travels before colliding with another, the gas inside can barely carry heat from one side of the material to the other. As a result, the material's ability to transmit heat is not merely reduced but ______; a thin slab can shield a hand from a blowtorch flame, which is why engineers have used aerogel to insulate Mars rovers against nighttime temperatures near −100°C.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: nearly eliminated
gradually restored
slightly lowered
widely debated
g.explanation: "not merely reduced but ______" 구조는 '감소'보다 더 강한 정도를 요구하고, 얇은 판이 토치 불꽃을 막는다는 뒷받침도 극단적 차단을 보여 주므로 A가 정답이다. C는 열전도가 줄었다는 방향은 맞지만 'not merely reduced'와 대비되지 않고 오히려 더 약하다. B는 열 전달 능력이 다시 회복된다는 뜻이라 기공이 열 전달을 막는다는 설명과 반대된다. D는 문장 자체로는 말이 되지만, 지문은 논쟁이 아니라 물리적 효과를 서술하고 있다.
g.explanation_en: The frame "not merely reduced but ______" calls for something stronger than a reduction, and the blowtorch example shows heat being almost completely blocked, so A is correct. C points in the right direction, since heat transfer does go down, but it is weaker than "reduced," so it doesn't work with the "not merely... but" contrast. B means the ability comes back, which contradicts the explanation that the pores block heat flow. D makes sense as a phrase on its own, but the passage describes a physical effect, not a debate.
g.design: Two steps: the reader must notice the intensifying "not merely reduced but" structure and connect it to the blowtorch evidence. C is a tempting choice for skimmers because it points the right way, and D reads naturally as a phrase.

c.seed: physical science — Starch gelatinization amylose leaching and viscosity changes during controlled heating wet cooking

g.passage: When starch granules are heated in water, they absorb liquid and swell, a process called gelatinization. Cooks have long assumed that the sauce thickens simply because the swollen granules crowd together. Food chemist Hana Okafor tested this assumption by heating cornstarch suspensions at a controlled rate and filtering samples at intervals. __She found that the sharpest rise in viscosity occurred not when the granules reached their maximum size but slightly later, as amylose molecules leached out of the granules and formed a tangled network in the surrounding water.__ Okafor's results suggest that the thickness of a starch-based sauce depends less on the granules themselves than on what escapes from them.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It explains how Okafor designed her heating procedure so that the swelling of starch granules could be measured precisely.
It presents an observation that complicates a widely held view and supports the conclusion drawn in the final sentence.
It offers evidence confirming that crowding of swollen granules is the main cause of a sauce's thickening.
It describes a limitation of Okafor's filtering method that the final sentence attempts to resolve.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 점도가 가장 크게 오르는 시점이 입자가 최대로 부푼 때가 아니라 아밀로스가 빠져나온 뒤라는 관찰을 제시한다. 이는 입자가 서로 밀집해서 걸쭉해진다는 요리사들의 통념을 흔들고, 마지막 문장의 결론을 뒷받침하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 실험 절차를 언급하지만, 밑줄 문장은 방법이 아니라 결과를 보고한다. C는 통념을 확인한다고 하여 실제 기능과 반대이다. D는 방법의 한계를 말하지만, 지문에는 그런 한계가 제시되지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence reports that viscosity rose most sharply after the granules reached full size, when amylose leached out. That challenges the cooks' belief that crowded granules cause thickening, and it supports the final sentence's conclusion, so B is correct. A mentions the experiment, but the sentence reports a result rather than describing how the procedure was designed. C reverses the sentence's role, because the finding undercuts the crowding view instead of confirming it. D is wrong because the text never presents a limitation of the filtering method.
g.design: 통념→실험→발견→결론 구조로 만들었다. 학생은 밑줄 문장을 통념과 결론에 모두 연결해야 한다. 오답 A와 C는 지문 요소(실험, 입자 부풂)에 부분적으로 걸쳐 있어서 대충 읽으면 고르게 된다.

c.seed: physical science — Photonic crystal photonic bandgap optical properties and structural color generation in beetle exoskeletons

g.passage: The metallic green of many weevils and longhorn beetles contains no green pigment at all. Instead, their scales are filled with photonic crystals: lattices of chitin and air whose spacing repeats at roughly the scale of a light wave. Within such a lattice, reflected waves of certain wavelengths reinforce one another, while other wavelengths pass through or cancel out. The band of wavelengths that cannot travel through the structure, called a photonic bandgap, is what the eye sees as color. __Because the color depends on lattice geometry rather than on chemistry, physicist Pete Vukusic and colleagues found that soaking beetle scales in a liquid that fills the air gaps shifts or erases the hue, which a pigment-based color would not do.__ Engineers now study these scales as models for fade-resistant paints and coatings that produce color through structure alone.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents a finding that challenges the claim that photonic bandgaps account for beetle coloration.
It explains how engineers have adapted beetle scale structures to manufacture fade-resistant coatings.
It offers experimental evidence supporting the text's account of where the beetles' color comes from.
It describes a chemical process by which beetles change the color of their scales over time.
g.design: 오답 A는 '색이 사라진다'는 표면 정보를 반박으로 오독하게, B는 다음 문장과 혼동하게, D는 'liquid/shift' 표현으로 화학 변화로 착각하게 설계해 실험 결과와 앞선 설명을 연결하는 두 단계 판단을 요구했다.
g.explanation: 앞부분은 딱정벌레의 색이 색소가 아니라 격자 구조(광자 밴드갭)에서 나온다고 설명한다. 밑줄 문장은 공기 틈을 액체로 채우면 색이 바뀌거나 사라진다는 실험 결과를 제시해 그 설명을 뒷받침하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 색이 사라진다는 결과가 구조색 설명과 오히려 일치하므로 반박이 아니라서 틀리다. B는 공학적 응용을 말하는데, 그 내용은 밑줄 문장이 아니라 마지막 문장에 나온다. D는 연구자들이 비늘을 실험으로 처리한 것이지, 딱정벌레가 스스로 화학적으로 색을 바꾸는 것이 아니므로 틀리다.
g.explanation_en: The earlier sentences explain that the beetles' color comes from lattice structure (a photonic bandgap), not from pigment. The underlined sentence reports an experiment: when the air gaps are filled with liquid, the hue shifts or disappears. That result backs up the structural explanation, so C is correct. A is wrong because losing the color when the structure is changed fits the bandgap explanation; it doesn't challenge it. B is wrong because the engineering uses come up in the final sentence, not the underlined one. D is wrong because researchers soaked the scales in an experiment; the beetles aren't changing their own color through chemistry.

c.instruction: 텍스트 1의 저자가 좋은 설명이나 해결책의 기준(예: 재현 가능성, 단순성, 장기적 효과)을 분명히 드러내게 쓰고, 텍스트 2는 그 기준과 어긋날 수 있는 결론을 내리게 쓴다. 질문은 '텍스트 1의 저자의 기준에서 텍스트 2의 결론을 어떻게 평가할 것인가'로 한다. 오답 3개는 텍스트 2 저자의 기준으로 평가한 결과, 두 저자의 기준을 섞은 평가, 일반 상식에 따른 평가로 만든다.
c.seed: physical science — Ionic gel polymer electrolyte ionic conductivity temperature dependence and electrochemical cell performance

g.passage:
Text 1
Researchers developing ionic gel polymer electrolytes for batteries often celebrate high ionic conductivity measured at a single temperature, usually around 25°C. But a battery in a car or a phone sees winter mornings and summer dashboards. In my view, an electrolyte deserves to be called promising only if its conductivity remains adequate across the full range of temperatures a working cell will actually encounter; a peak value at one comfortable temperature tells us little about real performance.

Text 2
A team at a materials laboratory recently reported an ionic gel electrolyte that, at 25°C, conducts ions nearly as well as conventional liquid electrolytes while resisting leakage and flammability. The team measured conductivity only at room temperature, where cells assembled with the gel cycled stably for 500 charges. Given this combination of safety and room-temperature conductivity, the researchers conclude that the gel is a highly promising candidate for commercial batteries.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 1 most likely evaluate the conclusion reached by the researchers described in Text 2?
options: As well supported, because conductivity close to that of liquid electrolytes, combined with stable cycling over 500 charges, shows the gel would perform reliably in commercial cells.
As partly supported, because the gel's resistance to leakage and flammability establishes its promise even though its room-temperature conductivity has not yet been confirmed by other laboratories.
As premature, because 500 charge cycles is too few to predict how long a commercial battery containing the gel would last before needing replacement.
As premature, because evidence from a single temperature cannot show whether the gel conducts ions adequately under the conditions batteries actually face.
g.explanation:
정답 D: Text 1 저자의 기준은 '실제 셀이 겪는 전체 온도 범위에서 전도도가 충분히 유지되는가'이다. Text 2 연구진은 25°C에서만 측정했으므로, 이 기준에 따르면 결론은 성급하다.
A: Text 2 저자의 기준(실온 전도도+안정적 사이클)으로 평가한 것으로, 온도 범위 문제를 무시한다.
B: 두 기준을 섞었다. 안전성이 유망함을 입증한다는 Text 2 쪽 논리에 '재현 여부'라는 엉뚱한 단서를 덧붙였고, Text 1의 온도 기준은 빠져 있다.
C: '사이클 수명이 짧다'는 일반 상식에 따른 비판이며, Text 1 저자가 제시한 기준이 아니다.
g.explanation_en:
Correct answer D: The author of Text 1 judges an electrolyte by one standard: does its conductivity stay adequate across the full range of temperatures a real cell will face? The researchers in Text 2 measured conductivity only at 25°C, so by that standard their conclusion is premature.
A judges the conclusion by Text 2's own standard (room-temperature conductivity plus stable cycling) and ignores the temperature-range issue.
B blends the two standards. It keeps Text 2's idea that safety shows the gel is promising and adds an unrelated worry about replication, while leaving out Text 1's temperature standard.
C relies on a general assumption that 500 cycles is too few, which is not the standard the author of Text 1 sets out.
g.design: Text 1 states a standard (adequate conductivity across the full operating temperature range). Text 2 reaches a conclusion from data at a single temperature. The wrong answers apply Text 2's own standard (A), mix the two authors' standards (B), and use a common-sense objection about cycle life (C).

c.instruction: 텍스트 1은 주장과 이유를, 텍스트 2는 같은 주제의 다른 접근을 각각 짧게 제시하되 서로를 언급하지 않게 쓴다. 질문은 '텍스트 2의 저자라면 텍스트 1의 주장에 어떻게 반응할 것인가'로 한다. 정답은 텍스트 2의 전제에서만 도출되는 반응으로 만들고, 오답 3개는 텍스트 1의 내용을 반복하는 선택지, 텍스트 2의 결론만 되풀이하는 선택지, 텍스트 2가 다루지 않은 쟁점을 끌어온 선택지로 만든다.
c.seed: physical science — Thermochromic liquid crystal temperature-dependent color change and thermal imaging applications detection

g.passage:
Text 1
Thermochromic liquid crystal (TLC) sheets, whose molecular layers reflect different wavelengths of light as temperature shifts, offer engineers an inexpensive way to map heat across a surface. Because a single photograph of a coated circuit board reveals its full temperature pattern at once, some engineers argue that TLC coatings can replace infrared cameras for detecting overheating components in electronics testing.

Text 2
A TLC's color is not a direct reading of temperature: the hue an observer records depends on the angle of viewing and on the spectrum of the light illuminating the surface. For this reason, laboratories that use TLCs for heat-transfer measurements first calibrate each coating under the exact lighting and camera position of the experiment, and they repeat the calibration whenever that arrangement changes. Treated this way, TLCs can yield temperature maps of impressive precision.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the engineers' argument in Text 1?
options: By cautioning that a single photograph's colors could be misread unless the coating had been calibrated for the specific lighting and viewing angle used to take it
By agreeing that a single photograph of a coated board shows its whole temperature pattern and is therefore a cheaper alternative to infrared cameras
By noting that a properly calibrated coating can yield temperature maps of impressive precision in heat-transfer research
By objecting that a coating applied to a circuit board might itself trap heat and thus cause the components to overheat
g.explanation:
정답 A: Text 2의 전제는 TLC의 색이 조명 스펙트럼과 관찰 각도에 따라 달라지므로 실험 조건마다 보정해야 한다는 것이다. 따라서 "사진 한 장으로 온도 분포 전체가 드러난다"는 Text 1의 근거는 보정이 전제될 때만 성립하며, Text 2의 저자는 이 점을 경고할 것이다. 이 반응은 Text 2에 직접 쓰여 있지 않고, Text 2의 전제를 Text 1의 주장에 적용해야 도출된다.
B: Text 1의 내용을 그대로 반복할 뿐이며, Text 2가 제기하는 보정 문제를 무시한다.
C: Text 2의 결론(정밀한 측정이 가능하다)만 되풀이하고, Text 1의 주장에 대한 반응이 되지 못한다. 보정이라는 조건을 빼면 오히려 동의처럼 읽힌다.
D: 코팅이 열을 가둔다는 쟁점은 Text 2에서 전혀 다루지 않는다.
g.explanation_en:
A is correct. Text 2's key premise is that a TLC's color depends on the viewing angle and on the light illuminating it, so each setup has to be calibrated. Text 1's argument relies on the idea that one photograph shows the full temperature pattern. Applying Text 2's premise, its author would warn that such a photo can't be trusted unless the coating was calibrated for that exact lighting and camera position. Text 2 never says this directly; you have to infer it by applying its premise to Text 1's claim.
B is wrong because it only repeats Text 1's claim and ignores Text 2's concern about calibration.
C is wrong because it only restates Text 2's conclusion about precision. It drops the calibration condition, so it doesn't actually respond to Text 1's argument.
D is wrong because Text 2 never discusses coatings trapping heat. This issue comes from outside the texts.
g.design: Text 2 doesn't mention Text 1. The answer is reached only by applying Text 2's premise (color depends on viewing angle and lighting, so calibration is needed) to the "single photograph" reasoning in Text 1. Each wrong answer matches one of the required types: B repeats Text 1, C repeats only Text 2's conclusion, and D brings in an issue Text 2 doesn't cover. All four options use the same "By ...ing that" structure.

c.instruction: 텍스트 1은 하나의 결론을 이끄는 주장을, 텍스트 2는 그 주장의 핵심 근거를 약하게 만들 수 있는 별개의 관찰이나 연구를 제시한다. 질문은 '텍스트 2의 저자가 텍스트 1의 어느 부분에 가장 이의를 제기할 것인가'로 한다. 정답은 텍스트 1의 결론이 아니라 그 결론이 기대는 가정으로 하고, 오답 3개는 결론 자체, 텍스트 1의 부수적 세부, 텍스트 2가 오히려 동의하는 부분으로 만든다.
c.seed: physical science — Electrospinning polymer jet formation and nanofiber diameter control through voltage and flow rate optimization

g.passage:
Text 1
In electrospinning, a high voltage draws a charged polymer solution from a needle into a thin jet that stretches and dries into nanofibers. Materials engineer Priya Venkataraman argues that fiber diameter can be reliably minimized by tuning just two dials: raising voltage while lowering flow rate. Her reasoning is that a stronger electric field pulls harder on the jet, and that this added stretching, applied to less fluid per second, must translate directly into thinner fibers. Her lab's tests used a single polyvinyl alcohol solution at room temperature.

Text 2
A team led by Tomás Ferreira measured jet behavior directly with high-speed imaging. Like other groups, they found that a modest reduction in flow rate generally yields finer fibers. But beyond a moderate threshold, increasing voltage did not lengthen the stretching phase; instead, the jet began whipping erratically and ejecting from several points on the droplet at once, producing fibers with widely scattered and often larger diameters. The added field strength, the team concluded, changes how the jet forms rather than simply how much it is drawn out.
g.question: Based on the texts, which element of Venkataraman's argument in Text 1 would Ferreira's team (Text 2) most likely challenge?
options: The claim that fiber diameter can be reliably minimized by adjusting voltage and flow rate together
The idea that each increase in field strength produces a corresponding increase in how far the jet is drawn out
The decision to conduct the tests with a single polyvinyl alcohol solution kept at room temperature
The view that delivering less solution per second to the needle tends to yield finer fibers
g.explanation:
정답 B: Venkataraman의 결론은 '전압과 유속을 함께 조절하면 섬유를 가늘게 할 수 있다'는 것이지만, 이 결론은 전기장이 강해질수록 제트가 그만큼 더 늘어난다는 가정에 기대고 있다. Text 2는 일정 문턱을 넘으면 전압을 높여도 늘어나는 단계가 길어지지 않고 제트가 불안정해진다고 보여 주므로, 바로 이 가정을 겨냥한다.
A: 결론 자체를 가리킨다. Text 2는 결론을 간접적으로 약하게 만들지만, 그 근거는 결론이 기대는 가정을 깨뜨리는 데 있다. 또한 Text 2는 유속을 낮추는 쪽은 인정하므로, 결론 전체를 반박한다고 보기 어렵다.
C: 실험 조건이라는 부수적 세부이다. Text 2는 용액 종류나 온도를 전혀 언급하지 않는다.
D: Text 2는 유속을 적당히 줄이면 대체로 섬유가 가늘어진다고 말하므로, 오히려 이 점에 동의한다.
g.explanation_en:
B is correct. Venkataraman's conclusion rests on an assumption: that a stronger field always stretches the jet more. Text 2 shows that above a threshold, raising the voltage does not lengthen the stretching phase. Instead, the jet whips and splits into several jets, so this assumption is exactly what Text 2 undermines.
A states the conclusion itself. Text 2 weakens the conclusion only indirectly, by attacking the assumption beneath it. It also accepts the point about flow rate, so it doesn't reject the conclusion outright.
C is an incidental detail of the experiments. Text 2 never mentions the solution type or the temperature.
D is something Text 2 actually agrees with: it says a modest reduction in flow rate generally gives finer fibers.
g.design: Text 1의 결론(두 변수를 조절하면 섬유가 가늘어진다)은 '전기장이 강할수록 제트가 비례해 늘어난다'는 가정에 기대고 있고, Text 2의 고속 촬영 관찰은 바로 그 가정을 무너뜨린다. 오답은 각각 결론 자체(A), 부수적인 실험 세부(C), Text 2가 동의하는 유속 관련 내용(D)이다. 네 선택지는 모두 같은 'The ~ that/to ...' 틀로 썼다.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: physical science — Ferrimagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles magnetic moment alignment and hyperthermia heating in biomedical therapy

g.passage: Iron oxide nanoparticles are tiny magnetic particles that doctors hope to use to treat tumors. When the particles are placed in a rapidly alternating magnetic field, their magnetic moments flip back and forth, and this motion releases heat that can damage nearby cancer cells. Materials scientist Lena Okafor hypothesizes that the amount of heat a particle produces depends on how well its internal magnetic moments are aligned: particles whose moments line up more uniformly, she argues, will heat their surroundings more than particles whose moments point in mixed directions.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Okafor's hypothesis?
options: Particles with uniformly aligned moments and particles with mixed moments raised the temperature of a test solution by the same amount.
Particles with mixed moments were easier to manufacture in large quantities than particles with uniformly aligned moments.
Particles with uniformly aligned moments raised the temperature of a test solution more than particles with mixed moments did.
Particles with uniformly aligned moments stayed in tumor tissue longer than particles with mixed moments did.
g.explanation: Okafor의 가설은 자기 모멘트가 더 균일하게 정렬된 입자일수록 열을 더 많이 낸다는 것이다. C는 정렬된 입자가 용액 온도를 더 많이 올렸다고 하므로 이 관계를 직접 보여 준다. A는 가열량에 차이가 없다고 하므로 오히려 가설을 약화한다. B는 제조 용이성, D는 조직 내 체류 시간에 관한 것이어서 둘 다 열 발생과 관련이 없다.
g.explanation_en: Okafor's hypothesis says that particles with more uniformly aligned magnetic moments produce more heat. Choice C shows exactly that: the aligned particles warmed the solution more than the mixed ones did. Choice A finds no difference in heating, so it actually weakens the hypothesis. Choice B is about how easy the particles are to make, and Choice D is about how long they stay in tissue, so neither one tells you anything about heat output.
g.design: To solve it, students only need to match the claim (more alignment means more heat) to a finding that compares heat output. The wrong options are typical traps: one finding goes against the claim, and two compare the same particles on traits that have nothing to do with heating.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: physical science — Silica colloidal crystal self-assembly and optical diffraction pattern formation through particle sedimentation

g.passage: When tiny silica spheres are suspended in water and left undisturbed, they slowly sink and pile up at the bottom of the container. Under the right conditions, the spheres stack into neat, repeating rows, forming what scientists call a colloidal crystal. These crystals often shimmer with bright colors because the evenly spaced spheres bend light in a regular pattern. Materials scientist Lena Okafor hypothesizes that slow settling is the key to this order: when the spheres sink slowly, they have time to roll into tidy positions, but when they sink quickly, they become jammed in a disordered heap.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Okafor's hypothesis?
options: Silica spheres of a larger size were found to sink faster through water than silica spheres of a smaller size did.
Silica spheres that settled at different speeds were found to produce layers of about the same thickness at the bottom of the container.
Silica spheres that settled quickly were found to form deposits with the same bright colors as deposits formed by spheres that settled slowly.
Silica spheres that settled slowly were found to form evenly spaced, colorful deposits, while spheres that settled quickly formed jumbled, dull deposits.
g.explanation: Okafor의 가설은 느리게 가라앉으면 질서 있는 결정이, 빠르게 가라앉으면 무질서한 더미가 생긴다는 것이다. D는 느린 침강은 고르고 색이 나는 퇴적층, 빠른 침강은 뒤엉키고 탁한 퇴적층을 만든다고 보여 주므로 가설을 직접 뒷받침한다. A는 입자 크기와 침강 속도의 관계만 말할 뿐 질서 여부를 언급하지 않는다. B는 층의 두께에 관한 것이라 배열의 질서와 무관하다. C는 속도와 상관없이 같은 색이 나타난다고 하므로 오히려 가설을 약화한다.
g.explanation_en: Okafor claims that slow settling produces ordered crystals, while fast settling produces a disordered heap. D directly supports this because it links slow settling to evenly spaced, colorful deposits and fast settling to jumbled, dull ones. A only tells you how sphere size affects sinking speed and says nothing about order. B is about layer thickness, which has nothing to do with whether the spheres line up neatly. C actually weakens the hypothesis, since it shows that fast settling gives the same ordered colors as slow settling.
g.design: 쉬운 난이도에 맞춰 단일 인과 규칙(느린 침강 → 질서)만 확인하도록 했다. 오답은 같은 문장 틀을 쓰되 관련 없는 변수(크기, 두께)나 반대 결과를 담았고, 질문에는 정답의 핵심어를 쓰지 않았다.
