- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: physical science — Osmotic pressure in polymer solutions and membrane transport driving force for reverse osmosis desalination

g.passage: In reverse osmosis desalination, pumps push seawater against a membrane that lets water molecules pass but blocks dissolved salt. Seawater naturally resists this process: its dissolved salt creates an osmotic pressure that pulls water back toward the salty side. Water flows through the membrane toward the fresh side only when the pressure applied by the pumps is greater than this osmotic pressure. Engineers note that saltier water has a higher osmotic pressure than less salty water. Therefore, compared with a plant treating mildly salty groundwater, a plant treating highly salty seawater will likely ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: need its pumps to apply more pressure before any fresh water moves through the membrane.
need its pumps to apply less pressure, since salt helps water cross the membrane.
need its pumps to apply the same pressure, since membranes block salt equally well in both cases.
need its pumps to apply no pressure, since osmotic pressure alone moves water to the fresh side.
g.explanation: 지문에 따르면 펌프 압력이 삼투압보다 커야만 물이 담수 쪽으로 흐르고, 염도가 높을수록 삼투압도 높다. 따라서 염도가 높은 바닷물을 처리하는 시설은 더 큰 압력이 필요하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 염분이 물의 이동을 돕는다고 보지만, 지문에서 염분은 물을 짠 쪽으로 다시 끌어당긴다. C는 막의 염분 차단 성능만 보고 염도에 따른 삼투압 차이를 무시한다. D는 삼투압의 방향을 거꾸로 이해한 것으로, 삼투압은 물을 짠 쪽으로 끌어당긴다.
g.explanation_en: The passage says water reaches the fresh side only when pump pressure is greater than the osmotic pressure, and saltier water has a higher osmotic pressure. So a plant treating very salty seawater has to push harder, which makes A correct. B is wrong because salt doesn't help water cross the membrane; it pulls water back toward the salty side. C focuses on how well the membrane blocks salt and ignores the fact that osmotic pressure changes with saltiness. D gets the direction backward: osmotic pressure works against the flow toward the fresh side, so it can't move water there by itself.
g.design: Easy: the passage directly states the two rules (applied pressure must be greater than osmotic pressure, and more salt means higher osmotic pressure), so one simple deduction gives the answer. Each wrong choice reflects a common misunderstanding of how osmosis works.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: physical science — Spark plasma sintering rapid densification and grain growth suppression in ceramic composite materials

g.passage: When ceramic powders are heated to make solid parts, two things happen at once: the tiny particles fuse together and the gaps between them close, a process called densification, and the small crystals, or grains, inside the material slowly grow larger. Engineers want high density but small grains, because ceramics with small grains tend to be stronger. Grain growth depends heavily on how long the material stays at high temperature. In spark plasma sintering, an electric current passes directly through the powder, heating it so quickly that a part can become fully dense in minutes rather than the hours required by conventional furnaces. Therefore, compared with ceramics made in conventional furnaces, ceramics made by spark plasma sintering are likely to ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: have larger grains, since electric current makes the material hotter than a furnace does.
have smaller grains, since the material spends much less time at high temperature.
have lower density, since the powder is heated for too short a time to fuse completely.
have the same grain size, since grain growth is not affected by the heating method.
g.explanation: 지문은 결정립 성장이 고온에 머무는 시간에 크게 좌우된다고 밝히고, 스파크 플라스마 소결은 몇 시간 대신 몇 분 만에 치밀화를 끝낸다고 말한다. 따라서 고온 노출 시간이 짧아 결정립이 더 작을 것이므로 B가 정답이다. A는 온도가 더 높다는 근거가 지문에 없고, 핵심 요인인 시간을 무시한다. C는 지문에서 몇 분 만에 '완전히 치밀해진다'고 했으므로 틀리다. D는 결정립 성장이 시간에 좌우된다는 지문 내용과 모순된다.
g.explanation_en: The text says grain growth depends heavily on how long the material stays at high temperature, and that spark plasma sintering makes a part fully dense in minutes instead of hours. Less time at high temperature means less grain growth, so B is correct. A is wrong because the text never says the material gets hotter, and it ignores the key factor, which is time. C contradicts the text, which says the parts become fully dense. D is wrong because the text directly ties grain growth to heating time, and that time is very different between the two methods.
g.design: 쉬운 난이도: 규칙 하나(결정립 성장은 시간에 좌우됨)에 '분 대 시간'이라는 직접 단서를 적용하는 한 단계 추론. 오답은 흔한 오개념(전류가 더 뜨겁다, 너무 빨라서 덜 치밀하다, 방법과 무관하다)을 같은 문장 틀로 썼다.

c.instruction: 지문에 가설(주장)만 제시하고, 그 가설을 뒷받침하려면 어떤 추가 증거나 결과가 있어야 하는지 묻는 문항을 만들어라. 정답은 지문에 없는 가상의 결과이지만 가설의 논리 구조와 정확히 들어맞아야 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 '가설과 무관한 사실', '가설을 반박하는 결과', '이미 지문에 있는 사실을 재진술한 것'으로 구성하라.
c.seed: physical science — Ziegler-Natta catalyst stereospecific polymerization and polypropylene tacticity control in industrial synthesis

g.passage: When propylene is polymerized with a Ziegler-Natta catalyst, the resulting polypropylene is usually isotactic: nearly every methyl group along the chain points to the same side, which lets the chains pack into rigid crystals. Chemists have long debated where this stereochemical control comes from. One view holds that the growing chain end steers each new monomer. A competing hypothesis, advanced by researchers studying titanium chloride catalysts, holds that control comes from the chiral geometry of the metal site itself: the asymmetric arrangement of atoms around each titanium center lets an incoming propylene molecule bind in only one orientation, no matter how the chain attached to that site happens to be arranged.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the competing hypothesis about the source of stereochemical control?
options: When the reaction temperature was raised, the catalyst produced polypropylene chains of higher average molecular weight but similar crystallinity.
When a chain grown on the catalyst contained an occasional misinserted unit, the monomers added after that error took on the misinserted unit's orientation and carried it forward along the chain.
When a chain grown on the catalyst contained an occasional misinserted unit, the monomers added after that error went back to the orientation they had before the error.
Polypropylene produced with the titanium chloride catalyst was found to have methyl groups that mostly pointed to the same side of the chain, so it was stiff and highly crystalline.
g.design: 가설의 핵심인 '사슬 배열과 무관하게 금속 자리가 방향을 결정'을 검증할 가상 실험(삽입 오류 후 원래 방향 복귀)을 정답으로 했고, 오답은 무관한 사실, 사슬 말단 제어를 지지하는 반박 결과, 지문의 이소택틱 사실을 재진술한 것으로 구성했다.
g.explanation:
정답 C: 경쟁 가설은 입체 제어가 성장 사슬의 배열과 관계없이 티타늄 자리의 키랄 구조에서 나온다고 본다. 사슬에 잘못 삽입된 단위가 있어도 다음 단량체들이 오류 이전의 방향으로 돌아간다면, 방향을 정하는 것은 사슬 말단이 아니라 금속 자리라는 뜻이므로 가설을 직접 지지한다.
A (무관한 사실): 온도에 따른 분자량 변화는 입체 제어가 어디서 오는지와 상관이 없다.
B (반박하는 결과): 새 단량체가 오류 단위의 방향을 따른다는 것은 사슬 말단이 다음 삽입을 조종한다는 뜻이므로, 경쟁 가설이 아니라 첫 번째 견해를 지지한다.
D (재진술): 이소택틱하고 결정성이 높다는 내용은 지문에 이미 나와 있다. 두 견해 모두 이 결과를 설명할 수 있으므로 둘 중 어느 쪽인지 가려 주지 못한다.
g.explanation_en:
Correct answer C: The competing hypothesis says stereocontrol comes from the chiral titanium site, no matter how the growing chain is arranged. Suppose a chain picks up a misinserted unit, and the monomers added after it go back to their earlier orientation. Then the chain end isn't setting the orientation. The metal site is, so this finding directly supports the hypothesis.
A (irrelevant fact): How temperature affects molecular weight tells you nothing about where stereocontrol comes from.
B (weakening result): If new monomers copy the error's orientation, the chain end is steering each insertion. That supports the chain-end view, not the competing hypothesis.
D (restatement): The passage already says the polymer is isotactic and crystalline. Both views can explain that, so this finding doesn't help you choose between them.

c.instruction: 그래프나 표에 두 개 이상의 변수(또는 텍스트 설명과 그래프 수치)가 함께 제시된 자료를 주고, 두 요소를 동시에 봐야만 결론을 낼 수 있는 질문을 만들어라. 정답은 두 변수를 모두 반영해야 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 '한쪽 변수만 본 결론', '다른 쪽 변수만 본 결론', '자료에 없는 제3의 변수로 결론'을 만든 것으로 구성하라.
c.seed: physical science — Hydrophobic coating contact angle measurement and lotus leaf superhydrophobic surface mimicry self-cleaning

g.passage: The lotus leaf stays clean because water beads up on its waxy, micro-bumpy surface and rolls away, carrying dust with it. Engineers who try to copy this effect usually measure a coating's static contact angle, which is the angle a resting droplet makes with the surface. Angles above 150° count as "superhydrophobic." Materials scientist Leena Varga and colleagues argue that this measurement alone is misleading. Some surfaces, such as rose petals, have very high contact angles, yet droplets stick to them even when the surface is tipped upside down. Varga's team therefore claims that a coating will reliably clean itself only if it has a high static contact angle and also a low sliding angle, which is the tilt at which a droplet starts to move.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Varga's team's claim?
options: Across twelve tested coatings, those with higher static contact angles removed, on average, more applied dust during simulated rainfall than those with lower static contact angles did.
Across twelve tested coatings, those on which droplets began moving at tilts below 10° removed, on average, more applied dust during simulated rainfall than those requiring steeper tilts did.
Across twelve tested coatings, thicker coatings removed more applied dust during simulated rainfall than thinner coatings did, whatever their contact angles or sliding angles.

Across twelve tested coatings, those with contact angles above 150° and sliding angles below 10° removed most applied dust during simulated rainfall, while those meeting only one of these thresholds removed little.
g.explanation:
정답 D: 연구팀은 높은 정적 접촉각과 낮은 미끄럼각이 '둘 다' 있어야 자가세정이 된다고 주장한다. D는 두 조건을 모두 갖춘 코팅만 먼지를 잘 제거했고, 한 조건만 갖춘 코팅은 거의 제거하지 못했다고 보여 주므로 두 조건이 모두 필요하다는 점을 직접 뒷받침한다.
A(접촉각만 봄): 접촉각이 높을수록 평균적으로 더 잘 닦였다는 결과일 뿐이어서 미끄럼각도 필요하다는 점은 보여 주지 못한다. 오히려 접촉각 하나로 충분하다는, 연구팀이 반박하는 관점에 더 가깝다.
B(미끄럼각만 봄): 미끄럼각과 세정 효과의 관계만 보여 주며, 높은 접촉각도 함께 있어야 하는지는 알 수 없다.
C(제3의 변수): 코팅 두께는 지문의 주장과 관련이 없고, 접촉각·미끄럼각과 관계없이 결과가 달라졌다면 오히려 주장을 약화시킨다.
g.explanation_en:
Correct answer D: The team claims that reliable self-cleaning requires both a high static contact angle and a low sliding angle. D shows that only coatings meeting both thresholds removed most of the dust, while coatings meeting just one threshold removed little. That shows both conditions are needed, so it directly supports the claim.
A (contact angle only): A only shows that higher contact angles were linked to better cleaning on average. It says nothing about whether a low sliding angle is also needed. In fact, it fits the single-measurement view that the team rejects.
B (sliding angle only): B links cleaning to sliding angle alone. It doesn't show whether a high contact angle is also required.
C (third variable): Coating thickness isn't part of the claim. If thickness predicted cleaning regardless of either angle, the claim would actually be weakened.
g.design: The passage combines two variables, static contact angle and sliding angle, so only the option that shows both conditions are needed together (D) supports the claim. The wrong options are built from contact angle alone (A), sliding angle alone (B), and a third variable that isn't in the passage, coating thickness (C), and all four options use the same sentence frame.

c.instruction: 지문에 상관관계나 동시 발생 사실만 제시하고, 이를 근거로 특정 가설(주장)의 인과성을 지지하는지 판단해야 하는 문항을 만들어라. 정답은 인과 방향과 대안 설명 가능성을 함께 고려해 타당하게 지지하는 것이어야 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 '상관을 그대로 인과로 오해', '인과 방향을 반대로 설정', '무관한 제3의 원인을 인과로 제시'로 구성하라.
c.seed: physical science — Thermal cycling induced fatigue crack initiation in solder joints and mechanical reliability microelectronics

g.passage: Engineers examining failed circuit boards returned from automotive customers noticed that solder joints with large intermetallic layers—brittle copper-tin compounds that form where solder meets a copper pad—were also the joints most likely to contain fatigue cracks. Materials scientist Leena Varkonyi has proposed that the thick intermetallic layers cause the cracks: because these compounds are stiff and brittle, she argues, they concentrate the stress produced as the board repeatedly heats and cools, letting cracks start there. Some of her colleagues point out, however, that joints on hotter parts of a board both grow thicker intermetallic layers and go through larger temperature swings, so the two features might simply occur together.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Varkonyi's hypothesis?
options: When identical boards were put through the same temperature cycles, joints whose intermetallic layers had been thickened in advance by extra heating before testing developed cracks after fewer cycles than joints with thin layers.

When boards from many customers were surveyed, joints with thicker intermetallic layers were found to contain cracks more often than joints with thinner layers, no matter which vehicle model the boards came from.

When cracked joints were compared with joints that had not cracked, the intermetallic layers were found to have thickened more quickly after the cracks appeared, as heat built up along the crack surfaces.

When boards were mounted near engines rather than in cabin areas, the joints went through larger temperature swings and developed cracks after fewer cycles, whatever the thickness of their intermetallic layers.
g.explanation:
정답 A: 온도 사이클 조건을 똑같이 맞추고 금속간화합물층 두께만 미리 조작했는데도 두꺼운 층의 균열이 더 빨리 생겼다. 동료들이 제시한 대안 설명(뜨거운 위치가 두께와 균열을 둘 다 키운다)을 차단하고, 두께가 균열보다 먼저 정해졌으므로 인과 방향도 확인해 준다.
B(상관을 인과로 오해): 차종이 달라도 같은 상관이 나온다는 것은 상관을 재확인할 뿐이다. 보드 위 온도라는 교란 요인은 그대로 남아 있다.
C(인과 방향 반대): 균열이 생긴 뒤 층이 두꺼워졌다면 균열이 원인이고 두께가 결과라는 뜻이다. 가설과 정반대 방향이다.
D(제3의 원인): 층 두께와 상관없이 온도 변동폭이 균열을 일으킨다는 결과로, 동료들의 대안 설명을 지지하고 가설은 약하게 만든다.
g.explanation_en:
A is correct. All boards went through the same temperature cycles, and only the intermetallic thickness was changed, set in advance. Joints with thicker layers still cracked sooner. This rules out the colleagues' alternative explanation, that hotter locations cause both thick layers and cracks. It also shows the right causal direction, because the thickness was in place before any cracking.
B mistakes correlation for causation. Finding the same link across vehicle models only repeats the correlation. Board temperature could still be causing both thick layers and cracks.
C reverses the causal direction. If layers thickened after cracks appeared, the cracks are driving the thickening, not the other way around.
D points to a third factor. It shows temperature swings cause cracking regardless of layer thickness, which supports the colleagues' alternative and weakens Varkonyi's hypothesis.
g.design: 지문에는 두께와 균열이 함께 나타난다는 상관과 교란 요인(온도)만 제시했다. 정답은 교란 요인을 통제한 상태에서 원인을 미리 조작한 실험이다. 오답은 같은 'When..., ...' 문장 틀로 각각 상관 반복, 인과 방향 반대, 제3의 원인을 담았다.

c.instruction: 지문에 '한때 ~라고 여겨졌으나(통념)' 다음 'however/but/실제로는' 류의 전환어와 함께 이를 뒤집는 새 증거나 반박 문장을 제시하고, 빈칸이 그 반박된 결과를 표현하도록 한다. 정답은 통념과 정반대 방향의 의미를 가진 어휘로 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 통념 쪽 단어를 그대로 쓴 것, (2) 전환어를 못 읽고 통념과 같은 방향이지만 강도만 다른 단어, (3) 반박 대상과 무관한 제3의 의미 단어로 구성한다. 전환 지점 앞뒤 문장만으로 답이 결정되게 하고 문장 길이나 어휘 난이도는 중간 수준을 유지한다.
c.seed: physical science — Rheological thixotropy non-Newtonian fluid viscosity time-dependency in shear-thinning paint formulations

g.passage: For decades, paint chemists assumed that a shear-thinning paint's drop in viscosity under a brush depended only on how hard it was being stirred or spread: remove the force, and the paint would instantly return to its original thickness. However, rheologist Mei Tanaka's measurements of several commercial latex formulations revealed that viscosity recovery after brushing was far from immediate, with some paints needing nearly a minute to thicken again. This lag, Tanaka argued, shows that the paints' structural rebuilding is ______ rather than instantaneous, a property that lets fresh coats level out brush marks before they set.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: immediate
gradual
abrupt
reversible
g.explanation: 정답 B(gradual): 'However' 뒤에서 점도 회복이 즉각적이지 않고 거의 1분이 걸린다고 했으므로, 구조 재형성은 '점진적'이며 'rather than instantaneous'와도 대비된다. A(immediate)는 반박된 통념(즉시 회복)을 그대로 쓴 단어다. C(abrupt)는 전환어를 놓치고 통념과 같은 '빠름' 방향을 더 세게 말한 단어다. D(reversible)는 회복이 일어난다는 사실과는 맞지만 쟁점인 속도(시간 의존성)와 관계없는 제3의 의미라 'rather than instantaneous'와 대비가 되지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: B (gradual) is correct. After "However," the text says viscosity recovery was "far from immediate," with some paints taking nearly a minute. So the rebuilding happens gradually, which fits the contrast "rather than instantaneous." A (immediate) just repeats the old assumption that the text rejects. C (abrupt) comes from missing the shift: it points the same "fast" way as the old view, only more strongly. D (reversible) is true in the sense that the paint does recover, but it says nothing about speed, which is the actual point here, so it doesn't work as the opposite of "instantaneous."
g.design: 통념(즉시 회복)→However→지연 증거 구조로, 정답은 통념 반대(gradual), 오답은 통념어·같은 방향 강화어·무관한 제3 의미로 구성.

c.instruction: 지문에 'is not X, but rather Y' 또는 'it isn't that A; instead B' 형태로 부정어 뒤에 대조 표현이 이어지는 문장을 만들고, 빈칸이 그 대조 표현(B) 자리에 오게 한다. 정답은 부정된 개념(X)과 반대 극성을 가진 어휘로 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 부정어를 무시하고 X와 같은 의미 단어, (2) 부정 구조를 이중으로 잘못 해석해 극성을 다시 뒤집은 단어, (3) 대조 구조와 무관한 유사 발음/철자 단어로 구성한다.
c.seed: physical science — Crystallographic phase transformation martensitic versus displacive mechanisms in steel tempering heat treatment

g.passage: When steel is quenched from high temperature, its iron atoms rearrange into a hard, needle-like phase called martensite. Metallurgists stress that this change is not a slow migration in which individual carbon atoms diffuse one by one across long distances through the crystal; instead, it is a ______ shear, in which entire planes of iron atoms shift together by less than one atomic spacing, often in microseconds. Only during later tempering, when the steel is reheated, does carbon diffusion begin to play a significant role.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: piecemeal
protracted
concerted
conceited
g.explanation: 정답 C(concerted). 'not A; instead B' 구조에서 부정된 것은 원자가 '하나씩(one by one)' 천천히 확산하는 개별적·점진적 과정이다. 빈칸 뒤 '전체 원자면이 함께(together) 이동'한다는 설명이 B를 규정하므로, 개별성과 반대 극성인 '일제히 협조된'이라는 뜻의 concerted가 맞다. A(piecemeal, 조금씩): 부정어를 무시하고 부정된 개념 'one by one'과 같은 뜻을 고른 오답. B(protracted, 오래 끄는): 'not slow'를 이중으로 잘못 읽어 다시 '느린' 쪽으로 극성을 뒤집은 오답으로, 'microseconds'와 모순된다. D(conceited, 자만하는): concerted와 철자·발음만 비슷할 뿐 원자 운동을 묘사할 수 없다.
g.explanation_en: The answer is C, "concerted." The sentence uses a "not A; instead B" structure. What gets rejected (A) is a slow process where atoms move individually, "one by one." The words after the blank describe B: whole planes of atoms "shift together" in microseconds. So the blank needs a word with the opposite polarity from individual, step-by-step motion. "Concerted," meaning coordinated or done all together, fits. A, "piecemeal," means little by little. It ignores the negation and simply restates the rejected one-by-one idea. B, "protracted," means drawn out. It flips the polarity a second time, back to "slow," which contradicts "microseconds." D, "conceited," means vain. It looks and sounds like "concerted" but has nothing to do with how atoms move.
g.design: I put the blank in the "instead" slot after a negated idea of individual, diffusive motion. The distractors are a synonym of the negated idea (it ignores the negation), a word that flips the polarity back again (double negation), and a word that only looks or sounds similar.

c.instruction: 지문을 두 단계(예: 상황 묘사 후 화자의 숙고, 또는 기존 주장 소개 후 저자의 반박/선언)로 구성하고, 빈칸을 두 번째 단계의 시작 지점에 배치해 앞 단계와 다른 서술 기능을 하도록 한다. 정답은 두 번째 단계의 기능(숙고, 반박, 선언 등)에 맞는 어휘로 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 첫 번째 단계에 어울리는 단어, (2) 두 단계 어디에도 맞지 않는 중립적 단어, (3) 의미는 비슷하나 문장이 요구하는 품사/기능이 다른 단어로 구성한다.
c.seed: physical science — Electrokinetic flow zeta potential and electrophoretic particle motion in microfluidic channel design

g.passage: In microfluidic chip design, engineers have long treated the zeta potential—the electric potential at the slip plane near a charged channel wall—as a fixed property of the wall material, so that the speed of electroosmotic flow could be predicted from the applied voltage alone. Recent experiments by chemical engineer Priya Raman, however, ______ this assumption: by showing that proteins adsorbing onto the wall during operation steadily shift the zeta potential, Raman demonstrates that flow rates and the electrophoretic separation of particles can drift over a single run.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: rely on
address
doubtful of
undermine
g.explanation: 지문은 두 단계로 되어 있다. 먼저 엔지니어들이 제타 전위를 고정값으로 여겨 왔다는 기존 가정을 소개하고, "however" 뒤에서 Raman의 실험이 그 가정에 반박한다. 콜론 뒤를 보면 운전 중 단백질이 벽에 흡착해 제타 전위가 계속 바뀌므로 유속과 분리가 한 번의 실행 동안에도 변할 수 있다고 한다. 즉 이 실험은 가정의 근거를 약화시키므로 정답은 D "undermine"이다. A "rely on"(의존하다)은 가정을 받아들이던 첫 번째 단계에나 맞는 말이라 "however"와 콜론 뒤의 반증과 충돌한다. B "address"(다루다)는 중립적인 말이라 실험이 가정을 반박한다는 점을 담지 못하므로 정확하지 않다. C "doubtful of"는 '의심하는'이라는 뜻은 비슷하지만 형용사구라서 주어 "experiments" 뒤에 와야 할 동사 자리에 들어가지 못하고, 실험이 무언가를 의심한다는 의미도 어색하다.
g.explanation_en: The text has two stages. First it describes an old assumption: engineers have treated zeta potential as fixed. Then "however" introduces Raman's challenge to that assumption. The colon spells out what she found: proteins sticking to the wall change the zeta potential, so flow rates and particle separation can drift during a single run. Her experiments therefore weaken the basis of the assumption, so the answer is D, "undermine." A, "rely on," fits the first stage, where engineers accepted the assumption. It contradicts "however" and the evidence after the colon. B, "address," is too neutral. It doesn't say that the experiments push back against the assumption. C, "doubtful of," has a similar meaning, but it's an adjective phrase. The sentence needs a verb after the subject "experiments," and experiments can't be "doubtful" anyway.
g.design: 빈칸을 두 번째 단계(반박)가 시작되는 지점에 두었다. 오답은 첫 번째 단계에 맞는 말(rely on), 중립적인 말(address), 뜻은 비슷하지만 품사가 다른 말(doubtful of)로 구성했다.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: physical science — Viscoelastic polymer stress relaxation modulus decay and damping mechanisms in tire rubber applications

g.passage: When a tire rubber sample is stretched and then held at a fixed length, the force needed to keep it stretched does not stay constant. Instead, the stress inside the rubber slowly ______ over time as its long polymer chains shift and untangle. Engineers measure this drop to predict how well a tire will absorb bumps and vibrations on the road.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: decreases
accumulates
intensifies
stabilizes
g.explanation: 지문은 고무를 고정된 길이로 유지할 때 필요한 힘이 일정하지 않으며, 엔지니어가 이 '감소(drop)'를 측정한다고 직접 밝힌다. 따라서 응력이 시간에 따라 줄어든다는 뜻의 A(decreases)가 정답이다. B(accumulates)와 C(intensifies)는 응력이 커진다는 의미로 'drop'과 정반대이다. D(stabilizes)는 응력이 일정해진다는 뜻으로 '일정하게 유지되지 않는다'는 진술과 모순된다.
g.explanation_en: The text says the force needed to hold the stretched rubber does not stay constant, and that engineers measure "this drop." So the stress must go down over time, which makes A (decreases) correct. B (accumulates) and C (intensifies) both mean the stress grows, the opposite of a drop. D (stabilizes) means the stress levels off and stays steady, which contradicts the statement that it does not stay constant.
g.design: 쉬운 난이도: 빈칸 뒤 문장의 'this drop'과 앞 문장의 'does not stay constant'라는 직접 단서만 보면 한 단계로 풀린다. 오답은 같은 품사(동사 3인칭)로 증가와 안정이라는 전형적인 반대 방향 오개념을 넣었다.

c.instruction:
- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: physical science — Nanoparticle agglomeration van der Waals forces and dispersion stability in colloidal suspension stabilization

g.passage: When tiny particles are mixed into a liquid, weak attractive forces called van der Waals forces pull them toward one another, causing them to clump into larger masses that sink. To keep the particles evenly spread, chemists often coat them with molecules that push neighboring particles apart. These coatings ______ the attraction between particles, so the mixture stays uniform for months instead of separating within hours.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: strengthen
counteract
reveal
imitate
g.explanation: 지문은 코팅이 입자들을 서로 밀어내어 혼합물이 오래 균일하게 유지된다고 설명하므로, 코팅은 입자 간 인력에 맞서 그 효과를 상쇄해야 한다. 따라서 '대항하다, 상쇄하다'를 뜻하는 B가 정답이다. A는 인력을 강화한다는 뜻이라 입자가 오히려 더 빨리 뭉치게 되므로 결과와 반대된다. C는 인력을 드러낸다는 뜻으로, 혼합물이 안정되는 이유를 설명하지 못한다. D는 인력을 흉내 낸다는 뜻이라 입자를 밀어낸다는 코팅의 역할과 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The text says the coatings push neighboring particles apart, which keeps the mixture uniform for a long time, so the coatings must work against the attraction between particles. That makes B, meaning "to oppose or cancel the effect of," the best choice. A would mean the coatings make the attraction stronger, which would make the particles clump faster—the opposite of what the text describes. C would mean the coatings simply make the attraction visible, which doesn't explain why the mixture stays stable. D would mean the coatings copy the attraction, which doesn't fit their job of pushing particles apart.
g.design: This is an easy item that tests one direct clue. The phrase "push neighboring particles apart" and the stable result point straight to a word meaning "oppose." The wrong answers are common verbs that a student might pick by misreading the cause-and-effect relationship.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Perovskite solar cell halide stability and moisture-induced degradation mechanisms reducing photovoltaic efficiency longevity

g.passage:
Perovskite solar cells have attracted intense interest because they can convert sunlight to electricity nearly as efficiently as conventional silicon cells while being far cheaper to manufacture. Their weakness is durability. The light-absorbing layer in many perovskite cells contains methylammonium lead iodide, a crystal whose organic and halide components are held together by relatively weak bonds. When water molecules from humid air penetrate the layer, they form a hydrated intermediate that gradually breaks the crystal apart, releasing methylammonium and leaving behind lead iodide, which absorbs visible light poorly.

Engineers have often responded by sealing cells in protective coatings, but such encapsulation adds cost and can fail at the edges over time. Materials scientist Leena Okafor and her colleagues pursued a different strategy: replacing part of the methylammonium with cesium, an inorganic ion that binds more tightly within the crystal. In their tests, cells with the modified composition retained most of their initial output after weeks of exposure to damp air, whereas unmodified cells lost much of theirs within days, suggesting that stability may be built into the absorber itself rather than supplied only from outside.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Because moisture converts methylammonium lead iodide into lead iodide, perovskite cells are unlikely to ever match the efficiency of conventional silicon cells.
Protective coatings have proven to be the most reliable way to keep humid air from degrading the light-absorbing layer of perovskite cells.
Research suggests that changing the chemical makeup of the perovskite layer can reduce the moisture damage that limits how long these cells perform well.
Adding cesium to perovskite cells raises their initial efficiency above that of cells made only with methylammonium lead iodide.
g.explanation: 지문은 페로브스카이트 전지가 습기에 의해 결정이 분해되어 수명이 짧다는 문제를 제시한 뒤, Okafor 연구팀이 흡수층 조성 자체(세슘 일부 치환)를 바꿔 습기 저항성을 높였다는 결과를 중심으로 전개되므로 C가 정답이다. A는 습기 분해 메커니즘은 맞지만, 지문은 효율이 실리콘에 거의 근접한다고 했고 수명 문제를 다룰 뿐 효율 한계를 주장하지 않는다. B는 보호 코팅이 언급되긴 하나 비용과 가장자리 결함이 지적되며 대안이 제시되므로 '가장 신뢰할 만한 방법'은 지문과 반대이다. D는 세슘 첨가를 다루지만, 지문은 초기 효율이 아니라 시간이 지나도 출력을 유지하는 정도를 비교했다.
g.explanation_en: The text first describes how moisture breaks down the perovskite crystal and shortens cell life, then centers on Okafor's team changing the absorber's own composition (partly swapping in cesium) to resist that damage, so C is correct. A gets the degradation mechanism right, but the text says perovskites are nearly as efficient as silicon; the issue is durability, not an efficiency ceiling. B mentions coatings, but the text points out their cost and edge failures and presents an alternative, so calling them the most reliable approach contradicts the passage. D involves cesium, but the study compared how well output was retained over time, not initial efficiency.
g.design: 오답 A·B·D가 각각 지문의 실제 세부(분해 메커니즘, 코팅, 세슘)를 포함해 부분적으로 맞아 보이게 하고, 문제 제기와 해결 연구를 연결해야 정답을 고를 수 있게 했다. 정답은 'cesium', 'durability' 같은 표면어를 피하고 다른 말로 바꿔 썼다.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Magnetorheological fluid damper controllable viscosity and electromagnetic coil activation in seismic building isolation systems

g.passage: Engineers protecting buildings from earthquakes have long relied on passive dampers, devices filled with oil that resist motion by a fixed amount. Such dampers work well for the shaking they were designed for but cannot adjust when an earthquake proves stronger or weaker than expected. Magnetorheological (MR) dampers offer an alternative. They contain a fluid with suspended iron particles; when an electromagnetic coil inside the damper is switched on, the particles line up into chains, and the fluid thickens from a liquid with the consistency of motor oil to something close to a soft solid within milliseconds. By varying the current, sensors and a controller can tune the damper's resistance as ground motion changes. Because the coil needs only about as much power as a household light bulb, MR dampers can keep running on backup batteries even when an earthquake knocks out the electrical grid. This is an important advantage, since the stronger kinds of adjustable systems need large power supplies that may fail at exactly the moment they are needed.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: MR dampers resist ground motion more strongly than passive dampers because their iron particles form chains that turn the fluid into a solid.
MR dampers are useful mainly because they draw so little electricity that they can keep working even after the electrical grid fails.
MR dampers are better than passive dampers because sensors allow them to detect an earthquake before its strongest shaking reaches a building.
MR dampers can change their resistance to match shifting ground motion, and they need little enough power to remain dependable during an earthquake.
g.explanation: 지문은 고정된 저항을 가진 수동형 댐퍼와 대비하여, MR 댐퍼가 전류 조절을 통해 지반 운동에 맞춰 저항을 조절할 수 있고 적은 전력만 필요해 정전 시에도 작동한다는 두 가지 장점을 함께 제시한다. D는 이 두 요소를 모두 담고 있다. A는 입자가 사슬을 이루는 세부를 담았지만 글의 핵심은 저항의 '조절 가능성'이지 더 강한 저항이 아니며, 유체가 '부드러운 고체에 가깝게' 될 뿐이라는 점도 왜곡한다. B는 전력 측면이라는 맞는 근거를 담았지만 그것만이 주된 장점이라고 하여 핵심인 조절 기능을 빠뜨린다. C는 센서를 언급하지만 지진을 미리 감지한다는 내용은 지문에 없다.
g.explanation_en: The text contrasts passive dampers, which have fixed resistance, with MR dampers, which can tune their resistance as ground motion changes and need so little power that they keep working during grid failures. D captures both of these points. A uses a real detail about particle chains, but the text's focus is adjustability, not greater strength, and it says the fluid becomes only close to a soft solid. B correctly mentions the low power use but treats it as the main benefit, leaving out the central idea of adjustable resistance. C mentions sensors, but the text never says they detect earthquakes before the shaking arrives.
g.design: 조절 가능성과 저전력 신뢰성이라는 두 정보를 연결해야 하며, 오답 A·B는 각각 지문의 실제 세부를 담고 있지만 일부만 다루거나 과장해 정답과 비교해야 배제된다.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Enzymatic biofuel cell glucose oxidation and direct electron transfer catalysis for implantable bioelectric power generation

g.passage: Enzymatic biofuel cells could one day power implanted medical devices by drawing on glucose already present in the body. In these cells, an enzyme such as glucose oxidase strips electrons from glucose at one electrode. Early designs relied on small "mediator" molecules to shuttle those electrons from the enzyme to the electrode, but mediators can leak into surrounding tissue and slowly lose effectiveness. Engineers have therefore pursued direct electron transfer, in which the enzyme passes electrons straight to the electrode surface. The difficulty is that the enzyme's active site is buried deep inside its protein structure, too far from the electrode for electrons to cross efficiently. Recent work suggests a solution: by anchoring enzymes to carbon nanotubes oriented so that the active site faces the conductive surface, researchers have shortened that distance enough to produce usable current without any mediator.
g.question: According to the text, what has kept direct electron transfer from working well in enzymatic biofuel cells?
options: The part of the enzyme where glucose reacts sits too far from the electrode for electrons to move across easily.
The small molecules used to carry electrons tend to escape into nearby tissue and degrade over time.
The glucose available inside the body is too scarce to supply electrons at a steady rate.
The carbon nanotubes used as electrodes tend to block the enzyme from contacting glucose.
g.design: 정답은 'buried deep inside... too far'를 패러프레이즈해 표면 일치를 피했고, B는 지문에 있지만 매개체 방식의 문제(다른 방식)라 두 정보를 구분해야 배제되며, D는 해결책을 문제로 뒤집은 부분 근거 오답이다.
g.explanation: 지문은 직접 전자 전달의 어려움이 효소의 활성 부위가 단백질 구조 깊숙이 묻혀 있어 전극과의 거리가 너무 멀다는 점이라고 밝히므로 A가 정답이다. B의 누출과 효과 저하는 지문에 나오지만, 직접 전자 전달이 아니라 그 이전 매개체 방식의 문제이다. C의 포도당 부족은 지문 어디에도 언급되지 않는다. D는 탄소 나노튜브를 장애물로 묘사하지만, 지문에서 나노튜브는 문제를 해결하는 수단이다.
g.explanation_en: The text says the difficulty with direct electron transfer is that the enzyme's active site is buried deep inside the protein, too far from the electrode for electrons to cross efficiently, so A is correct. B describes leaking and loss of effectiveness, which the text does mention, but those are problems with the earlier mediator-based designs, not with direct electron transfer. C, a shortage of glucose, is never mentioned. D treats carbon nanotubes as an obstacle, but in the text they are the solution that shortens the distance.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Metamaterial negative refractive index and acoustic cloaking design bending sound waves around protected objects

g.passage:
Engineers designing acoustic cloaks often borrow an idea first developed for light: metamaterials, structures built from repeating units smaller than the waves they manipulate, can be arranged to give a material properties no natural substance has, including a negative refractive index that bends waves the "wrong" way. By grading these properties carefully, a shell of metamaterial can steer incoming sound around an object and release it on the far side as if nothing had been in the way. Early laboratory demonstrations were striking, but they worked only within a narrow band of frequencies, because the tiny resonating units that produce the unusual behavior respond strongly to some pitches and hardly at all to others.

Researchers at several universities have therefore shifted their focus. Rather than pursuing a perfect cloak, many now design shells that hide objects from the specific frequencies that matter in a given setting, such as the sonar pulses used to locate submarines or the low hum of machinery in a factory. This narrower aim, they argue, turns a laboratory curiosity into something that could actually be built and used.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Because metamaterials can produce a negative refractive index, engineers have succeeded in building acoustic cloaks that conceal objects from sound at all frequencies.
Because metamaterial cloaks perform well only over limited frequency ranges, engineers are increasingly tailoring them to block particular sounds relevant to practical uses.
Because acoustic cloaks were adapted from designs for light, engineers have found that they are more effective at hiding submarines than at reducing factory noise.
Because the resonating units in metamaterials are smaller than sound waves, engineers have abandoned acoustic cloaking in favor of cloaks that manipulate light.
g.explanation: 첫 단락은 메타물질 음향 클로킹이 좁은 주파수 대역에서만 작동한다는 한계를 제시하고, 둘째 단락은 그 때문에 연구자들이 특정 상황에 중요한 주파수만 숨기는 실용적 설계로 방향을 바꿨다고 설명하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 음의 굴절률이라는 세부는 맞지만 '모든 주파수'에서 성공했다는 것은 지문과 정반대이다. C는 빛에서 아이디어를 빌렸다는 점과 잠수함·공장 예시를 언급하지만 두 용도의 효과를 비교한 내용은 지문에 없다. D는 단위 구조가 파장보다 작다는 세부를 쓰지만 음향 클로킹을 포기했다는 주장은 근거가 없다.
g.explanation_en: The first paragraph lays out a limitation: metamaterial acoustic cloaks work only within narrow frequency bands. The second paragraph explains that because of this, researchers now design cloaks that hide objects from the specific frequencies that matter in a given setting, so B is correct. A correctly mentions the negative refractive index, but it claims success at all frequencies, which is the opposite of what the text says. C uses the light origin and the submarine and factory examples, but the text never compares how well the cloaks work for those two uses. D uses the detail that the units are smaller than the waves, but nothing in the text suggests engineers abandoned acoustic cloaking.
g.design: Every option follows the same 'Because X, engineers...' frame and borrows a real detail from the passage, so readers have to connect the limitation in paragraph 1 to the shift in paragraph 2. The question uses none of the key words from the correct answer.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Phase-change material thermal energy storage and paraffin wax latent heat capacity in building envelope insulation

g.passage: Many buildings overheat in the afternoon and cool too quickly at night. Some engineers address this problem by adding phase-change materials, such as paraffin wax, to wall panels. When indoor temperatures rise, the wax melts and absorbs a large amount of heat without getting much warmer itself. __For example, a thin layer of paraffin in a test wall in Spain kept the room behind it about four degrees cooler during the hottest part of the day.__ Later, as the air cools, the wax hardens again and slowly releases the stored heat back into the room.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It introduces the main problem that phase-change materials are meant to solve.
It describes a drawback that limits the use of paraffin wax in buildings.
It gives a specific case showing the heat-absorbing effect described in the previous sentence.
It explains what happens to the wax after the air in a room cools down.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 "For example"로 시작하며, 바로 앞 문장에서 설명한 '왁스가 녹으며 열을 흡수한다'는 효과를 스페인 시험 벽 사례로 보여 준다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A의 문제(건물 과열)는 첫 문장에서 제시되므로 밑줄 문장의 기능이 아니다. B처럼 단점을 말하는 내용은 지문 어디에도 없다. D의 왁스가 굳으며 열을 방출하는 과정은 마지막 문장의 내용이다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence starts with "For example" and uses the test wall in Spain to show the effect described just before it: the wax melts and soaks up heat. That makes C the answer. A doesn't work because the problem of buildings overheating is introduced in the first sentence, not the underlined one. B is wrong because the text never mentions a drawback. D describes the wax hardening and releasing heat, which is what the last sentence does, not the underlined one.
g.design: 이 문항은 예시를 알리는 표지어 "For example" 하나만 알아보면 풀 수 있다(easy). 오답 3개는 지문 속 다른 문장들이 맡은 기능이나, 지문에 없는 단점을 설명하도록 만들었다.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Electrochromic smart window vanadium oxide film and ion intercalation enabling variable light transmission control

g.passage: Electrochromic smart windows can shift from clear to tinted when a small voltage is applied. Many of these windows use a thin film of vanadium oxide placed between layers of glass. When voltage is applied, lithium ions move into the film, a process called intercalation, and the film changes how much light it lets through. __For example, on a hot afternoon, a building manager can darken the windows to block glare and reduce heat, then lighten them again in the evening to let in more daylight.__ Because the change can be reversed many times, engineers see these windows as a way to cut cooling costs without installing blinds.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It introduces a problem with vanadium oxide films that engineers have not yet solved.
It explains the chemical steps by which lithium ions enter the vanadium oxide film.
It presents a reason that some engineers prefer blinds over electrochromic windows.
It offers a practical situation showing how the windows' adjustable tint might be used.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 "For example"로 시작하며, 앞에서 설명한 빛 투과량 조절 기능을 건물 관리자가 실제로 활용하는 상황으로 보여 준다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 지문에 해결되지 않은 문제가 언급되지 않으므로 틀리다. B의 이온 삽입 과정 설명은 밑줄 앞 문장의 역할이다. C는 지문이 오히려 블라인드 없이 비용을 줄일 수 있다고 하므로 틀리다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence begins with "For example" and shows a building manager using the windows' ability to change light transmission in a real situation. That makes D the correct answer. A is wrong because the text never mentions an unsolved problem. B describes the sentence before the underlined one, which explains ion intercalation. C is wrong because the text actually says the windows can cut costs without blinds.
g.design: 쉬운 문항이다. 명시적 신호어 "For example" 하나로 '예시' 기능을 파악할 수 있게 했고, 오답은 다른 문장의 역할을 가져오거나 지문 내용을 뒤집는 전형적 오개념으로 구성했다.

c.instruction: 짧은 지문에 '주장→근거→결론' 또는 순서가 있는 2~3개 사건을 넣고, 특정 문장 하나가 전체 흐름에서 어떤 논리적 역할(예: 결론을 예비하는 전환, 앞선 주장을 제한하는 단서)을 하는지 묻는다. 정답은 두 단계 이상을 연결해야 나오도록 만들고, 오답 3개는 각각 '한 단계만 본 역할', '역할을 인접 문장과 혼동', '전체 목적과 개별 문장 기능을 뒤바꾼 것'으로 구성한다.
c.seed: technology and engineering — Friction-stir welding tool rotation mechanics and thermomechanical bonding in aluminum aircraft fuselage assembly

g.passage: Conventional fusion welding melts the edges of two metal sheets so that they flow together, but many high-strength aluminum alloys used in aircraft fuselages crack or grow porous when they melt and then solidify again. Friction-stir welding avoids this problem. A rotating tool with a protruding pin is plunged into the seam and moved along it, and friction raises the metal's temperature to roughly 80 percent of its melting point. __At that temperature the aluminum does not liquefy; instead it softens enough that the spinning pin can sweep material from the front of the tool around to its back, where the two sheets are pressed together into a single mass.__ Because the joint forms without the metal ever passing through a liquid state, it is spared the solidification defects that weaken fusion welds, which is why several aircraft manufacturers have replaced thousands of rivets with friction-stir seams.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It explains how a joint can form while the metal stays solid, which provides the basis for the text's claim that friction-stir seams avoid a weakness of fusion welds.
It explains why high-strength aluminum alloys crack when they are melted, which sets up the problem that friction-stir welding is designed to solve.
It explains how the rotating tool generates heat through friction, which accounts for the temperature the metal reaches during the process.
It explains why aircraft manufacturers have replaced rivets with friction-stir seams, which is the main purpose of the text as a whole.
g.design: 밑줄 문장은 '고체 상태 접합 메커니즘'을 설명하는 동시에 마지막 문장의 결론(응고 결함 회피)의 전제가 되는 2단계 역할을 한다. 오답은 문제 제기(앞 문장 역할 혼동), 열 발생 설명(한 단계만 본 역할), 전체 목적과의 뒤바꿈으로 구성했다.
g.explanation:
정답 A: 밑줄 문장은 알루미늄이 녹지 않고 연화된 상태에서 핀이 재료를 옮겨 접합한다는 원리를 설명한다. 마지막 문장은 바로 이 점(액체 상태를 거치지 않음)을 근거로 응고 결함이 없다는 결론을 내린다. 즉 메커니즘 설명과 결론의 근거라는 두 단계를 모두 연결해야 한다.
B: 용융 시 균열 문제는 첫 문장이 제시한 내용으로, 인접 문장의 역할과 혼동한 것이다. 밑줄 문장은 문제를 제기하지 않고 해결 원리를 설명한다.
C: 마찰에 의한 열 발생과 온도는 앞 문장의 내용이다. 밑줄 문장은 그 온도를 출발점으로 삼을 뿐 열 발생을 설명하지 않으므로, 한 단계만 본 해석이다.
D: 리벳을 대체한 이유는 마지막 문장의 결론이다. 또한 밑줄 문장 하나의 기능을 글 전체의 목적과 뒤바꿔 놓았다.
g.explanation_en:
Correct answer A: The underlined sentence explains that the aluminum softens without melting, so the pin can move material around the tool and press the sheets together. The final sentence then relies on exactly this point—that the metal never becomes liquid—to conclude that the seams avoid solidification defects. To get the answer, you have to connect two steps: the sentence explains the mechanism, and that mechanism is the support for the conclusion.
B: The cracking of melted alloys is described in the first sentence. This choice mixes up the underlined sentence with an earlier one. The underlined sentence explains the solution; it doesn't raise the problem.
C: Frictional heating and the resulting temperature come from the sentence just before. The underlined sentence starts from that temperature but doesn't explain how the heat is produced, so this choice sees only one step.
D: Replacing rivets is the conclusion in the final sentence. This choice also swaps the role of one sentence for the purpose of the whole text.

c.instruction: 두 인물 또는 두 텍스트의 입장을 짧게 제시하고, 한쪽이 다른 쪽의 특정 주장에 대해 보일 반응(동의/반박/보완)을 직접 언급하지 않은 채 추론하도록 묻는다. 정답은 두 입장의 차이를 바탕으로 간접 추론해야 나오게 하고, 오답 3개는 '두 입장을 뒤바꿔 반응을 반대로 서술', '한쪽 입장만 근거로 사용', '텍스트에 없는 새로운 반응을 지어낸 것'으로 만든다.
c.seed: technology and engineering — Microelectromechanical systems MEMS accelerometer capacitive sensing and Coriolis force detection in smartphone motion sensing

g.passage: Engineers who design the tiny motion sensors inside smartphones disagree about where accuracy problems originate. Rina Takahashi, a MEMS designer, argues that the capacitive accelerometer itself is close to its physical limits: a silicon proof mass shifts by less than a nanometer, and the resulting change in capacitance between interleaved comb fingers is so small that thermal noise in the structure, not anything downstream, sets the floor on precision. Electrical engineer Marcus Obi accepts that such noise exists but contends that most errors users actually notice, such as a compass that drifts or a step counter that miscounts, arise when software misreads the signals. In vibrating MEMS gyroscopes, for instance, a resonating mass is deflected sideways by the Coriolis force when the phone rotates, and that deflection is likewise read capacitively. __Obi points out that when such gyroscopes are recalibrated in software to correct for temperature-dependent shifts in their output, drift in phone orientation readings drops sharply even though the sensing structures remain unchanged.__
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents evidence that Takahashi would cite to show that software corrections confirm that thermal noise in the sensing structure limits accuracy.
It offers an observation suggesting that the physical limit Takahashi emphasizes may not account for the errors that phone users typically encounter.
It describes a result that Obi uses to argue that Coriolis-based gyroscopes are more reliable than capacitive accelerometers.
It reports a finding that leads both engineers to agree that MEMS sensors should be redesigned to reduce temperature sensitivity.
g.explanation: 정답 B: 밑줄 문장은 구조(하드웨어)는 그대로인데 소프트웨어 보정만으로 오차가 크게 줄었다는 관찰이다. 이는 오차의 주원인이 구조의 열잡음이라는 Takahashi의 주장과 달리, 사용자가 겪는 오류는 신호 해석 문제라는 Obi의 입장을 뒷받침하므로, Takahashi가 강조하는 물리적 한계가 실제 사용자 오류를 설명하지 못할 수 있음을 시사한다. A: 두 입장을 뒤바꾼 오답. 소프트웨어 보정의 성공은 Takahashi가 아니라 Obi에게 유리한 증거다. C: Obi의 입장 일부만 근거로 삼아 지문에 없는 센서 간 신뢰도 비교를 지어냈다. Obi는 자이로스코프를 예시로 썼을 뿐이다. D: 지문에 없는 새로운 반응을 지어낸 오답. 두 사람이 합의한다는 내용도, 하드웨어를 다시 설계하자는 결론도 없으며, 오히려 구조는 바꾸지 않았다는 점이 핵심이다.
g.explanation_en: B is correct. The underlined sentence reports that drift dropped sharply after software recalibration alone, while the sensing structures stayed the same. That supports Obi's view that the errors users notice come from how software reads the signals. It also challenges Takahashi's claim that thermal noise in the structure sets the limit on accuracy. So the sentence suggests that the physical limit she stresses may not explain everyday errors. A swaps the two positions. A software fix working is evidence for Obi, not for Takahashi. C relies only on Obi's side and adds a reliability comparison between gyroscopes and accelerometers that the text never makes. Obi uses gyroscopes only as an example. D invents a new reaction. The engineers never agree, and nobody calls for a redesign. In fact, the point is that the hardware was left unchanged.
g.design: 이 문항은 두 엔지니어의 입장을 대비시켰습니다. 밑줄 문장은 Obi의 관찰이 Takahashi의 주장을 간접적으로 반박한다는 점을 추론해야 기능을 판단할 수 있게 만들었습니다. 오답은 지시에 맞춰 세 유형으로 구성했습니다. A는 두 입장을 뒤바꿨고, C는 한쪽 입장만 근거로 삼았으며, D는 지문에 없는 반응을 지어냈습니다.

c.instruction: 실험 결과나 비용-효과 같은 구체적 근거 하나를 지문에 제시하고, 이 근거가 특정 결론을 뒷받침하는 정확한 논리적 역할(전면 입증/부분 입증/반증/조건부 지지)을 고르게 한다. 정답은 근거의 범위와 결론의 범위가 정확히 일치하는 것으로 하고, 오답 3개는 각각 '근거가 실제보다 넓은 결론을 지지한다고 과장', '근거의 일부만 반영해 좁게 해석', '근거와 결론의 인과 방향을 뒤바꾼 것'으로 만든다.
c.seed: technology and engineering — Electrowetting-on-dielectric digital microfluidic device electrode voltage control and droplet movement for chemical reactions

g.passage: In electrowetting-on-dielectric (EWOD) devices, tiny droplets sit on a grid of electrodes coated with a thin insulating layer. Applying voltage to the electrode next to a droplet makes that edge of the droplet spread, pulling the whole droplet forward, so chemists can move, merge, and mix reagents without pumps or channels. Engineer Lena Osei suspected that the slow, steady voltage ramps used in most EWOD devices were not needed for reliable movement and that sharp, brief pulses could move droplets just as well while reducing the charge that slowly builds up in the insulating layer and eventually stalls droplets. In her tests with aqueous droplets, pulsed control moved droplets across 2,000 electrode steps with a failure rate no higher than ramped control, and measured charge buildup was about 40 percent lower. __However, when Osei repeated the trials with droplets containing dissolved proteins, which tend to stick to the surface, pulsed control failed to move droplets far more often than ramped control did.__ Osei concludes that pulsed control is a better choice for moving simple aqueous droplets, though not yet for every type of sample used in EWOD chemistry.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents a finding indicating that pulsed control is unsuitable for EWOD devices in general, overturning the advantage reported in the earlier tests.
It presents a finding showing only that protein droplets stick to EWOD surfaces, a detail separate from the comparison of the two voltage methods.
It presents a finding that marks the limit of the earlier results, explaining why Osei confines her recommendation to one kind of sample.
It presents a finding suggesting that the high failure rate of protein droplets is what caused Osei to develop pulsed control in the first place.
g.explanation:
정답 C: 밑줄 문장은 단백질 시료에서는 펄스 제어가 실패율이 훨씬 높았다는 결과를 제시한다. 이 결과가 앞의 수용액 실험 결과의 적용 범위를 제한하므로, 오세이는 결론을 '단순 수용액 방울'로 한정한다. 근거의 범위와 결론의 범위가 정확히 일치한다.
A(과장): 밑줄 결과는 단백질 시료에만 해당하므로, 펄스 제어가 EWOD 전반에 부적합하다거나 수용액 결과를 뒤집는다는 결론까지 지지하지 않는다. 결론에서도 수용액에 대한 이점은 그대로 유지된다.
B(일부만 반영해 좁게 해석): 단백질이 표면에 달라붙는다는 점만 보고 두 방식의 비교를 놓쳤다. 밑줄 문장의 핵심은 펄스 제어와 램프 제어의 실패율 비교이며, 이것이 결론의 단서 조항과 직접 연결된다.
D(인과 방향 역전): 펄스 제어는 전하 축적을 줄이려는 동기에서 나왔고, 단백질 실험은 그 뒤에 진행된 후속 시험이다. 단백질 실패가 펄스 제어 개발의 원인이었던 것이 아니다.
g.explanation_en:
C is correct. The underlined sentence reports that pulsed control failed far more often than ramped control when the droplets contained proteins. That finding sets a boundary on the earlier aqueous-droplet results, which is why Osei's conclusion recommends pulsed control only for simple aqueous droplets. The scope of the evidence matches the scope of the conclusion exactly.
A overstates the evidence. The result applies only to protein-containing droplets, so it doesn't show that pulsed control is unsuitable in general, and it doesn't overturn the aqueous results. Osei still keeps that advantage in her conclusion.
B reads the sentence too narrowly. It picks up on protein stickiness but ignores the main point: the sentence compares the failure rates of the two voltage methods, and that comparison is what leads to the qualification in the conclusion.
D reverses cause and effect. Pulsed control was motivated by the goal of reducing charge buildup. The protein trials were a later follow-up test, so protein failures did not prompt the method's development.
g.design: I gave one concrete result (pulsed control failing more often with protein droplets) and made its exact role partial, condition-limiting support for a narrowed conclusion. Each wrong answer matches one assigned error type: A overgeneralizes, B reflects only part of the evidence, and D reverses the causal direction. All four options use the same sentence frame.
